children.translated_text: that is unfounded, because:

children.text: sambhinnālāpahiṃsādikutsitārthopadarśanam |
children.translated_text: 'Incoherent speech, the display of reprehensible purposes such as violence,

children.text: krīḍāśīlapiśācādeḥ kāryaṃ tāsu na vidyate ||
children.translated_text: which is the work of playful ghosts and the like — none of that is found in those [teachings].

children.text: pramāṇadvayasaṃvādi mataṃ tadviṣaye 'khile |
children.translated_text: The doctrine that accords with both means of valid cognition (<s>pramāṇas</s>), in its entire subject matter,

children.text: yasya bādhā pramāṇābhyāmaṇīyasy api nekṣate ||
children.translated_text: whose contradiction by the two means of valid cognition is not seen even by the minutest [investigation],

children.text: yathātyantarokṣe 'pi na pūrvāparabādhitam |
children.translated_text: which, even though thoroughly imperceptible [in some aspects], is not contradicted in its earlier and later [portions],

children.text: karuṇādiguṇotpatteḥ sarvapuṃsāṃ pravartakam ||
children.translated_text: which promotes the arising of compassion and other virtues in all people,

children.text: sarvānuśayasaṃdohapratipakṣābhidhāyakam |
children.translated_text: which proclaims the antidote to the entire mass of latent afflictions (<s>anuśaya</s>),

children.text: nirvāṇagaradvārakapāṭapuṭabhedam ||
children.translated_text: which opens the bolt on the door of the city of <s>nirvāṇa</s> —

children.text: tac cet krīḍanaśīlānāṃ rakṣasāṃ vā vaco bhavet |
children.translated_text: if that were indeed the speech of playful <s>Rākṣasas</s> (demons),

children.text: ta eva santu sambuddhāḥ sarvatallakṣaṇasthiteḥ ||
children.translated_text: then let them indeed be the fully enlightened <s>Buddhas</s>, since they possess all those characteristics!'

children.text: na ca nāmni vivādaḥ | na ca nāmanivṛttau vastu nirvartate | pratyuta vedasyaiva krīḍanaśīlapiśācādipraṇītatvaṃ yuktaṃ sambhāvayitum | yena gośavādiṣu yogeṣv agamyāgamanādayo 'satyasamudācārāḥ saṃprakāśitāḥ | lokaprasiddhiś ca | trayo vedasya kartāro munibhaṇḍaniśācarāḥ | iti alam atinirbandhena ||
children.translated_text: And there is no dispute about the name. And merely by removing the name, the thing is not negated. On the contrary, it would be more appropriate to consider the <s>Vedas</s> themselves as composed by playful ghosts and the like, since in rituals such as the <s>gośava</s> (bull sacrifice) and the like, conduct such as approaching forbidden women and other false practices are promulgated. And there is the well-known popular saying: 'The three makers of the <s>Vedas</s> are the buffoon, the rogue, and the night-stalker (demon).' Enough of this excessive insistence.

children.text: nanu sarvajñatvaṃ vītarāgāditvena vyāptam iṣyate | tadviruddhaṃ ca rāgādiyogitvam, tatkāryaṃ ca vacanam | tad etad vyāpakaviruddhakāryabhūtaṃ vacanaṃ sarvajñābhāvaṃ sādhayati paramparayā viruddhatvād iti cet | na | rāgādīnāṃ vacasaś ca kāryakāraṇabhāvāsiddheḥ | tathā hi vacanaviśeṣo rāgādikāryam, yo rāgeṇaiva janitaḥ, vacanamātraṃ vā |
children.translated_text: [Objection:] Now, omniscience (<s>sarvajñatva</s>) is accepted as pervaded by freedom from passion (<s>vītarāgatva</s>) and the like. And the possession of passion (<s>rāga</s>) and the like is contradictory to that [freedom from passion], and speech is an effect of that [passion]. Therefore, this speech — being an effect that contradicts the pervader — establishes the non-existence of omniscience, indirectly, through contradiction. [Reply:] No — because the causal relation between passion and the like, on the one hand, and speech, on the other, is unestablished. For either a specific speech is the effect of passion and the like — i.e., that which is produced solely by passion — or else speech in general [is such an effect].

children.text: tatra na tāvat prathamaḥ pakṣaḥ | tādṛśasya vacanasya niścayopāyāsambhavāt | asabhyamaithunācāraprakāśakaṃ vacanaṃ tatkāryam iti cet | na | abhiprāyasya durlakṣyatvāt | virakto 'pi raktavac ceṣṭate, rakto 'pi viraktavad ity abhiprāyo durbodaḥ | tataś ca viśiṣṭavyavahārasya sāṃkaryeṇa na tatraikāntena rāgānumānaṃ yujyate | nāpi vacanamātraṃ rāgādikāryam | asaṃmukhībhūtarāgādayo 'pi hi svābhimatadevatāstutividhāne mātrādigurujanasambhāṣaṇādau ca vacanamātram uccārayantaḥ samupalabhyante | na ca yad yadabhāve bhavati tasya tatkāryatocyate, atiprasaṅgāt | rāgādiyogyatā tarhi vacasaḥ kāraṇam, tayā vinopalakhaṇḍalādau vacanasyādarśanād iti cen | na | karaṇaguṇavaktukāmate hi vacanasya hetuḥ | tadabhāvād evopalakhaṇḍalādau nivartate, na rāgādiyogyatāyā abhāvāt | yadi kāraṇaguṇādisakalatadanyakāraṇabhāve 'pi rāgādiyogyatābhāvān notpadyate vacanam iti sidhyet tasyāḥ kāraṇatvam | upalakhaṇḍalādau tu vaktukāmatā nāsti | tat kathaṃ tatkāraṇatvaṃ vacasām iti | evaṃ tarhi vaktukāmataiva rāgo 'stu | iṣṭatvān na kiñcid bādhitaṃ syāt, nāmni vivādābhāvāt | paramārthataḥ punar nityasukhātmātmīyadarśanākṣiptaṃ sāśravaviṣayaṃ cetaso 'bhiṣvaṅgaṃ rāgam āhuḥ |
children.translated_text: In that regard, the first alternative is untenable — because there is no means of ascertaining such a [specific type of] speech [as caused by passion]. [Objection:] Speech that reveals obscene sexual conduct — that is an effect of [passion]. [Reply:] No — because one's real intention is difficult to discern. Even one who is detached may behave like one who is attached; even one who is attached may behave like one who is detached — thus the intention is hard to know. Therefore, because of the confusion in distinguishing specific behaviors, it is not possible to infer passion from [speech] with certainty. Nor is speech in general the effect of passion and the like. For even those in whom passion and the like have not arisen are observed uttering speech in general when composing hymns to their beloved deity, in conversation with mothers and other elders, and so forth. And one cannot say that whatever occurs in the absence of [something else] is the effect of that [something], because of over-extension. [Objection:] Then the capacity for passion is the cause of speech, because speech is not observed in stones and the like, which lack that capacity. [Reply:] No — because the cause of speech is the possession of vocal organs, the quality of the instrument, and the desire to speak. It is from the absence of these alone that [speech] does not occur in stones and the like — not from the absence of the capacity for passion. If, even in the presence of all other causes including the quality of the instruments, speech did not arise due to the absence of the capacity for passion — then the causal status of that [capacity] would be established. But in stones and the like, there is no desire to speak — so how can that [capacity for passion] be the cause of speech? [Objection:] Then let the desire to speak itself be [what is meant by] passion — since this is accepted [by us], nothing is refuted, there being no dispute about the name. [Reply:] But in the ultimate sense, they define passion (<s>rāga</s>) as the mind's attachment to contaminated objects (<s>sāśravaviṣaya</s>), impelled by the view of self and 'mine' as eternal and blissful.

children.text: niṣpannasarvasampatter vivakṣāpi na yujyata iti cet | adoṣo 'yam, parārthatvādivivakṣāyāḥ | vītarāge 'rthāsaṅgābhāvāt kathṃ parārthāpi pravṛttir iti cet | na | āsaṅgam antareṇa karuṇayāpi pravṛtteḥ |
children.translated_text: [Objection:] For one who has accomplished all perfections, even the desire to speak is not appropriate. [Reply:] This is no fault — because the desire to speak is for the benefit of others. [Objection:] In one free from passion, how can there be activity even for the benefit of others, given the absence of attachment to objects? [Reply:] No — because activity is possible through compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>) even without attachment.

children.text: saiva rāga iti cet | iṣṭatvād adoṣaḥ | rāgasya tu svarūpam uktam | kāruṇikasyāpi niṣphalārambho na yukta iti cet | na | parārthasyaiva phalatvāt | iṣṭalakṣaṇatvāt phalasyeti yat kiñcid etat |
children.translated_text: [Objection:] That [compassion] itself is passion. [Reply:] Since it is accepted [by us as different from passion], this is no fault. The nature of passion has been stated [above]. [Objection:] Even for one who is compassionate, an effort without result is not appropriate. [Reply:] No — because benefiting others is itself the result. [Objection:] Because the result is defined by what is desired. [Reply:] This is inconsequential.

children.text: nanu nirvikalpasya bhagavataḥ kathaṃ tasyām avasthāyāṃ karuṇāsambhavaḥ | duḥkhavikalpaprabhavā hi karuṇety anvayavyatirekābhyām anyatvena niścitam |
children.translated_text: [Objection:] But how is compassion possible for the Blessed One who is in the non-conceptual state? For compassion arises from the conceptual cognition of suffering — this is ascertained through positive and negative concomitance as something different [from non-conceptual cognition].

children.text: tataś ca kāraṇābhāvāt kathaṃ kāryasambhava iti cet | na | yathā kumbhakāranivṛttāv api svasantānamātrabhāvinī ghaṭādisthitis tathotthāpakavikalpābhāve 'pi samanantarapratyayabalād anālambanakaruṇāpravṛtter avāryatvāt | yad āhur guruvaḥ
children.translated_text: And therefore, how can the effect [compassion] arise in the absence of its cause? [Reply:] No — just as even after the potter has ceased [his activity], pots and so forth persist through the continuation of their own series alone, so too, even in the absence of the conceptual cognition that generated [compassion], compassion without an object (<s>anālambanā karuṇā</s>) flows forth by the force of the immediately preceding condition (<s>samanantarapratyaya</s>) and cannot be obstructed. As our teachers have said:

children.text: sattāropakṛto 'pi bhāvanavaśāt kāṭhinyam āpat tathā śaithilye 'pi yathāsya duḥkhahataye sāndras tathaiva śramaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Even the one who benefits living beings, through the power of meditation (<s>bhāvanā</s>), attains a state of hardness (impassivity); and even in that slackening [of effort], his exertion for the removal of their suffering is nonetheless intense.'

children.text: utpāde tu phalasya hetuniyamo no tu prabandhasthitau tasmād duḥkhadṛśaḥ kṣaye 'pi vilasanmaitryādaye 'smai namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'There is a fixed rule of cause regarding the origination of the result, but not regarding the continuity of the series. Therefore, even at the cessation of the perception of suffering, we bow to Him in whom loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>) and the like shine forth.'

children.text: etenaitad api nirastaṃ yad āha Kārikāyām
children.translated_text: By this, the following [objection] is also refuted, which is stated in the <s>Kārikā</s>:

children.text: rāgādirahite cāsamin nirvyāpāre vyavasthite |
children.translated_text: 'And in this one, who is free from passion (<s>rāga</s>) and the like, who has become inactive,

children.text: deśanānyapraṇītaiva syād ṛte pratyavekṣaṇāt ||
(ŚV II 137)

children.translated_text: the teaching would only be composed by others — without [his own] reflection.'

children.text: nanu yadi nāmaiva vaktṛtvaṃ sarvajñatvena sahāviruddhaṃ dehendriyabuddhyādiyogitvaṃ tu viruddham eva | sarvajñatāvyāpakavītarāgatvaviruddharāgādikāraṇatvād dehādīnām |
children.translated_text: [Objection:] Now, even if speech itself is not contradictory to omniscience, still, the possession of body, sense-organs, intellect, and so forth is indeed contradictory. Because body and the like are causes of passion and the like, which contradict freedom from passion — the pervader of omniscience.

children.text: tataś ca pratiṣedhyavyāpakaviruddhakāraṇopalambhāt sarvajñābhāva iti cet | ucyate | dehādīnāṃ hetutve 'pi naiṣāṃ kevalānāṃ sahakārimātrāṇām ātmābhiniveśalakṣaṇopādānakāraṇavikalānāṃ rāgādijanakatvam ity agamakā eva dehādayaḥ sarvajñābhāvasya | tasmāj jñeyatvādīnām apy asāmarthyān na paraparikalpitānumānato 'pi sarvajñābhāvaḥ |
children.translated_text: And therefore, from the apprehension of a cause that contradicts the pervader of what is to be negated, the non-existence of omniscience [follows]. [Reply:] It is said: even granting that body and the like are causes [of passion], they alone — being merely auxiliary causes, incomplete without the material cause (<s>upādānakāraṇa</s>) characterized by attachment to self (<s>ātmābhiniveśa</s>) — are not productive of passion and the like. Therefore, body and the like are simply non-indicative of the non-existence of omniscience. Thus, even from the inference fabricated by others based on cognizability (<s>jñeyatva</s>) and the like, the non-existence of omniscience [does not follow], due to [those reasons'] incapacity.

children.text: nāpi svavikalpitaṃ śābdādikaṃ bhagavato bādhakam | tathā hi yady api teṣāṃ sati prāmāṇye 'numāna evāntarbhāvaḥ, anantarbhāve cāprāmāṇyam eveti sthūlaṃ dūṣaṇam asti, tathāpi tatprāmāṇyam abhyupagamyāpi brūmaḥ | yat tāvat pauruṣeyavacanaṃ tadapramāṇam eva bhavatām | na ca vaidikaṃ kiñcid vacanaṃ sarvanarāsarvajñatvapratipādakam upalabhyate | pratyuta nimittanāmni śākhāntare sphuṭataram eva sarvajñaḥ pratipāditaḥ |
children.translated_text: Nor are the verbal and other [arguments] devised by oneself invalidating for the Blessed One. For, although there is a rough objection that if they are valid, they are subsumed under inference, and if not subsumed, they are simply invalid — nevertheless, even conceding their validity, we say: Whatever speech is of human origin (<s>pauruṣeya</s>) — that is simply not a valid means of knowledge, according to you. And no Vedic statement is found that establishes the non-omniscience of all human beings. Rather, in another branch [of the <s>Veda</s>] known as <s>Nimitta</s>, an omniscient being is established quite explicitly.

children.text: tathā hi:	sa vetti viśvaṃ na ca tasya vettā ityādinā ca sarvajño vede pratipāditaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For instance: 'He knows the universe, and no one knows Him' — by this and similar [statements], an omniscient being is established in the <s>Veda</s>.

children.text: nāpy upamānāt tadabhāvaḥ sidhyati | tathā hi smaryamāṇam eva gavādivastu purovartigavayādisādṛśyopādhi gavādyupādhi vā sādṛśyam upamānena pratīyata iti sthitiḥ | na ca sarvajñasantānavartīni cetāṃsi kenacit sarvajñenānubhūtāni yataḥ smaraṇena viṣayīkriyeran, paracittavitter ayogāt ||
children.translated_text: Nor is the non-existence [of an omniscient being] established through analogy (<s>upamāna</s>). For the established position is that through analogy, a similarity is cognized — either the similarity that is the qualification of a remembered thing like a cow with the gayal and the like present before one, or the similarity that is the qualification of the gayal and the like with the cow. And the cognitions occurring in the mental continuum of an omniscient being have not been experienced by any [other] omniscient being, such that they could be made the object of memory — because cognition of others' minds is impossible.

children.text: yat punar uktaṃ Kumārilena
children.translated_text: Now as for what <s>Kumārila</s> has said:

children.text: narān dṛṣṭvā tv asravajñān sarvān evādhunātanān |
children.translated_text: 'Having observed that all present-day human beings are non-omniscient,

children.text: tatsādṛśyopamānena śeṣāsarvajñaniścayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: by analogy based on their similarity, the certainty of the non-omniscience of the rest [follows].'

children.text: tad apy ayuktam, adhunātanasarvajñatvāniścayāt | niścaye cātmany eva sarvajñatvābhyupagamaprasaṅgāt |
children.translated_text: That too is untenable — because the non-omniscience of present-day [beings] is itself uncertain. And if it were certain, there would be the unwanted consequence of accepting omniscience in oneself.

children.text: nāpy arthāpattir bādhikā | yato dṛṣṭaḥ śruto vārtho 'nyathā nopapadyata iti adṛṣṭārthaparikalpanam arthāpattir ucyate | na cāsarvajñatvam antareṇa sarvanareṣu kaścid artho dṛṣṭaḥ śruto vā nopapadyate yatas tadarthāpattyā parikalpyeta | nanu saṃsārasya tāvad anāditvaṃ pramāṇena pratītam | tac ca na sarvajñena jñāyate, tajjñānāvadheḥ parastād asattve 'nāditākṣatiprasaṅgāt, tadanyathānupapadyamānaṃ sarvabhāvānām anāditvaṃ sarvajñābhāvaṃ sādhayatīti cet |
children.translated_text: Nor is <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) an invalidator. For presumption is said to be the supposition of an unseen [fact] when a seen or heard fact cannot be accounted for otherwise. And there is no fact, either seen or heard, regarding all human beings, that cannot be accounted for without [positing] non-omniscience, such that [non-omniscience] would be presumed from [the impossibility of accounting for] that. [Objection:] But the beginninglessness of <s>saṃsāra</s> is established by a valid means of knowledge. And that cannot be known by an omniscient being — because if there were a point beyond which [his] knowledge did not extend, the beginninglessness [of <s>saṃsāra</s>] would be violated. The beginninglessness of all entities, which cannot be accounted for otherwise, establishes the non-existence of omniscience.

children.text: ucyate | upayuktasarvajñāpekṣayā tāvad idam adūṣaṇam | tasyānāditvājñāne 'pi upayuktasarvajñatvāvyāhateḥ | sarvasarvajñasyāpy abhāve sādhye 'samartheyam arthāpattiḥ | tathā hi yathā saṃsārasyānāditve pūrvapūrvavastusattāyā anavadhitvaṃ tathā sarvajñajñānasyāpi pūrvapūrvavastusattāvyāpakatvenānavadhiprasaratā iti | ajñātasyaikasyāpi vastuno 'navasthiteḥ | saty api sarvajñe 'nāditvam upapadyamānaṃ na sarvajñābhāvam ākṣipati | tataś cārthāpattir api na sarvajñasya bādhikā |
children.translated_text: [Reply:] With respect to an omniscient being of practical [rather than absolute] scope, this is no refutation at all — because even if he does not know the beginninglessness [as such], the practically useful omniscience is not violated. And even when the non-existence of an absolutely omniscient [being] is to be proved, this presumption is incapable [of proving it]. For just as, when <s>saṃsāra</s> is beginningless, the existence of prior and prior things has no limit — so too the knowledge of the omniscient being, pervading the existence of prior and prior things, extends without limit. Because not even one thing remains unknown. Even with an omniscient being existing, the beginninglessness [of <s>saṃsāra</s>] is accounted for and therefore does not necessitate the non-existence of an omniscient being. Thus presumption too is not an invalidator of the omniscient [being].

children.text: na cābhāvapramāṇabādhyaḥ sarvajñaḥ | pramāṇapañcakanivṛttir
children.translated_text: Nor is the omniscient [being] invalidated by the means of knowledge [called] absence (<s>abhāvapramāṇa</s>). The cessation of [apprehension by] the five means of knowledge

children.text: abhāvapramāṇam iṣyate | tatra nivṛttir iti prasajyavṛttyā
children.translated_text: is accepted as the means of knowledge [called] absence. In this regard, 'cessation' —

children.text: pramāṇānutpattimātram abhipretam, atha vā paryudāsavṛttyā
children.translated_text: in the <s>prasajyavṛtti</s> (verbally qualified negation) sense, means the mere non-arising of [valid] means of knowledge; or alternatively, in the <s>paryudāsa</s> (nominally bound negation) sense,

children.text: vastvantaram, vastvantaram api jaḍarūpaṃ jñānarūpaṃ vā, jñānam api
children.translated_text: [it means] some other real entity; and that other entity is either of an insentient nature or of the nature of cognition; and cognition is either

children.text: jñānamātram, ekajñānasaṃsargivastujñānaṃ veti vikalpāḥ |
children.translated_text: mere cognition, or cognition of the entity associated with a single [act of] cognition — these are the alternatives.

children.text: tatra na tāvan nivṛttimātram abhāvapramāṇam upapadyate | tat
children.translated_text: Among these, first, mere cessation is not tenable as the means of knowledge [called] absence. For

children.text: khalu nikhilaśaktivikalatayā na kiñcit | yac ca na kiñcit tat kathaṃ
children.translated_text: that [mere cessation], being devoid of all capacities, is nothing whatsoever. And what is nothing — how can it

children.text: prameyaṃ paricchindyāt, tadviṣayaṃ vā vijñānaṃ janayet, pratītaṃ vā
children.translated_text: delimit an object of knowledge, or generate a cognition having that as its object? And if it is [supposedly] apprehended,

children.text: tat katham iti sarvam andhakāranartanam | yathoktam: na hy abhāvaḥ
children.translated_text: how [is that so]? — all this is dancing in darkness. As it has been said: 'Absence is neither anyone's

children.text: kasyacit pratipattiḥ pratipattihetur vā | tasyāpi vā kathaṃ
children.translated_text: cognition nor the cause of cognition. And of it, too, how

children.text: pratipattir
iti |
children.translated_text: [End of quote.]
[can there be] cognition?'

children.text: nāpi vastvantaratāpakṣe jaḍarūpaḥ pramāṇābhāvaḥ saṅgacchate, tasya prameyaparicchedāyogāt | paricchedasya jñānadharmatvāt | nāpi jñānamātrasvabhāvo 'bhāvaḥ | deśakālasvabhavaviprakṛṣṭasyāpi tato 'bhāvaprasaṅgāt | tadapekṣayāpi vijñānamātratvāt tasya | athaikajñānasaṃsargisvabhāvo 'numanyate, tadā kṣatam abhāvapramāṇapratyāśayā, adhyakṣaviśeṣasyaivābhāvapramāṇanāmakaraṇāt | tasya cāsmābhir dṛśyānupalambhākhyasādhanatvena svīkṛtatvāt | dṛśyānupalambhaś ca bhagavadabhāvasādhane 'samartha iti pūrvam evāveditam |
children.translated_text: Nor does [absence] as a real entity of an insentient nature succeed as a means of knowledge [called] absence, because it is incapable of delimiting the object of knowledge — since delimitation is a property of cognition. Nor is absence of the nature of mere cognition — because even what is remote in place, time, and nature would then [have to count as] absent from it [i.e., from any cognition]. Since [any cognition] is merely cognition with respect to that [remote thing] too. If, however, [absence is accepted as] having the nature of [an entity] associated with a single cognition, then the hope for a distinct means of knowledge [called] absence is shattered — because [it would simply be] a naming of a particular type of perception (<s>adhyakṣa</s>) as 'absence-knowledge.' And that [perception] has been accepted by us as having the nature of the proof called 'non-apprehension of what is fit to be apprehended' (<s>dṛśyānupalambha</s>). And 'non-apprehension of what is fit to be apprehended' is incapable of proving the non-existence of the Blessed One — as was already stated earlier.

children.text: kiṃ ca, kaḥ punar ayaṃ pramāṇābhāvo 'bhimato bhavatām | svapramāṇagaṇanivṛttir atha sarvaprāṇigaṇapramāṇanivṛttiḥ | tatra svapramāṇagaṇanivṛttir vyabhicāriṇī, tasyāṃ satyām api vyavahitasyārthasyānapahnavatvāt | parapramāṇanivṛttis tv asarvavido 'siddhā | yad āha
children.translated_text: Furthermore, what exactly is this 'non-apprehension by a means of knowledge' that is intended by you [as proving absence]? Is it the cessation of [apprehension by] your own set of means of knowledge, or the cessation of [apprehension by] the means of knowledge of all sentient beings? Among these, the cessation of [apprehension by] one's own set of means of knowledge is deviant [i.e., commits the fallacy of deviation] — because even when it obtains, the existence of a remote object cannot be denied. But the cessation of [apprehension by] others' means of knowledge is unestablished for one who is not omniscient. As it is said:

children.text: sarvādṛṣṭiś ca sandigdhā svādṛṣṭir vyabhicāriṇī |
children.translated_text: '[The claim of] non-perception by all is doubtful, and non-perception by oneself is deviant —

children.text: vindhyādrirandhradūrvāder adṛṣṭāv api sattvataḥ || iti ||
children.translated_text: because of the existence [of things] even when unseen, like <s>dūrvā</s> grass in the caves of the <s>Vindhya</s> mountains.'

children.text: tad evaṃ nābhāvapramāṇato 'pi sarvajñaniṣedha iti sthitam ||
children.translated_text: Thus it is established that even from the means of knowledge [called] absence, there is no negation of the omniscient [being].

children.text: nanu tathāpi sadvyavahārārthaṃ sādhakam apy asya na vidyate | tathā hi sarvavido 'tīndriyatvāt na tāvad asmadādipratyakṣam asya sādhakam | yathā cāsmābhir asau nopalabhyate tathāsmajjātīyair apy apratyakṣasvabhāvaniyamāt | na cāyaṃ kālāntare 'bhūd iti ca kalpanā yujyate | yathā hi kālatvādidānīntanakālavad iti anenānumānena nirākartuṃ śakyate, na tathā sādhayitum | Kārikā
children.translated_text: [Objection:] Even so, there is no proof (<s>sādhaka</s>) for [the omniscient being's] positive existence either, for the purpose of valid everyday usage. For, since the omniscient being is supersensory, our perception and that of others like us is not a proof for it — because those like us are of the same nature [as us], necessarily unable to perceive [what is supersensory]. And the conjecture that 'this [omniscient being] existed at another time' is also not appropriate. For just as it can be refuted by the inference 'it is a time, therefore like the present time,' it cannot similarly be proved. The <s>Kārikā</s>:

children.text: sarvajñakalpanā tv anyair vede vāpauruṣeyatā |
children.translated_text: 'The supposition of an omniscient being by some, or the uncreated-ness of the <s>Veda</s> —

children.text: tulyavat kalpyate yena tenedaṃ saṃpradhāryate ||
children.translated_text: by him who equally supposes [both], this should be considered.'

children.text: sarvajño dṛśyate tāvan nedānīm asmadādibhiḥ |
children.translated_text: 'An omniscient being is not seen at present by us and the like;

children.text: nirākaraṇavac chakyā na cāsīd iti kalpanā ||
children.translated_text: the supposition that [such a one] existed [in the past] is not possible — just as refutation [is possible through inference].'

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: [End of quote.]

children.text: nāpy anumānataḥ sarvajñasiddhiḥ | tatpratibaddhaliṅgāniścayāt |
children.translated_text: Nor is the establishment of the omniscient being possible through inference — because there is no certainty of a logical mark invariably connected with it.

children.text:
kiṃ ca sarvajñasattāsādhane sarvo hetuḥ trayīṃ doṣajātiṃ
	nātivartate asiddhatvaṃ viruddhatvam anaikāntika-tvaṃ ceti | tathā hi
	sarvajñe dharmaṇi kriyamāṇe na taddharmo hetuḥ siddhaḥ | tasyaiva
	dharmiṇaḥ sādhyatvenāsiddhatvāt | siddhau vā vaiyarthyaprasaṅgāt |
	asarvajñe dharmiṇi na sarvajñasiddhiḥ | hetoḥ
	sarvajñaviparītasādhanatvena viruddhatvāt | nāpi
	sarvajñāsarvajñadharmo hetuḥ | tasyānaikāntikatvāt | tasmān nānumānato
	'pi sarvajñasiddhiḥ |
children.translated_text: Furthermore, in proving the existence of an omniscient being, every logical reason does not escape the three classes of faults: unestablished-ness (<s>asiddhatva</s>), contradiction (<s>viruddhatva</s>), and inconclusiveness (<s>anaikāntikatva</s>). For when [the inference is] constructed with respect to the omniscient being as the subject, the logical reason is not established as a property of the subject — because that very subject is unestablished, being what is to be proved; or if [the subject is already] established, there would be the unwanted consequence of pointlessness. When the subject is a non-omniscient [being], the establishment of omniscience [in it] does not follow — because the logical reason would be contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>), proving the opposite of omniscience. Nor can a property of both omniscient and non-omniscient [beings] serve as the logical reason — because it would be inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>). Therefore, even through inference, the establishment of omniscience is not possible.

children.text: Kārikā
children.translated_text: The <s>Kārikā</s>:

children.text: dṛṣṭo na caikadeśo 'sti liṅgaṃ yo vānumāpayet |
children.translated_text: 'No partial [instance] is seen, nor any logical mark that could lead to inference [of the omniscient being].'

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: [End of quote.]

children.text: nāpy āgamagamyaḥ | āgamo hi dvividhaḥ pauruṣeyo nityaś ca | tatra pauruṣeyo 'py āgamaḥ tadīyo vā tatra pramāṇam, narāntarapraṇīto vā | na tāvat tadīyaḥ | anyonyasaṃśrayāpatteḥ | tathā hy āgamasya sarvajñoktatve prāmāṇyam | asya ca prāmāṇye satyasmāt sarvajñasiddhir iti | narāntarapraṇītas tu pramāṇatvenānabhimata evety ato 'pi na sarvajñasiddhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Nor is [the omniscient being] knowable through <s>āgama</s> (scripture). For <s>āgama</s> is of two kinds: human-authored and eternal. Among these, the human-authored <s>āgama</s> — either the <s>āgama</s> of that [omniscient being] himself is the authority therein, or one composed by another person. It is not, first of all, his own [scripture], because of the fallacy of mutual dependence (<s>anyonyāśraya</s>). For thus: the <s>āgama</s> has validity [only] if spoken by an omniscient being; and the establishment of the omniscient being [depends] on the validity of this [āgama] — [this is circular]. And a scripture composed by another person is simply not accepted as a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid cognition), and therefore too there is no proof of the omniscient being.

children.text: kiṃ ca sarvajñapraṇītād vacanāt sarvajñasiddhau kim aparāddhaṃ svavacanena yenāto 'py asau na gamyeta | nāpi nityāgamagamyaḥ sarvajñaḥ, tathāvidhasya sarvajñapratipādakasya nityāgamasyābhāvāt | yac copaniṣadādau sarvajñapratipādakavākyaṃ tasyānyārthatvaṃ draṣṭavyam | na ca nityavākyasyānityasarvajñatvapratipādakatvam, nirviṣayatvaprasaṅgāt |
children.translated_text: Moreover, if the omniscient being is established from the words of an omniscient being, what fault has one's own words committed that the omniscient being should not be known from them as well? Nor is the omniscient being knowable through eternal <s>āgama</s>, because there is no such eternal <s>āgama</s> that establishes an omniscient being. And as for the statements in the <s>Upaniṣads</s> and elsewhere that speak of an omniscient being, they should be understood as having a different meaning. And an eternal statement cannot establish a non-eternal omniscient being, because it would then be without a [real] referent.

children.text: kiṃ ca yady aṅgīkṛto nityāgamaḥ, kiṃ sarvajñakalpanayā, nitya evāgamo dharme pramāṇaṃ bhaviṣyati |
children.translated_text: Moreover, if eternal <s>āgama</s> is accepted, what need is there to postulate an omniscient being? The eternal <s>āgama</s> itself will serve as the <s>pramāṇa</s> (authority) regarding <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: Kārikā
children.translated_text: Verse:

children.text: na cāgamena sarvajñas tadīye 'nyonyasaṃśrayāt |
children.translated_text: The omniscient being is not [established] through <s>āgama</s>; if [one relies on] his own [scripture], there is mutual dependence.

children.text: narāntarapraṇītasya prāmāṇyaṃ gamyate katham ||
children.translated_text: How can the validity of a scripture composed by another person be ascertained?

children.text: na cāpy evaṃ paro nityaḥ śakyo labdhum ihāgamaḥ |
children.translated_text: Nor can the opponent's eternal <s>āgama</s> be obtained in this way.

children.text: dṛṣṭaś ced arthavādatvaṃ tatpare syād anityatā ||
children.translated_text: If [such a statement] is observed [in scripture], it would be a mere laudatory passage (<s>arthavāda</s>); and with regard to that [omniscient being], there would be non-eternality.

children.text: āgamasya ca nityatve siddhe tatkalpanā vṛthā |
children.translated_text: And if the eternality of <s>āgama</s> is established, the postulation of that [omniscient being] is futile,

children.text: yatas taṃ pratipatsyante dharmam eva tato narāḥ ||
children.translated_text: since people will then understand <s>dharma</s> directly from that [āgama] itself.

children.text: Bṛhaṭṭīkāpi
children.translated_text: The <s>Bṛhaṭṭīkā</s> also [states]:

children.text: na cāgamavidhiḥ kaścin nityaḥ sarvajñabodhakaḥ |
children.translated_text: There is no eternal scriptural injunction that reveals the omniscient being.

children.text: ityādi saptacatvāriṃśat ślokāḥ saprapañcam etam arthaṃ pratipādayanti | tad evam āgamato 'pi na sarvajñasiddhiḥ |
children.translated_text: And so on — forty-seven verses elucidate this meaning in detail. Thus, the omniscient being is not established through <s>āgama</s> either.

children.text: nāpy upamānapramāṇasamadhigamyaḥ | upamānaṃ hi sadṛśagrahaṇanāntarīyakapravṛttikam asannikṛṣṭārthagocaram | yathā gavanagrahaṇadvāreṇa goḥ smaraṇam | na ca sarvajñasadṛśaḥ kaścid asti | Kārikā
children.translated_text: Nor is [the omniscient being] ascertainable through the <s>pramāṇa</s> of <s>upamāna</s> (comparison). For <s>upamāna</s> operates necessarily through the apprehension of similarity and has as its object something not in direct contact [with the senses] — as, for example, the recollection of a cow through the apprehension of a <s>gavana</s> (wild ox). But there is nothing similar to an omniscient being. Verse:

children.text: sarvajñasadṛśaṃ kañcid yadi paśyema samprati |
children.translated_text: If we could now perceive someone similar to an omniscient being,

children.text: upamānena sarvajñaṃ jānīyāmas tato vayam ||
children.translated_text: then we could know the omniscient being through <s>upamāna</s> (comparison).

children.text: nāpy arthāpattitaḥ sarvajñasiddhiḥ | dṛṣṭaḥ śruto vārtho 'nyathā nopapadyata ity adṛṣṭārthaparikalpanam arthāpattilakṣaṇam | na cātra pramāṇapratītaṃ kiñcid vastv asti yat sarvajñam anatareṇānupapadyamānaṃ tat sattām upanayet | tan nārthāpattir api sarvajñasādhanī |
children.translated_text: Nor is the omniscient being established through <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption). The definition of <s>arthāpatti</s> is the postulation of an unperceived fact when a seen or heard fact cannot be explained otherwise. But here there is no entity cognized through a <s>pramāṇa</s> which, being inexplicable without an omniscient being, would lead to the positing of its existence. Therefore <s>arthāpatti</s> too does not prove the omniscient being.

children.text: na ca pramāṇapañcakābhāvasvabhāvād abhāvapramāṇād asya siddhiḥ, vastvabhāvasādha

natvād asya | pratyutāyam evāsyābhāvaṃ sādhayatīti pratipāditam | yad apīdaṃ kārikābṛhaṭtīkayor ekaṣaṣṭyā ślokaiḥ sarvajñasiddhaye bauddhasya sādhanam āśaṅkya dūṣitaṃ tad api ghṛṇākaram iti granthavistarabhayān na likhitam |
children.translated_text: On the contrary, it has been demonstrated that this very [abhāva-pramāṇa] proves the non-existence of this [omniscient being]. As for the objection raised and refuted in sixty-one verses of the <s>Kārikā</s> and <s>Bṛhaṭṭīkā</s> regarding the Buddhist's proof for establishing the omniscient being — that too is pitiable, and has not been written out here for fear of excessive length of the treatise.

Nor is its establishment through <s>abhāva</s> (absence) — a <s>pramāṇa</s> whose nature is the non-existence of the five <s>pramāṇas</s> — [possible], since this [abhāva-pramāṇa] establishes the non-existence of entities.

children.text: tathā hy etāni kila saugataiḥ sarvajñasādhanāya sādhanāny abhidhīyante | sarvajño 'stīti satyam, sarvajñoktatvāt, dharmābhyupadeśakatvāt, buddhaḥ sarvajña iti cirapravṛttadṛḍhasmṛteḥ, prathamataram aśeṣaśiṣyajanavargasyānekavidhacittacaittādiparijñānāt, sakalapadārtharāśitattvopadeśād iti ||
children.translated_text: For the Buddhists are said to put forward these proofs for establishing the omniscient being: 'An omniscient being exists' — this is true, because [the teaching] was spoken by an omniscient being; because it teaches <s>dharma</s>; because of the long-standing firm tradition that '<s>Buddha</s> is omniscient'; because at the very outset he comprehended the manifold mental states (<s>citta</s>), mental factors (<s>caitta</s>), and so forth of all his disciples without exception; and because he taught the true nature of all categories of reality.

children.text: tasmāt sthitam etat nātīndriyadarśī sākṣād asti, api tu nityavacanadvāreṇaiva tasya darśanam iti | tad evaṃ sarvathā sarvajñasādhakapramāṇāsabhavād ayukto bauddhānāṃ sarvajñe sadvyavahāra iti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, it stands established that there is no direct seer of what is beyond the senses; rather, the perception of such [truths] is only through the medium of eternal statements. Thus, since there is in every way an impossibility of a <s>pramāṇa</s> that establishes an omniscient being, the Buddhists' positive discourse regarding an omniscient being is unjustified.

children.text: atrocyate | anumānād anyato 'siddhau siddhasādhanam | anumānād apīty asiddham, anumānasya pūrvam uktatvāt | tatpratibaddhaliṅgāniścayād ityādidūṣaṇaprabandho 'pi prativyūḍha ity upayuktasarvajñas tāvat trailokyālokaḥ siddhaḥ |
children.translated_text: To this we reply: [The objection] 'Since it is not established from sources other than inference, it is a case of <s>siddhasādhana</s> (proving what is already proved)' — [the sub-argument] 'from inference also [it is not established]' is itself unestablished, since inference has already been demonstrated [to be valid] earlier. The series of objections beginning with 'because of the uncertainty of the logical mark connected with that' has also been refuted. Therefore, <s>Sarvajña</s> (the Omniscient One), who is of practical benefit — that is, the Light of the Three Worlds — is established.

children.text: sarvasarvjñapakṣe 'pīdaṃ sādhanam |
children.translated_text: And this proof [applies] even on the thesis that all [Buddhas] are omniscient:

children.text:
yat pramāṇasaṃvādiniścitārthavacanaṃ tat sākṣāt paramparayā vā
	    tadarthasākṣātkārijñānapūrvakam | yathā dahano dāhaka iti vacanam |
	    pramāṇasaṃvādi niścitārthavacanaṃ cedam | kṣaṇikāḥ sarvajñasaṃskārā
	    ity arthataḥ kāryahetuḥ | nāsyāsiddhiḥ,
	    sarvabhāvakṣaṇabhaṅgaprasādhanād asya vacanasya satyārthatvāt | nāpi
	    virodhaḥ, sapakṣe bhāvāt | na cānaikāntikaḥ, vacanamātrasya
	    saṃśayaviparyāsapūrvakatve 'pi pramāṇaniścitārthavacanasya
	    sākṣātpāramparyeṇa tadarthasākṣātkārijñānapūrvakatvāt | anyathā
	    niyamena pramāṇasaṃvādāyogāt ||
children.translated_text: A statement whose determined content accords with the <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid cognition) is preceded — directly or through a chain — by knowledge that directly perceives that content. Just as the statement 'fire burns.' A statement whose determined content accords with the <s>pramāṇas</s> — this is what we have here. 'All <s>saṃskāras</s> (conditioned formations) are momentary' — this is in substance a <s>kāryahetu</s> (inference from effect). There is no <s>asiddhi</s> (unestablishedness) of this, since this statement has true content, as the momentary destruction of all entities has been fully demonstrated. Nor is there <s>virodha</s> (contradiction), because [the reason] is present in the <s>sapakṣa</s> (similar instances). Nor is it <s>anaikāntika</s> (inconclusive), because although mere statements in general may be preceded by doubt or error, a statement whose determined content accords with the <s>pramāṇas</s> is preceded — directly or through a chain — by knowledge that directly perceives that content. Otherwise, there could be no invariable accord with the <s>pramāṇas</s>.

children.text: ayaṃ ca bhāṣyakārīyaḥ sarvasarvajñaprasādhakaprayogaḥ paṇḍitajitāribhiḥ prapañcita iti tata eva pracayato 'avadhārya iti |
children.translated_text: And this method of proof for establishing the omniscience of all [Buddhas], which belongs to the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> (<s>Dharmakīrti</s>), has been elaborated by the learned <s>Jitāri</s>, and should be ascertained from that [work] in full.

children.text: durvāraprativādivikramam anādṛtya pramāprauḍhitaḥ sarvajño jagadekacakṣurudagād eṣa prabhāvo 'tra ca |
children.translated_text: Disregarding the irresistible prowess of opponents, the Omniscient One, the sole eye of the world, arose, exalted by right reasoning — and herein lies this power.

children.text: sambuddhasthitimedinīkulagirer asmadguroḥ kin tv ayaṃ saṃkṣepo mama ratnakīrtikṛtinas tadvistaratrāsinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But this is merely a summary by me, <s>Ratnakīrti</s>, who is daunted by the elaboration, of [the teaching of] our master, the mountain at the base of the earth where the <s>Sambuddha</s> (Fully Awakened One) stands.

children.text: viśvam astu śubhād asmād yathecchaṃ ratimanmataḥ |
children.translated_text: May the universe, through this merit, attain the desire of <s>Rati</s> and <s>Manmatha</s> (Love) as it wishes.

children.text: mañjuvajraś ca paryante tatpādaṃ satphalapradam ||
children.translated_text: And may <s>Mañjuvajra</s>, at the end, [grant] the fruit-bestowing feet of that [Buddha].

children.text: ahañ ca mañjuvajraḥ syāṃ mañjughoṣo 'tha mañjuvāk |
children.translated_text: And may I become <s>Mañjuvajra</s>, or <s>Mañjughoṣa</s>, or <s>Mañjuvāk</s>,

children.text: mañjuśrīr vādirāṇmamañjukumāro jinadhūrdharaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, king of debaters, <s>Mañjukumāra</s>, upholder of the <s>Jina</s>'s [teaching].

children.text: || sarvjñasiddhiḥ samāptā ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Sarvajñasiddhi</s> (Proof of Omniscience) is concluded.

children.text: Īśvarasādhanadūṣaṇam
children.translated_text: <s>Īśvarasādhanadūṣaṇam</s> (Refutation of the Proof of God)

children.text: Mikogami_Ms 18b1
oṃ namas tārāyai |
children.translated_text: Oṃ, homage to <s>Tārā</s>.

children.text: sūktaratnāśrayatvena jitaratnākarād idam |
children.translated_text: Being a receptacle of jewels of well-spoken words, surpassing the ocean of jewels,

children.text: guror vāgambudheḥ smartuṃ kiñcid ākṛṣya likhyate ||
children.translated_text: this [work] is written, drawing a little [water] to bring to mind the ocean of the speech of my <s>Guru</s>.

children.text: rītiḥ sudhānidhir iyaṃ sattame madhyavartini |
children.translated_text: This style is a treasury of nectar for one who stands in the excellent middle path,

children.text: vidveṣiṇi viṣajvālā kiñcij jñe tu na kiñcana ||
children.translated_text: a flame of poison for the hostile, and nothing at all for one who knows but little.

children.text: ihaite naiyāyikādayo vivādapadasya kṣitidharādeḥ svarūpopādānopakaraṇasaṃpradānaprayojanavibhāgapravīṇaṃ sarvajñatādiguṇaviśiṣṭaṃ puruṣaviśeṣam icchanti | yad āhuḥ
children.translated_text: Here, these <s>Naiyāyikas</s> and others posit a special <s>Puruṣa</s> (Person) who is skilled in the essential nature, material cause, instrumental cause, recipient, and purpose of the objects under dispute such as the earth and so forth, and who is distinguished by qualities such as omniscience. As they state:

children.text: eko vibhuḥ sarvavidekabuddhisamāśrayaḥ śāśvata īśvarākhyaḥ |
children.translated_text: One, all-pervading, omniscient, the substratum of a single cognition, eternal, called <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord),

children.text: pramāṇam iṣto jagato vidhātā svargāpavargārthibhir arthanīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He is accepted as the <s>pramāṇa</s> (authority), the creator of the world, to be sought by those desiring heaven and liberation.

children.text: iti |
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: sa ca kathaṃ sidhyatīti paryanuyuktāḥ sādhanam idam ācakṣate |
children.translated_text: And when asked how this [Īśvara] is established, they state this proof:

children.text: vivādādhyāsitaṃ buddhimaddhetukam |
children.translated_text: The object under dispute has an intelligent cause,

children.text: kāryatvāt |
children.translated_text: because it is an effect (<s>kārya</s>).

children.text: yat kāryaṃ tadbuddhimadhetukam | yathā ghaṭaḥ |
children.translated_text: Whatever is an effect has an intelligent cause — as, for example, a pot.

children.text: kāryaṃ cedam |
children.translated_text: And this [world] is an effect.

children.text: tasmād buddhimadhetukam iti |
children.translated_text: Therefore it has an intelligent cause.

children.text: hetoḥ parokṣārthapratipādakatvam anubhūteṣu hetvābhāseṣu na śakyam āvedayitum | hetvābhāsāś ca pañca | yathoktam
children.translated_text: The capacity of the logical reason (<s>hetu</s>) to demonstrate an imperceptible object cannot be revealed when [the reason falls among] perceived pseudo-reasons (<s>hetvābhāsa</s>). And there are five pseudo-reasons. As stated:

children.text: savyabhicāraviruddhaprakaraṇasamasādhyasamātītakālā iti |
children.translated_text: The deviant (<s>savyabhicāra</s>), the contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>), the reason that is equivalent to the thesis (<s>prakaraṇasama</s>), the reason that is equivalent to the <s>sādhya</s> (<s>sādhyasama</s>), and the one whose time has passed (<s>atītakāla</s>).

children.text:
tatra na tāvad ayaṃ sādhyasamo
	  hetuḥ | asiddho hi sādhyasamaḥ kathyate | sa ca saṃkṣepato
	  vibhajyamāno dvidhā vyavatiṣṭhate | āśrayāsiddhatvād vāsiddho yathā
	  surabhi gaganāravindamaravindatvād iti | saty api cāśraye pramāṇena
	  sambandhāsiddher asiddho yathā anityaḥ śabdaḥ sāvayavatvād iti | na
	  cābhyāṃ prakārābhyāṃ prastutasya hetor asiddhir asti |

kṣmāruhādau
	  dharmiṇi pramāṇasamadhigate kāryatvasya sādhanasya pramāṇpratītatvāt |
	  cirotpannaparvatādau ca dharmiṇi kāryatvaṃ sāvayavatvena hetunā
	  boddhavyam | tad yathā: vivādapadaṃ kāryam | sāvayavatvāt | yat
	  sāvayavaṃ tat kāryam | yathā vastram | tathā cedam | tasmāt kāryam
	  iti |
children.translated_text: because <s>kāryatva</s> (being an effect), the proving property, is cognized by a <s>pramāṇa</s> in the <s>dharmin</s> (subject) such as trees and the like. And in the case of a <s>dharmin</s> such as a mountain that arose long ago, its <s>kāryatva</s> should be understood through the reason of having parts (<s>sāvayavatva</s>). Thus: the object under dispute is an effect, because it has parts. Whatever has parts is an effect — as, for example, cloth. And this [object] is likewise. Therefore it is an effect.

Among these, first, this reason is not <s>sādhyasama</s> (equivalent to what is to be proved). For <s>sādhyasama</s> is said to be unestablished (<s>asiddha</s>). And that, when analyzed briefly, is of two kinds: unestablished because the locus (<s>āśraya</s>) is unestablished — as in 'the sky-lotus is fragrant, because it is a lotus'; and unestablished because the connection [of the reason with the locus] is not established by a <s>pramāṇa</s> even though the locus exists — as in 'sound is non-eternal, because it has parts.' And neither of these two forms of unestablishedness applies to the reason under consideration,

children.text: nanu sāvayavatvena hetunā dravyāṇām eva kāryatvaṃ sidhyati | na tu tatsamavetānāṃ guṇakarmādīnām | teṣām avayavasambandhābhāvād iti cet | satyam | teṣāṃ kāryaguṇāditvena hetvantareṇa kāryatvam adhigantavyam | tathā hi;
children.translated_text: Objection: Through the reason of having parts, the <s>kāryatva</s> of substances (<s>dravya</s>) alone is established, but not that of qualities (<s>guṇa</s>), actions (<s>karma</s>), and so forth that inhere in them, since those lack the relation of having parts. Reply: True. Their <s>kāryatva</s> should be understood through another reason, namely their being effect-qualities and the like. Thus:

children.text: janmabhājo vivādādhyāsitanityetarasamavāyino guṇādayaḥ |
children.translated_text: Qualities and other [categories] that are subject to origination and that inhere in the non-eternal [substances] that are objects of dispute,

children.text: kāryaguṇā
ditvāt |
children.translated_text: and the like.
[are established as effects] because they are effect-qualities

children.text: yo yaḥ kāryaguṇādiḥ sa sarvas tathā, yathā ghaṭādirūpādiḥ |
children.translated_text: Every such effect-quality and the like is so — as, for example, the color and other [qualities] of a pot and so forth.

children.text: tathā caite |
children.translated_text: And these [qualities under dispute] are likewise.

children.text: tasmāj janmabhājaḥ | iti |
children.translated_text: Therefore they are subject to origination.

children.text: kāryañca
children.translated_text: And 'effect' (<s>kārya</s>)

children.text: na svakāraṇasamavāyaḥ, sāmānyaviśeṣo vā
children.translated_text: should not be understood as [meaning] inherence in its own cause, or as universality and particularity (<s>sāmānya</s> and <s>viśeṣa</s>),

children.text: boddhavyaṃ
children.translated_text: but should be understood

children.text: , yenāsya pradhvaṃsāvyāpakatvād bhāgāsiddhatā syāt, kiṃ tu kāraṇādhīnasvarūpamātram | tac ca śabdādiṣv iva pradhvaṃsādāv api pratyakṣeṇādhigatam iti na tāvad ayam asiddho hetuḥ |
children.translated_text: as merely having one's essential nature dependent on a cause. And that is cognized through direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) even in the case of destruction (<s>pradhvaṃsa</s>) and the like, just as in the case of sound and so forth — since [kāryatva defined as cause-dependence] is not excluded by destruction [as kāryatva defined as inherence would be]. Therefore this reason is not unestablished.

children.text: nāpi viruddhaḥ | tathā

hi yo vipakṣa eva vartate sa khalu sādhyaviparyayavyāpteḥ sādhyaviruddhaṃ sādhayan viruddho 'bhidhīyate | yathā nityaḥ śabdaḥ kṛtakatvād iti | na cāyaṃ tathā, prasiddhakartṛkeṣu ghaṭādiṣu sapakṣeṣu sadbhāvadarśanāt |
children.translated_text: indeed, that [reason] which occurs only in the <s>vipakṣa</s> (dissimilar instances) is called contradictory, because being pervaded by the opposite of the <s>sādhya</s>, it proves what is contrary to the <s>sādhya</s> — as in 'sound is eternal, because it is produced.' But this [reason of kāryatva] is not like that, because it is observed to be present in the <s>sapakṣa</s> (similar instances), namely pots and the like, which are known to have a [intelligent] maker.
Nor is it contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>). For

children.text: nanu
children.translated_text: Objection:

children.text: buddhimatpūrvakatve sādhye siddhasādhanam | abhimataṃ hi pareṣām api karmajatvaṃ kāryajātasya, karmaṇaś ca cetanātmakatvāt, cetanāhetukatvād vā | taddhetukatvaṃ ca jaga
children.translated_text: If what is to be proved (<s>sādhya</s>) is merely 'being preceded by an intelligent being,' then it is <s>siddhasādhana</s> (proving what is already established). For even the opponents accept that the entire class of effects is produced by action (<s>karma</s>), and action is of the nature of consciousness, or [at least] has consciousness as its cause. And the world has that [consciousness] as its cause.

children.text: taḥ |
children.translated_text: [continued from above]

children.text: sarvajñapūrvakatve tu sādhye vyāptiḥ svapne 'pi
children.translated_text: But if what is to be proved is 'being preceded by an omniscient being,' then the <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) has never been observed,

children.text: nopalabdhā |
children.translated_text: even in a dream.

children.text: dṛṣṭāntaś ca sādhyahīnaḥ, kulālādīnām asarvajñatvāt | viruddhatā ca hetor asarvajñapūrvakatvenaiva kumbhādau kāryatvasya vyāpter upalabdheḥ | na copalabdhimatpūrvakatvamātraṃ sādhanaviṣayaḥ, tadviśeṣasya tu sarvajñapūrvakatvasyātadviṣayasyāpi tataḥ siddhir iti sāmpratam | tathā
children.translated_text: And the example (<s>dṛṣṭānta</s>) lacks the <s>sādhya</s>, since potters and the like are not omniscient. And the reason would be contradictory, since <s>kāryatva</s> is observed to be pervaded only by being preceded by a non-omniscient [agent] in the case of pots and the like. And it is not the case that mere 'being preceded by a cognizing being' is the scope of the proof while the specific [claim of] 'being preceded by an omniscient being,' which is not within its scope, is nevertheless established from it — that would be improper. For

children.text: hi yady asau viśeṣo na sādhanaviṣayaḥ katham atas tatsiddhiḥ,
children.translated_text: if that specific [claim] is not within the scope of the proof, how can it be established from it?

children.text: sidhyan vā
children.translated_text: And if it is established,

children.text: katham aviṣayaḥ, viṣayaś cet katham ananvayadoṣaṃ na spṛśed iti cet |
children.translated_text: how is it not within the scope? And if it is within the scope, how does it not incur the fault of non-concomitance (<s>ananvaya</s>)?

children.text: ucyate | sāmānyamātravyāptāv apy antarbhāvitaviśeṣasya sāmānyasya pakṣadharmatāvaśena sādhyadharmiṇy anumānāt viśeṣaviṣayam anumānaṃ bhavaty eva | itarathā sarvānumānocchedaprasaṅgā
children.translated_text: We reply: Even when the <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) extends only to the universal (<s>sāmānya</s>), since the universal contains the particular within it, through the force of the universal being a property of the <s>sādhyadharmin</s> (the subject in which the sādhya is to be proved), inference concerning the particular does indeed arise. Otherwise, there would be the absurd consequence of the destruction of all inference.

children.text: t | tathā hi vahnyanumānam api na sāmānyamātraviṣayam, tasya prāg eva siddhatvāt | nāpi tadviśiṣṭagirigocaram vahnitvasāmānyasya tatsambandhābhāvena tadviśeṣaṇatvānupapatteḥ |
children.translated_text: For even the inference of fire is not concerned with the mere universal [fire], since that is already established beforehand. Nor does it concern fire as qualified by [being on] that mountain, since the universal 'firehood' cannot qualify that [mountain] due to the absence of a connection between them.

children.text: itarathā gotvasamavāyād iva gāvaḥ śābaleyādayaḥ parvato 'pi vahnitvasamavāyād vahniḥ prasajyeta | asty eva girer vahnitvena saṃyuktasamavāyaḥ sa
children.translated_text: Otherwise, just as cows such as <s>Śābaleya</s> and others [are cows] by the inherence of cowness, a mountain too, by the inherence of firehood, would absurdly become fire. If [you say] there is indeed a relation of conjunct-inherence (<s>saṃyuktasamavāya</s>) between the mountain and firehood,

children.text: mbandha iti cet | tarhi nāpratipadya parvatasaṃyuktaṃ vahniviśeṣam asau śakyapratipattir iti vahniviśeṣasyāpy ananumānam | tathā cānanvayadoṣaprasaṅgaḥ | indriyānumāne 'py ayam eva nyāyo draṣṭavyaḥ, yathendriyalakṣaṇakaraṇaviśeṣasiddhiḥ | tathā hi tatrāpi nendriyakaraṇikā kācit kriyopalabdhā | na khalu
children.translated_text: then that [firehood] cannot be cognized without first cognizing the particular fire conjoined with the mountain — hence the particular fire too would not be inferred. And thus the fault of non-concomitance would follow. The same reasoning should be applied to the inference of the sense organs as well — namely, how a specific instrument characterized as a sense organ is established. For there too, no activity brought about by a sense-organ instrument is directly perceived. Indeed,

children.text: cchidādyaḥ
children.translated_text: cutting and such

children.text: kriyā
children.translated_text: activities

children.text: indriyasādha
children.translated_text: do not prove sense organs

children.text: nāḥ,
children.translated_text: [as their instruments],

children.text: vraścanādīnām
children.translated_text: since cutting and the like

children.text: anindriyatvāt |
children.translated_text: are not [performed by] sense organs.

children.text: na ca vraścanādisādhanā sambhavati rūpādiparicchittilakṣaṇā kriyā |
children.translated_text: Nor is the activity characterized as the apprehension of color and the like possible as one whose instrument is cutting and the like.

children.text: tasmād yathā kriyātvasāmānyasya karaṇamātrādhīnatvavyāptatve pakṣadharmatāvaśād indriyalakṣaṇakaraṇaviśeṣasiddhis
children.translated_text: Therefore, just as from the invariable concomitance of the general property of being an activity (<s>kriyātva</s>) with dependence on a mere instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>), the specific instrument characterized as a sense-faculty is established by the force of the property belonging to the subject (<s>pakṣadharmatā</s>),

children.text: tathehāpi saty api kāryatvasyopādānopakaraṇasaṃpradānaprayojanajñakartṛmātravyāptatve 'pi vivādādhyāsiteṣu pakṣadharmatāvaśā
children.translated_text: so here too, even though the property of being an effect (<s>kāryatva</s>) is pervaded by dependence on a mere agent who knows the material cause (<s>upādāna</s>), the accessory instrument (<s>upakaraṇa</s>), the recipient (<s>saṃpradāna</s>), and the purpose (<s>prayojana</s>) — by the force of the property belonging to the subject as superimposed by the dispute,

children.text: d upādānādyabhijñasāmānyasyākṣiptaviśeṣasyaiva siddhiḥ | anyathā sāmānyasyāpi vyāpakābhimatasya na siddhiḥ syāt,
children.translated_text: what is established is only the general [property] of being one who knows the material cause and the like, whose specific determination is implied. Otherwise, even the general [property] that is considered the pervader would not be established,

children.text: nirviśeṣasyāsambhavādviśeṣasya vā tasyānupapatteḥ |
children.translated_text: because a [general] without specific determination is impossible, or because that specific determination [itself] would be untenable.

children.text: asarvajñasya cātrādṛṣṭādibhedavijñānasahitasyādhiṣṭhātṛbhāvāsambhavāt sarvajñātmaka eva viśeṣo balād āpatati |
children.translated_text: And since it is impossible for a non-omniscient being — even one possessing knowledge of distinctions such as <s>adṛṣṭa</s> (unseen merit) and the like — to be a superintending agent in this [creation], the specific determination as constituted by omniscience necessarily imposes itself.

children.text: nanūpādānādyabhijñakartṛmātreṇevāsarvajñatvadehitvādibhir api vyāptir aśakyaparihārā, vyabhicārādarśanasya samānatvād iti cet | na | sarvajñatvāsarvajñatvayor dehitvādehitvayor vā kāryotpattāv anupayogāt | na hi sārvajñyaṃ kartṛṇām yogyatām upasthāpayati, asarvajñebhyaḥ kumbhakārādibhyaḥ kumbhādīnām aprasavaprasaṅgāt | nāpy asārvajñyaṃ kumbhakārād eva keyūrādīnām apy utpattiprasaṅgāt | tathā na dehitvaṃ kāryotpattāv upayogi kumbhakārād eva keyūrādīnām utpattiprasaṅgāt | nādehitvaṃ kumbhakārād ghaṭādīnām anutpādaprasaṅgāt | tataś copādānādyabhijñapuruṣapūrvakatvam eva kāryatvasya vyāpakam | tad eva ca buddhimatpuruṣapūrvakatvaśabdavācyam |
children.translated_text: If one objects: 'Invariable concomitance is equally irrefutable with non-omniscience, embodiment, and the like, just as with the mere agent who knows the material cause and the like — because the non-observation of deviation is the same [in both cases]' — [we reply:] No. Because omniscience and non-omniscience, or embodiment and non-embodiment, have no relevance to the production of effects. For omniscience does not establish the capacity of agents — otherwise, there would be the absurd consequence that pots and the like would not be produced by non-omniscient potters and the like. Nor does non-omniscience [establish capacity] — otherwise, bracelets and the like would also be produced by a potter [who makes pots]. Likewise, embodiment is not useful for the production of effects — otherwise, bracelets and the like would be produced by a potter. Nor is non-embodiment [useful] — otherwise, pots and the like would not be produced by a potter. Therefore, what pervades the property of being an effect is precisely being preceded by a person who knows the material cause and the like. And that alone is what is expressed by the term 'being preceded by an intelligent person.'

children.text: tena yady api buddhimatpūrvakatvamātraṃ vyāptiviṣayas tathāpi tadviśeṣasya sarvajñatvasya pakṣadharmatābalāt pratilambha iti viśeṣaviṣayam anumānam | na coktadoṣaprasaṅgaḥ, tasya sādhyadṛṣṭāntayor dharmavikalpād utkarṣāpakarṣalakṣaṇaparyanuyogasya sarvānumānasādhāraṇyenānumānamātraprāmāṇyapratikṣepahetutvāt ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, even though the scope of the invariable concomitance is merely 'being preceded by an intelligent being,' nevertheless, the specific [determination] of omniscience is obtained by the force of the property belonging to the subject (<s>pakṣadharmatā</s>) — thus the inference has a specific [conclusion] as its object. Nor does the aforementioned fault arise, because the objection based on degrees of superiority and inferiority [between subject and example], arising from the differentiation of properties in the provable and the example, is common to all inferences and would therefore undermine the validity of inference as such.

children.text: etena yad uktaṃ kaṇikāyāṃ
yadi kulālādīnāṃ katipayopakaraṇādijñānam, na samastopakaraṇādijñatā, tarhi tenaiva nidarśanena īśvarasyāpi
children.translated_text: 'If potters and the like have knowledge of only some instruments and the like, and not knowledge of all instruments and the like, then by that very example, God too

children.text: tadupakaraṇādimātrajñānam | tanmātrajñāne na sarvajñatāsiddhiḥ |
children.translated_text: would have knowledge of only those instruments and the like. If [He knows] only those, omniscience is not established;

children.text: katipayajño hi tathā sati syāt |
children.translated_text: for He would then be only a knower of some things.'
By this, the following statement in the <s>Kaṇikā</s> is [also refuted]:

children.text: na vā tanmātrajñānam apīśvarasya
bālādivad ity āha | bālonmattādīnāṃ
children.translated_text: like a child and the like,' he says. '[For] of children, madmen, and the like,

children.text: svakāryaprayojanāparijñāne 'pi nirabhiprāyāṇāṃ tatra tatra pravṛttidarśanāt | na ca kulālādayo nidarśanaṃ na bālādaya ity atra niyamahetur astī
children.translated_text: even without comprehension of the purpose of their own actions, purposeless activity is observed here and there. And there is no reason for the restriction that potters and the like are the example but not children and the like' —

children.text: ti tan nirastam ||
children.translated_text: that is refuted.
'Or, God too would not know even just those —

children.text: īśvarasya hi katipayātīndriyopakaraṇādijñāne tatkāraṇasya sarvatra samānatvād aśeṣopakaraṇādijñatāyā durvāratvāt | kāraṇam ca tajjñāne sattām antareṇa nānyat, dharmādharmādīnāṃ laukikapratyāsattihetūnāṃ tatrāsambhavāt | kāraṇābhede ca kāryābhedaḥ | anyathā katipayātīndriyajñānam api na syāt | yathā hi
kulālādis
children.translated_text: a potter and the like —

children.text: tulyadarśanasāmagrīkeṣu nākiñcij
children.translated_text: among those who possess an equal cognitive faculty,

children.text: jñaḥ
children.translated_text: [is] not one who knows nothing;

children.text: tathātīndriyopakaraṇādiṣv apīśvaraḥ, sāmarthyasyāviśeṣāt | na ca bālonmattādinidarśanena katipayopakaraṇajñatāniṣedho yuktaḥ, bījadṛṣṭāntena buddhimanmātrasyāpi niṣedhābhidhānaprasaṅgāt | tasmād yathopādānādyabhijñasyāpi sambhavād bījādibhir na vyabhicārābhidhānam, tathā bālonmattādibhir apīti kulālādīnām eva dṛṣṭāntatā yuktimatī, upādānādyabhijñabuddhivanmātrakāryatvayoḥ sādhyasādhanayos tatra prasiddhatvāt | tathā jñānavad īśvarasya cikīrṣāprayatnau nityāv ity atrāpi |
children.translated_text: likewise, God [is not ignorant] even with respect to supersensible instruments and the like, because the capacity [for knowledge] is not different. And the negation of knowledge of some instruments [for God] by the example of children and madmen is not justified, because of the example of the seed proving [the existence of] an intelligent [cause].

For if God knows even some supersensible instruments and the like, then since the cause [of that knowledge] is the same everywhere, knowledge of all instruments and the like without remainder cannot be prevented. And the cause of that knowledge, apart from [His] existence,

children.text: yad abhihitam: nityau cet kim īśvarasya jñānena cikīrṣāprayatnopayoginā, tayor nityatvāt, svotpādopayogānapekṣaṇādityādi | tad apy asāram | ajñātakartṛtvānupaptteḥ | jñānaṃ hi yatra cikīrṣāpratyatnāv anityau tatra tāv upasthāpayadupakaraṇādikam upadarśayati | yatra tu tau nityau tatropakaraṇādikam upadarśayad api saphalam | tasmāt saty api cikīrṣāpratyatnayor nityatve saphalam īśvarajñānaṃ sākṣātkāryopattāv anupayogy api | ata eva ca so 'yam īdṛśo viśeṣo vicārāsahaḥ kathaṃ pakṣadharmatābalād api sādhyadharmiṇy upasaṃhriyata ityādir api pralāpa eva | īśvarajñānasyāvyāhatau sarvajñatāviśeṣasya durvāratvāt |
children.translated_text: The objection that was raised — 'If [God's knowledge and will] are eternal, what use is God's knowledge that serves desire-to-act and effort, since those being eternal, they do not depend on their own production for [any] purpose?' and so on — that too is without substance. [For] the agent whose [nature is] unknown —

children.text: yad abhihitam:
prekṣāvatāṃ pravṛttiḥ prayojanavattayā vyāptā | na ceśvarasya prekṣāvato jagannirmāṇe prayojanam utpaśyāmaḥ, prāptanikhilaprāpaṇīyasya prāptavyābhāvāt |
children.translated_text: 'The activity of purposive agents (<s>prekṣāvat</s>) is pervaded by having a purpose. And we do not perceive any purpose for God, a purposive agent, in the creation of the world — because for one who has already attained everything attainable, there is nothing left to attain' —

children.text: tad api sāvadyam, tadabhiprāyasya durbodhatvāt, prayojanābhāvāsiddheḥ, vyāpakānupalabdheḥ, sandigdhatvāt | vicitrā hi puruṣamātrasya cetovṛttiḥ prāg eva viśvasya kartuḥ | prāptanikhilaprāpaṇīyasyāpi karuṇayāpi parārtha
children.translated_text: that too is faulty, because His intention is difficult to comprehend, because the absence of purpose is not established, because of the non-apprehension of the pervader, and because of doubt. For the mental activity of a [divine] person is variegated even before

children.text: pravṛtteḥ
children.translated_text: activity,

children.text: sambhāvyamānatvāt | na cāsya narakādinirmāṇapravṛttiḥ kāruṇikatām upahanti, pratyuta pituḥ putragaṇḍapāṭanavṛttir ivālpaduḥkhadānena prabhūtadāruṇaduḥkhāpanayanāt karuṇātiśayam eva gamayati | prekṣāvatām ivāsyāpi niyatasthirapravṛttisiddheḥ prayojanānumitir eva nyāyaprāptā ||
children.translated_text: because it is conceivable. And His activity in creating hells and the like does not impugn His compassionate nature — rather, just as a father's act of slapping his son's cheek [does not negate his compassion], it is [an act of compassion,] preventing greater and more terrible suffering by administering a small amount of pain.
The objection that was raised:

children.text: yac cedam udīritam: yadi hi sarvakāryāṇām ekaḥ kartā syāt tato 'jñasya tattvānupapatteḥ sarvajñatā syāt |
adya
children.translated_text: But now,

children.text: punar ekaikaṃ kāryam ekaikena kartrā
children.translated_text: each individual effect is produced by each individual maker;

children.text: janyata iti yo yaj janayati sa tatkāraṇamātrajña eva na tu sarvajña iti |
children.translated_text: therefore, whoever produces whatever is a knower of only the causes of that — and not omniscient.'
And the following objection that was raised: 'If there were one maker of all effects, then, since the nature [of such a maker] cannot be that of an ignorant one, [He] would be omniscient.

children.text: atrocyate |
kāryaliṅgāviśeṣād ekaḥ kartā
children.translated_text: Due to the non-differentiation of the logical mark of being an effect, [there is] one maker —

children.text: sad iti jñānāviśeṣāt sattaikatvavat | kutaścil liṅgād anumitasya vastuno nānātvasya liṅgāntarānumeyatvāt, nānātvam upapādayituṃ pramāṇāntaraṃ vaktavyam | yathātmanānātvam avasthāpayadbhiḥ
children.translated_text: exists — and due to the non-differentiation of the knowledge [required], just as [we infer] the unity of existence [from uniform existents]. Since the plurality of an entity inferred through one logical mark is to be inferred through another logical mark, one who would establish plurality must state a different means of valid cognition.

children.text: sukhādibhir nānātvavyavasthāpanam
children.translated_text: The establishment of plurality through [differences in] pleasure and the like —

children.text: ucyate | na ceha kartur anekatvādhigame pramāṇāntaram asti |
children.translated_text: is stated [by the opponent]. But here there is no other means of valid cognition for ascertaining the multiplicity of the maker.

children.text: ekatve tu na pramāṇātaram anveṣṭavyam, ekasya kartur abhāve
children.translated_text: For unity, no other means of valid cognition need be sought, since in the absence of a single maker,

children.text: bahūnāṃ vyāhatamanasāṃ
children.translated_text: many [makers] with conflicting intentions,

children.text: svātantryeṇa
children.translated_text: independently,

children.text: parasparavirodhena mithaḥ svānukūlābhiprāyānavabodhena yugapatkāryānutpattiḥ, utpannasya vā vilopādiprasaṅgaḥ syād
children.translated_text: due to mutual opposition, due to the impossibility of each comprehending the other's favorable intention, there would be the non-production of simultaneous effects, or the absurd consequence of the destruction and the like of what has been produced.

children.text: iti | ekatve tu siddhe sarvajñatāsiddhir avirodhinī | na ceśvarasya sakalakṣetrajñasamavāyidharmādharmajñānakāraṇābhāvena tadajñānam, tatsamavetānāṃ jñānacikīrṣāpratyatnānāṃ nityatvāt | na ca buddhitannityatvayoḥ kaścit virodhaḥ | na ca buddher anityatāyās tatra tatropalabdher īśvarabuddher api tathātvaṃ yuktam, rūpādīnām apy anityānāṃ tatra tatropalabdhes toyādiparamāṇusamavetānām api rūpādīnām anityatvaprasaṅgāt | parapuruṣasamavetadharmādharmādhiṣṭhānam apy asya yuktam eva, saṃyuktasaṃyogisamavāyasya sambandhasya sadbhāvāt | saṃyuktāḥ khalv īśvareṇa paramāṇavaḥ, taiś ca kṣetrajñāḥ, tatsamavetau ca dharmādharmāv iti ||
children.translated_text: But once unity is established, the establishment of omniscience follows without contradiction. And God's ignorance [of dharma and adharma] is not [established] by the absence of a cause of knowledge — namely, the <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> co-inherent in all individual souls (<s>kṣetrajña</s>) — because for [entities] co-inherent with those [souls], the cognition —
To that, we reply:

children.text:
tad evaṃ kaṇikāyāṃ vācaspater īśvaradūṣaṇaṃ yathāsāram utthāpya vyudastam asmābhiḥ |
	  aparaṃ ca busaprāyam anabhyupagamaprasiddhasiddhāntagrastam iha granthavistarabhayān na likhitam | tad evam abhimatasyaiva sarvajñatālakṣaṇasya viśeṣasya siddher naiṣa viśeṣaviruddho hetuḥ | nāpi karmabhiḥ siddhasādhanam iti sthitam ||
children.translated_text: Thus, the refutation of God (<s>Īśvara</s>) by <s>Vācaspati</s> in the <s>Kaṇikā</s> has been raised [by us] point by point and countered according to its substance. And other [objections], being largely chaff — vitiated by non-acceptance and by reliance on well-known established doctrines — here

children.text:
na cānaikāntikaḥ | sa hi bhavann
	  asādhāraṇo vā syāt, yathā nityā pṛthvī gandhavattvād iti,
	  anupasaṃhāryo vā, yathā sarvaṃ nityaṃ prameyatvād iti, sādhāraṇo vā
	  yathā nityaḥ śabdaḥ, asparśavattvād iti |
children.translated_text: Nor is [the reason] inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>). For if it were, it would be either: the uncommon (<s>asādhāraṇa</s>) [type], as in 'Earth is eternal because it has smell'; or the uninstantiated (<s>anupasaṃhārya</s>) [type], as in 'Everything is eternal because it is an object of knowledge';

children.text: tatra na tāvad ādimau pakṣau, sapakṣasadbhāvadarśanena pratikṣiptatvāt | nāpy antimaḥ, adhigatakartṛnivṛtter vyomāder vipakṣād vyāvṛtter upalabdheḥ |
children.translated_text: Of these, the first two alternatives do not [apply], because they are refuted by the observation of the positive example (<s>sapakṣa</s>). Nor does the last [apply], because the exclusion from the negative example (<s>vipakṣa</s>) — such as space and the like, whose exclusion of [having] a known maker is ascertained — is observed.

Moreover, what exactly is this 'conviction of having been made'? Is it (1) the determination that the activity of another was required, or (2) the certainty of having been made by a person, i.e., the conviction of being human-made?
