children.text: yac ca pṛṣṭaṃ keyaṃ kṛtabuddhir ityādi | tatra kāmaṃ sādhyabuddhir eveti brūmaḥ | yac cātroktaṃ sādhyabuddhir api yadi gṛhītavyāptikasya sā bhavaty eva | athāgṛhītavyāptikasya kim anyatrāpi sā bhavatī dṛṣṭeti ||
children.translated_text: As for the question 'What is this conviction of being made?' and so forth: here we readily say it is indeed a cognition of the thesis (<s>sādhyabuddhi</s>). As for the statement: 'If a cognition of the thesis, then for one who has grasped the pervasion, it arises naturally; and for one who has not grasped the pervasion, has it been observed arising elsewhere too?' —

Thus, even when pots, cloths, mountains, and the like share properties such as effecthood and substantiality, conventional perception operates by taking into account the subordinate class-distinctions (<s>avāntarajāti</s>) of pot-hood, cloth-hood, mountain-hood, and the like to grasp the pervasion — to demonstrate this, with reference to the understanding of a person who is experienced in practical affairs, it was said: 'From the sight of which the conviction of being made arises even in one who has not observed the making.' This was not said with reference to a person whose understanding is dependent on treatises. For thus: when an experienced, practically competent person, who has ascertained the temple-kind as preceded by a person, enters a forest from a city and sees both a mountain and a temple — even though he has not observed the manufacture of either — the conviction of being made arises with respect to the temple, not the mountain. Now, although these two — the temple and the mountain — are of the same kind through effecthood and the like, the presence and absence of the conviction of being made in them cannot be accounted for without establishing the subordinate class-distinction characterized by temple-hood and mountain-hood. And when the class-distinction is established, since pervasion is grasped for the temple-kind, and not for the mountain-kind or the palace-kind, there is no inference of an intelligent being from those [kinds]. And when the pervasion of the palace-kind is also separately grasped, then inference of an intelligent being from that kind too is possible. But the pervasion of the earth-bearing-mountain-kind and the like is not grasped even in a dream, because toy-mountains and the like, despite having merely a shared name,

children.text: atrocyate | gṛhītavyāptikasyānumānaṃ bhavati, agṛhītavyāptikasya na bhavatīty atrāsmākaṃ na kācid vipratipattiḥ | kevalaṃ gṛ
hītavyāptiko 'smin viṣaye na sambhavatīti brūmaḥ |
children.translated_text: is not possible in this subject matter [i.e., regarding mountains and the earth],

children.text: uktakrameṇa vyatirekāsiddher
children.translated_text: because the negative concomitance of effecthood is unestablished through the method described,

children.text: vyāvahārikapratyakṣeṇa kāryatvasya vyāptatvāniścayāt | tasmād avāntarajātibhedaprasiddhyarthaṃ vyāvahārikapuruṣāpekṣayaivāsyā buddher bhāvābhāvāv uktau | jātibhede ca prayojanaṃ pūrvam eva pratipāditam |
children.translated_text: [and] because there is no certainty that effecthood is pervaded [by intelligent creation] through conventional perception. Therefore, the presence and absence of this conviction [of being made] were stated with reference to a practically experienced person, precisely for the purpose of establishing the subordinate class-distinction. And the purpose of the class-distinction has already been demonstrated.

To this we reply: For one who has grasped the pervasion, inference arises; for one who has not grasped it, it does not — in this we have no disagreement. We merely say that one who has grasped the pervasion

children.text: yad apy atra
nipuṇamanyena
children.translated_text: by <s>Vācaspati</s>,

children.text: vācaspattinā kathi
children.translated_text: who considers himself astute —

children.text: taṃ tat kiṃ kāryajātīyaṃ prāsādādi buddhimaddhetukaṃ na dṛṣṭaṃ yenotpattimattanubhuvanādi tathā na syāt, na khalu tajjātīyakatve kascidviśeṣa iti | tad asaṅgatam | tathā hi bhavatu prāsādaparvatādīnāṃ kāryatvādinā sajātī
children.translated_text: 'What kind of effect — palaces and the like — has not been seen as caused by an intelligent being, such that bodies, worlds, and the like, being of that kind, should not be so? For there is no distinguishing factor in being of that kind' — that is unfounded. For thus: let palaces, mountains, and the like be of the same kind through effecthood and the like. But that

children.text: yatvam | tat tu na
children.translated_text: cannot

children.text: vyāvahārikapratyakṣeṇa buddhimadvyāptaṃ pratyetuṃ śakyam, vyāptigrahaṇasamaye dṛṣṭānte buddhimadabhāva
children.translated_text: be apprehended by conventional perception as pervaded by an intelligent being, because at the time of grasping the pervasion, the negative concomitance of mere effecthood in the example — [which would require observing] the absence of an intelligent being —

children.text: prayuktasya kāryamātravyatirekasya darśayitum aśakyatvāt |
children.translated_text: cannot be demonstrated.
As for what was said here

children.text: tad ayaṃ saṃkṣepārthaḥ | kāryatvamātrasyāvyatirekād avyāptasyāgamakatvam | avāntaraṃ tu ghaṭaprāsādādisādhāraṇaṃ kāryatvamātram asmābhir api na svīkṛtam eva | yathā tu ghaṭatvapaṭatvādiprātisvikānekajātipuraskāreṇa prasiddhānumānavyavasthā sā cānavadyam ava
sthāpiteti |
children.translated_text: Thus it is established.

This is the summary meaning: mere 'being an effect' (<s>kāryatva</s>), lacking counter-concomitance, is not a valid indicator because it is too narrow. However, a subordinate [version of] mere 'being an effect' that is common to pots, palaces, and the like has not been accepted by us either. But just as the well-established arrangement of inference is conducted with multiple specific class-properties (<s>jāti</s>) such as pot-ness, cloth-ness, and the like — that arrangement has been established without fault.

children.text: saṃprati sādhyātmā vicāryate | nanu vādinā sādhane samupanyaste taddūṣaṇopanyāsam apāsya sādhyasvarūpavikalpanaṃ nāma naiyāyikamate niranuyojyānuyogaḥ, saugatamate tv adoṣodbhāvanaṃ nigrahasthānam iti cet | tad etaj jālmajalpitam | tathā hi sādhyasvarūpe 'pariniṣṭhite tadanusāriṇī pakṣasapakṣavipakṣavyavasthā kutaḥ | tadasiddhau cāsiddhatādayo doṣāḥ pakṣadharmatādayaś ca guṇā na vyavasthitā ity uktam | nedānīṃ hetor doṣaguṇakatheti mūkena prativādinā sthātavyam | tasmād dhetudoṣopanyāsaiveyaṃ sādhyaniruktir ity ayam eva vādī svamate niranuyojyānuyogadūṣaṇena nigrahasthānena nigṛhyata iti kim atra nirbandhena |
children.translated_text: Now the nature of the provable (<s>sādhya</s>) is examined. The objection that 'when the proponent has presented his proof, to set aside the refutation of that [proof] and instead analyze the nature of the provable is, in the <s>Naiyāyika</s> view, a fallacious questioning of the unquestionable; but in the Buddhist view, the failure to produce a fault [in the proof] is a point of defeat (<s>nigrahasthāna</s>)' — that is mere sophistry. For if the nature of the provable is not well-determined, whence comes the arrangement of the thesis (<s>pakṣa</s>), the positive example (<s>sapakṣa</s>), and the negative example (<s>vipakṣa</s>) that follows upon it? And if that is not established, then faults such as unestablished-ness (<s>asiddhatā</s>) and the like, and qualities such as the property's belonging to the subject (<s>pakṣadharmatā</s>) and the like, are not determined — so the respondent should remain silent, [saying] 'Now is not the time for discussing the faults and merits of the reason.' Therefore, this determination of the provable is itself the presentation of the fault of the reason — thus this proponent himself is defeated by the point of defeat called 'fallacious questioning of the unquestionable' in his own system. What use is further insistence here?

children.text: yad etat kārya

tvaṃ sādhanaṃ kim anena viśvasya buddhimanmātrapūrvakatvaṃ sādhyate | āhosvid ekatvavibhutvasarvajñatvanityatvādiguṇaviśiṣṭabuddhimatpūrvakatvam | prathamapakṣe siddhasādhanam | dvitīye tu vyāpter abhāvād anaikāntikatā |
children.translated_text: is the means of proof — does it prove that the universe is preceded by a mere intelligent being? Or that it is preceded by an intelligent being endowed with specific qualities such as unity, omnipresence, omniscience, eternality, and the like? In the first case, [the fault is] proving what is already established (<s>siddhasādhana</s>). In the second, [there is] inconclusiveness (<s>anaikāntikatā</s>) due to the absence of invariable concomitance.
This property of being an effect (<s>kāryatva</s>) —

children.text: nanu sāmānyena vyāptau pratītāyām api pakṣadharmatābalād viśeṣasiddhiḥ | yathāgneḥ parvatāyogavyavacchedādisiddhiḥ | anyathā sarvānumānocchedaḥ | anumānadve
ṣī hy evaṃ jalpati:
children.translated_text: For one who hates inference speaks thus:

One objects: 'Even when the invariable concomitance is cognized with respect to the general [property], the specific [determination] is established by the force of the property belonging to the subject. Just as the specific [properties] of fire — such as being on the mountain and being distinct from [other instances of fire] — are established. Otherwise, all inference would be destroyed.'

children.text: anumānabhaṅgapaṅke 'smin nimagnā vādidantinaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Sunk in the mud of the demolition of inference, the elephant-debaters [flounder]:

children.text: viśeṣe 'nugamābhāvaḥ sāmānye siddhasādhyatā ||
children.translated_text: in the specific, there is no positive concomitance; in the general, [there is the fault of] proving what is already established.'

children.text: atrocyate |
sidhyaty eva pakṣadharmatābalato viśeṣaḥ | na tu sarvaḥ | yena hi vinā
children.translated_text: A specific [determination] is indeed established by the force of the property belonging to the subject — but not every [specific determination]. Let that specific determination be established without which

children.text: pakṣasthaṃ sādhanaṃ
children.translated_text: the means of proof present in the subject

children.text: nopapadyate sa viśeṣaḥ sidhyatu | yathā vahner eva parvatavartitvādiviśeṣo
children.translated_text: would be untenable. Just as the specific [property] of fire being located on the mountain and the like [is established] —

children.text: na pañcavarṇaśikhākalāpakamanīyaḥ | na ca girīṇāṃ tarūṇāṃ kāryatvaṃ kartur ekatvavibhutvasarvajñatvādikam antareṇa nopapadyate, taditareṣv api darśanāt | tasmāt
children.translated_text: not [the specific property of] being beautiful with a plume of five-colored crests. And the property of being an effect of mountains and trees does not become untenable without the maker's unity, omnipresence, omniscience, and the like.
To that we reply:

children.text: pakṣāyogavyavaccheda
bhedamātre na
children.translated_text: regarding mere difference, there is no

children.text: dūṣaṇam |
children.translated_text: fault.
The distinction of exclusion from the subject —

children.text: iṣṭasiddhyanvayābhāvād atirikte tu dūṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: Because there is no positive concomitance [required] for the establishment of the desired [conclusion] with respect to mere [difference]; but with respect to what is additional, there is a fault.

children.text: yady evaṃ
svasvarūpopā
children.translated_text: the maker who knows his own nature,

children.text: dānopakaraṇasaṃpradānaprayojanābhijña eva kartā
children.translated_text: the material cause, the accessory instrument, the recipient, and the purpose —

children.text: sādhyate | svarūpam iha ca dvyaṇukaṃ kāryam | upādānam
children.translated_text: alone is proved. And the 'own nature' here is the dyad (<s>dvyaṇuka</s>) as effect; the material cause

children.text: iha paramāṇujātica
children.translated_text: here is the four classes of atoms (<s>paramāṇu</s>);

children.text: tuṣṭayam | upakaraṇaṃ samastakṣetrajñasamavāyidharmādharmau | sampradanaṃ kṣetrajñāḥ, yānayaṃ bhagavān svakarma
children.translated_text: the accessory instruments are the <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> co-inherent in all individual souls (<s>kṣetrajña</s>); the recipients are the individual souls, whom the Lord approaches through their own

children.text: bhir abhipraiti |
children.translated_text: <s>karmas</s>.

children.text: prayojanaṃ sukhaduḥkhopabhogaḥ kṣetrajñānām |
children.translated_text: The purpose is the experience of pleasure and pain by the individual souls.

children.text: evaṃbhūte
children.translated_text: For a provable of such a nature —

children.text: buddhimati sādhye kutaḥ siddhasādhanam | na cāvyāptiḥ |
children.translated_text: an intelligent being — whence the [fault of] proving what is already established? Nor is there non-pervasion,

children.text: kulāladṛṣṭānte upādānā
children.translated_text: because in the potter example, the knowledge of the material cause

children.text: dyabhijñatvasya sambhavāt |
children.translated_text: and the like is possible.
If so, then

children.text: tathā ca vācaspatiḥ pramāṇyati:
vivā
children.translated_text: 'The objects under dispute —

children.text: dādhyāsitās tanugirisāgarādayaḥ upādānādyabhijñakartṛkāḥ | kāryatvāt | yad yat kāryaṃ tat tad upādānādyabhijñakartṛkam | yathā prāsādādi | tathā ca vivādādhyāsitās tanvādayaḥ | tasmāt tatheti
children.translated_text: bodies, mountains, oceans, and the like — have a maker who knows the material cause and the like, because they are effects. Whatever is an effect has a maker who knows the material cause and the like.
And <s>Vācaspati</s> validates [this]:

children.text: evam ataḥ sādhanād upādānādyabhijñakartṛmātraṃ prasādhya tasya sarvajñatvasādhanāya vācaspatir eva punar apīdam āha:
bhavatu tā
children.translated_text: 'Let there be,

children.text: vad upādānādyabhijñakartṛmātrasiddhiḥ | pāriśeṣyāt tu vyatirekidvitīyanāmno 'numānād viśeṣasiddhiḥ | tathā hi: tanubhuvanādyupādānādyabhijñaḥ kartā nānityāsarvaviṣayabuddhimān | tatkartus tadupādānādyanabhijñatvaprasaṅgāt | na hy evaṃvidhas tadupādānādyabhijño
children.translated_text: for the present, the establishment of merely a maker who knows the material cause and the like. But by the method of elimination (<s>pāriśeṣya</s>), through the inference called "the second [type], involving positive and negative concomitance" (<s>vyatirekin</s>), the specific [determination] is established. Namely: bodies and realms

children.text: yathāsmadādiḥ | tadupādānādyabhijñaś
children.translated_text: [have a maker] like us and the like. And this [maker] knows the material cause and the like of those.

children.text: cāyam | ta
children.translated_text: Therefore,

children.text: smāt tatheti |
children.translated_text: so [he is omniscient].'
Thus, having established through this proof merely a maker who knows the material cause and the like, <s>Vācaspati</s> again states the following for proving his omniscience:

children.text: no khalu paramāṇubhedān kṣetrajñasamavāyinaś ca karmāśayabhedān aparimeyān anyaḥ śakto jñātum ṛte tādṛgīśvarād
iti |
children.translated_text: Thus.

'For no one other than such a Lord is capable of knowing the immeasurable distinctions of atoms and the distinctions of the repositories of <s>karma</s> (<s>karmāśaya</s>) co-inherent in the individual souls.'

children.text: atrocyate | yāvanti dvyaṇukāni bhinnadeśakālasvabhāvāni kāryāṇi santi teṣu sarveṣv eva kim eka eva buddhimān vyāpriyate | aneko vā | yad vā svasvaviṣayamātropādānādivedinaḥ parasparavyāpārānabhijñā bhinnadeśakāla
svabhāvāḥ pratidvyaṇukam anya eva buddhimanto vyāpriyante iti trayaḥ pakṣāḥ |
children.translated_text: or do different intelligent beings, with different natures, operate upon each dyad? — these are the three alternatives.
To that we reply: For all the dyads that are effects, differing in spatial, temporal, and essential nature — does a single intelligent being operate upon all of them,

children.text: na tāvat
prathamaḥ pakṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: the first alternative [is not tenable].

children.text: de
children.translated_text: Because

children.text: śakālasvabhāvabhinnānāṃ sarveṣāṃ dvyaṇukānāṃ kartur ekatvāsiddheḥ | yac caikatvasādhanāya
children.translated_text: the unity of the maker of all dyads, which differ in spatial, temporal, and essential nature, is not established. And the proof that was presented to establish unity —

children.text: kāryaliṅgāviśeṣād ityādy
children.translated_text: 'due to the non-differentiation of the logical mark of being an effect' and the like —

children.text: api sādhanam upanyastaṃ tad asaṅgatam | dhūmaliṅgāviśeṣe 'pi hy agner anekatvavat tatrāpi tacchaṅkāsambhavāt |
children.translated_text: that too is incoherent. For just as fire is multiple despite the non-differentiation of the logical mark of smoke, so too in this case the suspicion [of multiplicity] is possible.

children.text: sad iti liṅgāviśeṣād
children.translated_text: '[Something] exists' — 'due to the non-differentiation of the logical mark [of existence]' —

children.text: iti
children.translated_text: this

children.text: tu dṛṣṭānto 'smān pratyasiddha eva | tasmād yathā mayā nānātvasādhanāya pramāṇaṃ vaktavyaṃ tathā tvayāpy ekatvasādhanāya sādhanam abhidhānīyam |
children.translated_text: example is not established for us. Therefore, just as I must state a means of valid cognition to prove multiplicity, so must you to prove unity.
First,

children.text: atha manyate anekatvasādhanābhāvād ekatvasiddhir iti | yady evam ekatvasādhanābhāvad anekatvam eva kiṃ nāvagacchasi |
children.translated_text: If one thinks 'In the absence of proof of multiplicity, unity is established' — if so, then in the absence of proof of unity, why do you not understand [that there is] multiplicity?

children.text: yad apy uktam:
ekatve tu na pramāṇāntaram anveṣṭavyam ekasya kartur abhāve bahūnāṃ vyāhatamanasām ityādi
children.translated_text: 'For unity, no other means of valid cognition need be sought, since in the absence of a single maker, many [makers] with conflicting intentions' and so on —

children.text: tad api cintyatām | bahubhiḥ karaṇe yugapat kāryānutpattir iti kiṃ bhinnadeśakālānāṃ kāryāṇām anutpattir vivakṣitā | ekasyaiva vā mahāvayavinaḥ kṣitighaṭādirūpasya | tatra ekasminn api kārye bahubhiḥ karaṇe utpattivirodhinaṃ na paśyāmaḥ | bahūnāṃ parasparaṃ vaimatyaniyamābhāvāt | parasparāvyāghātapuruṣatvayor dvividhasyāpi virodhasyāsambhavāt | puruṣatvaṃ hi apuruṣatvena viruddham | na tu parasparāvyāghātena |
children.translated_text: that too should be considered. [The claim that] 'with many [makers], simultaneous effects would not be produced' — does this mean the non-production of effects in different spaces and times? Or one
And the following was stated:

children.text: ye tv anantadeśakālasvabhāvabhedabhinnāsteṣu sutarām evānekavyāpāraniṣedho 'sambhavīti dvitīyo 'pi pakṣo vyudastaḥ | na ca kartur ekatvena dṛṣṭā vyāptisiddhiḥ |

anekenāpi svatantreṇa svasvaprayojanārthinā grāmapraviṣṭahariṇādimāraṇaikakāryadarśanāt | tasyāpi pakṣīkaraṇe ekakartṛpūrvakābhimatasyāpi pakṣīkaraṇe ātmakartṛpūrvakatvam astu | tad evaṃ na sarvadvyaṇukānāṃ kartur ekatvasiddhiḥ |
children.translated_text: is there [a problem] even with many independent [agents], each seeking their own purpose, because the production of a single effect — like the killing of a deer that has entered a village — is observed [to be accomplished by many]. And if even that [case] is subsumed under [the argument for] a single maker,

children.text: tathā coktam
children.translated_text: and as has been said:

[effect in one place and time]? Those that differ in innumerable distinctions of space, time, and essential nature — for those, the negation of multiple [agents'] operation is all the more impossible — thus the second alternative too is rejected. Nor

children.text: ekakartur na siddhau tu sarvajñatvaṃ kim āśrayam |
children.translated_text: 'If the unity of the maker is not established, on what does omniscience rest?'

children.text: ata eva dvitīyo 'pi pakṣaḥ kṣīṇaḥ | saveṣu dvyaṇukeṣv ekasyāpi kartur apravṛttau bahūnāṃ sutarām apravṛtteḥ |
children.translated_text: For this very reason, the second alternative too is exhausted — because if even one maker does not operate upon all dyads, then all the more [so] many [makers would not].

children.text: tṛ
tīyas tu pakṣo yadi bhavet tadā svasvavyāpāraviṣayamātropādānādyabhijñatve 'pi naikaḥ kaścit sarvajñaḥ sidhyati | na ca
children.translated_text: third alternative, however, if it were [accepted], then even though [each maker] knows the material cause and the like of only the object of his own operation, no single [being] is established as omniscient. Nor

children.text: jñānasattāmātreṇa
children.translated_text: is it the case that by the mere existence of knowledge,

children.text: katipayātīndriyadarśanavat sarvārthagrahaṇaṃ yena tadabhedāt prastutaparamāṇuvat sarvasyaivāviśeṣeṇa grahaṇāt sarvajñatā syāt | anumānato hi katipayātīndriyadarśane siddhe 'pīśvarasya tatkāraṇayogitvaṃ niścīyate | na tu jñāna
children.translated_text: like the seeing of a few supersensible things, all objects are grasped — since, by the non-differentiation [of that argument] with the atom in question, all [things] would be grasped without distinction by everyone — [resulting in] omniscience [for all].

children.text: sāttāmātreṇa prakārāntareṇeti niścaya iti kutaḥ sarvajñatā |
children.translated_text: In another way, [based on] mere existence — the certainty [of omniscience] arises from whence? How is omniscience [established]?
The

children.text: nanv atīndriyaṃ paramāṇvādikaṃ jānato na kathaṃ sārvajñyam iti cet | tat kim idānīm asarvadarśitveṣv atīndriyadarśanamātreṇa sarvajñatāpratyayāśā | evam eveti cet | hanta yadi nāma nyāyavihastena tvayā īdṛśo hastasamāracitaḥ sarvajñaḥ paribhāvitas tathāpy anyeṣām apāradūradeśakālavartināṃ dvyaṇukādīnām upādānādiṣu januṣāndhaprakhyasya paramapuruṣārthāvedino vā lokaiḥ prāmāṇikaiś ca nāsya sārvajñyam anumanyate ||
children.translated_text: If one objects: 'How is there not omniscience for one who knows supersensible things such as atoms and the like?' — then, what now? From the mere seeing of supersensible things by those who are not all-seeing —

children.text: asmākan tu nātīndriyadarśimātre pradveṣaḥ | evaṃ ca kartur ekatvāsiddhau vyatireky api hetur asamarthaḥ viśveṣām ekasya kartur asiddhau tadupādānādyabhijñabhāvasyāsiddhatvāt | yaś ca yanmātrakāraḥ sa tanmātropādānādyabhijño bhavan na sarvajñaḥ | anekāśrayeṇāpi upādānādyabhijñasāmānyasya caritārthatvāt | tad evam upādānādyabhijñapuruṣamātrasiddhāv api naikatvasarvajñatvādiviśiṣṭapuruṣaviśeṣasiddhiḥ | puruṣamātre ca siddhasādhanam uktam | buddhimanmātrapūrvakatām icchatām upādānādyabhijñabuddhimatpūrvakatve sā
dhye kathaṃ
children.translated_text: [might ask:] How is there

children.text: siddhasādhanam
children.translated_text: [the fault of] proving what is already established?

children.text: iti cet | na tadapekṣayā siddhasādhyatāyā janitatvāt kevalam asiddhoddhāre 'bhimate viśeṣe siddhe 'pi naiyāyikasyāpi nābhimatasiddhir iti brūmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The [fault of] proving what is already established does not arise with reference to that [general property], because it is generated [only] with respect to what is desired as not-yet-established. When the specific [determination], even though established, is desired to be extracted [from the general], even the <s>Naiyāyika</s> does not —

for us, however, there is no hostility toward the mere seeing of supersensible things. And thus, when the unity of the maker is not established, even the <s>vyatirekin</s> (negative) reason is incapable. For all [effects], one

children.text: saugatasya tāvad aniṣṭasiddhir iti cet, na, svābhimatasādhyasādhanenaiva hi parasyāniṣṭam api sādhanīyam | anyathā mātṛśokasmaraṇādināpi tadaniṣṭasiddhiḥ syād iti | asya saṅgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: If one says 'For the Buddhist, at least, there is the establishment of what is undesired (<s>aniṣṭasiddhi</s>)' — no, because one must prove even what is undesired for the opponent through one's own accepted provable and proof. Otherwise, [the objection against] the inference for maternal uncle —

children.text: pareṣṭasiddhir napareṣṭabādhakaṃ prasādhane vedanayatnamātrayoḥ |
children.translated_text: 'In proving what is desired by the opponent and defeating what is desired by the opponent, [one must exert] effort in experience and experience alone.

children.text: ananvayo 'bhīṣṭaviśeṣasādhane vipakṣasandehasahantu sādhanam ||
children.translated_text: There is no positive concomitance in proving the desired specific [determination]; the proof should tolerate doubt in the negative example.'

children.text: sādhyacintādhikāras tṛtīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This concludes the third section: the examination of the provable (<s>sādhya</s>).

children.text: evam anye 'pi hetavo yathāyogam abhyūhya dūṣaṇīyāḥ | tad evaṃ tāvad īśvarasya sadvyavahāro niṣiddhaḥ | asadvyavahārārthan tu tallakṣaṇavilakṣaṇakṣaṇabhaṅgasādhakaṃ sattādisādhanam eva draṣṭavyam iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus, other reasons too should be inferred and refuted as appropriate. So, to this extent, the affirmative usage regarding God (<s>Īśvara</s>) has been negated. For the purpose of establishing the negative usage —

children.text: ity abodhajanakartṛvikalpa vyāpi mohatimirapratirodhi |
children.translated_text: Thus, pervading the conceptual construction of a maker who is not an awakened one, opposing the darkness of delusion,

children.text: ratnakīrtir acanāmalaramya jyotir astu ciramapratirodhi ||
children.translated_text: may the stainless, beautiful, jewel-light of <s>Ratnakīrti</s> shine unobstructed for a long time!

children.text: Apohasiddhiḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Apohasiddhi</s> (Proof of Exclusion)

children.text: || namas tārāyai ||

apohaḥ śabdārtho nirucyate | nanu ko 'yam apoho nāma | kim idam anyasmād apohyate | asmād vānyad apohyate | asmin vānyad apohyata iti vyutpattyā vijātivyāvṛttaṃ bāhyam eva vivakṣitam | buddhyākāro vā | yadi vā apohanam apoha ity anyavyāvṛttimātram iti trayaḥ pakṣāḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Apoha</s> (exclusion) is analyzed as the meaning of words. Now, what is this thing called <s>apoha</s>? Is it that [something] is excluded from another? Or that another is excluded from this? Or that another [is excluded] in this?

children.text: na tāvad ādimau pakṣau apohanāmnā vidher eva vivakṣitatvāt | antimo 'py asaṅgataḥ, pratītibādhitatvāt | tathā hi parvatoddeśe vahnir astīti śābdī pratītir vidhirūpam evollikhantī lakṣyate | nānagnir na bhavatīti nitrṛttimātram āmukhayantī | yac ca pratyakṣabādhitaṃ na tatra sādhanāntarāvakāśa ity atiprasiddham ||
children.translated_text: The first two alternatives are not [correct], because by the term <s>apoha</s> (exclusion), only a positive [entity] is intended to be expressed. The last too is incoherent, because it is contradicted by cognition. For a mountain —
Homage to <s>Tārā</s>!

children.text:
atha yady api nivṛttim ahaṃ
	  pratyemīti na vikalpaḥ tathāpi nivṛttapadārthollekha eva
	  nivṛttyullekhaḥ | na hy anantrbhāvitaviśeṣaṇapratītir viśiṣṭapratītiḥ | tato yathā sāmānyam ahaṃ pratyemīti vikalpābhāve 'pi
	  sādhāraṇākāraparisphuraṇād vikalpabuddhiḥ sāmānyabuddhiḥ pareṣām,
	  tathā nivṛttapratyayākṣiptā nivṛttibuddhir
	  apohapratītivyavahāramātanotīti cet |
children.translated_text: [Objection:] Now, even though there is no conceptual cognition of the form 'I apprehend exclusion,' nevertheless, the delineation of an excluded object is itself the delineation of exclusion. For there is no qualified cognition without the cognition of the qualifier being included within it. Therefore, just as, even in the absence of a conceptual cognition of the form 'I apprehend the universal,' others [i.e., realists] consider the conceptual cognition to be a cognition of the universal because of the shining forth of a common form — similarly, the cognition of exclusion, implied by the cognition of the excluded [object], extends the practice of <s>apoha</s>-apprehension.

children.text:
nanu sādhāraṇākāraparisphuraṇe
	  vidhirūpatayā yadi sāmānyabodhavyavasthā, tat kim āyātam
	  asphuradabhāvākāre cetasi nivṛttipratītivyavasthāyāḥ | tato nivṛttim
	  ahaṃ pratyemīty evam ākārābhāve 'pi nivṛttyākārasphuraṇaṃ yadi syāt ko
	  nāma nivṛttipratītisthitim apalapet | anyathā asati pratibhāse
	  tatpratītivyavahṛtir iti gavākāre 'pi cetasi turagabodha ity astu ||
children.translated_text: [Reply:] But if the established position regarding universal-cognition rests on the shining forth of a common form in the mode of a positive entity (<s>vidhi</s>), then what follows for the established position regarding exclusion-cognition when the form of absence does not shine forth in the mind? Therefore, if — even without the form 'I apprehend exclusion' — the form of exclusion were to shine forth, who indeed would deny the established position of exclusion-cognition? Otherwise, if there were a practice of 'cognition of that' in the absence of the appearance [of that], then even in the mind having the form of a cow, let there be the cognition of a horse!

children.text:
atha viśeṣaṇtayā antarbhūtā
	  nivṛttipratītir ity uktam | tathāpi yady agavāpoḍha itīdṛśākāro
	  vikalpas tadā viśeṣaṇatayā tadanupraveśo bhavatu kiṃ tu gaur iti
	  pratītiḥ | tadā ca sato 'pi nivṛttilakṣaṇasya viśeṣaṇasya
	  tatrānutkalanāt kathaṃ tatpratītivyavasthā |
children.translated_text: [Objection:] But it was said that the cognition of exclusion is included as a qualifier. Even so, if the conceptual cognition has the form 'excluded from non-cow' (<s>agavāpoḍha</s>), then let [exclusion] enter as a qualifier — but [the cognition is simply] 'This is a cow.' And since, even though the qualifier characterized by exclusion exists in that [cognition], it does not manifest there — how can the established position of its cognition [be maintained]?

children.text: athaivaṃ matiḥ:  yad vidhirūpaṃ sphurati tasya parāpoho 'py astīti tatpratītir ucyate | tadāpi sambandhamātram apohasya | vidhir eva sākṣān nirbhāsī | api caivam adhyakṣasyāpy apohaviṣayatvam anivāryam viśeṣato vikalpād ekavyāvṛttollekhino 'khilānyavyāvṛttam īkṣamāṇasya | tasmād vidhyākārāvagrahād adhyakṣavad vikalpasyāpi vidhiviṣayatvam eva nānyāpohaviṣayatvam iti katham apohaḥ śabdārtho ghuṣyate |
children.translated_text: [Objection:] But the view is this: whatever shines forth in the form of a positive entity — of that, the exclusion of others also exists, and its cognition is [thereby] spoken of. Even then, the <s>apoha</s> has only a relational [status]. The positive entity alone directly appears. Moreover, in that case, even perception would unavoidably have <s>apoha</s> as its object — especially since perception, which delineates exclusion from one [thing], sees the exclusion from all other things. Therefore, just as perception, from the apprehension of a positive form, has a positive entity as its object — similarly, even conceptual cognition has a positive entity as its object and not exclusion-from-others (<s>anyāpoha</s>) — so how is <s>apoha</s> proclaimed as the meaning of words?

children.text: atrābhidhīyate | nāsmābhir apohaśabdena vidhir eva kevalo 'bhipretaḥ | nāpy anyavyāvṛttimātram | kin tv anyāpohaviśiṣṭo vidhiḥ śabdānām arthaḥ | tataś ca na pratyekapakṣopanipātidoṣāvakāśaḥ ||

yat tu goḥ pratītau na tadātmāparātmeti sāmarthyād apohaḥ
	  paścān niścīyata iti vidhivādināṃ matam, anyāpohapratītau vā
	  sāmarthyād anyāpoḍho 'vadhāryate iti pratiṣedhavādināṃ matam | tad
	  asundaram | prāthamikasyāpi pratipattikramādarśanāt | na hi vidhiṃ
	  pratipadya kaścid arthāpattitaḥ paścād apoham avagacchati | apohaṃ vā
	  pratipadyānyāpoḍham | tasmād goḥ pratipattir ity anyāpoḍhapratipattir
	  ucyate | yady api cānyāpoḍhaśabdānullekha uktas tathāpi nāpratipattir
	  eva viśeṣaṇabhūtasyāpohasya | agavāpoḍha eva gośabdasya niveśitatvāt |
	  yathā nīlotpale niveśitād indīvaraśabdān nīlotpalapratītau tatkāla eva
	  nīlimasphuraṇam anivāryaṃ tathā gośabdād apy agavāpoḍhe niveśitād
	  gopratītau tulyakālam eva viśeṣaṇtvād ago 'pohasphuraṇam anivāryam |
	  yathā pratyakṣasya prasajyarūpābhāvāgrahaṇam
	  abhāvavikalpotpādanaśaktir eva tathā vidhivikalpānām api
	  tadanurūpānuṣṭhānadānaśaktir evābhāvagrahaṇam abhidhīyate |
	  paryudāsarūpābhāvagrahaṇaṃ tu niyatasvarūpasaṃvedanam ubhayor
	  aviśiṣṭam | anyathā yadi śabdād arthapratipattikāle kalito na
	  parāpohaḥ katham anyaparihāreṇa pravṛttiḥ | tato gāṃ badhāneti codito
	  'śvādīn api badhnīyāt ||
children.translated_text: As for the view of the 'positive entity' camp (<s>vidhivādin</s>) that 'in the cognition of a cow, <s>apoha</s> is subsequently ascertained through implication (<s>sāmarthya</s>), i.e., it is neither this self nor another self,' or the view of the 'negation' camp (<s>pratiṣedhavādin</s>) that 'in the cognition of exclusion of others, what is excluded from others is subsequently determined through implication' — both are unattractive. Because no order of primary cognition [of one before the other] is observed. For no one, having first apprehended the positive entity, subsequently cognizes the <s>apoha</s> through <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption); nor, having apprehended the <s>apoha</s>, [subsequently cognizes] 'what is excluded from others.' Therefore, the cognition of a cow is [ipso facto] called the cognition of 'what is excluded from non-cow.' And although it was said that the word '<s>anyāpoḍha</s>' (excluded from others) is not explicitly delineated [in the cognition], still, the <s>apoha</s> that is the qualifier is not therefore uncognized — because the word 'cow' (<s>go</s>) is conventionally assigned precisely to [the entity as] excluded from non-cow (<s>agavāpoḍha</s>). Just as, from the word '<s>indīvara</s>' (blue lotus), conventionally assigned to a blue lotus, the shining forth of blueness at the time of the cognition of the blue lotus is unavoidable — similarly, from the word 'cow,' conventionally assigned to [what is] excluded from non-cow, the shining forth of the exclusion from non-cow is unavoidable at the time of cow-cognition, being a qualifier. Just as the non-apprehension of absence in the <s>prasajya</s> (verbally qualified negation) form by perception is itself the capacity to produce a conceptual cognition of absence — similarly, for positive conceptual cognitions too, the capacity to produce activity in conformity with that [positive cognition] is itself called the apprehension of absence. But the apprehension of absence in the <s>paryudāsa</s> (nominally bound negation) form — i.e., the awareness of a specific nature — is the same for both [perception and conceptual cognition]. Otherwise, if the exclusion of others is not discerned at the time of apprehending meaning from a word, how would there be activity excluding others? Then, one commanded 'tie up the cow' would tie up horses and the like as well!

children.text: yad apy avocad Vācaspatiḥ jātimatyo vyaktayo vikalpānāṃ śabdānāṃ ca gocaraḥ | tāsāṃ ca tadvatīnāṃ rūpam atajjātīyaparāvṛttim ity atas tadavagater na gāṃ badhāneti codito 'śvādīn badhnāti | tad apy anenaiva nirastam | yato jāter adhikāyāḥ prakṣepe 'pi vyaktīnāṃ rūpam atajjātīyaparāvṛttam eva cet, tadā tenaiva rūpeṇa śabdavikalpayor viṣayībhavantīnāṃ katham atadvyāvṛttiparihāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: As for what <s>Vācaspati</s> said — that individuals possessing universals are the objects of conceptual cognitions and words, and their form is exclusion from what is not of that class (<s>atajjātīyaparāvṛtti</s>); therefore, because of that understanding, one commanded 'tie up the cow' does not tie up horses and the like — that too is refuted by this very [argument]. For even if an additional universal is introduced, if the form of individuals is simply exclusion from what is not of that class, then for [individuals] that become the objects of words and conceptual cognitions through precisely that form, how is the exclusion from non-that avoided?

children.text: atha na vijātīyavyāvṛttaṃ vyaktirūpaṃ tathāpratītaṃ vā tadā jātiprasāda eṣa iti katham arthato 'pi tadavagatir ity uktaprāyam |
children.translated_text: [Objection:] But if the form of individuals is not excluded from what is of a different class, or if [it is] not so cognized — then this is a 'gift of the universal,' so how is there even indirectly a cognition of that [exclusion]? — This has already been essentially stated.

children.text: atha jātibalād evānyato 'vyāvṛttam | bhavatu jātibalāt svahetuparamparābalād vānyavyāvṛttam | ubhayathāpi vyāvṛttapratipattau vyāvṛttipratipattir asty eva |
children.translated_text: [Objection:] But [the individual] is excluded from others precisely by the force of the universal. [Reply:] Let it be excluded from others by the force of the universal or by the force of the chain of its own causes — in either case, in the cognition of what is excluded, the cognition of exclusion is certainly present.

children.text: na cāgavāpoḍhe gośabdasaṅketavidhāv anyonyāśrayadoṣaḥ | sāmānye tadvati vā saṃkete 'pi taddoṣāv akāśāt | na hi sāmānyaṃ nāma sāmānyamātram abhipretam, turage 'pi gośabdasaṃketaprasaṅgāt | kiṃ tu gotvam | tāvatā ca sa eva doṣaḥ | gavādiparijñāne gotvasāmānyāparijñānāt | gotvasāmānyāparijñāne gośabdavācyāparijñānāt |
children.translated_text: Nor is there the fault of mutual dependence (<s>anyonyāśraya</s>) in the conventional assignment of the word 'cow' to [the entity as] excluded from non-cow. Because the same fault would apply even if the convention were assigned to the universal, or to [something] possessing it. For the 'universal' cannot mean merely 'what is common' — because then there would be the consequence that the convention of the word 'cow' would apply to a horse as well. Rather, [it means] 'cowness' (<s>gotva</s>). And with just that much, the same fault [arises]: because without knowing cowness-as-universal, one cannot know what is expressible by the word 'cow'; and without knowing what is expressible by the word 'cow,' [one cannot know cowness-as-universal].

children.text: tasmād ekapiṇḍadarśanapūrvako yaḥ sarvavyaktisādhāraṇa iva bahiradhyasto vikalpabuddhyākāraḥ tatrāyaṃ gaur iti saṃketakaraṇe netaretarāśrayadoṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: Therefore, when — preceded by the observation of a single specimen — one assigns the convention 'This is a cow' to the form of a conceptual cognition that appears as if common to all individuals, being externally projected (<s>bahiradhyasta</s>), there is no fault of mutual dependence.

children.text: abhimate ca gośabdapravṛttāv agośabdena śeṣasyāpy abhidhānam ucitam | na cānyāpoḍhānyāpohayor virodho viśeṣyaviśeṣaṇabhāvakṣatir vā, parasparavyavacchedābhāvāt | sāmānādhikaraṇyasadbhāvāt | bhūtalaghaṭābhāvavat | svābhāvena hi virodho na parābhāvenety ābālaprasiddham | eṣa panthāḥ śrudhnam upatiṣṭhata ity atrāpy apoho gamyata eva | aprakṛtapathāntarāpekṣayā eṣa eva śrudhnapratyanīkāniṣṭasthānāpekṣayā śrudhnam eva | araṇyamārgavad vicchedābhāvād upatiṣṭhata eva | sārthadūtādivyavacchedena panthā eveti pratipadaṃ vyavacchedasya sulabhatvāt | tasmād apohadharmaṇo vidhirūpasya śabdād avagatiḥ puṇḍarīkaśabdād iva śvetim aviśiṣṭasya padmasya ||
children.translated_text: And when the application of the word 'cow' is accepted [as applying to what is excluded from non-cow], the designation of the remainder by the word 'non-cow' is also appropriate. Nor is there a contradiction or a breakdown of the qualifier-qualified relation between 'excluded from others' and 'exclusion of others' — because of the absence of mutual exclusion [between them], and because of the existence of co-referentiality (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>), like the absence of a pot on the ground. For contradiction is through one's own nature, not through the absence of another — this is well-known even to a child. Even in [the sentence] 'This is the path; proceed to the monastery (<s>śrudhna</s>),' <s>apoha</s> is indeed understood: with reference to other paths not under consideration, [this is] this very [path]; with reference to undesired destinations opposed to the monastery, [one should proceed] to the monastery alone; [proceed] with reference to the absence of discontinuity, as on a wilderness road, continuously; and with reference to the exclusion of fellow-travelers, messengers, and the like, [it is] a path [alone]. Because exclusion is easily obtained at every word. Therefore, the cognition from words of the positive entity that possesses the property of exclusion is like the cognition from the word '<s>puṇḍarīka</s>' (white lotus) of an undifferentiated lotus together with whiteness.

children.text: yady evaṃ vidhir eva śabdārtho vaktum ucitaḥ, katham apoho gīyata iti cet | uktamatrāpohaśabdenānyāpohaviśiṣṭo vidhir ucyate | tatra vidhau pratīyamāne viśeṣaṇatayā tulyakālam anyāpohapratītir iti |
children.translated_text: [Objection:] If so, it would be more appropriate to say that the positive entity alone is the meaning of words — how then is <s>apoha</s> proclaimed? [Reply:] It was stated here: by the word '<s>apoha</s>' is meant the positive entity qualified by the exclusion of others. When the positive entity is cognized, the cognition of exclusion of others [occurs] simultaneously, as a qualifier.

children.text: na caivaṃ pratyakṣasyāpy apohaviṣayatvavyavasthā kartum ucitā | tasya śābdapratyayasyeva vastuviṣayatve vivādābhāvāt | vidhiśabdena ca yathādhyavasāyam atadrūpaparāvṛtto bāhyo 'rtho 'bhimataḥ, yathāpratibhāsaṃ buddhyākāraś ca | tatra bāhyo 'rtho 'dhyavasāyād eva śabdavācyo vyavasthāpyate | na svalakṣaṇaparisphūrtyā | pratyakṣavad deśakālāvasthāniyatapravyaktasvalakṣaṇāsphuraṇāt | yac chāstram
children.translated_text: And thus, it is not appropriate to establish that perception too has <s>apoha</s> as its object. Because there is no dispute about [perception's] having a real thing (<s>vastu</s>) as its object, just like verbal cognition. And by the word 'positive entity' (<s>vidhi</s>), what is intended is: as determined, the external object that is turned away from what is not of that form; and as appearing, the form of cognition. Among these, the external object is established as what is expressible by words only through determination (<s>adhyavasāya</s>) — not through the shining forth of the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular). Because, unlike perception, the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s>, distinctly manifest and restricted to a specific place, time, and state, does not shine forth [in verbal cognition]. As the scripture [says]:

To this we reply: By the word '<s>apoha</s>' we do not intend the positive entity alone, nor mere exclusion of others. Rather, the meaning of words is the positive entity qualified by the exclusion of others (<s>anyāpohaviśiṣṭo vidhiḥ</s>). Therefore, there is no occasion for the fault of falling into either alternative alone.

children.text:
śabdenāvyāpṛtākṣasya buddhāv apratibhāsanāt |
	  arthasya dṛṣṭāv iva
(PVin I 15)

children.translated_text: 'Because of the non-appearance in the cognition of one whose senses are not engaged with the word,

children.text: iti | indriyaśabdasvabhāvopāyabhedād ekasyaivārthasya pratibhāsabheda iti cet | atrāpy uktam:
children.translated_text: — of the object, as if in [direct] seeing.' [Objection:] Because of the difference in the means — namely, the nature of sense-organs versus words — there is a difference in the appearance of one and the same object. [Reply:] To this too it has been said:

children.text:
jāto nāmāśrayo 'nyānyaḥ cetasāṃ tasya vastutaḥ |
	  ekasyaiva kuto rūpaṃ bhinnākārāvabhāsi tat ||
(PV III 235)

na hi spaṣṭāspaṣṭe dve rūpe parasparaviruddhe ekasya vastunaḥ staḥ | yata ekenendriyabuddhau pratibhāsetānyena vikalpe | tathā sati vastuna eva bhedaprāpteḥ | na hi svarūpabhedād aparo vastubhedaḥ | na ca pratibhāsabhedād aparaḥ svarūpabhedaḥ | anyathā trailokyam ekam eva vastu syāt ||
children.translated_text: For the two forms — clear and unclear — being mutually contradictory, do not belong to one and the same entity. That one [form] appears in sense-cognition and the other in conceptual cognition — in that case, the entity itself would be differentiated. For there is no difference in entities apart from the difference in own-nature. And there is no difference in own-nature apart from the difference in appearance. Otherwise, the three worlds would be a single entity.

children.text: dūrāsannadeśavartinoḥ puruṣayor ekatra śākhini spaṣṭāspaṣṭapratibhāsabhede 'pi na śākhibheda iti cet | na brūmaḥ pratibhāsabhedo bhinnavastuniyataḥ, kiṃ tv ekaviṣayatvābhāvaniyata iti | tato yatrārthakriyābhedādisacivaḥ pratibhāsabhedas tatra vastubhedaḥ, ghaṭavat | anyatra punarniyamenaikaviṣayatāṃ pariharatīty ekapratibhāso bhrāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: [Objection:] Even for two persons — one near and one far — though there is a difference of clear and unclear appearance regarding a single tree, there is no difference in the tree. [Reply:] We do not say that the difference in appearance is necessarily restricted to different entities. Rather, [we say] it is restricted to the absence of a single object. Therefore, where the difference in appearance is accompanied by a difference in causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyā</s>) and so forth, there is a difference in entity — as with a pot [vs. cloth]. In other cases, the mere fact that [it] invariably excludes single-object-hood [means that] one of the appearances is erroneous.

children.text: etena yad āha Vācaspatiḥ: na ca śabdapratyakṣayor vastugocaratve pratyayābhedaḥ kāraṇabhedena pārokṣyāpārokṣyabhedopapatter iti, tannopayogi | parokṣapratyayasya vastugocaratvāsamarthatāt | parokṣatāśrayas tu kāraṇabheda indriyagocaragrahaṇaviraheṇaiva kṛtārthaḥ | tan na | śābde pratyaye svalakṣaṇaṃ parisphurati | kiṃ ca svalakṣaṇātmani vastuni vācye sarvātmanā pratipatteḥ vidhiniṣedhayor ayogaḥ | tasya hi sadbhāve 'stīti vyartham, nāstīty asamartham | asadbhāve tu nāstīti vyartham, astīty asamartham | asti cāstyādipadaprayogaḥ | tasmāt śābdapratibhāsasya bāhyārthabhāvābhāvasādhāraṇyaṃ na tadviṣayatāṃ kṣamate ||
children.translated_text: By this, what <s>Vācaspati</s> says — 'Nor is there an identity of cognition when both verbal and perceptual [cognitions] have a real thing as their object, because the difference of mediate and immediate [character] is accounted for by the difference in cause' — that is not useful. Because mediate cognition is incapable of having a real thing as its object. And the difference in cause that is the basis of mediacy is sufficiently accounted for by the absence of apprehension within the scope of the senses — so it is not [the case] that the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> shines forth in verbal cognition. Furthermore, if the expressible [object of words] is a real thing that is the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> itself, then affirmation and negation would not be possible regarding it in their full sense. For when it exists, 'it exists' is pointless, and 'it does not exist' is incapable [of being true]. And when it does not exist, 'it does not exist' is pointless, and 'it exists' is incapable. But there is the use of words like 'exists' and 'does not exist.' Therefore, the fact that what appears in verbal cognition is common to both the existence and non-existence of the external object precludes [that appearance] having that [object] as its referent.

children.text: yac ca Vācaspatinā jātimadvyaktivācyatāṃ svavācaiva prastutyāntaram eva na ca śabdārthasya jāter bhāvābhāvasādhāraṇyaṃ nopapadyate | sā hi svarūpato nityāpi deśakālaviprakīrṇānekavyaktyāśrayatayā bhāvābhāvasādhāraṇībhavanty astināstisambandhayogyā | vartamānavyaktisambandhitā hi jāter astitā | atītānāgatavyaktisambandhitā ca nāstiteti sandigdhavyatirekitvād anaikāntikaṃ bhāvābhāvasādhāraṇyam, anyathāsiddhaṃ veti vikalpitam | tad aprastutam | tāvatā tāvan na prakṛtakṣatiḥ | jātau bharaṃ nyasyatā svalakṣaṇavācyatvasya svayaṃ svīkārāt | kiṃ ca sarvatra padārthaya svalakṣaṇasvarūpeṇaivāstitvādikaṃ cintyate | jātes tu vartamānādivyaktisambadhī 'stitvādikam iti tu bālapratāraṇam | evaṃ jātimadvyaktivacane 'pi doṣaḥ | vyakteś cet pratītisiddhiḥ jātir adhikā pratīyatāṃ mā vā, na tu vyaktipratītidoṣānmuktiḥ |
children.translated_text: And as for <s>Vācaspati</s>'s proposal that individuals possessing universals are the expressible [meanings of words] — elaborating it in his own words and [then claiming] that the commonality of the universal (as the meaning of words) to existence and non-existence is not untenable, since it, though eternal in its own nature, is common to existence and non-existence by virtue of residing in multiple individuals scattered across different places and times, and is thus fit for the relation of 'exists' and 'does not exist': its relation to a present individual being its existence, and its relation to past and future individuals being its non-existence — [this was then countered:] since the exclusion from the negative example is doubtful, the commonality to existence and non-existence is inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>), or alternatively, [the argument is] based on a falsely construed [condition] (<s>anyathāsiddha</s>). This is not to the point. For at the very least, there is no damage to the present topic thereby. Since in placing the burden on the universal, [the opponent has] himself accepted that <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (the particular) is expressible [by words]. Furthermore, everywhere, the existence and the like of any entity is considered with respect to its own particular nature (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>). But [the claim] that the existence and the like of the universal pertains to its relation with present individuals and so forth — that is a deception of children. Thus, even in the [theory of] expressing individuals-possessing-universals, there is a fault. If the cognition establishes the individual, let the universal be additionally cognized or not — but there is no escape from the faults of individual-cognition.

children.text: etena yad ucyate Kaumārilaiḥ sabhāgatvād eva vastuno na sādhāraṇyadoṣaḥ | vṛkṣatvaṃ hy anirdhāritabhāvābhāvaṃ śabdād avagamyate | tayor anyatareṇa śabdāntarāvagatena sambadhyata iti | tad apy asaṅgatam | sāmānyasya nityasya pratipattāv anirdhāritabhāvābhāvatvāyogāt |
children.translated_text: By this, what the followers of <s>Kumārila</s> say — 'Because of the homogeneity (<s>sabhāgatva</s>) of the [real] entity, there is no fault of commonality [to existence and non-existence]. For tree-ness (<s>vṛkṣatva</s>) is apprehended from a word without its existence or non-existence being determined; and it is then connected with one or the other through another word that is understood' — that too is incoherent. Because when the universal is eternal, it is impossible for it to have undetermined existence/non-existence at the time of cognition.

children.text: yac cedam - na ca pratyakṣasyeva śabdānām arthapratyāyanaprakāro yena taddṛṣṭa ivāstyādiśabdāpekṣā na syāt, vicitraśaktitvāt pramāṇānām iti | tad apy aindriyakaśābdapratibhāsayor ekasvarūpagrāhitve bhinnāvabhāsadūṣaṇena dūṣitam | vicitraśaktitvaṃ ca pramāṇānāṃ sākṣātkārādhyavasāyābhyām api caritārtham | tato yadi pratyakṣārthapratipādanaṃ śābdena tadvad evāvabhāsaḥ syāt | abhavaṃś ca na tadviṣayakhyāpanaṃ kṣamate ||
children.translated_text: As for this [objection]: 'The manner in which words convey meaning is not like that of perception, so that there would be no need for words like "exists" as in the case of something seen, because the means of valid cognition have diverse capacities' — that too has been refuted by the objection of differing appearances, given that the perceptual and verbal appearances have the same essential form as their object. And the diverse capacity of the means of valid cognition is already accounted for by direct apprehension (<s>sākṣātkāra</s>) and determination (<s>adhyavasāya</s>). Therefore, if verbal [cognition] were to convey the object of perception, its appearance would have to be exactly like that [of perception]. And if it does not [appear so], it cannot claim to reveal the object of that [perception].

children.text: nanu vṛkṣaśabdena vṛkṣatvāṃśo codite sattvādyaṃśaniścayanārtham astyādipadaprayoga iti cet |
children.translated_text: Objection: The word '<s>vṛkṣa</s>' (tree) conveys the tree-universal aspect, and the words 'exists' and the like are used for the purpose of ascertaining the other aspects such as being (<s>sattva</s>) and the like.

children.text: niraṃśatvena pratyakṣasamadhigatasya svalakṣaṇasya ko 'vakāśaḥ padāntareṇa | dharmāntaravidhiniṣedhayoḥ pramāṇāntareṇa vā | pratyakṣe 'pi pramāṇāntarāpekṣā dṛṣṭeti cet | bhavatu tasyāniścayātmakatvād anabhyastasvarūpaviṣaye | vikalpas tu svayaṃ niścayātmako yatra grāhī tatra kim apareṇa | asti ca śabdaliṅgāntarāpekṣā | tato na vastusvarūpagrahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Since the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular) apprehended by perception is without parts, what scope is there for another word? Or for another means of valid cognition regarding the affirmation or negation of other properties? [Objection:] Even in perception, dependence on another means of valid cognition is observed. [Reply:] Let it be so, since [perception] is not of the nature of determination and [may be] regarding an object whose form has not been habituated. But conceptual cognition (<s>vikalpa</s>) is itself of the nature of determination — where it apprehends, what need is there for another? And there is dependence on other words and inferential marks (<s>liṅga</s>). Therefore, there is no apprehension of the real nature of the thing.

children.text: nanu bhinnā jātyādayo dharmāḥ parasparaṃ dharmiṇaś ceti jātilakṣaṇaikadharmadvāreṇa pratīte 'pi śākhini dharmāntaravattayā na pratītir iti kiṃ na bhinnābhidhānādhīno dharmāntarasya nīlacaloccais taratvāder avabodhaḥ | tad etad asaṅgatam | akhaṇḍātmanaḥ svalakṣaṇasya pratyakṣe 'pi pratibhāsāt | dṛśyasya dharmadharmibhedasya pratyakṣapratikṣitpatatvāt | anyathā sarvaṃ sarvatra syād ity atiprasaṅgaḥ | kālpanikabhedāśrayas tu dharmadharmivyavahāra iti prasādhitaṃ śāstre
children.translated_text: Objection: Since the properties such as universals (<s>jāti</s>) and the like are distinct from each other and from the property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>), even when a tree is cognized through one property in the form of a universal-characteristic, there is no cognition of it as possessing other properties — so why should not the knowledge of other properties such as blue, moving, tall, and the like depend on different designations? This is incoherent. Because even in perception, the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular), whose nature is undivided, appears. Because the visible distinction of property and property-bearer is rejected by perception. Otherwise, everything would be everywhere — that would be an over-extension. But the conventional usage of property and property-bearer is based on fictitious distinctions — this has been established in the treatise.

children.text: (PVin?)

children.translated_text: 'The support of cognitions is, in reality, one after another; of one and the same [object], whence the form that appears in different modes?'

children.text:
bhavatu vā pāramārthiko 'pi dharmadharmibhedaḥ | tathāpy
	  anayoḥ samavāyāder dūṣitatvād upakāralakṣaṇaiva pratyāsattir eṣitavyā | evaṃ ca yathendriyapratyāsattyā pratyakṣeṇa dharmipratipattau
	  sakalataddharmapratipattis tathā śabdaliṅgābhyām api
	  vācyavācakādisambandhapratibaddhābhyāṃ dharmipratipatau
	  niravaśeṣataddharmapratipattir bhavet | pratyāsattimātrasyāviśeṣāt ||
children.translated_text: Or let the distinction of property and property-bearer be ultimately real as well. Even so, since <s>samavāya</s> (inherence) and the like have been refuted, only a relation characterized by being of assistance (<s>upakāra</s>) should be sought. And thus, just as through the proximity of the sense faculty, when the property-bearer is apprehended by perception, all its properties are apprehended, so too through words and inferential marks — which are bound by the relation of signifier and signified and the like — when the property-bearer is apprehended, all its properties without remainder should be apprehended, because there is no difference in mere proximity.

children.text: yac ca Vācaspatiḥ, na caikopādhinā sattvena viśiṣṭe tasmin gṛhīte upādhyantaraviśiṣṭas tadgrahaḥ | svabhāvo hi dravyasyopādhibhir viśiṣyate | na tūpādhayo vā viśeṣyatvaṃ vā tasya svabhāva iti | tad api plavata eva | na hy abhedād upādhyantaragrahaṇam āsañjitam | bhedaṃ punas kṛtyaivopakārakagrahaṇe upakāryagrahaṇaprasañjanāt | na cāgnidhūmayoḥ kāryakāraṇabhāva iva svabhāvata eva dharmadharmiṇoḥ pratipattiniyamakalpanam ucitam | tayor api pramāṇāsiddhatvāt | pramāṇsiddhe ca svabhāvopavarṇanam iti nyāyaḥ ||

yac cātra Nyāyabhūṣaṇena sūryādigrahaṇe tadupakāryāśeṣavasturāśigrahaṇaprasañjanam uktam, tadabhiprāyānavagāhanaphalam | tathā hi tvanmate dharmadharmiṇor bhedaḥ, upakāralakṣaṇaiva ca pratyāsattis tadopakārakagrahaṇe samānadeśasyaiva dharmarūpasyaiva copakāryasya grahaṇam āsañjitam | tat kathaṃ sūryopakāryasya bhinnadeśasya dravyāntarasya vā dṛṣṭavyabhicārasya grahaṇaprasaṅgaḥ saṅgataḥ | tasmād ekadharmadvāreṇāpi vastusvarūpapratipattau sarvātmapratīteḥ kva śabdāntareṇa vidhiniṣedhāvakāśaḥ | asti ca | tasmān na svalakṣaṇsya śabdavikalpaliṅgapratibhāsitvam iti sthitam ||
children.translated_text: As for what the author of the <s>Nyāyabhūṣaṇa</s> has said here — that in the apprehension of the sun and the like, there would follow the apprehension of the entire mass of things assisted by it — that results from not grasping the intent. For thus: in your view, property and property-bearer are different, and the proximity is characterized only by being of assistance. In [such] apprehension of that which assists, what is entailed is the apprehension of only the property that occupies the same location and is of the nature of a property of that assisted thing. How then is the consequence of apprehending what is assisted by the sun — which occupies a different location and is a different substance — and which exhibits observed deviation, coherent? Therefore, even through a single property, when the real nature of the thing is apprehended, there is cognition of its entire self — so where is there scope for affirmation or negation by another word? And yet there is [such scope]. Therefore, it is established that the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular) does not appear in verbal cognition, conceptual cognition, or inferential cognition.

children.text: nāpi sāmānyaṃ śābdapratyayapratibhāsi | saritaḥ pāre gāvaś carantīti gavādiśabdāt sāsnāśṛṅgalāṅgūlādayo 'kṣarākāraparikaritāḥ sajātīyabhedāparāmarśanāt sampiṇḍitaprāyāḥ pratibhāsante | na ca tad eva sāmānyam |
children.translated_text: Nor does a universal (<s>sāmānya</s>) appear in verbal cognition. From the word '<s>go</s>' (cow) in the sentence 'cows are grazing on the far bank of the river,' [what appears are] dewlap, horns, tail, and the like — fashioned in the form of syllabic shapes, and appearing as if lumped together due to the non-discrimination of distinctions among members of the same class. But that is not the universal itself.

As for what <s>Vācaspati</s> [says]: 'When that [particular] qualified by one attribute, namely being (<s>sattva</s>), is grasped, it is not the case that it is grasped as qualified by another attribute. For the essential nature of a substance is qualified by attributes. But the attributes, or the state of being qualified, are not its essential nature.' — That too simply floats [i.e., is groundless]. For the apprehension of the other attribute has not been challenged on the basis of non-difference. But if difference is assumed, then from the apprehension of that which assists, the apprehension of that which is assisted would follow. And it is not proper to posit a necessary restriction of cognition between property and property-bearer as if it were naturally [fixed], as in the cause-and-effect relation between fire and smoke. Because that [relation] too is not established by any means of valid cognition. And the principle is: when established by a means of valid cognition, one merely describes the essential nature.

children.text: varṇākṛtyakṣarākāraśūnyaṃ gotvaṃ hi kathyate |
(PV III 147)

children.translated_text: <s>Gotva</s> (cow-universal) is said to be devoid of color, shape, and syllabic form.

children.text:
tad eva ca sāsnāśṛṅgādimātram
	  akhilavyaktāv atyantavilakṣaṇam api svalakṣaṇenaikīkriyamāṇaṃ sāmānyam
	  ity ucyate tādṛśasya bāhyasyāprāpter bhrāntir evāsau
	  keśapratibhāsavat | tasmād vāsanāvaśād buddher eva tadātmanā vivarto
	  'yam astu | asad eva vā tadrūpaṃ khyātu | vyaktaya eva vā
	  svajātīyabhedatiraskāreṇānyathā bhāsantām anubhavavyavadhānāt
	  smṛtipramoṣo vābhidhīyatām | sarvathā nirviṣayaḥ khalv ayaṃ
	  sāmānyapratyayaḥ | kva sāmānyavārtā |
children.translated_text: And that very [appearance of] mere dewlap, horns, and the like — even though absolutely different in each individual (<s>vyakti</s>) — when identified with the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular), is called a 'universal.' Since such an external [entity] is unattainable, that [cognition] is nothing but an error, like the appearance of hair [to one with an eye disease]. Therefore, let this be a transformation (<s>vivarta</s>) of the mind itself into that form, through the force of latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>). Or let what is non-existent appear in that form. Or let the individuals themselves appear otherwise through the concealment of distinctions among members of the same class — or let it be called a failure of memory due to the interruption of experience. In every case, this cognition of a universal is without any [real] object. Where then is there any talk of a universal?

children.text: yat punaḥ sāmānyābhāve sāmānyapratyayasyākasmikatvam uktaṃ tad ayuktam | yataḥ pūrvapiṇḍadarśanasmaraṇasahakāriṇātiricyamānaviśeṣapratyayajanikā sāmagrī nirviṣayaṃ sāmānyavikalpam utpādayati | tad evaṃ na śābde pratyaye jātiḥ pratibhāti | nāpi pratyakṣe | na cānumānato 'pi siddhiḥ | adṛśyatve pratibaddhaliṅgād adarśanāt | nāpīndriyavad asyāḥ siddhiḥ jñānakāryataḥ kādācitkasyaiva nimittāntarasya siddheḥ | yadā piṇḍāntare antarāle vā gobuddher abhāvaṃ darśayet tadā śāvaleyādisakalagopiṇḍānām evābhāvād abhāvo gobuddher upapadyamānaḥ katham arthāntaram ākṣipet | atha gotvād eva gopiṇḍaḥ | anyathā turago 'pi gopiṇḍaḥ syāt | yady evaṃ gopiṇḍād eva gotvam anyathā turagatvam api gotvaṃ syāt | tasmāt kāraṇaparamparāta eva gopiṇḍo gotvaṃ tu bhavatu mā vā | nanu sāmānyapratyayajananasāmarthyaṃ yady ekasmāt piṇḍād abhinnaṃ tadā vijātīyavyāvṛttaṃ piṇḍāntaram asamartham | atha bhinnam, tadā tad eva sāmānyam, nāmni paraṃ vivāda iti cet | abhinnaiva sā śaktiḥ prativastu | yathā tv ekaḥ śaktasvabhāvo bhāvas tathānyo 'pi bhavan kīdṛśaṃ doṣam āvahati | yathā bhavatāṃ jātir ekāpi samānadhvaniprasavahetuḥ, anyāpi svarūpeṇaiva jātyantaranirapekṣā, tathāsmākaṃ vyaktir api jātinirapekṣā svarūpeṇaiva bhinnā hetuḥ ||
yat tu
children.translated_text: And as for what

children.text: trilocanaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Trilocana</s>

children.text: : aśvatvagotvādīnāṃ sāmānyaviśeṣāṇāṃ svāśraye samavāyaḥ sāmānyaṃ sāmānyam ity abhidhānapratyayor nimittam iti | yady evaṃ vyaktiṣv apy ayam eva tathābhidhānapratyayahetus tu, kiṃ sāmānyasvīkārapramādena | na ca samavāyaḥ sambhavī |
children.translated_text: [says]: 'The <s>samavāya</s> (inherence) of universals and particulars such as horse-ness, cow-ness, and the like in their own substrata is the ground for the designation and cognition "this is a universal"' — if so, this very same [ground] is the cause of such designation and cognition in individuals too; what then is the point of the blunder of accepting a universal? And <s>samavāya</s> (inherence) is not possible.

As for the further statement that in the absence of a universal, the cognition of a universal would be without a cause — that is unjustified. Because the causal complex — assisted by the memory of seeing a previous individual and generating a cognition of a particular that transcends [the individual seen] — produces a contentless universal-concept (<s>vikalpa</s>). Thus, universals (<s>jāti</s>) do not appear in verbal cognition. Nor in perception. Nor is there establishment through inference either, because no inferential mark bound to what is invisible is observed. Nor is its establishment like that of the sense faculty from the effect of cognition, because only an occasional cause [other than the universal] is established. When someone demonstrates the absence of cow-cognition in another individual or in the interval [between individuals], then — since the absence of cow-cognition is accounted for by the absence of all cow-individuals such as dogs and all [other] cow-individuals — how could it point to something else [i.e., a universal]? [Objection:] A cow-individual exists precisely because of <s>gotva</s> (cowness); otherwise a horse too would be a cow-individual. [Reply:] If so, then <s>gotva</s> exists precisely because of the cow-individual; otherwise horse-ness too would be <s>gotva</s>. Therefore, a cow-individual [arises] from a chain of causes alone — let <s>gotva</s> exist or not. [Objection:] If the capacity to generate a universal-cognition is non-different from a single individual, then another individual, excluded from the heterogeneous, would be incapable [of generating it]. If it is different, then that itself is the universal — the dispute is merely about the name. [Reply:] That capacity is indeed non-different in each individual thing. But just as one entity has a capable nature, so does another — what fault does that bring? Just as for you, a single universal (<s>jāti</s>) is the cause of producing the same name, and another [universal] too, by its own nature alone, independent of any other universal — so for us, each individual (<s>vyakti</s>) too, independent of a universal, is by its own nature alone a distinct cause.

children.text:
iheti buddheḥ samavāyasiddhir iheti dhīś ca dvayadarśanena |
	  na ca kvacit tadviṣaye tv apekṣā svakalpanāmātramato 'bhyupāyaḥ ||

etena seyaṃ pratyayānuvṛttir anuvṛttavastvanuyāyinī katham atyantabhedinīṣu vyaktiṣu vyāvṛttaviṣayapratyayabhāvānupātinīṣu bhavitum arhatīty ūhāpravartanam asya pratyākhyātam | jātiṣv eva parasparavyāvṛttatayā vyaktīyamānāsv anuvṛttapratyayena vyabhicārāt |
children.translated_text: By this, the speculation — 'How can this regularity of cognition, which follows a persisting entity, occur in individuals that are absolutely different and whose cognitions follow objects that are mutually exclusive?' — has been refuted. Because even among universals (<s>jāti</s>), which manifest as mutually exclusive, there is deviation from the regular cognition [that should follow a persisting entity].

children.text: yat punar anena viparyaye bādhakam uktam, abhidhānapratyayānuvṛttiḥ kutaścin nivṛttya kvacid eva bhavantī nimittavatī, na cānyannimittam ityādi | tan na samyak | anuvṛttam anyatreṇāpy abhidhānapratyayānuvṛtter atadrūpaparāvṛttasvarūpaviśeṣād avaśyaṃ svīkārasya sādhitatvāt | tasmāt
children.translated_text: As for the counter-proof (<s>bādhaka</s>) stated by him regarding the contrary — 'The regularity of designation and cognition, occurring somewhere after ceasing from something else, has a cause, and no other cause [is possible],' and so forth — that is not correct. Because, even without anything persisting, the regularity of designation and cognition has already been established as necessarily arising from a specific nature that is excluded from what is not of that form.

The establishment of <s>samavāya</s> (inherence) [depends on] the cognition 'it is here,' and the cognition 'it is here' [depends on] the observation of two [distinct entities]. But nowhere is there need for that regarding that object — therefore the [only] recourse is to [acknowledge it as] mere self-fabrication.

children.text: tulye bhede yayā jātiḥ pratyāsattyā prasarpati |
children.translated_text: Given that difference is equal [everywhere], the proximity by which a universal extends

children.text: kvacin nānyatra saivāstu śabdajñānanibandhanam ||
children.translated_text: to some [things] and not to others — let that very [proximity] be the basis for words and cognitions.

children.text: PV I 162

yat punar atra Nyāyabhūṣaṇoktam: na hy evaṃ bhavati, yayā pratyāsattyā daṇḍasūtrādikaṃ prasarpati kvacin nānyatra saiva pratyāsattiḥ puruṣasphaṭikādiṣu daṇḍisūtritvādivyavahāranibandhanam astu, kiṃ daṇḍasūtrādineti | tad asaṅgatam | daṇḍasūtrayor hi puruṣasphaṭikapratyāsannyoḥ dṛṣṭayoḥ daṇḍisūtritvapratyayahetutvaṃ nāpalapyate | sāmānyaṃ tu svapne 'pi na dṛṣṭam | tad yadīdaṃ parikalpanīyaṃ tadā varaṃ pratyāsattir eva sāmānyapratyayahetuḥ parikalpyatām, kiṃ gurvyā parikalpanayety abhiprāyāparijñānāt |
children.translated_text: As for what was said in the <s>Nyāyabhūṣaṇa</s>: 'For it is not the case that the proximity by which a stick, string, and the like extend to some [things] and not to others — that very proximity should be the basis for the conventional usage of "possessing a stick," "possessing a string," and the like in persons, crystals, and the like — what need is there of a stick, string, and the like?' — that is incoherent. For the proximity of a stick and string to a person and crystal, being observed, is not denied as the cause of the cognition of 'possessing a stick' and 'possessing a string.' But a universal has never been seen even in a dream. So if this [proximity] is to be postulated, then it is better to postulate proximity itself as the cause of the universal-cognition — what is the point of a more burdensome postulation? — [this objection arises] from not grasping the intent.

children.text: athedaṃ jātiprasādhakam anumānam abhidhīyate | yad viśiṣṭajñānaṃ tadviśeṣaṇagrahaṇanāntarīyakam | yathā daṇḍijñānam | viśiṣṭajñānaṃ cedaṃ gaurayam ity arthataḥ kāryahetuḥ | viśeṣaṇānubhavakāryaṃ hi dṛṣṭānte viśiṣṭabuddhiḥ siddheti | atrānuyogaḥ | viśiṣṭabuddher bhinnaviśeṣaṇagrahaṇanāntarīyakatvaṃ vā sādhyaṃ viśeṣaṇamātrānubhavanāntarīyakatvaṃ vā |
children.translated_text: Now, the following inference is stated as establishing universals (<s>jāti</s>): Whatever is a qualified cognition necessarily involves the apprehension of its qualifier — like the cognition of 'one possessing a stick.' And this cognition 'this is a cow' is a qualified cognition — hence, by the force of the reason of effecthood (<s>kāryahetu</s>): for the qualified cognition is established in the example as the effect of the experience of the qualifier. Here is the examination: Is the provable that qualified cognition necessarily involves the apprehension of a different qualifier, or that it necessarily involves the experience of any qualifier whatsoever?

children.text: prathamapakṣe pakṣasya pratyakṣabādhā sādhanāvadhānam anavakāśayati, vastugrāhiṇaḥ pratyakṣasyobhayapratibhāsābhāvāt | viśiṣṭabuddhitvaṃ ca sāmānyahetur anaikāntikaḥ, bhinnaviśeṣaṇagrahaṇam antareṇāpi darśanāt | yathā svarūpavān ghaṭaḥ, gotvaṃ sāmānyam iti vā |
children.translated_text: In the first alternative, perceptual contradiction (<s>pratyakṣabādhā</s>) of the thesis precludes the establishment of the proof, since perception, which grasps reality, lacks the appearance of both [a qualifier and what is qualified as separate]. And 'being a qualified cognition' as the reason for [the existence of] a universal is inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>), because [qualified cognition] is observed even without the apprehension of a distinct qualifier — as in 'a pot having its own nature' or '<s>gotva</s> is a universal.'

children.text: dvitīyapakṣe tu siddhasādhanam | svarūpavān ghaṭa ityādivat gotvajātimān piṇḍa iti parikalpitaṃ bhedam upādāya viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvasyeṣṭatvād agovyāvṛttānubhavabhāvitvād gaurayam iti vyavahārasya | tad evaṃ na sāmānyasiddhiḥ | bādhakaṃ ca sāmānyaguṇakarmādyupādhicakrasya kevalavyaktigrāhakaṃ paṭupratyakṣaṃ dṛśyānulambho vā prasiddhaḥ |
children.translated_text: In the second alternative, however, the proof establishes what is already established (<s>siddhasādhana</s>). Because, just as in 'a pot having its own nature' and the like, the relation of qualifier and qualified in 'an individual possessing the universal <s>gotva</s>' is accepted as based on a postulated distinction. And the conventional usage 'this is a cow' arises from the experience of exclusion from non-cow. Thus, the establishment of a universal is not achieved. And the well-known counter-proof is keen perception that grasps mere individuals to the exclusion of the circle of superimposed [categories] such as universals, qualities, actions, and the like — or the apprehension of what is visible.

children.text: tad evaṃ vidhir eva śabdārthaḥ | sa ca bāhyo 'rtho buddhyākāraś ca vivakṣitaḥ | tatra na buddhyākārasya tattvataḥ saṃvṛtyā vā vidhiniṣedhau, svasaṃvedanapratyakṣagamyatvāt | anadhyavasāyāc ca | nāpi tattvato bāhyasyāpi vidhiniṣedhau, tasya śābde pratyaye 'pratibhāsanāt | ata eva sarvadharmāṇāṃ tattvato 'nabhilāpyatvaṃ pratibhāsādhyavasāyābhāvāt | tasmād bāhyasyaiva sāṃvṛttau vidhiniṣedhau | anyathā saṃvyavahārahāniprasaṅgāt | tad evaṃ
children.translated_text: Thus, affirmation (<s>vidhi</s>) alone is the meaning of words. And that [affirmation] is intended as both an external object and a mental image (<s>buddhyākāra</s>). Of these, there is neither affirmation nor negation of the mental image, whether ultimately or conventionally, because it is known through the self-awareness (<s>svasaṃvedana</s>) of direct perception. And because it is not the object of determination (<s>adhyavasāya</s>). Nor is there ultimately affirmation or negation of the external [object] either, because it does not appear in verbal cognition. For this very reason, all <s>dharmas</s> are ultimately inexpressible, due to the absence of both appearance and determination. Therefore, affirmation and negation are only of the external [object] in the conventional [domain]. Otherwise, there would be the consequence of the loss of all practical transactions. Thus,

children.text: nākārasya na bāhyasya tattvato vidhisādhanam |
children.translated_text: There is no ultimate establishment of affirmation — neither of the mental image nor of the external [object].

children.text:
bahir eva hi saṃvṛtyā samvṛtyāpi tu
	    nākṛteḥ ||
children.translated_text: Only of the external, conventionally; but not even conventionally of the [mental] form.

children.text:
Corresponds to AP 229.3–4, SāSiŚā
	    443.13–14.
etena yad
Dharmottaraḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Dharmottara</s>

children.text:
āropitasya
	  bāhyatvasya vidhiniṣedhāv ity alaukikam anāgamamatārkikīyaṃ kathayati,
	  tad apy apahastitam |
children.translated_text: says — that affirmation and negation are of the superimposed externality — which is an extraordinary, non-scriptural, mere logician's [view] — that too has been dismissed.

children.text:
nanv
	  adhyavasāye yady adhyavaseyaṃ vastu na sphurati tadā tad adhyavasitam
	  iti ko 'rthaḥ | apratibhāse 'pi pravṛttiviṣayīkṛtam iti yo 'rthaḥ |
	  apratibhāsāviśeṣe viṣayāntaraparihāreṇa kathaṃ niyataviṣayā pravṛttir
	  iti cet | ucyate | yady api viśvam agṛhītaṃ tathāpi vikalpasya
	  niyatasāmagrīprasūtatvena niyatākāratayā, niyataśaktitvāt niyataiva
	  jalādau pravṛttiḥ | dhūmasya parokṣāgnijñānajananavat |
children.translated_text: [Objection:] If in determination (<s>adhyavasāya</s>) the determined object does not appear, then what does it mean to say 'it is determined'? [Reply:] The meaning is: even without appearing, [the object] is made the domain of purposive activity. [Objection:] In the absence of any distinction in non-appearance, how can there be purposive activity restricted to a specific object rather than other objects? [Reply:] We say: Even though the universal [particular] is not grasped, still, because a conceptual cognition (<s>vikalpa</s>), being produced from a specific aggregate [of causes], has a specific form and therefore a specific capacity, purposive activity is necessarily restricted to water and the like — just as smoke generates cognition of fire that is not directly perceived.

children.text:
niyataviṣayā hi bhāvāḥ
	  pramāṇapariniṣṭhitasvabhāvā na śaktisāṃkaryaparyanuyogabhājaḥ | tasmāt
	  tadadhyavasāyitvam ākāraviśeṣayogāt tatpravṛttijanakatvam | na ca
	  sādṛśyād āropeṇa pravṛttiṃ brūmaḥ, yenākāre bāhyasya bāhye
	  vākārasyāropadvāreṇa dūṣaṇāvakāśaḥ | kiṃ tarhi svavāsanāvipākavaśād
	  upajāyamānaiva buddhir apaśyanty api bāhyaṃ bāhye pravṛttim ātanotīti
	  viplutaiva | tad evam anyābhāvaviśiṣṭo vijātivyāvṛtto 'rtho vidhiḥ |
	  sa eva cāpohaśabdavācyaḥ śabdānām arthaḥ pravṛttinivṛttiviṣayaś ceti
	  sthitam |
children.translated_text: For entities whose natures are established by valid cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>) have restricted objects and are not subject to the objection of confusion of capacities. Therefore, [the conceptual cognition's] being a determiner of that [object] is due to its possessing a specific form, [and] its being a generator of purposive activity toward that [object] [is due to the same]. And we do not say that purposive activity occurs through superimposition on the basis of similarity, such that there would be room for the objection that external [reality] is superimposed on the form [of cognition] or the form [is superimposed] on the external [object]. Rather, cognition itself, arising through the ripening of its own latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>), even without perceiving the external [object], extends purposive activity toward the external — and so it is indeed erroneous [in that sense]. Thus, an object that is qualified by the absence of what is other, i.e., excluded from what is of a different kind, is positive reality (<s>vidhi</s>). And that very thing, which is expressible by the word '<s>apoha</s>' (exclusion), is the referent of words and the domain of purposive engagement and disengagement — this is established.

children.text:
atra prayogaḥ | yad
	  vācakaṃ tat sarvam adhyavasitātadrūpaparāvṛttavastumātragocaram |
	  yatheha kūpe jalam iti vacanam | vācakaṃ cedaṃ gavādiśabdarūpam iti
	  svabhāvahetuḥ | nāyam asiddhaḥ | pūrvoktena nyāyena
	  pāramārthikavācyavācakabhāvasyābhāve 'pi adhyavasāyakṛtasyaiva
	  sarvavyavahāribhir avaśyaṃ svīkarttavyatvāt |anyathā
	  sarvavyavahārocchedaprasaṅgāt | nāpi viruddhaḥ | sapakṣe bhāvāt | na
	  cānaikāntikaḥ | tathā hi śabdānām
	  adhyavasitavijātivyāvṛttavastumātraviṣayatvam anicchadbhiḥ paraiḥ
	  paramārthato
children.translated_text: Here is the formal argument: Whatever is a signifier (<s>vācaka</s>), all of that has as its domain merely a real entity that is excluded from what is not of that nature, as determined [by cognition] — just like the statement 'There is water in this well.' And this [thing in question] — namely, words such as 'cow' and the like — is a signifier: this is a proof based on essential nature (<s>svabhāvahetu</s>). This [reason] is not unestablished (<s>asiddha</s>), because — although there is no ultimately real signifier-signified relation, as shown by the reasoning set forth above — [the relation] established through determination must necessarily be accepted by all who engage in practical transactions. Otherwise, there would be the absurd consequence of the cessation of all practical transactions. Nor is it contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>), because it is present in the positive example (<s>sapakṣa</s>). Nor is it inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>). For thus: those opponents who do not wish words to have as their domain merely a real entity excluded from what is of a different kind [must accept that] ultimately
By this, what
