children.text: vācyaṃ svalakṣaṇam upādhir upādhiyogaḥ sopādhir astu yadi vā kṛtir astu buddhaḥ |
children.translated_text: the signified is the particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>), or a limiting condition (<s>upādhi</s>), or the relation with a limiting condition, or a qualified [entity], or alternatively, let it be an artificial construction (<s>kṛti</s>) — the [whole position is] already refuted.

children.text: gatyantarābhāvāt | aviṣayatve ca vācakatvāyogāt | tatra
children.translated_text: Because there is no other alternative. And if it is not an object [of the word], then it cannot be a signifier. In that regard,

children.text: ādyantayor na samayaḥ phalaśaktihāner madhye 'py upādhivirahāt tritayena yuktaḥ ||
tad evaṃ vācyāntarasyābhāvāt viṣayavattvalakṣaṇasya vyāpakasya nivṛttau vipakṣato nivarttamānaṃ vācakatvam adhyavasitabāhyaviṣayatvena vyāpyata iti vyāptisiddhiḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus, since there is no other signified, when the pervader — namely, having an object as its defining characteristic — ceases in the counter-positive, the property of being a signifier, which ceases from the counter-positive, is pervaded by having a determined external [object] as its domain — thus the pervasion is established.

'For the first and last [alternatives], there is no convention, due to the loss of result and capacity; for the middle [alternative] too, due to the absence of the limiting condition, [none of these] is tenable with respect to all three.'

children.text: mahāpaṇḍitaratnakīrtipādaviracitam apohaprakaraṇaṃ samāptam ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Apoha</s> treatise composed by the great scholar (<s>mahāpaṇḍita</s>) <s>Ratnakīrti</s> is completed.

children.text: Kṣaṇabhaṅgasiddhiḥ
Anvayātmikā
children.translated_text: <s>Anvayātmikā</s> (The Positive Concomitance Form)
<s>Kṣaṇabhaṅgasiddhi</s> (Proof of Momentariness)

children.text: namas tārāyai ||
children.translated_text: Salutation to <s>Tārā</s>!

children.text: ākṣiptavyatirekā yā vyāptir anvayarūpiṇī |
children.translated_text: The pervasion in the form of positive concomitance, which implies negative concomitance,

children.text: sādharmyavati dṛṣṭānte sattvahetor ihocyate ||
children.translated_text: is here stated for the reason of existence (<s>sattva</s>), with respect to a positive example (<s>sādharmyavat dṛṣṭānta</s>).

children.text: yat sat tat kṣaṇikam, yathā ghaṭaḥ, santaś cāmī vivādāspadībhūtāḥ padārthā
iti |
children.translated_text: thus [the inference].
Whatever exists is momentary, like a pot. And these entities that are the subject of dispute are existent —

children.text: hetoḥ parokṣārthapratipādakatvaṃ hetvābhāsatvaśaṅkānirākaraṇam antareṇa na śakyate
pratipādayitum | hetvābhāsāś ca asiddhaviruddhānaikāntikabhedena trividhāḥ |
children.translated_text: without dispelling the suspicion of its being a pseudo-reason (<s>hetvābhāsa</s>). And pseudo-reasons are of three kinds: unestablished (<s>asiddha</s>), contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>), and inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>).
The capacity of the logical reason to establish the imperceptible thesis cannot be demonstrated

children.text: tatra na tāvad ayam asiddho hetuḥ | yadi nāma darśane darśane nānāprakāraṃ sattvalakṣaṇa
m uktam āste, arthakriyākāritvaṃ, sattāsamavāyaḥ, svarūpasattvam, utpādavyayadhrauvya
children.translated_text: various ways — causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyākāritva</s>), inherence of the universal being (<s>sattāsamavāya</s>), existence as its own nature (<s>svarūpasattva</s>), the possession of origination, destruction, and permanence

children.text: yogitvaṃ, pramāṇaviṣayatvaṃ, sadupalambhakapramāṇagocaratvaṃ,
children.translated_text: (<s>utpādavyayadhrauvyayogitva</s>), being the object of a valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇaviṣayatva</s>), being within the scope of a valid cognition that apprehends what exists (<s>sadupalambhakapramāṇagocaratva</s>),

children.text: Read as in
Woo 1999
, against
tadupalambhakapramāṇagocaratvaṃ
vyapadeśaviṣayatvam ityādi,
children.translated_text: being the object of designation (<s>vyapadeśaviṣayatva</s>), and so forth —

children.text: tathāpi kim anenāprastutenedānīm eva niṣṭaṅkitena | yad eva hi pramāṇato nirūpyamāṇaṃ padārthānāṃ sattvam upapannaṃ bhaviṣyati tad eva vayam api svīkariṣyāmaḥ |  kevalaṃ tad etad artha
children.translated_text: nevertheless, what is the point of this irrelevant matter being stamped [with authority] right now? For whatever nature of existence of entities is demonstrated through valid cognition — that we too shall accept. Merely [we note that] this [nature] — namely,

children.text: kriyākāritvaṃ sarvajanaprasiddham āste tat khalv atra sattvaśabdenābhisandhāya sādhanatvenopāttam | tac ca yathāyogaṃ pratyakṣānumānapramāṇaprasiddhasadbhāveṣu bhāveṣu pakṣīkṛteṣu pratyakṣādinā pramāṇena pratītam iti na svarūpeṇāśrayadvāreṇa vāsiddhisambhāvanāpi ||
children.translated_text: causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyākāritva</s>) — which is well-known to all people, is here intended by the word 'existence' and taken as the reason. And that [causal efficacy] is apprehended by means of valid cognition such as perception and inference in entities whose existence is established — the entities included in the thesis. Thus, there is no possibility of unestablishment either in its own nature or through the locus [of the thesis].
To begin with, this reason is not unestablished. For even though in various philosophical systems, the defining characteristic of existence (<s>sattva</s>) has been stated in

children.text: nāpi viruddhatā, sapakṣīkṛte ghaṭe sadbhāvāt |
children.translated_text: Nor is there contradiction (<s>viruddhatā</s>), because [the reason] is present in the positive example — the pot — which is accepted as the positive class.

children.text: nanu katham asya sapakṣatvam, pakṣavad atrāpi kṣaṇabhaṅgāsiddheḥ | na hy asya pratyakṣataḥ kṣaṇabhaṅgasiddhiḥ, tathātvenāniścayāt | nāpi sattvānumānataḥ, punarnidarśanāntarāpekṣāyām anavasthāprasaṅgāt | na cānyad anumānam asti | sambhave vā tenaiva pakṣe 'pi kṣaṇabhaṅgasiddher alaṃ sattvānumāneneti cet |
children.translated_text: [Objection:] How can this [pot] be a positive example, since momentariness (<s>kṣaṇabhaṅga</s>) is unestablished there too, just as in the thesis? For its momentariness is not established through perception, since it is not ascertained as such. Nor through the inference from existence, since that would require yet another example, leading to an infinite regress. And there is no other inference. Or if there were, then by that alone momentariness could be established in the thesis too, making the inference from existence pointless.

children.text: ucyate | anumānāntaram eva prasaṅgaprasaṅgaviparyayātmakaṃ ghaṭe  kṣaṇabhaṅgaprasādhakaṃ pramāṇāntaram asti |
tathā hi ghaṭo vartamānakṣaṇe tāvad ekām arthakriyāṃ
children.translated_text: For thus: a pot at the present moment produces a single causal

children.text: karoti | atītānāgatakṣaṇayor api kiṃ tām evārthakriyāṃ kuryāt, anyāṃ vā, na vā kām api kriyām iti trayaḥ pakṣāḥ |
children.translated_text: effect. With respect to past and future moments too, would it produce that very same effect, or a different one, or no effect at all? — these are three alternatives.

[Reply:] We say: There does indeed exist another means of proof — in the form of <s>prasaṅga</s> (reductio ad absurdum) and <s>prasaṅgaviparyaya</s> (the converse of the reductio) — which is a separate proof establishing momentariness in the pot.

children.text: nātra prathamaḥ pakṣo  yuktaḥ, kṛtasya karaṇāyogāt |
children.translated_text: The first alternative is not tenable, because of the impossibility of doing what has already been done.

children.text: atha dvitīyo 'bhyupagamyate, tad idam atra vicāryatām | yadā ghaṭo vartamānakṣaṇabhāvi kāryaṃ karoti tadā kim atītānāgatakṣaṇabhāviny api kārye śakto 'śakto vā |

yadi śaktas tadā vartamānakṣaṇabhāvikāryavad atītānāgatakṣaṇabhāvy api kāryaṃ tadaiva  kuryāt | tatrāpi śaktatvāt | śaktasya ca  kṣepāyogāt, anyathā varttamānakṣaṇabhāvino 'pi kāryasyākaraṇaprasaṅgāt pūrvāparakālayor api śaktatvenāviśeṣāt | samarthasya ca sahakāryapekṣāyā ayogāt |
children.translated_text: If capable, then just as it produces the effect belonging to the present moment, it should produce the effect belonging to past and future moments at that very time too — because it is capable there too, and because it is impossible for a capable [entity] to delay; otherwise, there would be the absurd consequence of not producing even the present moment's effect, since there is no distinction [between the moments] with respect to its being capable in the earlier and later times. And because it is impossible for a competent [entity] to depend on auxiliary conditions.

children.text: athāśaktaḥ, tadaikatra kārye śaktāśaktatvaviruddhadharmādhyāsāt kṣaṇavidhvaṅso ghaṭasya durvāraprasaraḥ syāt |
children.translated_text: If incapable, then, because of the superimposition of contradictory properties — being capable and incapable — with respect to a single effect, the momentary destruction of the pot would be an irresistible consequence.

If the second is accepted, then let this be examined: When the pot produces the effect belonging to the present moment, is it capable or incapable with respect to the effect belonging to past and future moments too?

children.text: nāpi tṛtīyaḥ pakṣaḥ saṅgacchate, śaktasvabhāvānuvṛtter eva | yadā hi śaktasya padārthasya  vilambo 'py asahyas tadā dūrotsāritam  akaraṇam | anyathā vārtamānikasyāpi kāryasyākaraṇaṃ syād ity uktam |
children.translated_text: Nor does the third alternative hold, because the nature of being capable persists [at all times]. For when even delay is intolerable for a capable entity, non-production is a fortiori excluded. Otherwise, even the production of the present effect would not occur — as has been stated.

children.text: tasmād yad yadā yajjananavyavahārapātraṃ tat tadā tat kuryāt | akurvac ca na jananavyavahārabhājanam | tad evam ekatra kārye samarthetarasvabhāvatayā pratikṣaṇaṃ bhedād ghaṭasya sapakṣatvam akṣatam ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, whatever is at any time a candidate for the conventional designation of 'producing' something, that produces that at that time. And what does not produce is not a candidate for the conventional designation of producing. Thus, since the pot differs at each moment — being of a nature that is capable with respect to one effect and incapable [with respect to another] — its status as a positive example (<s>sapakṣa</s>) is unimpaired.

children.text: atra prayogaḥ | yad yadā yajjananavyavahārayogyaṃ tat tadā taj janayaty eva | yathā 'ntyā kāraṇasāmagrī svakāryam | atītānāgatakṣaṇabhāvikāryajananavyavahārayogyaś cāyaṃ ghaṭo vartamānakṣaṇabhāvikāryakaraṇakāle sakalakriyātikramakāle 'pīti
svabhāvahetuprasaṅgaḥ |
children.translated_text: this is a <s>prasaṅga</s> (reductio) based on the reason of essential nature (<s>svabhāvahetu</s>).

Here is the formal argument: Whatever is at any time fit for the conventional designation of producing something, that produces that at that time — just as the final aggregate of causes [produces] its own effect. And this pot, at the time of producing the effect belonging to the present moment — which is also the time of the transcending of all [other] activities — is fit for the conventional designation of producing the effect belonging to past and future moments too —

children.text: asya ca dvitīyādikṣaṇabhāvikāryakaraṇavyavahāragocaratvasya prasaṅgasādhanasya vārtamānikakāryakaraṇakāle  sakalakriyātikramakāle ca ghaṭe dharmiṇi parābhyupagamamātrataḥ siddhatvād asiddhis tāvad asambhavinī |
children.translated_text: And since this <s>prasaṅga</s>-proof — namely, that [the pot] is within the scope of the conventional designation of producing the effect belonging to the second and subsequent moments — is established in the locus of the thesis (the pot as the example), at the time of producing the present effect and at the time of the transcending of all activities, merely on the basis of the opponent's own acceptance, unestablishment is impossible.

children.text: nāpi viruddhatā, sapakṣe 'ntyakāraṇasāmagryāṃ sadbhāvasambhavāt|
children.translated_text: Nor is there contradiction, because it is possible for [the reason] to be present in the positive example — the final aggregate of causes.

children.text: nanv ayaṃ sādhāraṇānaikāntiko hetuḥ | sākṣādajanake 'pi kuśūlādyavasthitabījādau vipakṣe samarthavyavahāragocaratvasya sādhanasya darśanād iti cet |

na | dvividho hi samarthavyavahāraḥ pāramārthika aupacārikaś ca | tatra yat pāramārthikaṃ jananaprayuktaṃ jananavyavahāragocaratvaṃ tad iha sādhanatvenopāttam | tasya ca kuśūlādyavasthitabījādau kāraṇakāraṇatvād aupacārikajananavyavahāraviṣayabhūte sambhavābhāvāt kutaḥ sādhāraṇānaikāntikatā |
children.translated_text: [Reply:] No. For the conventional designation of being competent is of two kinds: ultimate (<s>pāramārthika</s>) and figurative (<s>aupacārika</s>). Of these, it is the ultimate fitness for the conventional designation of producing — that which is connected with actual production — that is here taken as the reason. And since seeds stored in a granary and the like, being [merely] causes of causes, are the domain of only a figurative conventional designation of producing, [and since the ultimate fitness] is absent there, how can there be the defect of being a common inconclusive [reason]?

[Objection:] This reason is inconclusive as common (<s>sādhāraṇānaikāntika</s>), because the proof — being within the scope of the conventional designation of being competent — is observed even in the counter-positive, such as seeds stored in a granary and the like, which do not directly produce [their effect].

children.text: na cāsya sandigdhavyatirekitā, viparyaye bādhakapramāṇasadbhāvat |
tathā hīdaṃ
children.translated_text: For thus:

children.text: jananavyavahāragocaratvaṃ niyataviṣayatvena vyāptam iti sarvajanānubhavaprasiddham | na cedaṃ nirnimittam, deśakālasvabhāvaniyamābhāvaprasaṅgāt | na ca jananād anyan nimittam upalabhyate, tadanvayavyatirekānuvidhānadarśanāt |
children.translated_text: this fitness for the conventional designation of producing is pervaded by having a restricted object — this is well-known from the experience of all people. And this [restriction] is not without a cause, because in its absence there would be the absurd consequence of the absence of restriction of place, time, and nature. And no cause other than [actual] production is apprehended, because conformity to the positive and negative concomitance of that [production] is observed.
Nor does this [reason] have doubtful negative concomitance (<s>sandigdhavyatirekitā</s>), because a defeating counter-proof exists in the case of the converse.

children.text: yadi ca jananam antareṇāpi jananavyavahāragocaratvaṃ syāt tadā sarvasya sarvatra jananavyavahāra ity aniyamaḥ syāt | ni
yataś cāyaṃ pratītaḥ | tato jananābhāve vipakṣe niyataviṣayatvasya vyāpakasya nivṛttau nivartamānaṃ jananavyavahāragocaratvaṃ janana eva viśrāmyatīti vyāptisiddher anavadyo hetuḥ |
children.translated_text: restriction is well-established. Therefore, when production is absent — in the counter-positive — the pervader, namely having a restricted object, ceases; and the fitness for the conventional designation of producing, ceasing along with it, comes to rest in production alone — thus the pervasion is established, and the reason is faultless.

And if fitness for the conventional designation of producing were possible even without [actual] production, then everyone would have the conventional designation of producing everything everywhere — there would be no restriction. But this

children.text: na caiṣa ghaṭo varttamānakāryakaraṇakṣaṇe sakalakriyātikramakāle  cātītānāgatakṣaṇabhāvikāryaṃ janayati | tato na jananavyavahārayogyaḥ, sarvaḥ prasaṅgaḥ prasaṅgaviparyayaniṣṭha iti nyāyāt |
children.translated_text: And this pot, at the time of producing the present effect and at the time of the transcending of all activities, does not produce the effect belonging to past and future moments. Therefore, it is not fit for the conventional designation of producing [those effects] — because every <s>prasaṅga</s> concludes in the converse of the <s>prasaṅga</s>.

children.text: atrāpi prayogaḥ | yad yadā yan na karoti na tat tadā tatra samarthavyavahārayogyam | yathā śālyaṅkuram akurvan kodravaḥ śālyaṅkure | na karoti caiṣa ghaṭo vartamānakṣaṇabhāvikāryakaraṇakāle sakalakriyātikramakāle cātītānāgatakṣaṇabhāvikāryam iti vyāpakānupalabdhir bhinatti samarthakṣaṇād asamarthakṣaṇam |
children.translated_text: Here too is a formal argument: Whatever does not produce something at some time is not fit for the conventional designation of being competent with respect to that at that time — just as <s>kodrava</s> (a type of grain) with respect to a rice-shoot, when it does not produce a rice-shoot. And this pot, at the time of producing the present moment's effect and at the time of the transcending of all activities, does not produce the effect belonging to past and future moments — this is a non-apprehension of the pervader (<s>vyāpakānupalabdhi</s>) that separates the moment of incapacity from the moment of capacity.

children.text: atrāpy asiddhir nāsti, vartamānakṣaṇabhāvikāryakaraṇakāle sakalakriyātikramakāle cātītānāgatakṣaṇabhāvikāryakaraṇasyāyogāt |
children.translated_text: Here too there is no unestablishment, because the production of the effect belonging to past and future moments is impossible at the time of producing the present moment's effect and at the time of the transcending of all activities.

children.text: nāpi virodhaḥ, sapakṣe bhāvāt |
children.translated_text: Nor is there contradiction, because [the reason] is present in the positive example.

children.text: na cānaikāntikatā, pūrvoktena nyāyena samarthavyavahāragocaratvajanakatvayor vidhibhūtayoḥ sarvopasaṃhāravatyā vyāpteḥ prasādhanāt ||
children.translated_text: Nor is there inconclusiveness, because the pervasion of the two positive properties — fitness for the conventional designation of being competent and the property of being productive — with complete inductive scope, is established by the reasoning stated above.

children.text: yat punar atro
ktam, yad yadā yan na
children.translated_text: here — 'Whatever does not

children.text: karoti na tat tadā tatra
children.translated_text: produce something at some time is not

children.text: samartham ity atra kaḥ karotyarthaḥ | kiṃ kāraṇatvam | uta  kāryotpādānuguṇasahakārisākalyam | ahosvit kāryāvyabhicāraḥ | kāryasambandho veti | tatra kāraṇatvam eva karotyarthaḥ | tataḥ pakṣāntarabhāvino doṣā anabhyupagamapratihatāḥ |
children.translated_text: competent with respect to that at that time' — what is the meaning of 'produces' here? Is it causality (<s>kāraṇatva</s>)? Or the completeness of auxiliary conditions conducive to the production of the effect? Or the invariable relation with the effect? Or the connection with the effect? [Reply:] Of these, 'produces' means precisely causality. Therefore, the defects belonging to the other alternatives are repelled by non-acceptance.
As for what was further stated

children.text: na cātra pakṣe kāraṇatvasāmarthyayoḥ paryāyatvena

vyāpakānupalambhasya sādhyāviśiṣṭatvam abhidhātum ucitam, samarthavyavahāragocaratvābhāvasya sādhyatvāt | kāraṇatvasamarthavyavahāragocaratvayoś ca vṛkṣaśiṃśapayor iva vyāvṛttibhedo 'stīty anavasara evaivaṃvidhasya kṣudrapralāpasya |
children.translated_text: because the absence of fitness for the conventional designation of being competent is [itself] the thesis. And between causality and fitness for the conventional designation of being competent, there is a difference of exclusion-scope, like between 'tree' and 'śiṃśapā' (a kind of tree) — so there is simply no occasion for such petty prattle.
Nor is it appropriate to state here that the non-apprehension of the pervader is indistinguishable from the thesis, on the grounds that causality and competence are synonyms in this thesis —

children.text: tad evaṃ prasaṅgaprasaṅgaviparyayahetudvayabalato ghaṭe dṛṣṭānte kṣaṇabhaṅgaḥ siddhaḥ | tat kathaṃ sattvād anyad  anumānam dṛṣṭānte kṣaṇabhaṅgasādhakaṃ  nāstīty ucyate |
na caivaṃ sattvahetor vaiyarthyam, dṛṣṭāntamātra eva prasaṅgaprasaṅgaviparyayābhyāṃ kṣaṇabhaṅgaprasādhanāt ||
children.translated_text: Nor is the reason of existence thereby rendered purposeless, because the <s>prasaṅga</s> and <s>prasaṅgaviparyaya</s> establish momentariness only in the example.

Thus, through the force of the two reasons — <s>prasaṅga</s> and <s>prasaṅgaviparyaya</s> — momentariness is established in the pot, which serves as the example. How then can it be said that no inference other than [the inference] from existence establishes momentariness in the example?

children.text: nanv ābhyām eva pakṣe 'pi kṣaṇabhaṅgasiddhir astv iti cet |
children.translated_text: [Objection:] But let momentariness be established in the thesis too by these very two [arguments]!

children.text: astu, ko doṣaḥ | yo hi pratipattā prativastu yad yadā yajjananavyavahārayogyaṃ tat tadā taj janayatītyādikam upanyasitum analasas tasya tata eva kṣaṇabhaṅgasiddhiḥ | yas tu prativastu tannyāyopanyāsaprayāsabhīruḥ sa khalv  ekatra dharmiṇi yad yadā yajjananavyavahārayogyaṃ tat tadā taj janayatītyādinyāyena sattvamātram asthairyavyāptam avadhārya sattvād evānyatra kṣaṇikatvam avagacchayatīti, katham apramatto vaiyarthyam asyācakṣīta |
children.translated_text: Let it be so — what is the fault? For one who is not too lazy to present the reasoning individually for each entity that 'whatever is capable of producing whatever at whatever time, that produces that at that time,' for him the proof of momentariness (<s>kṣaṇabhaṅgasiddhi</s>) follows from that very reasoning. But one who is afraid of the effort of presenting that reasoning for each individual entity, having ascertained through the reasoning 'whatever is capable of producing whatever at whatever time, that produces that at that time' that mere <s>sattva</s> (being) is pervaded by impermanence with respect to a single <s>dharmin</s> (property-bearer), understands momentariness (<s>kṣaṇikatva</s>) in other cases from <s>sattva</s> alone — so how could an attentive person declare this to be futile?

children.text: tad evam ekakāryakāriṇo  ghaṭasya dvitīyādikṣaṇabhāvikāryāpekṣayā samarthetarasvabhāvaviruddhadharmādhyāsād bheda eveti kṣaṇabhaṅgitayā  sapakṣatām āvahati ghaṭe sattvahetur upalabhyamāno na viruddhaḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus, in the case of a pot that produces a single effect, through the superimposition of contradictory properties — namely having the nature of being capable and incapable — with respect to effects belonging to the second and subsequent moments, there is indeed difference, and so it brings about the status of being a similar instance (<s>sapakṣa</s>) through momentariness. The <s>sattva</s> reason observed in the pot is therefore not contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>).

children.text: na cāyam anaikāntikaḥ, atraiva sādharmyavati dṛṣṭānte sarvopasaṃhāravatyā vyāpteḥ prasādhanāt |
children.translated_text: Nor is this inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>), since the <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) — which encompasses all instances — is established in this very similar example (<s>sādharmya-dṛṣṭānta</s>).

children.text: nanu viparyayabādhakapramāṇabalād vyāptisiddhiḥ | tasya copanyāsavārtāpi nāsti | tat kathaṃ vyāptiḥ prasādhiteti cet |
children.translated_text: Objection: The establishment of <s>vyāpti</s> is through the force of a counter-proof refuting cognition (<s>viparyayabādhaka-pramāṇa</s>). And there is not even any mention of presenting that. So how is <s>vyāpti</s> established?

children.text: tad etat taralabuddhivilasitam | tathā hi uktam etad vartamānakṣaṇabhāvikāryakaraṇakāle 'tītānāgatakṣaṇabhāvikārye 'pi ghaṭasya śaktisambhave tadānīm eva tatkaraṇam, akaraṇe ca śaktāśaktasvabhāvatayā pratikṣaṇaṃ bheda iti kṣaṇikatvena vyāptaiva sā arthakriyāśaktiḥ ||
children.translated_text: This is the play of a fickle intellect. For it has been stated: at the time when the pot performs the effect belonging to the present moment, if it also has the capacity for effects belonging to past and future moments, then it should perform those at that very time; and if it does not perform them, then there is difference at every moment due to its having the nature of being capable and incapable — thus that capacity for causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyāśakti</s>) is indeed pervaded by momentariness (<s>kṣaṇikatva</s>).

children.text: nanv evam anvayamātram astu | vipakṣāt punar ekāntena vyāvṛttir iti kuto labhyata  iti cet |
children.translated_text: Objection: Let there be mere positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) in this way. But how is the definite exclusion from dissimilar instances (<s>vipakṣa</s>) obtained?

children.text: vyāptisiddher eva |
children.translated_text: From the very establishment of <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion).

children.text: vyatirekasandehe vyāptisiddhir eva katham iti cet |
children.translated_text: If one asks: how is <s>vyāpti</s> established when there is doubt about negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>)?

children.text: na | dvividhā hi vyāptisiddhiḥ | anvayarūpā ca kartṛdharmaḥ sādhanadharmavati dharmiṇi sādhyadharmasyāvaśyambhāvo yaḥ, vyatirekarūpā ca karmadharmaḥ sādhyābhāve sādhanasyāvaśyamabhāvo  yaḥ | enayoś caikatarapratītir niyamena  dvītyapratītim ākṣipati, anyathaikasyā evāsiddheḥ |
children.translated_text: No. For the establishment of <s>vyāpti</s> is twofold: the positive form (<s>anvayarūpā</s>), which is a property of the agent — the necessary presence of the <s>sādhya</s> property in the <s>dharmin</s> possessing the <s>sādhana</s> property; and the negative form (<s>vyatirekarūpā</s>), which is a property of the object — the necessary absence of the <s>sādhana</s> in the absence of the <s>sādhya</s>. The cognition of either one of these necessarily entails the cognition of the other, since otherwise even the one would remain unestablished.

children.text: tasmād yathā viparyaye bādhakapramāṇabalāt niyamavati vyatireke siddhe 'nvayaviṣayaḥ saṃśayaḥ pūrvaṃ sthito 'pi paścāt parigalati tato 'nvayaprasādhārthaṃ na pṛthak sādhanam ucyate tathā prasaṅgatadviparyayahetudvayabalato niyamavaty anvaye siddhe vyatirekaviṣaye  pūrvaṃ sthito 'pi sandehaḥ paścāt parigalaty eva |
children.translated_text: Therefore, just as when negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>) involving invariable relation is established through the force of a counter-proof refuting cognition, the doubt previously existing regarding the domain of positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) subsequently dissolves — and hence no separate proof is stated for establishing <s>anvaya</s> — so too, when positive concomitance involving invariable relation is established through the force of the pair of reasons consisting of <s>prasaṅga</s> (reductio) and its reversal (<s>tadviparyaya</s>), the doubt previously existing regarding the domain of negative concomitance subsequently dissolves as well.

children.text: na ca vyatirekaprasādhakam  anyat pramāṇaṃ vaktavyam | tataś ca sādhyābhāve sādhanasyaikāntiko vyatirekaḥ, sādhane sati sādhyasyāvaśyam anvayo veti na kaścid arthabhedaḥ |
tad evaṃ viparyayabādhakapramāṇam antareṇāpi prasaṅgaprasaṅgaviparyayahetudvayabalād anvayarūpavyāptisiddhau sattvahetor anaikāntikatvasyābhāvād  ataḥ sādhanāt kṣaṇabhaṅgasiddhir anavadyeti ||
children.translated_text: Thus, even without a counter-proof refuting cognition (<s>viparyayabādhaka-pramāṇa</s>), since through the force of the pair of reasons — <s>prasaṅga</s> and the reversal of <s>prasaṅga</s> — the <s>vyāpti</s> in positive form is established, and since there is no inconclusiveness (<s>anaikāntikatva</s>) of the <s>sattva</s> reason, the proof of momentariness (<s>kṣaṇabhaṅga</s>) from this reason is faultless.

And no other <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of knowledge) need be stated to establish negative concomitance. Thus, whether one says 'there is definite negative concomitance of the <s>sādhana</s> in the absence of the <s>sādhya</s>' or 'there is necessarily positive concomitance of the <s>sādhya</s> when the <s>sādhana</s> is present' — there is no difference in meaning.

children.text:
nanu ca sādhanam idam asiddham |
	  na hi kāraṇabuddhyā kāryaṃ gṛhyate, tasya bhāvitvāt | na ca
	  kāryabuddhyā

kāraṇam, tasyātītatvāt | na ca
	  vartamānagrāhiṇā jñānenātītānāgatayor grahaṇaṃ atiprasaṅgāt |
children.translated_text: since the cause is past. Nor can a cognition that apprehends only the present grasp the past and future, for that would lead to overextension (<s>atiprasaṅga</s>).

Objection: This proof is unestablished (<s>asiddha</s>). For an effect is not apprehended through the cognition of its cause, since the effect is future. Nor is the cause [apprehended] through the cognition of the effect,

children.text:
na ca pūrvāparayoḥ kālayor ekaḥ
	  pratisandhātā asti, kṣaṇabhaṅgabhaṅgaprasaṅgāt | kāraṇābhāve tu
	  kāryābhāvapratītiḥ svasaṃvedanavādino manorathasyāpy aviṣayaḥ |
children.translated_text: Nor is there a single unifying cognizer (<s>pratisandhātṛ</s>) of the earlier and later moments, for that would lead to the collapse of momentariness (<s>kṣaṇabhaṅga</s>) itself. And the cognition of the absence of the effect in the absence of the cause is beyond the reach even of the wishful thinking of one who advocates self-awareness (<s>svasaṃvedana</s>).

children.text:
nanu ca pūrvottarakālayoḥ
	  saṃvittī, tābhyāṃ vāsanā, tayā ca
hetu
children.translated_text: a <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual construction) that determines the cause-

children.text:
phalāvasāyī vikalpa iti cet tad
	  ayuktam | sa hi vikalpo gṛhītā
children.translated_text: effect relation. Reply: That is not correct. For that <s>vikalpa</s> either connects what has been apprehended,

children.text:
nusandhāyako
	  'tadrūpasamāropako vā |
children.translated_text: or superimposes what is not of that nature [upon something].
Objection: There are cognitions (<s>saṃvitti</s>) of the earlier and later moments; from those two arises a latent impression (<s>vāsanā</s>); and from that,

children.text:
na prathamaḥ pakṣaḥ | ekasya pratisandhātur
	  abhāve pūrvāparagrahaṇayor ayogāt, vikalpavāsanāyā evābhāvāt |
children.translated_text: The first alternative does not hold. In the absence of a single unifying cognizer (<s>pratisandhātṛ</s>), the apprehension of earlier and later [moments] is impossible, and the <s>vāsanā</s> (latent impression) for the <s>vikalpa</s> itself would be absent.

children.text: nāpi dvitīyaḥ | marīcikāyām api jalavijñānasya  prāmāṇyaprasaṅgāt |
children.translated_text: Nor does the second alternative hold, for it would entail that the water-cognition in a mirage would also be valid (<s>prāmāṇya</s>).

children.text:
tad evam anvayavyatirekayor apratipatter
	  arthakriyālakṣaṇaṃ sattvam asiddham iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus, since positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvaya</s> and <s>vyatireka</s>) are not cognized, <s>sattva</s> (being) defined as causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyā</s>) is unestablished (<s>asiddha</s>).

children.text: kiṃ ca prakārāntarād apīdaṃ sādhanam a

siddham |
	  tathā hi bījādīnāṃ sāmarthyaṃ bījādijñānāt tatkāryād aṅkurāder vā
	  niścetavyam |
children.translated_text: For the capacity (<s>sāmarthya</s>) of seeds and the like must be ascertained either from cognition of the seeds and so forth, or from their effect, namely the sprout and so on.
Moreover, this proof is unestablished (<s>asiddha</s>) for yet another reason.

children.text:
kāryatvaṃ ca vastutvasiddhau sidhyati |
	  vastutvaṃ ca kāryāntarāt | kāryāntarasyāpi kāryatvaṃ vastutvasiddhau |
	  tadvastutvaṃ ca tadaparakāryāntarād ity anavasthā |
children.translated_text: And effecthood (<s>kāryatva</s>) is established only when real existence (<s>vastutva</s>) is established. And real existence is [established] from another effect. And the effecthood of that other effect too [is established] only when its real existence is established. And its real existence from yet another further effect — thus an infinite regress (<s>anavasthā</s>) ensues.

children.text:
athānavasthābhayāt paryante
	  kāryāntaraṃ nāpekṣate tadā tenaiva pūrveṣām asattvaprasaṅgān
	  naikasyāpy arthakri
yāsāmarthyaṃ sidhyati |
children.translated_text: <s>sāmarthya</s>) of not even a single thing would be established.

If, fearing the infinite regress, at the endpoint one does not require another effect, then by that very [reasoning] the non-being (<s>asattva</s>) of the preceding [entities] would follow, and the capacity for causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyā-

children.text:
nanu kāryatvasattvayor
	  bhinnavyāvṛttikatvāt
sattvāsiddhāv
children.translated_text: even when <s>sattva</s> is unestablished,

children.text: api kāryatvasiddhau kā kṣatir iti cet |
children.translated_text: what harm is there if effecthood is established?
Objection: Since effecthood (<s>kāryatva</s>) and being (<s>sattva</s>) have different exclusion domains (<s>vyāvṛtti</s>),

children.text:
tad asaṅgatam | saty api kāryatvasattvayor
	  vyāvṛttibhede
sattvāsiddhāu
children.translated_text: when <s>sattva</s> is unestablished,

children.text:
kutaḥ kāryatvasiddhiḥ |
	  kāryatvaṃ hy abhūtvābhāvitvaṃ | bhavanaṃ ca sattā | sattā ca
	  saugatānāṃ sāmarthyam eva | tataś ca sāmarthyasandehe bhavatīty eva
	  vaktum aśakyam | ka
children.translated_text: how is effecthood (<s>kāryatva</s>) established? For effecthood means 'the state of having come into being after not having existed.' And coming into being is existence (<s>sattā</s>). And existence, for the Buddhists (<s>Saugata</s>s), is nothing but capacity (<s>sāmarthya</s>). Therefore, when <s>sāmarthya</s> is in doubt, it is impossible even to say 'it comes into being.' How then will effecthood — the state of having come into being after not having existed — be established?

children.text: tham abhūtvābhāvitvaṃ kāryatvaṃ setsyati |
children.translated_text: How will effecthood (<s>kāryatva</s>) — the state of having come into being after not having existed — be established?
That is incoherent. Even granted that effecthood (<s>kāryatva</s>) and being (<s>sattva</s>) differ in their exclusion domains,

children.text:
apekṣitaparavyāpāratvaṃ kāryatvam ity api
	  nāsato dharmaḥ | sattvaṃ ca sāmarthyam | tac ca sandigdham iti kutaḥ
	  kāryatvasiddhiḥ | tadasiddhau pūrvasya sāmarthyaṃ na sidhyatīti
	  sandigdhāsiddho hetuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Nor can effecthood defined as 'requiring the operation of another' be a property of a non-existent. And being (<s>sattva</s>) is capacity (<s>sāmarthya</s>). And that is doubtful — so how is effecthood established? When that is not established, the capacity of the preceding [entity] is not established either — thus the reason suffers from doubtful unestablishment (<s>sandigdhāsiddha</s>).

children.text:
tathā viruddho 'py ayam | tathā hi
	  kṣaṇikatve sati na tāvad ajātasyānanvayaniruddhasya vā
	  kāryārambhakatvaṃ sambhavati |

na ca niṣpannasya tāvān kṣaṇo 'sti yam
	  upādāya kasmaicit kāryāya vyāpāryeta | ataḥ kṣaṇikapakṣa
	  evārthakriyānupapatter viruddhatā |
children.translated_text: Nor does a fully produced [entity] have even that much duration by virtue of which it could operate toward some effect. Therefore, since causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyā</s>) is impossible precisely on the thesis of momentariness, there is contradictoriness (<s>viruddhatā</s>).

Likewise, this [reason] is also contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>). For if momentariness (<s>kṣaṇikatva</s>) holds, then an entity that has not yet arisen, or one that has ceased without any continuity, cannot possibly be the initiator of an effect.

children.text:
athavā vikalpena yad upanīyate tat sarvam
	  avastu | tataś ca vastvātmake kṣaṇikatve sādhye 'vastūpasthāpayann
	  anumānavikalpo viruddhaḥ |
children.translated_text: Alternatively, whatever is presented through conceptual construction (<s>vikalpa</s>) is entirely unreal (<s>avastu</s>). Therefore, when momentariness — which is of the nature of a real entity (<s>vastu</s>) — is what is to be proved, the inferential <s>vikalpa</s>, which presents something unreal, is contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>).

children.text:
yadvā sarvasyaiva hetoḥ kṣaṇikatve sādhye
	  viruddhatvaṃ | deśakālāntarānanugame sādhyasādhanabhāvābhāvāt |
	  anugame ca nānākālam ekam akṣaṇikaṃ kṣaṇikatvena virudhyata iti ||
children.translated_text: Or again, every reason whatsoever is contradictory when momentariness is what is to be proved. For if there is no persistence across different places and times, the relation of <s>sādhya</s> and <s>sādhana</s> would be absent; and if there is persistence, then a single thing existing at different times, being non-momentary, would be contradicted by momentariness.

children.text: anaikāntiko 'py ayam, sattvasthairyayor virodhābhāvād  iti |
children.translated_text: This [reason] is also inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>), since there is no contradiction between being (<s>sattva</s>) and permanence (<s>sthairya</s>).

children.text:
atrocyate | yat tāvad uktaṃ sāmarthyaṃ na
	  pratīyata iti, tat kiṃ sarvathaiva na pratīyate kṣaṇabhaṅgapakṣe
	  vā |
children.translated_text: To this we reply: As for the statement that capacity (<s>sāmarthya</s>) is not cognized — does it mean it is not cognized at all under any circumstances, or [merely] not cognized on the thesis of momentariness?

children.text:
prathamapakṣe
	  sakalakārakajñāpakahetucakrocchedān mukhaspandanamātrasyāpy
	  akaraṇaprasaṅgaḥ | anyathā yenaiva vacanena sāmarthyaṃ nāstīti
	  pratipādyate tasyaiva tatpratipādanasāmarthyam avyāhatam āyātam |
	  tasmāt paramapuruṣārthasamīhayā vastutattvanirūpaṇapravṛttasya
	  śaktisvīkārapūrvakaiva pravṛttiḥ | tadasvīkāre tu na kaścit kvacit
	  pravarteteti nirīhaṃ jagaj jāyeta |
children.translated_text: On the first alternative, since the entire complex of factors and indicating reasons would be destroyed, there would follow the impossibility of even the mere movement of the mouth. Otherwise, the very sentence by which it is claimed 'there is no <s>sāmarthya</s>' would itself possess unimpaired capacity to convey that very meaning. Therefore, for one who has undertaken the investigation of the true nature of reality with the aspiration for the highest human goal, the undertaking itself presupposes the acceptance of capacity (<s>śakti</s>). If that is not accepted, no one would undertake anything anywhere, and the world would become devoid of activity.

children.text:
atha dvitīyaḥ pakṣaḥ, tadāsti tāvat
	  sāmarthyapratītiḥ | sā ca kṣaṇikatve yadi nopapadyate tadā viruddhaṃ
	  vaktum ucitam | asiddham iti tu nyāyabhūṣaṇīyaḥ prāyo vilāpaḥ |
children.translated_text: If the second alternative [is chosen], then there does exist a cognition of capacity (<s>sāmarthya</s>). And if that is not tenable under momentariness, then it would be proper to call [the reason] contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>). But to call it unestablished (<s>asiddha</s>) is mostly a lament worthy of the <s>Nyāyabhūṣaṇa</s>.

children.text:
na ca saty api kṣaṇikatve
	  sāmarthyapratītivyāghātaḥ | tathā hi kāraṇagrāhijñānopādeyabhūtena
	  kāryagrāhiṇā jñānena tadarpitasaṃskāragarbheṇa asya bhāve asya bhāva
	  ity anvayaniścayo janyate | tathā kāraṇāpekṣayā
	  bhūtalakaivalyagrāhijñānopādeyabhūtena kāryāpekṣayā
	  bhūtalakaivalyagrāhiṇā jñānena tadarpitasaṃskāragarbheṇa asyābhāve
	  asyābhāva iti vyatirekaniścayo janyate |
children.translated_text: Nor is there any conflict with the cognition of capacity even when momentariness holds. For the ascertainment of positive concomitance — 'when this exists, that exists' — is produced by a cognition apprehending the effect, which is the successor to the cognition apprehending the cause, and which contains within it the latent impression (<s>saṃskāra</s>) deposited by the latter. Similarly, the ascertainment of negative concomitance — 'when this is absent, that is absent' — is produced by a cognition apprehending the bare ground in the absence of the cause, which is the successor to a cognition apprehending the bare ground in the absence of the effect, and which contains within it the latent impression deposited by the latter.

children.text: yad āhur guravaḥ
children.translated_text: As the masters have said:

children.text: ekāvasāyasamanantarajātam anyavijñānam anvayavimarśam upādadhāti |
children.translated_text: "A cognition of one thing, arising immediately after a determination [of another], produces the reflection of positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>)."

children.text: evaṃ tadekavirahānubhavodbhavānyavyāvṛttidhīḥ prathayati vyatirekabuddhim ||
children.translated_text: "Likewise, a cognition of the exclusion of the other, arising from the experience of the absence of that one, gives rise to the understanding of negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>)."

children.text:
evaṃ sati gṛhītānusandhāyaka evāyaṃ
	  vikalpaḥ |
	  upādānopādeyabhūtakramipratyakṣadvayagṛhītānusandhānāt |
children.translated_text: This being so, this <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual construction) is indeed one that connects what has been apprehended — because it connects what has been apprehended by the two successive perceptions that stand in the relation of predecessor and successor.

children.text: yad āhālaṅkāraḥ
children.translated_text: As <s>Alaṅkāra</s> [i.e., <s>Prajñākaragupta</s>] has said:

children.text: yadi nāmaikam adhyakṣaṃ na pūrvāparavittimat |
children.translated_text: "Even if a single perception does not cognize the earlier and later,"

children.text: adhyakṣadvayasadbhāve prākparāvedanaṃ katham ||
(PVA)

children.translated_text: "When there are two perceptions, how could there fail to be awareness of the earlier and the later?"

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text:
nāpi dvitīyo 'siddhaprabhedaḥ | sāmarthyaṃ
	  hi sattvam iti saugatānāṃ sthitir eṣā | na caitatprasādhanārtham
	  asmākam idānīm eva prārambhaḥ | kiṃ tu yatra pramāṇapratīte bījādau
	  vastubhūte dharmiṇi pramāṇapratītaṃ sāmarthyaṃ tatra
	  kṣaṇabhaṅgaprasādhanāya |

tataś
	  cāṅkurādīnāṃ kāryādarśanād āhatya sāmarthyasandehe 'pi
	  paṭupratyakṣaprasiddham sanmātratvam avadhāryam eva | anyathā na
	  kvacid api vastumātrasyāpi pratipattiḥ syāt |
children.translated_text: Therefore, even when there is doubt about capacity on the whole due to not observing effects such as sprouts and the like, the mere existence [of the entity], which is well-established through acute perception (<s>paṭu-pratyakṣa</s>), must be ascertained. Otherwise, there would be no cognition of even the mere entity anywhere at all.

children.text: tasmā
children.translated_text: Therefore,

children.text:
c chāstrīyasattvalakṣaṇasandehe 'pi
	  paṭupratyakṣabalāvalambitavastubhāve 'ṅkurādau kāryatvam
	  upalabhyamānaṃ bījādeḥ sāmarthyam upasthāpayatīti
	  nāsiddhidoṣāvakāśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: even when there is doubt about the technical definition of <s>sattva</s> (being) in the treatises, effecthood (<s>kāryatva</s>) — which is observed — in the case of a sprout and so forth, whose real existence is grounded in the force of acute perception, establishes the capacity (<s>sāmarthya</s>) of the seed and so on. Hence there is no scope for the fault of unestablishment (<s>asiddhi</s>).

Nor does the second sub-type of unestablishment (<s>asiddha</s>) [apply]. For the position of the Buddhists (<s>Saugata</s>s) is that <s>sattva</s> (being) is capacity (<s>sāmarthya</s>). And our present undertaking is not for the purpose of establishing that. Rather, [the aim is]: where capacity (<s>sāmarthya</s>) is cognized by a <s>pramāṇa</s> in a <s>dharmin</s> that is a real entity — such as a seed and so on — there, to establish momentariness.

children.text:
nāpi kṣaṇikatve sāmarthyakṣatiḥ,
	  yato viruddhatā syāt, kṣaṇikatvaniyataprāgbhāvitvalakṣaṇakāraṇatvayor
	  virodhābhāvāt, kṣaṇamātrasthāyiny api sāmarthyasambhavād iti nādimo
	  virodhaḥ |

nāpi dvitīyo
	  viro
children.translated_text: Nor [does] the second sub-type of contra-

children.text:
dhaprabhedaḥ | avastuno vastuno vā svākārasya grāhyatve 'pi
	  adhyavaseyavastvapekṣayaiva sarvatra prāmāṇyapratipādanāt
	  vastusvabhāvasyaiva kṣaṇikatvasya siddhir iti kva virodhaḥ |
children.translated_text: diction [hold]. For even if what is apprehended is the <s>vikalpa</s>'s own form — whether unreal or real — since validity (<s>prāmāṇya</s>) is everywhere established only with reference to the real object that is determined (<s>adhyavaseya-vastu</s>), it is momentariness — which is of the nature of a real entity — that is established. So where is the contradiction?

Nor is capacity (<s>sāmarthya</s>) impaired under momentariness — which would give rise to contradictoriness (<s>viruddhatā</s>) — since there is no contradiction between causality defined as prior non-existence necessitated by momentariness and [causal efficacy], and since capacity is possible even in something that endures for only a single moment. Thus the first [type of] contradiction does not hold.

children.text:
yac ca gṛhyate yac cādhyavasīyate te dve 'py
	  anyanivṛttī na vastunī svalakṣaṇāvagāhitve 'bhilāpasaṃsargānupapatter
	  iti cet |
Cf.
na | adhyavasāyasvarūpāparijñānāt | agṛhī
children.translated_text: No. Because the nature of determination (<s>adhyavasāya</s>) has not been properly understood. Even when the real entity

children.text:
te
	  'pi vastuni
children.translated_text: is not [directly] apprehended,

children.text: mānasādi
children.translated_text: the capacity of <s>vikalpa</s> to cause activity directed toward mental and other

children.text: mānasyādi
children.translated_text: mental and other

children.text:
pravṛttikārakatvaṃ
	  vikalpasyādhyavasāyitvam | apratibhāse 'pi pravṛttiviṣayīkṛtatvam
	  adhyavaseyatvam | etac cādhyavaseyatvaṃ svalakṣaṇasyaiva yujyate,
	  nānyasya, arthakriyārthitvād arthipravṛtteḥ |
children.translated_text: actions is its nature as determination (<s>adhyavasāyitva</s>). Being made the object of activity even without appearing [in the <s>vikalpa</s>] is what it means to be the object of determination (<s>adhyavaseyatva</s>). And this status of being the object of determination belongs only to the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular), not to anything else, since the activity of a purposive agent is directed toward causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyā</s>).

children.text:
evaṃ cādhyavasāye svalakṣaṇasyāsphuraṇam
	  eva | na ca tasyāsphuraṇe 'pi sarvatrāviśeṣeṇa
	  pravṛttyākṣepaprasaṅgaḥ, pratini
children.translated_text: Thus, in determination (<s>adhyavasāya</s>), the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular) indeed does not manifest. Yet even though it does not manifest, there is no unwanted consequence that activity would be prompted indiscriminately toward everything, because for each

children.text:
yatasāmagrīprasūtāt
	  pratiniyatasvākārāt pratiniyataśaktiyogāt, pratiniyata
	  evātadrūpaparāvṛtte 'pratīte 'pi pravṛttisāmarthyadarśanāt | yathā
	  sarvasyāsattve 'pi bījād aṅkurasyaivotpattiḥ, dṛṣṭasya
	  niyatahetuphalabhāvasya pratikṣeptum aśakyatvāt | paraṃ bāhyenārthena
	  sati pratibandhe prāmāṇyam | anyathā tv aprāmāṇyam iti viśeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because [the cognition], produced from a specific causal complex, has a specifically delimited own-form and a specifically delimited capacity-connection, even without the cognition of what is excluded from non-that-form, the capacity for activity is observed to be specifically determined. Just as, even in the non-existence of everything [else], only a sprout is produced from a seed — because the observed determinate cause-effect relation cannot be overturned. The only difference is: when there is a necessary connection with an external object, [the cognition] is valid; otherwise, it is invalid.

Objection: Both what is apprehended and what is determined are merely exclusions from others (<s>anyāpoha</s>), not real entities, since if [<s>vikalpa</s>] apprehended the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular), the connection with verbal expression would be impossible.

children.text:
tathā tṛtīyo 'pi pakṣaḥ
	  prayāsaphalaḥ | nānākālasyaikasya vastuno vastuto 'sambhave 'pi
	  sarvadeśakālavartinor atadrūpaparāvṛttayor eva sādhyasādhanayoḥ
	  pratyakṣeṇa vyāptigrahaṇāt |
dvividho hi pratyakṣasya viṣayaḥ, grāhyo 'dhyavaseyaś ca |
children.translated_text: For perception has a twofold object: the apprehended (<s>grāhya</s>) and the determined (<s>adhyaveseya</s>).

children.text: sakalātadrūpaparāvṛttaṃ vastumātraṃ
children.translated_text: The real entity in its entirety, excluded from all non-that-forms —

children.text:
sākṣād asphuraṇāt pratyakṣasya
	  grāhyo viṣayo mā
children.translated_text: since it does not directly flash forth, may not be the apprehended object of perception.

children.text:
bhūt | tadekadeśagrahaṇe tu tanmātrayor
	  vyāptiniścāyakavikalpajananād adhyavaseyo viṣayo bhavaty eva |
	  kṣaṇagrahaṇe santānaniścayavat, rūpamātragrahaṇe
	  rūparasagandhasparśātmakaghaṭaniścayavac ca | anyathā
	  sarvānumānocchedaprasaṅgāt ||
children.translated_text: But upon the grasping of a portion of it, since it generates a conceptual construction (<s>vikalpa</s>) that ascertains the invariable concomitance of those two [properties] alone, it does become the determined object. Just as from the grasping of a moment, the certainty of the continuum [arises]; and just as from the grasping of mere form, the certainty of the pot consisting of form, taste, smell, and touch [arises]. Otherwise, there would follow the absurd consequence of the destruction of all inference.

Likewise, the third alternative too is fruitful. For even though a single entity existing at different times is impossible in reality, the invariable concomitance of the provable and the means of proof — both of which are excluded from non-that-form and exist in all places and times — is grasped by perception.

children.text:
tathā hi vyāptigrahaḥ sāmānyayoḥ,
	  viśeṣayoḥ, sāmānyaviśiṣṭaviśeṣayoḥ viśeṣaviśiṣṭasāmānyayor veti
	  vikalpāḥ |
children.translated_text: For the grasping of the invariable concomitance [may be] between generals, between particulars, between a general qualified by a particular, or between a particular qualified by a general — these are the alternatives.

children.text:
nādyo vikalpaḥ, sāmānyasya bādhyatvāt |
	  abādhyatve 'py adṛśyatvāt | dṛśyatve 'pi puruṣārthānupayogitayā
	  tasyānumeyatvāyogāt | nāpy anumitāt sāmānyād viśeṣānumānam |
	  sāmānyasarvaviśeṣayor vakṣyamāṇanyāyena pratibandhapratipatter
	  ayogāt |
children.translated_text: The first alternative is not [tenable], because the general (<s>sāmānya</s>) is [ultimately] sublated. Even if unsublated, [it is not tenable] because it is imperceptible. Even if perceptible, because it is of no use for human purposes, it is unfit to be an object of inference. Nor can the particular be inferred from an inferred general, because the apprehension of the necessary connection between the general and all its particulars is impossible according to the principle to be explained.

children.text: nāpi dvitīyaḥ | viśeṣasyānanugāmitvāt |
children.translated_text: Nor the second, because the particular does not recur [identically across instances].

children.text:
antime tu vikalpadvaye sāmānyādhāratayā
	  dṛṣṭa eva viśeṣaḥ sāmānyasya viśeṣyo viśeṣaṇaṃ vā kartavyaḥ | adṛṣṭa
	  eva vā deśakālāntaravartī | yadvā dṛṣṭādṛṣṭātmako atadrūpaparāvṛttaḥ
	  sarvo viśeṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: In the last two alternatives, the particular — seen as the substratum of the general — must be made the qualifier or the qualificand of the general. Or else, it is precisely the unseen [particular] existing in another place and time. Or, all the particulars, excluded from non-that-form, consisting of both seen and unseen [instances].

children.text:
na prathamaḥ pakṣo 'nanugāmitvāt | nāpi
	  dvitīyaḥ, adṛṣṭatvāt | na ca tṛtīyaḥ, prastutaikaviśeṣadarśane 'pi
	  deśakālāntaravartināṃ viśeṣāṇām adarśanāt |
children.translated_text: The first sub-alternative is not [tenable] because [the seen particular] does not recur. Nor the second, because it is unseen. Nor the third, because even when one particular at hand is seen, the particulars existing in other places and times are not seen.

children.text: atha teṣāṃ sarveṣām eva viśeṣāṇāṃ sadṛśatvāt sadṛśasāmagrīprasūtatvāt sadṛśakāryakāritvād iti pratyāsattyā ekaviśeṣagrāhakaṃ pratyakṣam atadrūpaparāvṛttamātre niścayaṃ janayad atadrūpaparāvṛttaviśeṣamātrasya vyavasthāpakam |
yathaikasāmagrīpratibaddharūpamātragrāhakaṃ pratyakṣaṃ ghaṭe niścayaṃ janayad ghaṭagrāhakaṃ vyavasthāpyate | anyathā ghaṭo 'pi ghaṭasantāno 'pi pratyakṣato na sidhyet, sarvātmanā grahaṇābhāvāt |
children.translated_text: Just as perception that grasps mere form bound to a single causal complex, generating a certainty with respect to the pot, is determined to be a grasper of the pot. Otherwise, neither a pot nor a pot-continuum would be established through perception, because it is not grasped in its entirety.

children.text: tadekadeśagrahaṇaṃ tv atadrūpaparāvṛtte 'py aviśiṣṭam | yady evam anenaiva krameṇa sarvasya viśeṣasya viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvavad vyāptipratipattir apy astu |
children.translated_text: But the grasping of a portion of it is not different even with respect to [the entity] excluded from non-that-form. If so, then by this very method, let the apprehension of the invariable concomitance of every particular too be [established], just like the qualifier-qualificand relation.

children.text: tat kimarthaṃ nānākālam ekam akṣaṇikam abhyupagantavyam, yena kṣaṇikatvasādhanasya viruddhatvaṃ syād iti na kaścid virodhaprabhedaprasaṅgaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, why should one accept a single non-momentary [entity existing at] different times, by which the proof of momentariness would be contradicted? Thus there is no occasion for any type of the fault of contradiction.

But since all those particulars are similar, are produced from similar causal complexes, and produce similar effects — by this proximity, perception that grasps a single particular, generating a certainty with respect to mere exclusion from non-that-form, establishes the mere particular excluded from non-that-form.

children.text: na cāyam anaikāntiko 'pi hetuḥ, pūrvoktakrameṇa sādharmyadṛṣṭānte prasaṅgaviparyayahetubhyām anvayarūpavyāpteḥ prasādhanāt |

nanu yadi prasaṅgaviparyayahetudvayabalato ghaṭe dṛṣṭānte kṣaṇabhaṅgaḥ sidhyet tadā sattvasya niyamena kṣaṇikatvena vyāptisiddher anaikāntikatvaṃ na syād iti yuktam | kevalam idam evāsambhavi | tathā hi śakto 'pi ghaṭaḥ krami sahakāryapekṣayā kramikāryaṃ kariṣyati |
children.translated_text: If one objects: 'If momentary destruction (<s>kṣaṇabhaṅga</s>) in the pot used as an example were established by the force of the two reasons — <s>prasaṅga</s> and its converse — then it would be justified that there is no inconclusiveness, since the invariable concomitance of existence (<s>sattva</s>) with momentariness would necessarily be established. But precisely this is impossible. For a pot, even though capable, being sequential, will produce a sequential effect in dependence on an auxiliary cause (<s>sahakārin</s>).'

Nor is this reason inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>), because the invariable concomitance in the form of positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) is established in the positive example (<s>sādharmyadṛṣṭānta</s>) through the two [arguments of] <s>prasaṅga</s> (reductio) and its converse (<s>viparyaya</s>), by the method stated earlier.

children.text: na caitad vaktavyam, samartho 'rthaḥ svarūpeṇa karoti, svarūpaṃ ca sarvadāstīty anupakāriṇi sahakāriṇy apekṣā na yujyata iti | saty api svarūpeṇa kārakatve sāmarthyābhāvāt kathaṃ karotu | sahakārisākalyaṃ hi sāmarthyam, tadvaikalyaṃ cāsāmarthyam | na ca tayor āvirbhāvatirobhāvābhyāṃ tadvataḥ kācit kṣatiḥ, tasya tābhyām anyatvāt | tasmād arthaḥ samartho 'pi syāt, na ca karotīti sandigdhavyatirekaḥ prasaṅgahetuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Nor should one say: 'A capable entity acts by its own nature, and its own nature always exists; therefore, dependence on an auxiliary cause that contributes nothing is not justified.' For even though causality exists by virtue of the entity's own nature, how can it act when it lacks the capacity [at that moment]? For the capacity is precisely the totality of auxiliary causes, and the lack of capacity is their deficiency. And neither the manifestation nor the concealment of those [auxiliary causes] causes any damage to the possessor [of the capacity], since it is different from them. Therefore, [the objection runs:] an entity may be capable and yet not act — thus the <s>prasaṅga</s> (reductio) reason has a doubtful counter-concomitance.

children.text: atrocyate | bhavatu tāvat sahakārisākalyam eva sāmarthyam | tathāpi so 'pi tāvad bhāvaḥ svarūpeṇa kārakaḥ |
tasya ca yādṛśaś caramakṣaṇe 'kṣepakriyādharmā svabhāvas tādṛśa eva cet |
children.translated_text: And if the nature of that [entity] — characterized by the property of propelling activity — is exactly the same in the final moment as

children.text: prathamakṣaṇe tadā tadāpi prasahya kurvāṇo brahmaṇāpy anivāryaḥ | na ca so 'py akṣepakriyādharmā svabhāvaḥ sākalye sati jāto bhāvād bhinna evābhidhātuṃ śakyaḥ, bhāvasyākartṛtvaprasaṅgāt | evaṃ yāvad yāvad dharmāntaraparikalpas tāvat tāvad udāsīno bhāvaḥ |
children.translated_text: in the first moment, then even then, acting forcefully, it would be unstoppable even by <s>Brahmā</s>. And that nature characterized by the property of propelling activity, having arisen when the totality [of conditions] is present, cannot be described as different from the entity — because there would follow the absurd consequence that the entity has no causal efficacy. Thus, the more and more additional properties one postulates, the more and more the entity remains indifferent [to them].

children.text: tasmād yadrūpam ādāya svarūpeṇāpi janayatīty ucyate tasya prāg api bhāve katham ajaniḥ kadācit | akṣepakriyāpratyanīkasvabhāvasya vā prācyasya paścād anuvṛttau kathaṃ kadācid api kāryasambhavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, that form by virtue of which [the entity] is said to 'produce even by its own nature' — if that exists before as well, how did it ever fail to produce? Or if the prior nature — which is opposed to the property of propelling activity — continues afterward, how can the effect ever be possible?
To that we reply: Let it be that the capacity is precisely the totality of auxiliary causes. Even so, that entity too acts by its own nature.

children.text: nanu yadi sa evaikaḥ kartā syād yuktam etat | kiṃtu sāmagrī janikā | tataḥ sahakāryantaravirahavelāyāṃ balīyaso 'pi na kāryaprasava iti kim atra viruddham | na hi bhāvaḥ svarūpeṇa karotīti svarūpeṇaiva karoti , sahakārisahitād eva tataḥ kāryotpattidarśanāt | tasmād vyāptivat kāryakāraṇabhāvo 'py ekatrānyayogavyavacchedenānyatrāyogavyavacchedenāvaboddhavyaḥ, tathaiva laukikaparīkṣakāṇāṃ saṃpratipatter iti ||
children.translated_text: If one objects: 'If that single [entity] itself were the maker, this would be valid. But the causal complex (<s>sāmagrī</s>) is what produces. Therefore, even for a powerful [entity], there is no production of the effect during the interval when another auxiliary cause is absent — what is contradictory here? For the statement "the entity acts by its own nature" does not mean it acts by its own nature alone, since the effect is observed to arise only from [the entity] together with auxiliary causes. Therefore, just like invariable concomitance, the cause-effect relation too should be understood as: in one case, exclusion of association with anything else; in the other, exclusion of non-association — for that is how worldly and expert investigators understand it.'

children.text: atrocyate | yadā militāḥ santaḥ kāryaṃ kurvate tadaikārthakaraṇalakṣaṇaṃ sahakāritvam eṣām astu | ko niṣeddhā | militair eva tu tatkāryaṃ kartavyam iti kuto labhyate | pūrvāparayor ekasvabhāvatvād bhāvasya sarvadā jananājananayor anyataraniyama prasaṅgasya durvāratvāt | tasmāt sāmagrī janikā, naikaṃ janakam iti sthiravādināṃ manorathasyāpy aviṣayaḥ |
children.translated_text: To that we reply: When [the entities] are assembled and produce the effect, let their auxiliary-cause-hood be characterized as cooperation toward a single purpose — who denies this? But whence is it obtained that the effect must be produced only by them assembled? Because, since the entity has the same nature in the earlier and later times, the relentless <s>prasaṅga</s> (reductio) that it is always either producing or not producing [follows]. Therefore, the claim 'the causal complex produces, not a single [entity]' is not even within the scope of the imagination of those who hold the permanence view.

children.text: dṛśyate tāvad evam iti cet | dṛśyatām | kiṃ tu pūrvasthitād eva sāmagrīmadhyapraviṣṭād bhāvāt kāryotpattir anyasmād eva vā viśiṣṭād bhāvād utpannād iti vivādapadam | tatra prāg api sambhave sarvadaiva kāryotpattir na vā kadācid apīti virodham asamādhāya cakṣuṣī nimīlya tata eva kāryotpattidarśanād iti sādhyānuvādamātrapravṛttaḥ kṛpām arhatīti |
children.translated_text: If one says: 'But it is observed to be so!' — Let it be observed. But the point of dispute is: does the effect arise from the very entity that existed before and has entered the causal complex, or from an entirely different qualified entity that has [newly] arisen? In that regard, without resolving the contradiction that if [the entity] was possible even before, the effect should arise always or never — one who merely states 'the production of the effect from that [permanent entity] is observed,' [closing his eyes and] merely restating the thesis, deserves pity.

children.text: na ca pratyabhijñā balād ekatvasiddhiḥ | tatpauruṣasya lūnapunarjātakeśanakhādāv apy upalambhato nirdalanāt | lakṣaṇabhedasya ca darśayitum aśakyatvāt | sthirasiddhi dūṣaṇe cāsmābhiḥ prapañcato nirastatvāt |

tasmāt sākṣāt kāryakāraṇabhāvāpekṣayobhayatrāpy anyayogavyavacchedaḥ | vyāptau tu sākṣāt paramparayā kāraṇamātrāpekṣayā kāraṇe vyāpake 'yogavyavacchedaḥ | kārye vyāpye 'nyayogavyavacchedaḥ | tathā tad atatsvabhāve vyāpake 'yogavyavacchedaḥ | tatsvabhāve ca vyāpye 'nyayogavyavacchedaḥ | vikalpārūḍharūpāpekṣayā vyāptau dvividham avadhāraṇam |
children.translated_text: Therefore, with respect to the direct cause-effect relation, in both [cause and effect] there is exclusion of non-association. But with respect to the invariable concomitance, considering the cause in general — directly or indirectly — in the cause as pervader there is exclusion of non-association, and in the effect as pervaded there is exclusion of association with anything else. Likewise, in the non-that-nature as pervader there is exclusion of non-association, and in the that-nature as pervaded there is exclusion of association with anything else. With respect to the form mounted upon conceptual construction (<s>vikalpa</s>), there are two modes of determination in the invariable concomitance.

Nor is unity established by the force of recognition (<s>pratyabhijñā</s>), because the human [activity of recognition] is demolished by its observation even in the case of hair and nails that are cut and regrown. And because the difference of defining characteristics cannot be shown [between moments]. And because [the argument from recognition] has been extensively refuted by us in the [section] refuting the proof of permanence.

children.text: nanu yadi pūrvāparakālayor ekasvabhāvo bhāvaḥ sarvadā janakatvenājanakatvena vā vyāpta upalabdhaḥ syāt, tadāyaṃ prasaṅgaḥ saṅgacchate | na ca kṣaṇabhaṅgavādinā pūrvāparakālayor ekaḥ kaścid upalabdha iti cet |

tad etad atigrāmyam | tathā hi pūrvāparakālayor ekasvabhāvatve satīty asyāyam arthaḥ, parakālabhāvī janako yaḥ svabhāvo bhāvasya sa eva yadi pūrvakālabhāvī, pūrvakālabhāvī vā yo 'janakaḥ svabhāvaḥ sa eva yadi parakālabhāvī, tadopalabdham eva jananam ajananaṃ vā syāt | tathā ca sati siddhayor eva svabhāvayor ekatvārope siddham eva jananam ajananaṃ vāsajyata iti |
children.translated_text: that is extremely naive. For the meaning of 'if having the same nature at earlier and later times' is this: if the nature of the entity that is a producer at the later time is the very same [as that which exists] at the earlier time, or if the non-producing nature at the earlier time is the very same at the later time — then production or non-production, which is already observed, would [simply] always obtain. And thus, when identity is superimposed upon two natures that are [already] established, the production or non-production that is [already] established is simply bound to [always hold].

If one objects: 'If the entity were observed to be pervaded by always being a producer or by always being a non-producer, due to having the same nature at earlier and later times, then this reductio would be coherent. But the proponent of momentariness does not observe a single [entity] at earlier and later times' —

children.text: nanu kāryam eva sahakāriṇam apekṣate , na tu kāryotpattihetuḥ | yasmād dvividhaṃ sāmarthyaṃ nijam āgantukaṃ ca sahakāryantaram | tato 'kṣaṇikasyāpi kramavatsahakārinānātvād api kramavatkāryanānātvopapatter aśakyaṃ bhāvānāṃ pratikṣaṇam anyatvam upapādayitum iti cet |

ucyate | bhavatu tāvan nijāgantukabhedena dvividhaṃ sāmarthyam | tathāpi tat prātisvikaṃ vastusvalakṣaṇam arthakriyādharmakam avaśyam abhyupagantavyam | tat kiṃ prāg api paścād eva veti vikalpya yad dūṣaṇam udīritaṃ tatra kim uktam aneneti na pratīmaḥ |
children.translated_text: we reply: Let the capacity be twofold — intrinsic and adventitious. Even so, that [capacity] must necessarily be accepted as the unique particular (<s>vastusvalakṣaṇa</s>), the individual real, characterized by causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyā</s>). Then, considering whether it existed before or only afterward — in the refutation that has been raised, what has this [objection] said that we cannot grasp?

children.text: yat tu kāryeṇaiva sahakāriṇo 'pekṣyanta ity upaskṛtaṃ tad api nirupayogam. yadi hi kāryam eva svajanmani svatantraṃ syād yuktam etat | kevalam evaṃ sati sahakārisākalyasāmarthyakalpanam aphalam | svātantryād eva hi kāryaṃ kādācitkaṃ bhaviṣyati | tathā ca sati santo hetavaḥ sarvathā 'samarthāḥ | asat tu kāryaṃ svatantram iti viśuddhā buddhiḥ |
children.translated_text: As for the revision that 'the auxiliary causes are required by the effect itself' — that too is useless. For if the effect itself were independent in its own production, this would be justified. But then, the postulation of the capacity as the totality of auxiliary causes would be fruitless — because the effect would be occasional by its own independence alone. And in that case, existing causes would be entirely incapable. But that an unreal effect is independent — this is pure insight indeed!

If one objects: 'It is the effect itself that depends on the auxiliary cause, not the cause of the effect's production. Because the capacity is twofold: intrinsic and adventitious (i.e., the other auxiliary cause). Therefore, even for a non-momentary [entity], since the multiplicity of effects in sequence is explicable by the multiplicity of sequential auxiliary causes, it is impossible to demonstrate that entities are different at each moment' —

children.text: atha kāryasyaivāyam aparādho yad idaṃ samarthe kāraṇe saty api kadācin nopapadyata iti cet | na tat tarhi tatkāryaṃ, svātantryāt |
yad bhāṣyam,
children.translated_text: As the <s>Bhāṣya</s> (commentary) states:
If one says: 'It is the fault of the effect itself that, even when a capable cause exists, it sometimes does not arise' — then it is not the effect of that [cause], due to its independence.

children.text: sarvāvasthāsamāne 'pi kāraṇe yady akāryatā |
children.translated_text: 'If there is non-effecthood even when the cause is the same in all conditions,

children.text: svatantraṃ  kāryam evaṃ syān na tatkāryaṃ tathā sati ||
(PV II 396)

children.translated_text: then the effect would be independent — and in that case it would not be the effect of that [cause].'

children.text: atha na tadbhāve bhavatīti tatkāryam ucyate, kiṃtu tadabhāve na  bhavaty eveti vyatirekaprādhānyād iti cet |
children.translated_text: If one says: 'It is called its effect not because it comes into being when that [cause] exists, but rather because it does not exist when that [cause] is absent — that is, the emphasis is on the negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>)' —

children.text: na | yadi hi svayaṃ bhavan  bhāvayed eva hetuḥ svakāryam , tadā tadabhāvaprayukto 'syābhāva iti pratītiḥ  syāt | no cet, yathā kāraṇe saty api kāryaṃ svātantryān  na bhavati, tathā tadabhāve 'pi svātantryād eva na bhūtam iti śaṅkā kena nivāryeta |
children.translated_text: no. For if the cause, existing by itself, would necessarily produce its own effect, then the cognition that 'its [the effect's] absence is caused by the absence of that [the cause]' would be justified. But if not — just as the effect does not come into being even when the cause exists, due to its independence — so too, even in the absence of that [cause], it might not have come into being precisely due to its independence — what would prevent this suspicion?

children.text: yad Bhāṣyam
children.translated_text: As the <s>Bhāṣya</s> states:

children.text: tadbhāve 'pi na bhāvaś ced abhāve 'bhāvitā  kutaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'If there is no existence [of the effect] even when it [the cause] exists, whence is the non-existence [established] in its absence?

children.text: tadabhāvaprayukto 'sya  so 'bhāva iti tat kutaḥ ||
(PVA II 411)

children.translated_text: That its absence is caused by the absence of that [cause] — whence [is this established]?'

children.text: tasmād yathaiva tadabhāve  niyamena na bhavati tathaiva tadbhāve niyamena bhaved eva | abhavac ca na tatkāraṇatām  ātmanaḥ kṣamate |
children.translated_text: Therefore, just as [the effect] necessarily does not exist in the absence of that [cause], so too it must necessarily exist in the presence of that [cause]. And if it did not [necessarily exist in its presence], it cannot claim causality for itself.

children.text: yac coktaṃ prathamakāryotpādanakāle hi uttarakāryotpādanasvabhāvaḥ, ataḥ prathamakāla evāśeṣāṇi kāryāṇi kuryād iti, tad idaṃ mātā me bandhyetyādivat svavacanavirodhād  ayuktam | yo hi uttarakāryajananasvabhāvaḥ sa katham ādau kāryaṃ kuryāt | na tarhi tatkāryakaraṇasvabhāvaḥ | na hi nīlotpādanasvabhāvaḥ pītādikam api karotīti |
children.translated_text: And as for the statement: 'At the time of producing the first effect, [the cause] has the nature of producing the subsequent effect; therefore, at the very first moment it should produce all effects without remainder' — this is untenable, like [the self-contradictory statement] 'My mother is barren,' due to contradiction with one's own words. For that which has the nature of producing the subsequent effect — how could it produce an effect at the beginning? Then it would not have the nature of producing that [subsequent] effect. For that which has the nature of producing blue does not also produce yellow and the like.

children.text: artocyate | sthirasvabhāvatve hi bhāvasyottarakālam evedaṃ  kāryaṃ na pūrvakālam iti kuta etat | tadabhāvāc ca kāraṇam apy uttarakāryakaraṇasvabhāvam ity api  kutaḥ |
children.translated_text: To this we reply: If the nature of the entity is stable, then whence [comes the restriction that] this effect [arises only] at a subsequent time and not at a prior time? And in the absence of that [restriction], whence [can one say] that the cause has the nature of producing the subsequent effect?

children.text: kiṃ kurmaḥ | uttarakālam eva tasya janmeti cet | astu, sthiratve tad anupapadyamānam, asthiratām ādiśatu |
children.translated_text: [Objection:] What are we to do? Its birth is simply at a subsequent time. [Reply:] Granted — but since that is untenable if [the cause] is stable, let it indicate instability.

children.text: sthiratve 'py eṣa eva svabhāvas tasya yad uttarakṣaṇa eva karotīti cet | hatedānīṃ  pramāṇapratyāśā | dhūmād atrāgnir  ity atrāpi svabhāva evāsya yad idānīm atra niragnir api dhūma iti vaktuṃ śakyatvāt | tasmāt pramāṇasiddhe  svabhāvāvalambanam | na tu svabhāvāvalambanena pramāṇavyālopaḥ |
children.translated_text: [Objection:] Even if stable, this is simply its nature — that it produces only at the subsequent moment. [Reply:] Then the hope for a valid means of knowledge is killed. For in 'There is fire here, because of smoke,' too, it would be possible to say 'It is simply the nature of this [smoke] that right now, right here, there is smoke without fire' — because [if natural facts override valid means of knowledge, anything could be asserted]. Therefore, one should rely on natural facts [only] when established by valid means of knowledge — not [allow] an appeal to natural facts to overturn valid means of knowledge.

children.text: tasmād yadi kāraṇasyottarakāryakārakatvam abhyupagamya kāryasya prathamakṣaṇabhāvitvam āsajyate, syāt svavacanavirodhaḥ | yadā tu kāraṇasya sthiratve kāryasyottarakālatvam evāsaṅgatam ataḥ kāraṇasyāpy uttarakāryajanakatvaṃ vastuto 'sambhavi tadā prasaṅgasādhanam idam | jananavyavahāragocaratvaṃ hi jananena vyāptam iti prasādhitam | uttarakāryajananavyavahāragocaratvaṃ  ca tvad abhyupagamāt prathamakāryakaraṇakāla eva ghaṭe dharmiṇi siddhaṃ | atas tanmātrānubandhina uttarābhimatasya kāryasya prathame kṣaṇe 'sambhavād eva prasaṅgaḥ kriyate |
children.translated_text: Therefore, if — having accepted that the cause produces the subsequent effect — the existence of the effect at the first moment is argued as a consequence, there would be a contradiction with one's own words. But when, given the stability of the cause, even the subsequence of the effect is incoherent — and therefore the cause's production of the subsequent effect is also actually impossible — then this is a <s>prasaṅga</s> argument (reductio ad absurdum). For it has been established that 'being within the scope of the convention of production' is pervaded by 'production.' And being within the scope of the convention of producing the subsequent effect — this is established in the subject, the pot, at the very time of producing the first effect, by your own admission. Therefore, the <s>prasaṅga</s> is constructed precisely because of the impossibility of the subsequently-intended effect — which is connected solely to that [first moment's cause] — [arising] at the first moment.

children.text: na hi nīlakārake 'pi pītakārakatvārope pītasambhavaprasaṅgaḥ svavacanavirodho nāma |
children.translated_text: For indeed, in the superimposition of the capacity to produce yellow upon that which produces blue, the consequence of the possibility of yellow [arising] is not called 'a contradiction with one's own words.'

children.text: tad evaṃ śaktaḥ sahakāryanapekṣitatvād jananena vyāptaḥ | ajanayaṃś ca śaktāśaktatvaviruddhadharmādhyāsād bhinna eva ||
children.translated_text: Thus, what is capable (<s>śakta</s>) — because it does not depend on cooperating [conditions] — is pervaded by production. And what does not produce, being the superimposition of contradictory properties — capacity and incapacity — upon one [and the same entity], is simply different [from what produces].

children.text: nanu bhavatu prasaṅgaviparyayabalād ekakāryaṃ prati śaktāśaktatvalakṣaṇaviruddhadharmādhyāsaḥ | tathāpi na tato bhedaḥ sidhyati |
children.translated_text: [Objection:] Granted, let there be, by the force of the <s>prasaṅga</s> and its reversal, the superimposition of the contradictory properties of capacity and incapacity with respect to a single effect. Even so, difference does not follow from that.

children.text: tathā hi bījam aṅkurādikaṃ kurvad  yadi yenaiva svabhāvenāṅkuraṃ  karoti tenaiva kṣityādikaṃ, tadā kṣityādīnām apy aṅkurasvābhāvyāpattiḥ | nānāsvabhāvatvena tu kārakatve svabhāvānām anyonyābhāvāvyabhicāritvād  ekatra bhāvābhāvau parasparaviruddhau syātām ity ekam api bījaṃ bhidyeta |
children.translated_text: For: if the seed, in producing the sprout and so forth, produces the earth-element and the like by precisely the same nature by which it produces the sprout — then the earth-element and the like too would have the nature of a sprout, because the cause is undifferentiated. But if [the seed] produces through multiple natures, then — because those natures are invariably accompanied by the mutual absence of one another — existence and non-existence, being mutually contradictory, would [both have to] be [present] in one [entity], and so even a single seed would be differentiated.

children.text: evaṃ pradīpo 'pi tailakṣayavarti dāhādikam |
children.translated_text: Similarly, a lamp too [produces] the burning and so forth of oil and wick.

children.text: tathā pūrvarūpam apy uttararūparasagandhādikam anekaiḥ  svabhāvaiḥ parikaritaṃ  karoti |
children.translated_text: Likewise, a prior [instance of] color too produces [the subsequent instances of] color, taste, smell, and the like through multiple natures.

children.text: teṣāṃ ca svabhāvānām anyonyābhāvāvyabhicārād viruddhānāṃ yoge pradīpādikaṃ bhidyeta | na ca bhidyate | tan na viruddhadharmādhyāso bhedakaḥ |
children.translated_text: And because those natures are invariably accompanied by the mutual absence of one another, being contradictory, if they were [all] present together, the lamp and the like would be differentiated. But they are not differentiated. Therefore, the superimposition of contradictory properties is not a differentiator.

children.text: tathā bījasyāṅkuraṃ  prati kārakatvaṃ gardabhādikaṃ  praty akārakatvam iti kārakatvākārakatve 'pi viruddhau dharmau | na ca tadyoge 'pi bījabhedaḥ |
children.translated_text: Likewise, the seed's being a cause with respect to the sprout and its being a non-cause with respect to a donkey and the like — [the properties of] being-a-cause and being-a-non-cause are also contradictory properties. But even with their conjunction, there is no differentiation of the seed.

children.text: tad evaṃ ekatra bīje pradīpe rūpe ca vipakṣe paridṛśyamānaḥ śaktāśaktatvādir viruddhadharmādhyāso na ghaṭāder bhedaka  iti |
children.translated_text: Thus, the superimposition of contradictory properties such as capacity and incapacity, which is observed in the negative examples — a single seed, lamp, and color — does not differentiate pots and the like.

children.text: atra brūmaḥ | bhavatu tāvad bījādīnām anekakāryakāritvād dharmabhūtānekasvabhāvabhedaḥ, tathāpi kaḥ prastāvo viruddhadharmādhyāsasya | svabhāvānāṃ hy anyonyābhāvāvyabhicāre bhedaḥ prāptāvasaro na virodhaḥ | virodhas tu yadvidhāne yanniṣedho yanniṣedhe  ca  yadvidhānaṃ tayor ekatra dharmiṇi parasparaparihārasthitatayā syāt | tad atraikaḥ svabhāvaḥ svābhāvena viruddho yukto bhāvābhāvavat | na tu svabhāvāntareṇa  ghaṭatvavastutvavat |
children.translated_text: To this we reply: Granted, let there be a differentiation of natures that are properties [of the entity], consisting of multiple natures, due to the production of multiple effects by seeds and the like. Even so, what occasion is there for the superimposition of contradictory properties? For when natures are invariably accompanied by the mutual absence of one another, it is difference that is appropriate, not contradiction. But contradiction would be when the positing of one entails the negation of the other and the negation of one entails the positing of the other — between those two, which [both] exist in a single subject by mutually excluding one another, like existence and non-existence.
