Here, one nature is appropriately contradicted by its own [negation] — like existence and non-existence — but not by something of a different nature, like pot-hood and thing-hood.

children.text: evam aṅkurādikāritvaṃ tadakāritvena viruddhaṃ, na punar vastvantarakāritvena | pratyakṣavyāpāraś cātra yathā nānādharmair adhyāsitaṃ bhāvam abhinnaṃ vyavasthāpayati tathā tatkāryakāriṇaṃ kāryāntarākāriṇaṃ  ca |
children.translated_text: Similarly, the capacity to produce sprouts and the like is contradicted by the incapacity to produce that [same sprout] — but not by the capacity to produce some other thing. And the operation of perception here is: just as it establishes the entity endowed with diverse properties as undifferentiated, so too [it establishes it as] producing that effect [and] not producing the other effect.

children.text: tad yadi pratiyogitvābhāvād anyonyābhāvāvyabhicāriṇāv  api svabhāvāv aviruddhau tatkārakatvānyākārakatve vā viṣayabhedād aviruddhe tat kim āyātam, ekakāryaṃ prati śaktāśaktatvayoḥ parasparapratiyoginor viruddhayor dharmayoḥ | etayor api punar avirodhe  virodho nāma dattajalāñ–jaliḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, if — due to the absence of the counter-relatum [i.e., genuine opposition] — natures invariably accompanied by the mutual absence of one another are [nonetheless] non-contradictory, and [if] capacity to produce that and incapacity to produce others are non-contradictory due to the difference in object — then what has been achieved? With respect to a single effect, capacity and incapacity — being mutually counter-relata, contradictory properties — [the argument still stands]. And if even these were non-contradictory, then contradiction itself would be a dead letter.

children.text: bhavatu tarhy ekakāryāpekṣayaiva sāmarthyāsāmarthyayor virodhaḥ | kevalaṃ yathā tad eva kāryaṃ prati kvacid deśe śaktir deśāntare cāśaktir iti deśabhedād aviruddhe śaktyaśaktī tathaikatraiva kārye kālabhedād  apy aviruddhe | yathā pūrvaṃ niṣkriyaḥ sphaṭikaḥ sa eva paścāt sakriya iti cet |
children.translated_text: [Objection:] Granted, then, that capacity and incapacity are contradictory only with respect to a single effect. But just as, with respect to that very effect, there is capacity in one location and incapacity in another location — and capacity and incapacity are non-contradictory due to the difference in location — so too, even with respect to the same effect, they are non-contradictory due to the difference in time. Just as a crystal is inert before and then active later.

children.text: ucyate | na hi vayaṃ paribhāṣāmātrād ekatra kārye deśabhedād aviruddhe śaktyaśaktī brūmaḥ, kiṃ tu virodhābhāvāt | taddeśakāryakāritvaṃ hi taddeśakāryākāritvena viruddham, na punar deśāntare tatkāryākāritvenānyakāryakāritvena vā ||
children.translated_text: [Reply:] We do not say that capacity and incapacity are non-contradictory with respect to a single effect due to the difference in location merely on the basis of stipulation — but rather due to the absence of contradiction. For the capacity to produce the effect at that location is contradicted by the incapacity to produce the effect at that location — but not by the incapacity to produce that effect at another location, or by the capacity to produce another effect.

children.text: yady evaṃ tatkālakāryakāritvaṃ tatkālakāryākāritvena viruddham | na punaḥ kālāntare tatkāryākāritvenānyakāryakāritvena  vā | tat kathaṃ kālabhede 'pi virodha iti cet |
children.translated_text: [Objection:] If so, the capacity to produce the effect at that time is contradicted by the incapacity to produce the effect at that time — but not by the incapacity to produce that effect at another time, or by the capacity to produce another effect. So how is there contradiction even with a difference in time?

children.text: ucyate | dvayor hi dharmayor ekatra dharmiṇy anavasthitiniyamaḥ parasparaparihārasthiti lakṣaṇo virodhaḥ | sa ca sākṣātparasparapratyanīkatayā bhāvābhāvavad vā bhavet, ekasya vā niyamena pramāṇāntareṇa bādhanān nityatvasattvavad vā bhaved iti na kaścid arthabhedaḥ | tad atraikadharmiṇi tatkālakāryakāritvādhāre  kālāntare tatkāryākāritvasyā nyakāryakāritvasya vā niyamena pramāṇāntareṇa  bādhanād virodhaḥ |
children.translated_text: [Reply:] Contradiction is defined as the rule that two properties cannot both abide in a single subject — the defining characteristic being mutual exclusion. And this [contradiction] may be either directly, through being mutually opposed, like existence and non-existence; or [it may be] through the negation of one by another valid means of knowledge with certainty, like eternality and being a real entity. There is no difference in meaning. Thus, in a single subject that is the locus of the capacity to produce the effect at that time, the incapacity to produce that effect at another time, or the capacity to produce another effect, is negated by another valid means of knowledge with certainty — and that is the contradiction.

children.text: tathā hi yatraiva dharmiṇi tatkālakāryakāritvam upalabdhaṃ na tatraiva kālāntare tatkāryākāritvam anyakāryakāritvaṃ vā brahmaṇāpy upasaṃhartuṃ śakyate , yenānayor avirodhaḥ syāt | kṣaṇāntare
children.translated_text: For in the very subject in which the capacity to produce the effect at that time is observed — in that same [subject], not even <s>Brahmā</s> can instantiate the incapacity to produce that effect at another time, or the capacity to produce another effect, such that there would be non-contradiction between them. Because at the next moment,

children.text: kathitaprasaṅgaviparyayahetubhyām avaśyambhāvena  dharmibhedaprasādhanāt ||
children.translated_text: by the reasons of the aforementioned <s>prasaṅga</s> and its reversal, a difference of subject is necessarily established.

children.text: na ca pratyabhijñānād ekatvasiddhiḥ, tatpauruṣasya nirmūlitatvāt | ata eva vajro 'pi pakṣakukṣau  nikṣiptaḥ | katham asau sphaṭiko varākaḥ kālabhedenābhedaprasādhanāya  dṛṣṭāntībhavitum arhati |
children.translated_text: Nor is unity established through recognition (<s>pratyabhijñā</s>), since the human [basis of recognition] has been uprooted. For this very reason, even the diamond is placed within the belly of the thesis-subject [as an example]. How can that wretched crystal deserve to serve as an illustration for establishing non-difference through the difference of time?

children.text: na caivaṃ samānakālakāryāṇāṃ deśabhede 'pi dharmibhedo yukto  bhedaprasādhaka pramāṇābhāvāt indriyapratyakṣeṇa nirastavibhramāśaṅkenābhedaprasādhanāc ceti na kālabhede 'pi śaktyaśaktyor virodhaḥ svasamayamātrād apahastayituṃ śakyaḥ, samayapramāṇayor apravṛtter iti |
children.translated_text: Nor [is it the case] that for effects at the same time but in different locations, there is a difference of subject even so — because there is no valid means of knowledge to establish the difference, and because non-difference is established by sense-perception that has dispelled the suspicion of error. Therefore, the contradiction of capacity and incapacity even with a difference in time cannot be waved away merely on the basis of one's own [doctrinal] convention, because convention and valid means of knowledge do not [both] apply [in the same way].

children.text: tasmāt sarvatra viruddhadharmādhyāsasiddhir eva bhedasiddhiḥ | vipratipannaṃ prati tu viruddhadharmādhyāsād bhedavyavahāraḥ sādhyate ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, in every case, the establishment of the superimposition of contradictory properties is itself the establishment of difference. But for the one who disputes [this], the convention of difference from the superimposition of contradictory properties is what is to be proved.

children.text: nanu tathāpi sattvam idam anaikāntikam evāsādhāraṇatvāt sandigdhavyatirekitvād  vā | yathā hīdaṃ kramākramanivṛttāv  akṣaṇikān nivṛttaṃ, tathā sāpekṣatvānapekṣatvayor  ekatvānekatvayor  api vyāpakayor nivṛttau kṣaṇikād api |
children.translated_text: [Objection:] Even so, this [property of] 'existence' (<s>sattva</s>) is inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>) — either because it is uncommon (<s>asādhāraṇa</s>), or because the negative concomitance is doubtful. For just as this [property of existence] is absent from what is non-momentary — [i.e.,] from the absence of sequence and non-sequence — so too it is absent from the momentary, with respect to [the pervaders] dependence/non-dependence and unity/multiplicity, which are also pervaders.

children.text: tathā hi upasarpaṇapratyayena devadattakarapallavādinā sahacaro bījakṣaṇaḥ pūrvasmād eva puñjāt samartho jāto 'napekṣa ādyātiśayasya janaka iṣyate |
children.translated_text: For the seed-moment, together with the proximate condition (<s>upasarpaṇapratyaya</s>) such as <s>Devadatta</s>'s palm and the like, being born from the very same heap, is accepted as capable, non-dependent, and the producer of the initial superior [quality].

children.text: tatra ca samānakuśūlajanmasu bahuṣu bījasantāneṣu kasmāt kiñcid eva bījaṃ paramparayāṅkurotpādānuguṇam  upajanayati bījakṣaṇaṃ, nānye bījakṣaṇā bhinnasantānāntaḥpātinaḥ | na hy upasarpaṇapratyayāt prāg eva teṣāṃ samānāsamānasantānavartināṃ  bījakṣaṇānāṃ kaścit paramparātiśayaḥ |
children.translated_text: But among many seed-series born in the same granary, why does only a particular seed produce — in succession — a seed-moment conducive to the production of a sprout, and not other seed-moments belonging to different series? For prior to the proximate condition, there is no superiority of succession whatsoever among those seed-moments, whether belonging to the same or different series.

children.text: athopasarpaṇapratyayāt  prāṅ na tatsantānavartino  'pi janayanti, paramparayāpy  aṅkurotpādānuguṇaṃ bījakṣaṇaṃ bījamātrajananāt teṣām | kasyacid eva bījakṣaṇasyopasarpaṇapratyayasahabhuva ādyātiśayotpādaḥ | hanta tarhi tadabhāve  saty utpanno 'pi janayed  eva |
children.translated_text: [Objection:] Prior to the proximate condition, the seed-moments belonging to that series also do not produce — in succession — a seed-moment conducive to the production of a sprout, because they merely produce a [bare] seed. The production of the initial superior [quality] belongs only to the seed-moment that co-exists with the proximate condition. [Reply:] Well then, even in the absence of that [proximate condition], having arisen, it should indeed produce [the sprout].

children.text: tathā  kevalānāṃ vyabhicārasambhavād ādyātiśayotpādakam  aṅkuraṃ vā prati kṣityādīnāṃ parasparāpekṣāṇām  evotpādakatvam akāmenāpi  svīkartavyam |
children.translated_text: Likewise, since deviation is possible for each [factor] taken individually, it must be accepted — even reluctantly — that with respect to the sprout, or [more precisely,] as producers of the initial superior quality, the earth-element and other [factors] produce only in mutual dependence.

children.text: ato na tāvad anapekṣā kṣaṇikasya sambhavinī | nāpy apekṣā yujyate, samasamayakṣaṇayoḥ savyetaragobiṣāṇayor ivopakāryopakārakabhāvāyogād iti nāsiddhaḥ prathamo vyāpakābhāvaḥ |
children.translated_text: Therefore, non-dependence is not possible for a momentary [entity]. Nor is dependence appropriate, because — for two things at the same time-moment — the relation of benefited and benefactor is impossible, like the two horns of a bull. So the first pervading absence [viz., the absence of dependence/non-dependence] is not unestablished.

children.text:
api cāntyo bījakṣaṇo 'napekṣo 'ṅkurādikaṃ kurvan yadi
	  yenaiva rūpeṇāṅkuraṃ karoti tenaiva kṣityādikaṃ, tadā kṣityādīnām apy
	  aṅkurasvābhāvyāpattir abhinnakāraṇatvād iti na tāvad ekatvasambhavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Moreover, if the final seed-moment, being non-dependent, in producing the sprout and the like — if it produces the earth-element and the like by precisely the same form by which it produces the sprout — then the earth-element and the like too would have the nature of a sprout, because the cause is undifferentiated. So unity is certainly not possible.

children.text:
nanu rūpāntareṇa karoti | tathā hi bījasyāṅkuraṃ praty
	  upādānatvam | kṣityādikaṃ tu prati sahakāritvam | yady evaṃ,
	  sahakāritvopādānatve kim ekaṃ tattvaṃ nānā vā | ekaṃ cet, kathaṃ
	  rūpāntareṇa janakam | nānātve tv anayor bījād bhedo 'bhedo vā | bhede
	  kathaṃ bījasya janakatvaṃ tābhyām evāṅkurādīnām utpatteḥ | abhede vā
	  kathaṃ bījasya na nānātvaṃ bhinnatādātmyāt, etayor vaikatvam
	  ekatādātmyāt |
children.translated_text: [Objection:] But it produces through a different form. For the seed is the material cause (<s>upādāna</s>) with respect to the sprout, but a cooperating condition (<s>sahakārin</s>) with respect to the earth-element and the like. [Reply:] If so — are the cooperating-condition-hood and material-cause-hood one reality or many? If one, how does it produce through a different form? If many: are those two different from or identical with the seed? If different, how is the seed a producer [at all], since the sprout and the like arise from those two alone? Or if identical, how is the seed not multiple — since it is identical with what is differentiated? And [conversely, how are] those two not one — since they are identical with what is one?

children.text:
yady ucyeta kṣityādau janayitavye tadupādānaṃ pūrvam eva
	  kṣityādi bījasya rūpāntaram iti | na tarhi bījaṃ tadanapekṣaṃ
	  kṣityādīnāṃ janakam | tadanapekṣatve teṣām aṅkurād bhedānupapatteḥ |
	  na cānupakārakāṇy apekṣanta iti tvayaivotkam | na ca kṣaṇasyopakāra
	  sambhavo 'nyatra jananāt, tasyābhedyatvād ity anekatvam api nāstīti
	  dvitīyo 'pi vyāpakābhāvo nāsiddhaḥ | tasmād asādhāraṇānaikāntikatvaṃ
	  gandhavattvavad iti |
children.translated_text: [Objection:] If it is said that the prior earth-element and the like, being the material cause of the earth-element and the like to be produced, are the 'different form' of the seed — then the seed is not the non-dependent producer of the earth-element and the like. Because if it were non-dependent upon those [earth-elements], their difference from the sprout would not be accounted for. And you yourself have said that non-helpful [factors] are not depended upon. And no benefit from a momentary [entity] is possible other than production, since it is indivisible — so multiplicity too does not exist. Therefore, the second pervading absence [viz., the absence of unity/multiplicity] is also not unestablished. Thus, [the property of existence] is [allegedly] uncommon and inconclusive, like 'having smell' [which is restricted to earth alone].

children.text: yadi manyetānupakārakā  api bhavanti sahakāriṇo 'pekṣaṇīyāś ca kāryeṇānuvihitabhāvābhāvāc ca  sahakāryakaraṇāc  ca |
children.translated_text: [Objection:] If one thinks that even non-helpful [factors] can be cooperating conditions, and that they are to be depended upon because their existence and non-existence conforms to [the existence and non-existence of] the effect, and because of the production of cooperating effects —

children.text: nanv  anena krameṇākṣaṇiko 'pi bhāvo 'nupakārakān api sahakāriṇaḥ kramavataḥ kramavat kāryeṇānukṛtānvayavyatirekān apekṣiṣyate | kariṣyate ca kramavatsahakārivaśaḥ krameṇa kāryāṇīti vyāpakānupalabdher asiddheḥ sandigdhavyatirekam anaikāntikaṃ sattvaṃ kṣaṇikatvasiddhāv iti |
children.translated_text: Objection: By this reasoning, even a non-momentary entity would require successive cooperative conditions (<s>sahakārin</s>) — even those that do not assist it — whose positive and negative concomitance is replicated by a successive effect. And it would produce effects successively, dependent on successive cooperative conditions. Therefore, the non-apprehension of the pervader (<s>vyāpakānupalabdhi</s>) is unestablished, and existence (<s>sattva</s>) as a reason for proving momentariness has doubtful negative concomitance and is therefore inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>).

children.text: atra brūmaḥ | kīdṛśaṃ punar apekṣārtham ādāya kṣaṇike sāpekṣānapekṣatvanivṛttir ucyate | kiṃ sahakāriṇam apekṣata iti sahakāriṇāsyopakāraḥ karttavyaḥ | atha pūrvāvasthitasyaiva bījādeḥ sahakāriṇā saha sambhūyakaraṇam | yadvā pūrvāvasthitasyety anapekṣya  militāvasthasya karaṇamātram apekṣārthaḥ | atra prathamapakṣasyāsambhavād anapekṣaiva kṣaṇikasya, katham ubhayavyāvṛttiḥ |
children.translated_text: To this we reply: What meaning of 'dependence' is taken up when the exclusion of being dependent or independent is stated with respect to the momentary? Does it mean: 'it depends on a cooperative condition' in the sense that the cooperative condition must render assistance to it? Or does it mean the joint operation of a previously existing seed and the like together with a cooperative condition? Or, setting aside 'previously existing,' does it mean merely the operation of [something] in its conjoined state? Here, since the first alternative is impossible, there is simply independence for the momentary — how then can the exclusion of both [dependence and independence] hold?

children.text: yady anapekṣaḥ kṣaṇikaḥ , kimity upasarpaṇapratyayābhāve 'pi na karoti | karoty eva yadi syāt | svayam asambhavī tu kathaṃ karotu | atha tad vā tādṛg vāsīd iti na kaścid viśeṣaḥ | tatas tādṛk svabhāvasambhave 'py akaraṇaṃ sahakāriṇi  nirapekṣān  na kṣamata iti cet |
children.translated_text: If the momentary is independent, why does it not produce [its effect] even in the absence of the condition of approach (<s>upasarpaṇapratyaya</s>)? It does produce [its effect], if it exists. But how can what is itself non-existent produce [anything]? [Objection:] Whether it was that [entity] or one of that kind — there is no difference. Therefore, even when an entity of that nature exists, its non-production, while being independent of a cooperative condition, is untenable.

children.text: asambaddham etat | varṇasaṃsthānasāmye 'py akartus tatsvabhāvatāyā virahāt | sa cādyātiśayajanakatvalakṣaṇaḥ svabhāvaviśeṣo  na samānāsamānasantānavartiṣu bījakṣaṇeṣu sarveṣv  eva sambhavī | kiṃ tu keṣucid eva karmakarakarapallavasahacareṣu |
children.translated_text: This is incoherent. Because even when there is similarity in color and configuration, the non-producer lacks the essential nature [of the producer]. And that specific essential nature — characterized by the capacity to generate the initial extraordinary [effect] — does not exist in all seed-moments occurring in the same or different continua. Rather, [it exists] only in certain ones that are accompanied by the action, cause, and sprout.

children.text: nanv ekatra kṣetre niṣpattilavanādipūrvakam ānīyaikatra kuśūle kṣiptāni sarvāṇy eva bījāni  sādhāraṇarūpāṇy eva pratīyante | tat kutastyo 'yam ekabījasambhavī viśeṣo 'nyeṣāṃ iti cet |
children.translated_text: Objection: When seeds, having been harvested with salt and the like from a single field, are brought and thrown into a single granary, all the seeds appear to be of a common form. So from where does this specific property arise that belongs to a single seed and not to the others?

children.text: ucyate | kāraṇam khalu sarvatra kārye dvividham | dṛṣṭam adṛṣṭaṃ ceti | sarvāstikaprasiddham etat | tataḥ pratyakṣaparokṣasahakāripratyayasākalyam asarvavidā pratyakṣato na śakyaṃ pratipattum | tato bhaved api kāraṇasāmagrīśaktibhedāt tādṛśaḥ svabhāvabhedaḥ keṣāñcid eva bījakṣaṇānāṃ yena ta eva bījakṣaṇā ādyātiśayam aṅkuraṃ vā paramparayā janayeyuḥ | nānye ca  bījakṣaṇāḥ |
children.translated_text: We reply: The cause in every effect is indeed of two kinds — seen and unseen (<s>dṛṣṭa</s> and <s>adṛṣṭa</s>). This is well-known to all who accept [the existence of things]. Therefore, the totality of perceptible and imperceptible cooperative conditions cannot be ascertained through perception by one who is not omniscient. Hence, due to the difference in the capacity of the causal aggregate, there may well be such a difference in essential nature in only certain seed-moments, by virtue of which those very seed-moments — and no other seed-moments — would generate the initial extraordinary [effect] or a sprout through a causal chain.

children.text: nanu yeṣūpasarpaṇapratyayasahacareṣu svakāraṇaśaktibhedād ādyātiśaya janakatvalakṣaṇo viśeṣaḥ sambhāvyate sa tatrāvaśyam astīti kuto labhyam iti cet |
children.translated_text: Objection: How can we be certain that the specific property — characterized by the capacity to generate the initial extraordinary [effect] — which is postulated on the basis of a difference in the capacity of one's own cause in [seed-moments] accompanied by the condition of approach, necessarily exists there?

children.text: aṅkurotpādād anumitād ādyātiśayalakṣaṇāt  kāryād iti brūmaḥ | kāraṇānupalabdhes tarhi tadabhāva eva bhaviṣyatīti cet | na | dṛśyādṛśyasamudāyasya kāraṇasyādarśane 'py abhāvāsiddheḥ kāraṇānupalabdheḥ sandigdhāsiddhatvāt |
children.translated_text: We reply: From the effect characterized as the initial extraordinary [quality], inferred from the production of a sprout. [Objection:] Then, from the non-apprehension of the cause, there would be the absence of that [effect] itself. [Reply:] No. Because even when the cause — which is an aggregate of seen and unseen [factors] — is not perceived, its absence is not established; the non-apprehension of the cause is itself unestablished.

children.text: tad ayam arthaḥ
children.translated_text: The meaning is this:

children.text: pāṇisparśavataḥ kṣaṇasya na bhidā  bhinnānyakālakṣaṇād bhedo veti matadvaye mitibalaṃ yasyāsty asau  jitvaraḥ |
children.translated_text: Whether the moment accompanied by the touch of the hand is different or not different from a moment at another time — in both views, whichever [position] has the strength of evidence, that one is victorious.

children.text: tatraikasya balaṃ nimittavirahaḥ kāryāṅgam anyasya vā sāmagrī tu na sarvathekṣaṇasahā kāryaṃ tu mānānugam ||
children.translated_text: In that [debate], the strength of one [position] is the absence of a cause [for the effect], or the other's [strength lies in] its being a component of the effect. But the [causal] aggregate is not in every case amenable to observation, while the effect conforms to the evidence.

children.text: iti |
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: tad evaṃ nopakāro 'pekṣārtha ity anapekṣaiva  kṣaṇikasya sahakāriṣu nobhayavyāvṛttiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, since assistance is not the meaning of dependence, the momentary is simply independent — there is no exclusion of both [dependence and independence] with respect to cooperative conditions.

children.text: atha sambhūyakaraṇam apekṣārthaḥ, tadā yadi pūrvasthitasyeti viśeṣaṇāpekṣā tadā kṣaṇikasya naivaṃ kadācid ity anapekṣaivākṣīṇā |
children.translated_text: Now, if joint operation is the meaning of dependence, then if the qualification 'of what previously existed' is required, since the momentary never [previously existed] in this way, its independence remains undiminished.

children.text: atha pūrvasthitasyety anapekṣya  militāvasthitasyaiva karaṇam apekṣārthas tadā sāpekṣataiva, nānapekṣā | tathā ca nobhayavyāvṛttir  ity asiddhaḥ prathamo vyāpakānupalambhaḥ |
children.translated_text: But if, setting aside 'of what previously existed,' the meaning of dependence is merely the operation of [something] in its conjoined state, then there is dependence only, not independence. And thus there is no exclusion of both — hence the first non-apprehension of the pervader is unestablished.

children.text:
tathaikatvānekatvayor api vyāpakayoḥ kṣaṇikād vyāvṛttir
	  asiddhā | tattadvyāvṛttibhedam āśrityopādānatvādi
	  kālpanikasvabhāvabhede 'pi paramārthata ekenaiva
	  svarūpeṇānekakāryaniṣpādanād ubhayavyāvṛtter abhāvāt |
children.translated_text: Likewise, the exclusion of the pervaders — unity and plurality — from the momentary is also unestablished. Because, based on different exclusions, even when there is a fictitious difference in essential nature such as being a material cause (<s>upādānatva</s>) and the like, ultimately, through a single essential nature, multiple effects are accomplished — hence the exclusion of both [is not established].

children.text:
yac ca bījasyaikenaiva svabhāvena kārakatve kṣityādīnām
	  aṅkurasvābhāvyāpattir anyathā kāraṇābhede 'pi kāryabhede 'pi
	  kāryasyāhetukatvaprasaṅgād ity uktam tad asaṅgatam | kāraṇaikatvasya
	  kāryabhedasya ca paṭunendriyapratyakṣeṇa prasādhanāt |
	  ekakāraṇajanyatvaikatvayor vyāpteḥ pratihatatvāt |
	  prasaṅgasyānupadatvāt |
children.translated_text: And as for the statement that if the seed produces through a single essential nature, then earth and the like would absurdly become sprouts, or else, even when the cause is the same, if the effect differs, there would follow the consequence that the effect is uncaused — that is incoherent. Because the unity of the cause [and its relation to] the effect

children.text: yac ca kāraṇābhede kāryābheda ity uktaṃ tatra sāmagrīsvarūpaṃ kāraṇam abhipretam | sāmagrīsajātīyatve na kāryavijātīyatety arthaḥ | na punaḥ sāmagrīmadhyagatenaikenānekaṃ kāryaṃ na kartavyaṃ nāma, ekasmād anekotpatteḥ pratyakṣasiddhatvāt | na caivaṃ pratyabhijñānāt kālabhede 'py abhedasiddhir  ity uktaprāyam | na cendriyapratyakṣaṃ bhinnadeśaṃ sapratighaṃ dṛśyam arthadvayam ekam evopalambhayatīti kvacid upalabdham | yena tatrāpi bhedaśaṅkā  syāt | śaṅkāyāṃ vā paṭupratyakṣasyāpy apalāpe sarvapramāṇocchedaprasaṅgād |
children.translated_text: [requires clarification]. And as for the statement that if the cause is the same, the effect is the same — there the causal aggregate as a whole is intended as the cause. The meaning is: when the aggregate is of the same kind, the effect is not of a different kind. But it is not the case that a single [element] within the aggregate cannot produce multiple effects —

children.text: nāpi sattvahetoḥ sandigdhavyatirekitvam , kṣityāder dravyāntarasya bījasvabhāvatvenāsmābhir asvīkṛtatvāt | anupakāriṇy apekṣāyāḥ pratyākhyātatvāt  vyāpakānupalambhasyāsiddhatvāyogāt |
children.translated_text: Nor does the reason of existence (<s>sattva</s>) have doubtful negative concomitance, because we do not accept earth and the like as different substances having the nature of seeds. Because dependence in the absence of assistance has been rejected. Because the non-apprehension of the pervader cannot be unestablished.

children.text: tad etau dvāv api vyāpakānupalambhāv asiddhau na kṣaṇikāt sattvaṃ nivartayata  iti nāyam asādhāraṇo hetuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, both these non-apprehensions of the pervader are unestablished and do not exclude existence from the momentary — hence this is not an uncommon reason (<s>asādhāraṇa hetu</s>).

children.text:
api ca vidyamāno bhāvaḥ sādhyetarayor aniścitānvayavyatireko
	  gandhavattādivad asādhāraṇo yuktaḥ | prakṛtavyāpakānupalambhāc ca
	  sarvathārthakriyaivāsatī ubhābhyāṃ vādibhyām ubhayasmād
	  vinivartitatvena nirāśrayatvāt | tat katham asādhāraṇānaikāntiko
	  bhaviṣyatīty alaṃ pralāpini nirbandhena |
children.translated_text: Moreover, an existing entity whose positive and negative concomitance with either the provable or its opposite is undetermined would properly be an uncommon [reason], like having smell and the like. And from the non-apprehension of the pervader under consideration, causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyā</s>) itself, being entirely absent [in the non-momentary], is excluded by both disputants from both [alternatives].

children.text: tad evaṃ śaktasya kṣepāyogāt  samarthavyavahāragocaratvaṃ jananena vyāptam iti prasaṅgaviparyayayoḥ sattve hetor  api nānaikāntikatvam | ataḥ kṣaṇabhaṅgasiddhir iti sthitam |
children.translated_text: Thus, since what is capable cannot be dismissed, being within the scope of the convention of 'capable' is pervaded by production. Therefore, in both the positive consequence (<s>prasaṅga</s>) and its converse (<s>viparyaya</s>), the reason of existence is not inconclusive. Hence, the proof of momentariness (<s>kṣaṇabhaṅgasiddhi</s>) stands established.

children.text: iti sādharmyadṛṣṭānte 'nvayarūpavyāptyā kṣaṇabhaṅgasiddhiḥ samāptā ||
children.translated_text: Thus concludes the proof of momentariness through the positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) in the example of similarity (<s>sādharmyadṛṣṭānta</s>).

children.text: kṛtir iyaṃ mahāpaṇḍitaratnakīrtipādānām iti ||
children.translated_text: This is the composition of the feet of the great <s>paṇḍita</s> <s>Ratnakīrti</s>.

children.text: Kṣaṇabhaṅgasiddhiḥ Vyatirekātmikā
children.translated_text: <s>Kṣaṇabhaṅgasiddhi Vyatirekātmikā</s> (Proof of Momentariness through Negative Concomitance)

children.text: namas tārāyai
vyatirekātmikā vyāptir ākṣiptānvayarūpiṇī |
children.translated_text: The pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>) in the form of negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>), which implies the form of positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>),

children.text: vaidharmyavati dṛṣṭānte sattvahetor ihocyate ||
children.translated_text: is stated here for the reason of existence (<s>sattva</s>) in the example of dissimilarity (<s>vaidharmyadṛṣṭānta</s>).

children.text: yat sat tat kṣaṇikam | yathā ghaṭaḥ | santaś cāmī vivādāspadībhūtāḥ padārthā iti svabhāvahetuḥ |
children.translated_text: Whatever exists is momentary — like a pot. And these entities that have become the subject of dispute are existent — thus [this is] a natural reason (<s>svabhāvahetu</s>).

children.text: na tāvad asyāsiddhiḥ sambhavati, yathāyogaṃ pratyakṣānumānapramāṇapratīte dharmiṇi sattvaśabdenābhipretasyārthakriyākāritvalakṣaṇasya sādhanasya pramāṇasamadhigatatvāt |
children.translated_text: To begin with, this [reason] cannot be unestablished (<s>asiddhi</s>), because the proof — characterized by causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyākāritva</s>), which is what is intended by the word 'existence' (<s>sattva</s>) — is established by valid cognition, the subject (<s>dharmin</s>) being ascertained through perception and inference as appropriate.

children.text: na ca viruddhānaikāntikate, vyāpakānupalambhātmanā viparyaye bādhakapramāṇena vyāpteḥ prasādhanāt |
children.translated_text: Nor is it contradictory or inconclusive, because the pervasion is established through a counter-proof (<s>bādhaka pramāṇa</s>) in the form of the non-apprehension of the pervader regarding the contrary.

children.text: yasya kramākramau na vidyete na tasyārthakriyāsāmarthyam | yathā śaśaviṣāṇasya | na vidyete cākṣaṇikasya kramākramāv iti vyāpakānupalambhaḥ |
children.translated_text: That which possesses neither succession (<s>krama</s>) nor simultaneity (<s>akrama</s>) has no capacity for causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyā</s>) — like a hare's horn. And the non-momentary possesses neither succession nor simultaneity — this is the non-apprehension of the pervader (<s>vyāpakānupalambha</s>).

children.text: na tāvad ayam asiddho hetuḥ, akṣaṇike dharmiṇi kramākramasadbhāvāyogāt | tathā hi prāptāparakālayor ekatve nityatvam | tasya kramākramayoge kṣaṇadvaye 'py avaśyaṃ bhedaḥ | bhedābhedayoś ca parasparavirodhāt kuto 'kṣaṇike kramākramasambhavaḥ | kṣaṇadvaye 'pi bhede kramākramayogaḥ | abhede hi prathama eva kṣaṇe śaktatvād bhāvino 'pi kāryasya karaṇaprasaṅge kathaṃ kāryāntarakaraṇe kramāntarāvakāśaḥ | na cākṣaṇikasyākrameṇaiva sakalasvakāryaṃ kṛtvā svāsthyam | kṣaṇāntare 'pi śaktatvāt punas tatkāryakaraṇaprasaṅgāt |
children.translated_text: To begin with, this reason is not unestablished, because succession and simultaneity cannot exist in a non-momentary subject (<s>dharmin</s>). For thus: if what has reached and what belongs to a later time are identical, then there is permanence. And if [permanence] were compatible with succession and simultaneity, there would necessarily be difference in two moments. And difference and non-difference, being mutually contradictory,

children.text: tasmād akṣaṇikam iti pūrvāparakālayor abhedaḥ | kramākramayoga iti pūrvāparakālayor bhedaḥ | anayoś ca parasparaparihārasthitilakṣaṇo virodhaḥ |
children.translated_text: therefore, 'non-momentary' means non-difference between earlier and later times. 'Compatible with succession and simultaneity' means difference between earlier and later times. And between these two there is a contradiction characterized by mutual exclusion.

children.text: tad ayam akṣaṇike dharmiṇi kramākramābhāvalakṣaṇo hetur nāsiddho vaktavyaḥ | kramākramayogitvākṣaṇikatvayor virodhād eva |
children.translated_text: Thus, this reason — characterized by the absence of succession and simultaneity in a non-momentary subject — should not be called unestablished, precisely because of the contradiction between being compatible with succession and simultaneity and being non-momentary.

children.text: nāpi viruddhaḥ, sapakṣe bhāvāt |
children.translated_text: Nor is it contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>), because it is present in the similar example (<s>sapakṣa</s>).

children.text: na cānaikāntikaḥ, kramākramābhāvasyārthakriyāsāmarthyābhāvena vyāptatvāt |
children.translated_text: Nor is it inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>), because the absence of succession and simultaneity is pervaded by the absence of the capacity for causal efficacy.

children.text: yenaiva hi pratyakṣātmanā pramāṇenāparaprakārābhāvād vidhibhūtābhyāṃ kramākramābhyāṃ vidhibhūtasyārthakriyāsāmarthyasya vyāptiḥ prasādhitā, tenaivārthakriyāsāmarthyābhāvena kramākramābhāvasya vyāptiḥ prasādhiteti svīkartavyam | na hi dahanādinā dhūmāder vyāptisādhakapramāṇād aparaṃ dhūmādyabhāvena dahanādyabhāvasya vyāptisādhakaṃ kiñcit pramāṇaṃ śaraṇabhūtam asti | tasmād vidhyor eva vyāptisādhakaṃ pramāṇam abhāvayor api vyāptisādhakam iti nyāyasya duratikramatvāt sattvābhāvena kramākramābhāvo vyāpta eveti nānaikāntika ity anavadyo vyāpakānupalambhaḥ | tad ayam akṣaṇikād vinivartamāṇaḥ svavyāpyaṃ sattvaṃ nivartya kṣaṇike viśrāmayatīti sattvahetoḥ kṣaṇabhaṅgasiddhir apy anavadyā |
children.translated_text: For the very means of valid cognition — perception itself — by which, due to the absence of any other form, the pervasion of the capacity for causal efficacy (which is a positive entity) by succession and simultaneity (which are positive entities) is established — by that very [means], the pervasion of the absence of succession and simultaneity by the absence of the capacity for causal efficacy is [also] established.

children.text: nanu vyāpakānupalambhataḥ sattvasya kathaṃ svasādhyapratibandhasiddhiḥ, asyāpy anekadoṣaduṣṭatvāt. tathā hi – na tāvad ayaṃ prasaṅgahetuḥ, sādhyadharmiṇi pramāṇasiddhatvāt, parābhyupagamasiddhatvābhāvāt, viparyayaparyavasānābhāvāc ca. atha svatantraḥ, tadāśrayāsiddhaḥ, akṣaṇikasyāśrayasyāsambhavād apratītatvād vā. pratītir hi2 [a] pratyakṣeṇa [b] anumānena [c] vikalpamātreṇa vā syāt |
children.translated_text: Objection: How is the invariable connection of existence (<s>sattva</s>) with its provable established from the non-apprehension of the pervader, since this [argument] too is vitiated by multiple defects? For thus: to begin with, this is not a <s>prasaṅga</s> (reductio) argument, because [the reason] is established by valid cognition in the subject of the provable, and because it is not established merely through the opponent's acceptance.

children.text: a
children.translated_text: In the first pair of alternatives, either directly or indirectly, if causal efficacy is characterized by self-apprehension, then the primary reason would be a common reason (<s>sādhāraṇa</s>), and the non-apprehension of the pervader would be essentially unestablished (<s>svarūpāsiddha</s>), because in [the case of]

children.text: [b] prathamapakṣadvaye sākṣāt pāramparyeṇa vā svapratītilakṣaṇārthakāritve maulaḥ sādhāraṇo hetuḥ vyāpakānupalambhaś ca svarūpāsiddhaḥ syāt, arthakriyākāritve kramākramayor anyatarasyāvaśyambhāvāt |
children.translated_text: causal efficacy, one or the other of succession and simultaneity necessarily exists.

children.text: c
children.translated_text: In the last alternative, however, no reason would be without a locus, because a subject established only through conceptual construction is easily available everywhere.

children.text: antimapakṣe tu na kaścid dhetur anāśrayaḥ syāt, vikalpamātrasiddhasya dharmiṇaḥ sarvatra sulabhatvāt.
api ca – tat kalpanājñānaṃ [c1] pratyakṣapṛṣṭhabhāvi vā syāt, [c2] liṅgajanma vā, [c3] saṃskārajaṃ vā, [c4] sandigdhavastukaṃ vā, [c5] avastukaṃ vā.
children.translated_text: Moreover, that conceptual cognition would be either [c1] subsequent to perception, or [c2] born from an inferential mark, or [c3] born from latent impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>), or [c4] having a doubtful object, or [c5] having no object.

children.text: tatra [c1][c2] ādyapakṣadvaye 'kṣaṇikasya sattaivāvyāhatā, kathaṃ bādhakāvatāraḥ.
children.translated_text: Of these, in the first pair of alternatives [c1][c2], the existence of the non-momentary is itself uncontradicted — how then can the counter-proof intervene?

children.text: c3
children.translated_text: In the third [alternative, c3]

children.text: tṛtīye tu na sarvadākṣaṇikasattāniṣedhaḥ, tadarpitasaṃskārābhāve tatsmaraṇāyogāt |
children.translated_text: , the existence of the non-momentary is not denied at all times, because in the absence of latent impressions deposited by that [cognition], there would be no memory of it.

children.text: c4
children.translated_text: In the fourth [alternative, c4]

children.text: caturthe tu sandigdhāśrayatvaṃ hetudoṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: , having a doubtful locus is a defect of the reason.

children.text: c5
children.translated_text: Fifth alternative:

children.text: pañcame ca tadviṣayasyābhāvo na tāvat pratyakṣataḥ sidhyati, akṣaṇikātmanaḥ sarvadaiva tvanmate 'pratyakṣatvāt | na cānumānatas tadabhāvas tatpratibaddhaliṅgānupalambhād ity āśrayāsiddhis tāvad uddhatā | evaṃ dṛṣṭānto 'pi pratihantavyaḥ |
children.translated_text: And the non-existence of that which has it [the non-momentary entity] as its object is not established through perception, since in your view what has a non-momentary nature is always imperceptible. Nor can its non-existence be [established] through inference, because no logical mark that is necessarily connected with it is apprehended — thus there is at least the defect of the locus being unestablished (<s>āśrayāsiddhi</s>). Similarly, the example must also be refuted.

children.text: svarūpāsiddho 'py ayaṃ hetuḥ, sthirasyāpi kramākramisahakāryapekṣayā kramākramābhyām arthakriyopapatteḥ | nāpi kramayaugapadyapakṣoktadoṣaprasaṅgaḥ | tathā hi kramisahakāryapekṣayā kramikāryakāritvaṃ tāvad aviruddham |
children.translated_text: This reason is also unestablished in its own nature (<s>svarūpāsiddha</s>), because even for a permanent entity, causal efficacy is explicable through sequential and simultaneous [production] in dependence on sequential and simultaneous auxiliary causes. Nor does the fault stated in the alternatives of sequential and simultaneous [production] apply. For thus: sequential causal efficacy in dependence on sequential auxiliary causes is entirely non-contradictory.

children.text: tathā ca Śaṅkarasya saṃkṣipto 'yam abhiprāyaḥ | sahakārisākalyaṃ hi sāmarthyam | tadvaikalyaṃ cāsāmarthyam | na ca tayor āvirbhāvatirobhāvābhyāṃ tadvataḥ kācit kṣatiḥ, tasya tābhyām anyatvāt | tat kathaṃ sahakāriṇo 'napekṣya kāryakaraṇaprasaṅga iti |
children.translated_text: And the gist of <s>Śaṅkara's</s> [argument] is as follows: The totality of auxiliary causes is precisely the capacity. And the deficiency of that [totality] is the incapacity. And no damage is done to the possessor [of the capacity] by the appearance and disappearance of those [auxiliary causes], since it is different from them. How then can there be the absurd consequence of producing the effect without regard to the auxiliary cause?

children.text: trilocanasyā
children.translated_text: The gist of <s>Trilocana's</s>

children.text: py ayaṃ saṃkṣiptārthaḥ | kāryam eva hi sahakāriṇam apekṣate | na kāryotpattihetuḥ | yasmāt dvividhaṃ sāmarthyaṃ nijam āgantukaṃ ca sahakāryantaram, tato 'kṣaṇikasyāpi kramavatsahakārinānātvād api kramavatkāryanānātvopapatter aśakyaṃ bhāvānāṃ pratikṣaṇam anyānyatvam upapādayitum iti |
children.translated_text: [argument] too is as follows: It is the effect itself that depends on the auxiliary cause, not the cause of the effect's production. For the capacity is twofold: intrinsic and adventitious — that is, the other auxiliary cause. Therefore, even for a non-momentary entity, since the multiplicity of effects in sequence is explicable by the multiplicity of sequential auxiliary causes, it is impossible to demonstrate that entities are different at each moment.

children.text: Nyāyabhūṣaṇo 'pi lapati | prathamakāryotpādanakāle hi uttarakāryotpādanasvabhāvaḥ | ataḥ prathamakāla evāśeṣāṇi kāryāṇi kuryād iti cet |
children.translated_text: <s>Nyāyabhūṣaṇa</s> also declares: At the time of producing the first effect, [the entity] has the nature of producing the later effect too. Therefore, it should produce all effects at the very first moment.

children.text: tad idaṃ mātā me bandhyetyādivat svavacanavirodhād ayuktaṃ | yo hi uttarakāryajananasvabhāvaḥ sa katham ādau tat kāryaṃ kuryāt | atha kuryāt na tarhi tatkāryakaraṇasvabhāvaḥ | na hi nīlotpādanasvabhāvaḥ pītādikam api karotīti |
children.translated_text: This is untenable, like [the statement] 'My mother is barren,' because of contradiction with one's own words. For that which has the nature of producing the later effect — how could it produce that effect at the beginning? If it could, then it would not have the nature of producing that [later] effect. For that which has the nature of producing blue does not also produce yellow and the like.

children.text: Vācaspatir api paṭhati | nanv ayam akṣaṇikaḥ svarūpeṇa kāryaṃ janayati | tac cāsya svarūpaṃ tṛtīyādiṣv iva kṣaṇeṣu dvitīye 'pi kṣaṇe sad iti tadāpi janayet | akurvan vā tṛtīyādiṣv api na kurvīta, tasya tādavasthyāt | atādavasthye vā tad evāsya kṣaṇikatvam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vācaspati</s> also writes: [Objection:] 'This non-momentary [entity] produces the effect by its own nature. And that nature of it exists in the second moment just as in the third and subsequent moments — therefore it should produce [the effect] then too. Or, if it does not produce, it should not produce in the third and subsequent moments either, since it is in the same condition. Or if it is not in the same condition, that itself would be its momentariness.'

children.text: atrocyate | satyaṃ svarūpeṇa kāryaṃ janayati na tu tenaiva | sahakārisahitād eva tataḥ kāryotpattidarśanāt | tasmād vyāptivat kāryakāraṇabhāvo 'py ekatrānyayogavyavacchedena | anyatrāyogavyavacchedenāvaboddhavyaḥ | tathaiva laukikaparīkṣakāṇāṃ saṃpratipatter iti na kramikāryakāritvapakṣoktadoṣāvasaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: To this we reply: True, it produces the effect by its own nature — but not by that [nature] alone, since the production of the effect is observed only from that together with auxiliary causes. Therefore, just as invariable concomitance, the cause-effect relation too should be understood as: in one case, exclusion of association with anything else; in the other, exclusion of non-association. For that is precisely how worldly and expert investigators understand it — so there is no occasion for the fault stated in the alternative of sequential causal efficacy.

children.text: nāpy akṣaṇike yaugapadyapakṣoktadoṣāvakāśaḥ | ye hi kāryam utpāditavanto dravyaviśeṣās teṣāṃ vyāpārasya niyatakāryotpādanasamarthasya niṣpādite kārye 'nuvartamāneṣv api teṣu dravyeṣu nivṛttārthādūnā sāmagrī jāyate | tat kathaṃ niṣpāditaṃ niṣpādayiṣyati | na hi daṇḍādayaḥ svabhāvenaiva kartāro yenāmī niṣpatter ārabhya kāryaṃ vidadhyuḥ | kiṃ tarhi vyāpārāveśinaḥ | na ceyatā svarūpeṇa na kartāraḥ, svarūpakārakatvanirvāhaparatayā vyāpārasamāveśād iti ||
children.translated_text: Nor is there occasion for the fault stated in the alternative of simultaneous [production] with respect to a non-momentary [entity]. For those specific substances that have produced an effect — when their operation, which was capable of producing the specific effect, has accomplished the effect, even though those substances persist, an aggregate deficient by one [factor] whose purpose is fulfilled arises. How then will it produce what has [already] been produced? For sticks and the like are not producers by their very nature alone, such that they would effect the product from the very beginning. Rather, they are [producers] by the entry of [their] operation. And it is not that they are not producers by their own nature, since the entry of the operation is for the purpose of accomplishing their role as producers by their own nature.

children.text: kiṃ ca kramākramābhāvaś ca bhaviṣyati na ca sattvābhāva iti sandigdhavyatireko 'py ayaṃ vyāpakānupalambhaḥ | na hi kramākramābhyām anyasya prakārasyābhāvaḥ siddhaḥ, viśeṣaniṣedhasya śeṣābhyanujñāviṣayatvāt |
children.translated_text: Moreover, this non-apprehension of the pervader (<s>vyāpakānupalabdhi</s>) is of doubtful negative concomitance — because there will be the absence of both sequential and simultaneous [production], but not the absence of existence. For the absence of some other mode [of production] beyond sequential and simultaneous has not been established, since a particular negation is the domain of permission of the remainder.

children.text: kiṃ ca prakārāntarasya dṛśyatve nātyantaniṣedhaḥ | adṛśyatve tu nāsattāniścayo viprakarṣiṇām iti na kramākramābhyām arthakriyāsāmarthyasya vyāptisidhiḥ | ataḥ sandigdhavyatireko 'pi vyāpakānupalambhaḥ |
children.translated_text: Furthermore, if that other mode is perceptible, there is no absolute negation [of it]. If imperceptible, then for those who are far removed [from direct knowledge], there is no certainty of its non-existence — thus the pervasion of causal efficacy by sequential-or-simultaneous [production] is not established. Therefore, even this non-apprehension of the pervader is of doubtful negative concomitance.

children.text: kiṃ ca dṛśyādṛśyasahakāripratyayasākalyavataḥ kramayaugapadyasyātyantaparokṣatvāt tena vyāptaṃ sattvam api parokṣam eveti na tāvat pratibandhaḥ pratyakṣataḥ sidhyati | nāpy anumānataḥ tatpratibaddhaliṅgābhāvād iti |
children.translated_text: Moreover, since sequential-and-simultaneous [production], for an entity possessing the totality of visible and invisible auxiliary conditions, is entirely imperceptible, existence (<s>sattva</s>) too, being pervaded by it, would be imperceptible — hence the invariable connection (<s>pratibandha</s>) is not established through perception. Nor through inference, because there is no logical mark that is necessarily connected with it.

children.text: api ca kramākramābhyām arthakriyākāritvaṃ vyāptam ity atisubhāṣitam | yadi krameṇa vyāptaṃ katham akrameṇa | athākrameṇa na tarhi krameṇa | kramākramābhyām vyāptam iti tu bruvatā vyāpter evābhāvaḥ pradarśito bhavati | na hi bhavati dhūmo vahnibhāvābhāvābhyāṃ vyāpta iti | ato vyāpter anaikāntikatvam |
children.translated_text: Furthermore, [the claim that] 'causal efficacy is pervaded by sequential-and-simultaneous [production]' is extremely well-spoken [i.e., ironically, absurd]! If pervaded by sequential [production], how by simultaneous? If by simultaneous, then not by sequential. And by saying 'pervaded by both sequential and simultaneous,' one demonstrates the very absence of pervasion. For one does not say 'smoke is pervaded by the presence-and-absence of fire.' Therefore, due to [the absence of] pervasion, [the reason is] inconclusive.

children.text: capi ca kim idaṃ bādhakam akṣaṇikānām asattāṃ sādhayati, utasvid akṣaṇikāt sattvasya vyatirekam, atha sattvakṣaṇikatvayoḥ pratibandham.
children.translated_text: And what does this defeating [argument] establish? Does it establish the non-existence of non-momentary entities, or the exclusion of existence (<s>sattva</s>) from non-momentary entities, or the invariable connection between existence and momentariness?

children.text: na pūrvo vikalpaḥ, uktakrameṇa hetor āśrayāsiddhatvāt |
children.translated_text: Not the first alternative, because the reason has the defect of an unestablished locus, as stated.

children.text: na ca dvitīyaḥ. yato vyāpakanivṛttisahitā vyāpyanivṛttir vyatirekaśabdasyārthaḥ. sā ca yadi pratyakṣeṇa pratīyate tadā taddhetuḥ syād iti sattvam anaikāntikam. vyāpakānupalambhaḥ svarūpāsiddhaḥ.  atha sā vikalpyate tadā pūrvoktakrameṇa pañcadhā vikalpya vikalpo dūṣaṇīyaḥ.
children.translated_text: Nor the second. For the meaning of the word 'negative concomitance' (<s>vyatireka</s>) is the cessation of the pervaded accompanied by the cessation of the pervader. If that is cognized through perception, then [existence] would be [directly] its cause — so existence would be inconclusive [as a reason]. [And] the non-apprehension of the pervader would be unestablished in its own nature. If, on the other hand, it is conceptually imagined, then, following the method stated above, it should be examined and refuted by dividing the conceptual alternative into five [sub-alternatives].

children.text: ata eva na tṛtīyo 'pi vikalpaḥ vyatirekāsiddhau sambandhāsiddheḥ |
children.translated_text: For this very reason, the third alternative too does not hold — because when the negative concomitance is unestablished, the necessary connection is also unestablished.

children.text: kiṃ ca na bhūtalavad atrākṣaṇiko dharmī dṛśyate | na ca svabhāvānupalambhe vyāpakānupalambhaḥ kasyacit dṛśyasya pratipattim antareṇāntarbhāvayituṃ śakyata iti |
children.translated_text: Moreover, unlike the case of the ground [as a subject], no non-momentary entity is observed here as a logical subject (<s>dharmin</s>). And the non-apprehension of the essential nature [of such an entity] cannot be subsumed under the non-apprehension of the pervader without the apprehension of something visible.

children.text: kiṃ cāsyābhāvadharmatve āśrayāsiddhatvam itaretarāśrayatvaṃ ca | bhāvadharmatve viruddhatvaṃ ca | ubhayadharmatve cānaikāntikatvam iti na trayīṃ doṣajātim atipatati |
children.translated_text: Moreover, if [the reason] has a non-existent entity as its subject, there is the defect of unestablished locus and mutual dependence. If it has an existent entity as its subject, there is contradiction. If it has both as its subject, there is inconclusiveness — thus it does not escape the triad of defects.

children.text: yat punar uktam akṣaṇikatve kramayaugapadyābhyām arthakriyāvirodhād iti | dtatra virodhasiddhim anusaratā virodhy api pratipattavyaḥ | tatpratītināntarīyakatvād virodhasiddheḥ | yathā tuhinadahanayoḥ sāpekṣadhruvabhāvayoś ca |
children.translated_text: As for the statement that 'in the case of non-momentariness, there is a contradiction with causal efficacy through both sequential and simultaneous [modes]' — one who follows the establishment of contradiction must also acknowledge the counter-positive (<s>virodhin</s>), since the establishment of contradiction is inseparable from the apprehension of that [counter-positive]. Just as in the case of frost and fire, and in the case of entities that are permanent with dependence [on conditions].

children.text: pratiyogī cākṣaṇikaḥ pratīyamānaḥ pratītikāritvāt sann eva syāt, ajanakasyāprameyatvāt |
children.translated_text: And the counter-positive — the non-momentary [entity] — when apprehended, would be existent, because of its causal efficacy in producing apprehension, since what is non-productive is not provable.

children.text: saṃvṛtisiddhenākṣaṇikatvena virodhasiddhir iti cet | saṃvṛtisiddham api vāstavaṃ kālpanikaṃ vā syāt |
children.translated_text: [Objection:] The contradiction is established through non-momentariness established conventionally (<s>saṃvṛtisiddha</s>). [Reply:] Even what is conventionally established would be either real or imagined.

children.text: yadi vāstavaṃ kathaṃ tasyāsattvam | kathaṃ cārthakriyākāritvavirodhaḥ | arthakriyāṃ kurvad dhi vāstavam ucyate |
children.translated_text: If real, how can it be non-existent? And how can there be a contradiction with causal efficacy? For that which performs causal activity is called 'real.'

children.text: atha kālpanikam | tatra kiṃ virodho vāstavaḥ, kālpaniko vā | na tāvad vāstavaḥ, kalpitavirodhivirodhatvāt, bandhyāputravirodhavat | atha virodho 'pi kālpanikaḥ na tarhi sattvasya vyatirekaḥ pāramārthika iti kṣaṇabhaṅgo dattajalāñjalir iti |
children.translated_text: If imagined: then is the contradiction real or imagined? Not real, because its opposite is imagined — like a contradiction with the son of a barren woman. If the contradiction too is imagined, then the exclusion of existence [from the non-momentary] is not ultimately real — and so momentariness has bowed farewell [i.e., is abandoned].

children.text:
ayam eva codyaprabandho 'smadgurubhiḥ saṅgṛhītaḥ |
	  enityaṃ nāsti na vā pratītiviṣayaṃ3 tenāśrayāsiddhatā 
	  hetoḥ svānubhavasya ca kṣatir ataḥ kṣiptaḥ sapakṣo 'pi ca |
	  śūnyaś ca dvitayena sidhyati na cāsattāpi sattā yathā 
	  no nityena virodhasiddhir asatā śakyā kramāder api || J 89,16-19; cf. R 94,21-24
	  iti |
children.translated_text: This very chain of objections has been summarized by our teachers: 'The permanent either does not exist or is not an object of apprehension — hence the locus of the reason is unestablished, and one's own experience is damaged; therefore the positive example is also overthrown. And being empty of both, non-existence too is not established — just as existence [is not established]. Nor can contradiction with the sequential and the like be established through a permanent [entity], since it is non-existent.'

children.text: atrocyate – iha vastuny api dharmidharmavyavahāro dṛṣṭaḥ, yathā gavi gotvam, paṭe śuklatvam, turage gamanam ityādi. avastuny api dharmidharmavyavahāro dṛṣṭaḥ, yathā śaśaviṣāṇe tīkṣṇatvābhāvaḥ, bandhyāputre vaktṛtvābhāvaḥ, gaganāravinde gandhābhāva ityādi. tatrāvastuni dharmitvaṃ nāstīti kiṃ vastudharmeṇa dharmitvaṃ nāsti, āhosvid avastudharmeṇāpi |
children.translated_text: To this we reply: In this [world], the subject-property convention (<s>dharmidharmavyavahāra</s>) is observed even with respect to real entities — as in 'cow-ness in a cow,' 'whiteness in cloth,' 'movement in a horse,' and so forth. The subject-property convention is also observed with respect to non-entities — as in 'absence of sharpness in a hare's horn,' 'absence of speech in the son of a barren woman,' 'absence of fragrance in a sky-lotus,' and so forth. With respect to the [claim that] non-entities cannot serve as subjects: does this mean they cannot serve as subjects with respect to real properties, or that they cannot serve as subjects even with respect to non-real properties?

children.text:
prathamapakṣe siddhasādhanam. dvitīyapakṣe tu svavacanavirodhaḥ. yad āhur guravaḥ –
	  fdharmasya kasyacid avastuni mānasiddhā 
	  bādhāvidhivyavahṛtiḥ kim ihāsti no vā | 
	  kvāpy asti cet katham iyanti na dūṣaṇāni 
	  nāsty eva cet svavacanapratirodhasiddhiḥ || J 89,21-24; cf. R 94,26-28
children.translated_text: In the first alternative, [the objection] proves what is already established (<s>siddhasādhana</s>). In the second alternative, there is a contradiction with one's own statement. As our teachers say: 'Is or is not a convention of contradiction, sublation, or positive determination — establishing some property — established by valid cognition with respect to a non-entity? If it is [established] somewhere, how [can you claim] these manifold objections? If it is not at all, then the self-contradiction of your own statement is established.'

children.text: avastuno dharmitvasvīkārapūrvakatvasya vyāpakasyābhāvād āśrayāsiddhidūṣaṇasyānupanyāsaprasaṅga ity arthaḥ | yenaiva hi vacanenāvastuno dharmitvaṃ pratiṣidhyate, tenaivāvastuno dharmitvābhāvena dharmeṇa dharmitvam abhyupagatam | paran tu pratiṣidhyata iti vyaktam idam īśvaraceṣṭitam | tathā hy avastuno dharmitvaṃ nāstīti vacanena dharmitvābhāvaḥ kim avastuni vidhīyate, anyatra vā, na vā kvacid apīti trayaḥ pakṣāḥ |
children.translated_text: The meaning is: since the pervader — namely, [the convention] being preceded by the acceptance of the non-entity's subject-hood — is absent, there would be the consequence of not being able to raise even the objection of unestablished locus. For by the very statement by which the subject-hood of a non-entity is denied, by that very [statement] the subject-hood of the non-entity is accepted — namely, through the property of the absence of subject-hood. But the other [the subject-hood itself] is being denied — this is clearly the play of the Lord! For thus: by the statement 'a non-entity cannot serve as a subject,' is the absence of subject-hood predicated of the non-entity, or of something else, or of nothing at all? — these are three alternatives.

children.text: prathamapakṣe 'vastuno na dharmitvaniṣedhaḥ dharmitvābhāvasya dharmasya tatraiva vidhānāt |
children.translated_text: In the first alternative, the denial of subject-hood with respect to the non-entity [fails], since the property of absence of subject-hood is predicated of that very [non-entity].

children.text: dvitīye 'vastuni kim āyātam anyatra dharmitvābhāvavidhānāt |
children.translated_text: In the second [alternative], what harm comes to the non-entity from the predication of the absence of subject-hood with respect to something else?

children.text: tṛtīyas tu pakṣo vyartha eva nirāśrayatvād iti katham avastuno dharmitvaniṣedhaḥ | tasmād yathā pramāṇopanyāsaḥ prameyasvīkārapūrvakatvena vyāptaḥ vācakaśabdopanyāso vā vācyasvīkārapūrvakatvena vyāptas tathāvastuno dharmitvaṃ nāstīti vacanopanyāso 'vastuno dharmitvasvīkārapūrvakatvena vyāptaḥ | anyathā tadvacanopanyāsasya vyarthatvāt |
children.translated_text: The third alternative is simply purposeless, because it has no locus — so how can the subject-hood of a non-entity be denied? Therefore, just as the presentation of a means of valid cognition is pervaded by being preceded by the acceptance of the provable, and just as the presentation of a signifying word is pervaded by being preceded by the acceptance of the signified, so too the presentation of the statement 'a non-entity cannot serve as a subject' is pervaded by being preceded by the acceptance of the non-entity's subject-hood. Otherwise, the presentation of that statement would be purposeless.

children.text: tad yadi vacanopanyāso vyāpyadharmas tadā 'vastuno dharmitvasvīkāro 'pi vyāpakadharmo durvāraḥ | atha na vyāpakadharmaḥ tadā vyāpyasyāpi vacanopanyāsasyāsambhava iti mūkataivātra balād āyāteti kathaṃ na svavacanapratirodhasiddhiḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus, if the presentation of the statement is the pervaded property, then the acceptance of the non-entity's subject-hood is also the pervader property and is unavoidable. If, however, it is not the pervader property, then even the possibility of the pervaded property — the presentation of the statement — would be impossible, and so muteness is forcibly brought upon [the opponent] — how then is there no self-contradiction?

children.text: yad āhācāryaḥ: na hy abruvan paraṃ bodhayitum īśaḥ | bruvan vā doṣam imaṃ parihartum iti mahati saṃkaṭe praveśaḥ |
children.translated_text: As the <s>Ācārya</s> (teacher) says: 'For one who does not speak cannot enlighten the opponent. And one who speaks cannot escape this defect — so he enters into a great predicament.'

children.text:
avastuprastāve sahṛdayānāṃ mūkataiva yujyata iti cet | aho
	  mahadvaidagdhyam | avastuprastāve svayam eva yathāśakti valgitvā
	  bhagno mūkataiva nyāyaprāpteti paribhāṣayā niḥsartum icchati | na
	  cāvastuprastāvo rājadaṇḍena vinā caraṇamardanādināniṣṭimātreṇa vā
	  pratiṣeddhaṃ śakyate | tataś cātrāpi kramākramabhāvasya sādhanatve
	  sattvābhāvasya ca sādhyatve sandigdhavastubhāvasyāvastvātmano vā
	  kṣaṇikasya dharmitvaṃ kena pratiṣidhyate |
children.translated_text: [Objection:] When the topic is a non-entity, the appropriate response for the discerning is simply silence. [Reply:] Ah, what great cleverness! Having yourself pranced about to the best of your ability on the topic of non-entities, [and now] being defeated, you wish to escape by declaring 'silence is the proper course'! But the topic of non-entities cannot be prohibited merely by displeasure or by the treading of feet, without [the threat of] a royal rod. And so, even here, when the presence or absence of sequential-and-simultaneous [production] is the proof, and the absence of existence is the thesis, what prevents the subject-hood of the momentary [entity] — which is of doubtful real existence or of non-real nature?

children.text: trividho hi dharmo dṛṣṭaḥ | kaścit vastuniyato nīlādiḥ | kaścid avastuniyato yathā sarvopākhyāvirahaḥ | kaścid ubhayasādhāraṇo yathā 'nupalabdhimātram | tatra vastudharmeṇāvastuno dharmitvaniṣedha iti yuktam | na tv avastudharmeṇa vastvavastudharmeṇa vā, svavacanasyānupanyāsaprasaṅgād ity akṣaṇikasyābhāve sandehe 'pi vā vastudharmeṇa dharmitvam avyāhatam iti nāyam āśrayāsiddho vyāpakānupalambhaḥ |
children.translated_text: For a threefold [classification of] properties is observed: some are restricted to real entities, such as blue and the like; some are restricted to non-entities, such as the absence of all designations; and some are common to both, such as mere non-apprehension. Among these, the denial of subject-hood of a non-entity through a real property is justified. But not through a property [restricted to] non-entities, or through a property common to both real and non-real entities — because there would be the consequence of not being able to present one's own statement. Therefore, whether a non-momentary [entity] is non-existent or doubtful, its subject-hood through a real property is unimpaired — so this non-apprehension of the pervader does not have the defect of unestablished locus.

children.text: akṣaṇikāpratītāv āśrayāsiddho hetur iti yuktam uktam, tadapratītau tadvyavahārāyogāt | kevalam asau vyavahārāṅgabhūtā pratītir vastvavastunor ekarūpā na bhavati | sākṣāt pāramparyeṇa vastusāmarthyabhāvinī hi vastupratītiḥ | yathā pratyakṣam anumānaṃ pratyakṣapṛṣṭhabhāvī ca vikalpaḥ | avastunas tu sāmarthyābhāvād vikalpamātram eva pratītiḥ | vastuno hi vastubalabhāvinī pratītir yathā sākṣāt pratyakṣam, paramparayā tatpṛṣṭhabhāvī vikalpo 'numānaṃ ca | avastunas tu na vastubalabhāvinī pratītis tatkārakatvenāvastutvahāniprasaṅgāt | tasmād vikalpamātram evāvastunaḥ pratītiḥ |
children.translated_text: It has been rightly stated that the <s>hetu</s> (logical reason) is <s>āśrayāsiddha</s> (unestablished in its substratum) when the <s>akṣaṇika</s> (non-momentary) is not apprehended, since in the absence of its apprehension, practical usage regarding it would be impossible. However, this apprehension (<s>pratīti</s>), which is a component of practical usage, is not of a single form for <s>vastu</s> (real entities) and <s>avastu</s> (non-entities). For the cognition of a real entity arises from the capacity of the real entity itself, either directly or indirectly — such as <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception), <s>anumāna</s> (inference), and <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual cognition) that arises subsequent to perception. But for a non-entity, due to the absence of [such] capacity, the apprehension is through <s>vikalpa</s> alone. For regarding a real entity, the cognition arises from the power of the real entity — directly as <s>pratyakṣa</s>, and indirectly as <s>vikalpa</s> and <s>anumāna</s> that arise subsequent to it. But for a non-entity, the cognition does not arise from the power of a real entity, since if it were caused by [a real entity], there would be the undesirable consequence of it losing its status as a non-entity. Therefore, the apprehension of a non-entity is through <s>vikalpa</s> alone.

children.text: na hy abhāvaḥ kaścid vigrahavān yaḥ sākṣāt kartavyo 'pi tu vyavahartavyaḥ | sa ca vyavahāro vikalpād api sidhyaty eva anyathā sarvajanaprasiddho 'vastuvyavahāro na syāt | iṣyate ca taddharmitvapratiṣedhānubandhād ity akāmakenāpi vikalpamātrasiddho 'kṣaṇikaḥ svīkartavya iti nāyam apratītatvād apy āśrayāsiddho hetur vaktavyaḥ | tataś cākṣaṇikasya vikalpamātrasiddhatve yad uktam |
children.translated_text: For absence (<s>abhāva</s>) is not some embodied thing that must be directly perceived; rather, it is to be dealt with through practical usage. And that practical usage is accomplished even through <s>vikalpa</s> alone — otherwise the universally recognized practical usage regarding non-entities would not exist. And since this is accepted because of the connection with the denial of its being a <s>dharmin</s> (subject of inference), even unwillingly one must accept that the <s>akṣaṇika</s> is established through <s>vikalpa</s> alone. Therefore, this <s>hetu</s> should not be called <s>āśrayāsiddha</s> on the grounds of non-apprehension. And given that the <s>akṣaṇika</s> is established through <s>vikalpa</s> alone, what was stated —

children.text: na kaścid dhetur anāśrayaḥ vikalpamātrasiddhasya dharmiṇaḥ sarvatra sulabhatvād iti tad asaṅgatam | vikalpamātrasiddhasya dharmiṇaḥ sarvatra sambhave 'pi vastudharmeṇa dharmitvāyogāt | vastudharmahetutvāpekṣayā āśrayāsiddhasyāpi hetoḥ sambhavāt |
children.translated_text: — that no <s>hetu</s> is without a substratum, because a <s>dharmin</s> established through <s>vikalpa</s> alone is readily available everywhere — that is irrelevant. For even though a <s>dharmin</s> established through <s>vikalpa</s> alone is possible everywhere, it cannot serve as a <s>dharmin</s> with respect to a property of a real entity (<s>vastudharma</s>). Because with respect to a <s>hetu</s> that is a property of a real entity, the <s>hetu</s> can indeed be <s>āśrayāsiddha</s>.

children.text: yathātmano vibhutvasādhanārtham upanyastaṃ sarvatropalabhyamānaguṇatvād iti sādhanam | vikalpaś cāyaṃ hetūpanyāsāt pūrvaṃ sandigdhavastukaḥ | samarthite tu hetāv avastuka iti brūmaḥ |
children.translated_text: For example, the proof adduced for establishing the omnipresence of the <s>ātman</s> (self) — 'because it has qualities that are apprehended everywhere' — is such a means of proof (<s>sādhana</s>). And this <s>vikalpa</s> [regarding the self] has a doubtful real object prior to the presentation of the <s>hetu</s>. But when the <s>hetu</s> is validated, we declare it to be without a real object (<s>avastuka</s>).

children.text: na cātra sandigdhāśrayatvaṃ nāma hetudośaḥ | āstāṃ tāvat | sandigdhasyāvastuno 'pi vikalpamātrasiddhasyāvastudharmāpekṣayā dharmitvaprasādhanāt | vastudharmahetvapekṣayaiva sandigdhāśrayasya hetvābhāsasya vyavasthāpanāt | yatheha nikuñje mayūraḥ kekāyitād iti | avastukavikalpaviṣayasyāsattvaṃ tu vyāpakānupalambhād eva prasādhitam | evaṃ dṛṣṭāntasyāpi vyomotpalāder dharmitvaṃ vikalpamātreṇa pratītiś cāvagantavyā | tad evam avastudharmāpekṣāyāvastuno dharmitvasya vikalpamātreṇa pratīteś cāpahnotum aśakyatvān nāyam āśrayāsiddho hetuḥ | na ca dṛṣṭāntakṣatiḥ |
children.translated_text: Nor is doubtful substratum (<s>sandigdhāśrayatva</s>) a defect of the <s>hetu</s> here. Let that be set aside for now. Because even for a non-entity of doubtful [status], established through <s>vikalpa</s> alone, its being a <s>dharmin</s> is demonstrated with respect to a property of a non-entity. And the fallacious <s>hetu</s> of doubtful substratum is to be established only with respect to a <s>hetu</s> that is a property of a real entity. For example, 'there is a peacock in this thicket, because of the cry' [could have a doubtful substratum]. But the non-existence of the object of a <s>vikalpa</s> concerning a non-entity has been established precisely through the non-apprehension of the pervader (<s>vyāpakānupalambha</s>). Similarly, the <s>dharmin</s>-status and the apprehension through <s>vikalpa</s> alone of the example (<s>dṛṣṭānta</s>) such as a sky-lotus and the like should also be understood [in the same way]. Thus, since it cannot be denied that a non-entity has <s>dharmin</s>-status with respect to non-entity properties, and that its apprehension is through <s>vikalpa</s> alone, this <s>hetu</s> is not <s>āśrayāsiddha</s>. Nor is there any deficiency in the example.

children.text: na caiṣa svarūpāsiddhaḥ, akṣaṇike dharmiṇi kramākramayor vyāpakayor ayogāt | tathā hi yadi tasya prathame kṣaṇe dvitīyādikṣaṇabhāvikāryakaraṇasāmarthyam asti tadā prathamakṣaṇabhāvikāryavat dvitīyādikṣaṇabhāvy api kāryaṃ kuryāt, samarthasya kṣepāyogāt |
children.translated_text: Nor is this [<s>hetu</s>] unestablished in its own nature (<s>svarūpāsiddha</s>), because in a non-momentary <s>dharmin</s>, neither sequential nor simultaneous [causal efficacy] is possible. For if it possesses, at the first moment, the capacity to produce the effect occurring at the second and subsequent moments, then it should produce the effect occurring at the second and subsequent moments just as it does the effect at the first moment, since it is impossible for a capable [entity] to delay.

children.text: atha tadā sahakārisākalyalakṣaṇasāmarthyaṃ nāsti, tadvaikalyalakṣaṇasyāsāmarthyasya sambhavāt | na hi bhāvaḥ svarūpeṇa karotīti svarūpeṇaiva karoti, sahakārisahitād eva tataḥ kāryotpattidarśanād iti cet |
children.translated_text: [Objection:] But at that [first moment] the capacity characterized by the completeness of cooperating conditions (<s>sahakārisākalya</s>) is not present, because there can be incapacity characterized by their incompleteness. For an entity does not act by its own nature alone — rather, it acts precisely through its own nature [only together with cooperating conditions], since the production of an effect is observed only from [a cause] together with cooperating conditions.

children.text: yadā tāvad amī militāḥ santaḥ kāryaṃ kurvate | tadaikārthakaraṇalakṣaṇaṃ sahakāritvam eṣām astu, ko niṣeddhā | militair eva tu tatkāryaṃ kartavyam iti kuto labhyate | pūrvāparakālayor ekasvabhāvatvād bhāvasya sarvadā jananājananayor anyataraniyamaprasaṅgasya durvāratvāt | tasmāt sāmagrī janikā, naikaṃ janakam iti sthiravādināṃ manorajyasyāpy aviṣayaḥ |
children.translated_text: When these [factors], being assembled together, produce an effect, let their cooperative character (<s>sahakāritva</s>), defined as joint action toward a single purpose, be accepted — who would deny it? But from where is it obtained that the effect must be produced only by those assembled [factors]? Since the entity has the same nature at earlier and later times, the undesirable consequence that it must either always produce or never produce cannot be avoided. Therefore, 'the aggregate (<s>sāmagrī</s>) is the producer, no single [entity] is the producer' — even the fantasy of the proponents of permanence (<s>sthiravādin</s>s) cannot encompass this.

children.text: kiṃ kurmo dṛśyate tāvad evam iti cet | dṛśyatāṃ, kiṃ tu pūrvasthitād eva paścāt sāmagrīmadhyapraviṣṭād bhāvāt kāryotpattir anyasmād eva viśiṣṭasāmagrīsamutpannāt kṣaṇād iti vivādapadam etat | tatra prāg api sambhave sarvadaiva kāryotpattir na vā kadācid apīti virodham asamādhāya tata eva kāryotpattir iti sādhyānuvādamātrapravṛttaḥ kṛpām arhati |
children.translated_text: [Objection:] What can we do? This is simply what is observed. [Reply:] Let it be observed, but whether the production of the effect comes from the very same entity that existed before and subsequently entered into the aggregate, or from an entirely different moment born from the distinctive aggregate — this is the point of dispute. Without resolving the contradiction that if [an entity] is capable even before [joining the aggregate], the effect should always be produced, or else never at all — one who merely restates the thesis by asserting that the effect arises from that [permanent entity] alone deserves compassion.

children.text: na ca pratyabhijñānād evaikatvasiddhiḥ, tatpauruṣasya lūnapunarjātakeśakuśakadalīstambādau nirdalanāt | vistareṇa ca pratyabhijñādūṣaṇam asmābhiḥ sthirasiddhidūṣaṇe pratipāditam iti tata evāvadhāryam |
children.translated_text: Nor is the unity [of the entity at different times] established through recognition (<s>pratyabhijñā</s>) alone, since the cogency of that [recognition] is refuted in cases such as hair that has been cut and regrown, and <s>kuśa</s> grass and plantain stalks [that regenerate]. And the detailed refutation of recognition has been presented by us in the <s>Sthirasiddhidūṣaṇa</s> (Refutation of the Proof of Permanence), so it should be ascertained from there.

children.text: nanu kāryam eva sahakāriṇam apekṣate | na tu kāryotpattihetuḥ | yasmād dvividhaṃ sāmarthyaṃ nijam āgantukaṃ ca sahakāryantaram tato akṣaṇikasyāpi kramavatsahakārinānātvād api kramavatkāryanānātvam iti cet |
children.translated_text: [Objection:] But it is only the effect that depends on cooperating conditions, not the cause of the effect's production. Since there are two kinds of capacity — intrinsic (<s>nija</s>) and extrinsic (<s>āgantuka</s>) — and since the cooperating conditions are another [extrinsic factor], even for a non-momentary [entity], the diversity of effects in sequence follows from the diversity of cooperating conditions in sequence.

children.text: bhavatu tāvat nijāgantukabhedena dvividhaṃ sāmarthyam | tathāpi tat prātisvikaṃ vastusvalakṣaṇaṃ sadyaḥ kriyādharmakam avaśyābhyupagantavyam | tad yadi prāg api, prāg api kāryaprasaṅgaḥ | atha paścād eva, na tadā sthiro bhāvaḥ |
children.translated_text: Let there be two kinds of capacity, distinguished as intrinsic and extrinsic. Even so, that [capacity] must necessarily be accepted as the particular real nature (<s>vastusvalakṣaṇa</s>) of each individual entity, having the character of immediate activity (<s>sadyaḥ kriyā</s>). If that [capacity] exists even before [the cooperating conditions arrive], then the effect should arise even before. But if it exists only afterwards, then the entity is not permanent.

children.text: na ca kāryaṃ sahakariṇo 'pekṣata iti yuktam, tasyāsattvāt | hetuś ca sann api yadi svakāryaṃ na karoti, tadā tatkāryam eva tan na syāt, svātantryāt |
children.translated_text: Nor is it correct to say that the effect depends on cooperating conditions, since [the effect, prior to its arising,] is non-existent. And if the cause, even while existing, does not produce its own effect, then that would not be its effect at all, due to [the cause's] independence.

children.text: yac coktam – yo hi uttarakāryajananasvabhāvaḥ sa katham ādau kāryaṃ kuryāt, atha kuryāt na tarhi tatkāryakaraṇasvabhāvaḥ, na hi nīlotpādanasvabhāvaḥ pītādikam api karotīti tad asaṅgatam | sthirasvabhāvatve bhāvasyottarakālam evedaṃ na pūrvakālam iti kuta etat | tadabhāvāc ca kāraṇam apy uttarakāryasvabhāvam ity api kutaḥ |
children.translated_text: And what was said — 'that which has the nature of producing a later effect, how could it produce an effect at the beginning? And if it could, then it would not have the nature of producing that [specific later] effect, for that which has the nature of producing blue does not also produce yellow and so forth' — that is irrelevant. If the entity has a permanent nature, on what basis [can one say] 'this [occurs] only at the later time, not at the earlier time'? And in the absence of that [basis], how can one say that the cause has the nature of [producing] the later effect?

children.text: kiṃ kurmaḥ, uttarakālam eva tasya janmeti cet | sthiratve tadanupapadyamānam asthiratām ādiśatu | sthiratve 'py eṣa eva svabhāvas tasya yad uttarakṣaṇa eva kāryaṃ karotīti cet | na | pramāṇabādhite svabhāvābhyupagamāyogād iti na tāvad akṣaṇikasya kramikāryakāritvam asti | nāpy akramikāryakāritvasambhavaḥ, dvitīye 'pi kṣaṇe kārakasvarūpasadbhāve punar api kāryakaraṇaprasaṅgāt |
children.translated_text: [Objection:] What can we do? It is simply born at the later time. [Reply:] If that cannot be explained under [the assumption of] permanence, let it point to impermanence. [Objection:] Even under permanence, this is simply its nature — that it produces the effect only at the later moment. [Reply:] No, because it is improper to accept a nature that is contradicted by valid cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>). Thus, the <s>akṣaṇika</s> does not possess the capacity to produce effects sequentially. Nor is simultaneous causal efficacy possible, because if the cause's own nature persists even at the second moment, there would be the undesirable consequence of producing the effect yet again.

children.text: kārye niṣpanne tadviṣayavyāpārābhāvād ūnā sāmagrī na niṣpāditaṃ niṣpādayed iti cet | na | sāmagrīsambhavāsambhavayor api sadyaḥ kriyākārakasvarūpasambhave janakatvam avāryam iti prāg eva pratipādanāt | kāryasya hi niṣpāditatvāt punaḥ kartum aśakyatvam eva kāraṇam asamartham āvedayati |
children.translated_text: [Objection:] Once the effect has been accomplished, there is no activity directed toward that [already produced] object, so the incomplete aggregate would not produce what has already been produced. [Reply:] No, because it has already been demonstrated that when the causal nature of immediate activity is present, its productive capacity cannot be obstructed regardless of whether the aggregate is present or absent. For the very fact that the effect, having been accomplished, cannot be produced again reveals that the cause is incapable [of further production].

children.text: tad ayam akṣaṇike kramākramikāryakāritvābhāvo na siddhaḥ | na ca kramākramābhyām aparaprakārasambhavo yena tābhyām avyāptau sandigdhavyatireko hetuḥ syāt | prakārāntaraśaṅkāyāṃ tasyāpi dṛśyatvādṛśyatvaprakāradvayadūṣaṇe 'pi svapakṣe 'py anāśvāsaprasaṅgāt | tasmād anyonyavyavacchedasthitayor nāparaḥ prakāraḥ sambhavati | svarūpāpraviṣṭasya vastuno 'vastuno vātatsvabhāvatvāt | prakārāntarasyāpi kramasvarūpāpraviṣṭatvāt | tathātīndriyasya sahakāriṇo 'dṛśyatve 'py ayogavyavacchedena dṛśyasahakārisahitasya dṛśyasyaiva sattvasya dṛśyakramākramābhyāṃ vyāptiḥ pratyakṣād eva sidhyati | evaṃ kramākramābhyām arthakriyākāritvaṃ vyāptam iti kramākramayor anyonyavyavacchedena sthitatvād etatprakāradvayaparihāreṇārthakriyākāritvam anyatra na gatam ity arthaḥ | ata evaitayor vinivṛttau nivartate ||
children.translated_text: Thus, the absence of both sequential and simultaneous causal efficacy in the <s>akṣaṇika</s> has not been established [by the opponent]. Nor is there any third alternative besides sequential and simultaneous, such that the <s>hetu</s> would have a doubtful negative concomitance due to non-pervasion by those two. If a suspicion of another alternative were raised, since refuting that [alternative] through the two modes of visible and invisible would lead to the undesirable consequence of uncertainty in one's own position as well — therefore, no other alternative is possible for [things] that exist through mutual exclusion. For anything not included in the nature of a <s>vastu</s> or an <s>avastu</s> would not have that nature at all. And any other alternative would likewise not be included in the nature of sequence. Similarly, even though a supersensory cooperating condition may be invisible, through the method of exclusion of the impossible (<s>ayogavyavaccheda</s>), the <s>vyāpti</s> (invariable concomitance) of existent things — which are visible when accompanied by visible cooperating conditions — with visible sequential and simultaneous [modes] is established from <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception) itself. Thus, since causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyākāritva</s>) is pervaded by sequential and simultaneous [modes], and since these two stand through mutual exclusion, by the elimination of these two modes, causal efficacy has nowhere else to go — this is the meaning. Therefore, when both of these are negated, [causal efficacy] ceases.

children.text: trilocanasyā
children.translated_text: Of <s>Trilocana</s>,

children.text: pi vikalpatraye prathamadūṣaṇam āśrayāsiddhidoṣaparihārato nirastam |
