children.text: viruddhānaikāntikatve ca pūrvam eva hetoḥ parihṛte | tad ataḥ siddham abhāvapramāṇābhimatasyāprāmāṇyam iti |
children.translated_text: And the [charges of] contradiction and inconclusiveness of the reason have already been addressed earlier. Therefore, from this it is established that what is claimed as the <s>pramāṇa</s> of <s>abhāva</s> lacks validity.

children.text: atha vābhāvapramāṇasvarūpam eva nirūpyatām | kaḥ punaḥ pramāṇābhāvātmābhimato bhavatām, kiṃ prasajyavṛttyā pramāṇānutpattimātram, atha vā paryudāsavṛttyā bhāvāntaram | vastvantaram api jaḍarūpaṃ jñānarūpaṃ vā | jñānarūpam api jñānamātrakam ekajñānasaṃsargivastujñānaṃ veti ṣaḍ vikalpāḥ |
children.translated_text: Or alternatively, let the very nature of the <s>pramāṇa</s> of <s>abhāva</s> be examined. What, according to you, is this thing whose nature is the absence of a <s>pramāṇa</s>? Is it, by the mode of simple negation (<s>prasajyavṛtti</s>), merely the non-arising of a <s>pramāṇa</s>? Or, by the mode of implicative negation (<s>paryudāsavṛtti</s>), something else that is a positive entity? And if a positive entity, is it of insentient nature or of cognitive nature? And if of cognitive nature, is it mere cognition, or cognition of an object conjoined with a single cognition? — thus there are six alternatives.

children.text: tatra na tāvan nivṛttirūpo 'bhāvo yujyate | sa khalu nikhilaśaktivikalatayā na kiñcit | yac ca na kiñcit tat katham abhāvaṃ paricchindyāt, tadviṣayaṃ vā jñānaṃ janayet, pratītaṃ vā tat katham iti sarvam andhakāranartanam | yad āhuḥ: na hy abhāvaḥ kasyacit pratipattiḥ pratipattihetur vā tasyāpi kathaṃ pratipattir iti

| nāpi vastvantaratāpakṣe jaḍarūpo 'bhāvaḥ saṅgacchate, tasyābhāvalakṣaṇaprameyaparicchedābhāvāt, paricchedasya jñānadharmatvāt | nāpi jñānamātrasvabhāvo 'bhāvo vaktavyaḥ, deśakālasvabhāvaviprakṛṣṭasyāpi tato 'bhāvaprasaṅgāt, tadapekṣayāpi jñānamātratvāt tasya | athaikajñānasaṃsargivastujñānasvabhāvo 'numanyate tadāstam abhāvapramāṇapratyāśayā, pratyakṣaviśeṣasyaivābhāvanāmakaraṇāt | tasya cāsmābhir dṛśyānupalambhākhyasādhanatvena svīkṛtatvāt | ato na kācid vipratipattir nāma | tasmād abhāvapramāṇasvarūpam api nirūpyamāṇaṃ viśīryata eva | yad apy asya lakṣaṇam uktam
children.translated_text: Nor does the alternative of absence being a positive entity of insentient nature work, because that [insentient entity] lacks the capacity to delimit what is to be known (<s>prameya</s>) as characterized by absence, since delimitation is a property of cognition. Nor can absence be said to have the nature of mere cognition, because even what is remote in space, time, and nature would absurdly be an absence of it [the pot], since even with respect to that [remote thing], there is mere cognition. But if absence is accepted as having the nature of cognition of an object conjoined in a single cognition — then let the hope for a <s>pramāṇa</s> of <s>abhāva</s> be abandoned, because it is merely a particular kind of perception given the name 'absence.' And since that has been accepted by us as a means of proof under the name 'non-apprehension of the visible' (<s>dṛśyānupalambha</s>), there is no disagreement whatsoever. Therefore, the very nature of the <s>pramāṇa</s> of <s>abhāva</s>, when examined, simply disintegrates. And as for the definition that has been stated for it —

Of these, first, absence in the form of sheer negation is not tenable. For that, being devoid of all capacities, is nothing at all. And what is nothing at all — how could it delimit absence, or generate a cognition having it as its object, or how could it be cognized? — all this is a dance in darkness. As they say: 'For absence is neither the cognition of anything nor the cause of any cognition — so how can there be cognition of it either?'

children.text: pratyakṣāder anutpattiḥ pramāṇābhāva ucyate |
children.translated_text: 'The non-arising of perception and the like is called the absence of a <s>pramāṇa</s>'

children.text: (ŚV, abhāva, 11ab)
ityādi, tad api yācitakam aṇḍanam | tasmāt sthitam etat, pramāṇasya sato 'traivāntarbhāvāt pramāṇa eva |
children.translated_text: — and so on, that too is a borrowed ornament. Therefore, this stands established: since a [genuine] <s>pramāṇa</s> that exists [in this case] is subsumed under these very [recognized <s>pramāṇas</s>], it is a <s>pramāṇa</s> [already accepted].

children.text: || pramāṇāntararbhāvaprakaraṇaṃ samāptam ||
children.translated_text: Thus concludes the chapter on the subsumption of other <s>pramāṇas</s> (<s>Pramāṇāntarabhāvaprakaraṇa</s>).

children.text: Vyāptinirṇayaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Vyāptinirṇaya</s> (Determination of Pervasion)

children.text:
iha dahanādinā dhūmāder arthāntarasya
	vyāptis tadutpattilakṣaṇā | sā ca
	viśiṣṭānvayavyatirekagrahaṇapravaṇaviśiṣṭapratyakṣānupalambhasādhaneti
	nyāyaḥ | atra ca bhaṭṭaprabhṛtayo vipratipadyante | tathā hi te
	'gnimati pradeśe dhūmasya bhūyodarśanaṃ tadvyukte ca tathaivādarśanam
	ity anvayavyatirekitvaṃ kalpayām babhūvuḥ |
children.translated_text: Here, the pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>) of smoke and the like by fire and the like — which is characterized by causal origination (<s>tadutpatti</s>) — is established through the means of distinguished perception and non-apprehension, which are directed toward the apprehension of distinguished positive and negative concomitance. And here, <s>Bhaṭṭa</s> [<s>Jayanta</s>] and others disagree. For thus, they formulated [pervasion as] repeated observation of smoke in a locus possessing fire, and likewise its non-observation in [a locus] devoid of that — that is, [the nature of] positive and negative concomitance.

children.text:
nanu bhūyasāpi pravṛtte darśanādarśane
	ghaṭakulaṭādāv upalabdho vyabhicāra iti cet | kim etāvatā tatrāpy
	tatrāpy anumānam astu, tadvad vā dhūmādāv api mā bhūt | prathamapakṣas
	tāvad vyabhicārād eva nirastaḥ | dvitīyo 'pi vyabhicārād eva | na hy
	anyasya vyabhicāre dhūmasya kiñcit | tasmād agnidhūmayor
	avyabhicārasyāsambhave śaktam api tadupapattayaḥ
	tatprasādhakaviśiṣṭapratyakṣānupalambhā vā nānumānopayoginaḥ |
	sambhave vā kiṃ tadutpattyā tadupayoginā viśiṣṭapratyakṣānupalambhena,
	darśanādarśanābhyām evāvyabhicārasiddheḥ | tathā ca Kāśikākāraḥ:
	prācīnānekadarśanajanitasaṃskārasahāyena carameṇa cetasā
	dhūmasyāgniniyatatvaṃ gṛhyata iti ||
children.translated_text: [Objection:] Even when observation and non-observation are multiplied, deviation is found in the case of pots, unchaste women, and the like. [Reply:] What of it? Let there be inference in those cases too in the same way, or let it not exist for smoke and the like either in the same way. The first alternative is already refuted by the very fact of deviation. The second too [is refuted] by deviation itself. For the deviation of something else has nothing to do with smoke. Therefore, when the non-deviation of fire and smoke is impossible, even the resources for establishing it — or the distinguished perception and non-apprehension that would establish it — are not useful for inference. Or, if [non-deviation] is possible, what need is there for the resources of causal origination or for the distinguished perception and non-apprehension that serve it, since non-deviation is established by observation and non-observation alone? And thus the author of the <s>Kāśikā</s> [states]: 'By the final cognition, aided by the latent impressions generated by numerous prior observations, the invariable confinement of smoke to fire is apprehended.'

children.text: trilocanas
children.translated_text: <s>Trilocana</s>

children.text: tv āha: pratyakṣānupalambhayor viśeṣaviṣayatvāt kathaṃ tābhyāṃ sāmānyayoḥ sambandhapratipattiḥ | athānagnivyāvṛttenādhūmavyāvṛttasya sambandhaḥ pratīyata eveti | nanu so 'pi kasya pramāṇasya viṣayaḥ | na tāvat pratyakṣasya, svalakṣaṇaviṣayatvāt tasya | nāpy anumānasya, tasyāpi tatpūrvakatvāt | na ca vyāvṛttyoḥ
children.translated_text: however says: Since perception and non-apprehension have particulars as their objects, how can the relation between universals be cognized through them? [Reply:] But the relation of what is excluded from the non-fire with what is excluded from the non-smoke is indeed cognized. [Objection:] But that too — of which <s>pramāṇa</s> is it the object? Not of perception, because perception has only particulars (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) as its objects. Nor of inference, because that too presupposes [pervasion]. And of the two exclusions,

children.text: (J2 vyāvṛttaḥ)

kaścit sambandhaḥ | atha pratyakṣapṛṣṭhabhāvī vikalpo dṛṣṭe bhede 'bhedam adhyavasyati, tad eva sāmānyam | evam api vikalpānāṃ na vastv eva viṣayaḥ | api tu grāhyākāraḥ | sa ca na vastu | vastu tu teṣāṃ parokṣam eveti, kathaṃ tenāpi sambandhagrahaḥ | asmākaṃ tu bhūyodarśanasahāyena manasā tajjātīyānāṃ sambandho gṛhīto bhavati | ato dhūmo nāgniṃ vyabhicarati | tadvyabhicāre dhūma upādhirahitaṃ sambandham atikrāmed iti hetor vipakṣaśaṅkānivartakaṃ pramāṇam upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptopādhivirahahetur anupalambhākhyaṃ pratyakṣam eva | tataḥ siddhaḥ svābhāvikaḥ sambandhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: there is no relation. [Objection:] But a conceptual cognition (<s>vikalpa</s>) that follows upon perception superimposes non-difference upon what is [actually] different — and that itself is the universal. [Reply:] Even so, the object of conceptual cognitions is not a real entity at all, but rather the apprehended image (<s>grāhyākāra</s>). And that is not a real entity. Real entities are entirely beyond the reach of those [conceptual cognitions] — so how can the relation be apprehended even through that? [Reply:] For us, however, the relation among things of that class is apprehended by the mind aided by repeated observation. Therefore, smoke does not deviate from fire. [The argument is:] were smoke to deviate from fire, it would transgress the relation free from limiting conditions (<s>upādhi</s>) — therefore, the <s>pramāṇa</s> that removes the suspicion of the reason's [presence in] the dissimilar domain is the non-apprehension, which is essentially a perception, having as its reason the absence of a limiting condition that satisfies the criterion of apprehensibility (<s>upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāpta</s>). From this, the natural (<s>svābhāvika</s>) relation is established.

children.text: Cf.

Vācaspates tu prapañcaḥ | tathā hi dhūmādīnāṃ vahnyādibhiḥ svābhāvikaḥ sambandhaḥ | na tu vahnyādīnāṃ dhūmādibhiḥ | te hi vināpi dhūmādibhir upalabhyante | vahnyādayas tu yadārdrendhanasambandham anubhavanti tadā dhūmādibhiḥ sambadhyante | vahnyādīnāṃ tu sphuṭamārdrendhanādyupādhikṛtaḥ sambandho na tu svābhāvikaḥ | tato 'niyataḥ | svābhāvikas tu dhūmādīnāṃ vahnyādibhiḥ sambandhaḥ, tadupādher anupalabhyamānatvāt | kvacid vyabhicārasyādarśanād anupalabhyamānasyāpi kalpanānupapatteḥ | na cādṛśyamāno 'pi darśanānarhatayā sādhakabādhakapramāṇābhāvena sagdihyamāna upādhiḥ sambandhasya svābhāvikatvaṃ pratibadhnātīti yuktam |
children.translated_text: Now, the elaboration of <s>Vācaspati</s> [<s>Miśra</s>]. For thus: the natural relation of smoke and the like is with fire and the like, but not of fire and the like with smoke and the like. For those [fires] are observed even without smoke and the like. But when fires and the like come into contact with moist fuel, then they are related to smoke and the like. The relation of fire and the like is clearly brought about by the limiting condition (<s>upādhi</s>) of moist fuel and the like — it is not natural. Hence it is non-invariable. But the relation of smoke and the like with fire and the like is natural, because no limiting condition for it is apprehended. Because deviation is nowhere observed, and because the postulation of [an <s>upādhi</s>] that is not apprehended is untenable. And it is not reasonable that a limiting condition — which, though unseen, is [merely] doubted due to the absence of establishing and refuting <s>pramāṇas</s>, being undeserving of being seen — should obstruct the naturalness of the relation.

children.text: avaśyaṃ śaṅkayā bhāvyaṃ niyāmakam apaśyatām
(PV I 324cd)

children.translated_text: 'Those who see no determining factor must necessarily entertain doubt'

children.text:
iti tu dattāvakāśā laukikamaryādātikrameṇa śaṅkāpiśācī labdhaprasarā na kvacin nāstīti nāyaṃ kvacit pravarteta | sarvatraiva kasyacid anarthasya kathañcic chaṅkāspadatvāt | anarthaśaṅkāyāś ca prekṣāvatāṃ nivṛttyaṅgatvāt | antataḥ snigdhānnapānopayoge 'pi maraṇadarśanāt | tasmāt prāmāṇikalokayātrām anupālayatā yathādarśanam eva śaṅkanīyam | na tv adṛṣṭapūrvam api | viśeṣasmṛtyapekṣa eva hi saṃśayo nāsmṛter bhavati | na ca smṛtir ananubhūtacare bhavitum arhati | tad uktaṃ Mīmāṃsāvārtikakṛtā: nāśaṅkā niḥpramāṇikā iti |
	tasmād upādhiṃ prayatnenānviṣyanto 'nupalabhamānā nāstīty avagamya svābhāvikatvaṃ sambandhasya niścinumaḥ ||

syād etat | anyasyānyena sahākāraṇena cet  svābhāvikaḥ sambandho bhavet, sarvaṃ sarveṇa svabhāvataḥ sambadhyeta | sarvaṃ sarvasmād gamyeta | athānyasya ced anyat kāryaṃ kasmāt sarvaṃ sarvasmān na bhavati, anyatvāviśeṣāt | tataś ca sa evātiprasaṅgaḥ | yady ucyeta na bhāvasvabhāvāḥ paryanuyojyāḥ, tasmād anyatvāviśeṣe 'pi kiñcid eva kāraṇaṃ kāryaṃ ca kiñcid iti | nanv eṣa svabhāvānām anuyogo bhinnānāṃ akāryakāraṇabhūtānām api svabhāvapratibandhe tulya eva | tasmād yatkiñcid etad api | kena punaḥ pramāṇenaiṣa svābhāvikaḥ sambandho gṛhyate | pratyakṣasambandhiṣu pratyakṣeṇa tathā hi abhijātamaṇibhedatattvavad bhūyodarśanajanitasaṃskārasahāyam indriyam eva dhūmādīnāṃ vahnyādibhiḥ svābhāvikasambandhagrāhīti yuktam utpaśyāmaḥ | evaṃ mānāntaraviditasambandheṣu mānāntarāṇy eva yathāsvaṃ bhūyodarśanasahāyāni svābhāvikasambandhagrahaṇe pramāṇāny unnetavyāni | svabhāvataś ca pratibaddhā hetavaḥ svasādhyena yadi sādhyam antareṇa bhaveyuḥ, svabhāvād eva pracyaverann iti tarkasahāyā nirastasādhyavyatir ekavṛttisandehā yatra dṛṣṭās tatra svasādhyam upasthāpayanty eveti ||
children.translated_text: It might be [objected] thus: If one thing has a natural connection (<s>svābhāvika sambandha</s>) with another as a co-cause, then everything would be naturally connected with everything; everything would be inferable from everything. Or, if one thing is the effect of another, why does not everything arise from everything, given the non-distinction of otherness? And so the same over-extension follows. If it is said that the essential natures of things (<s>bhāvasvabhāva</s>) are not to be questioned, and therefore, even in the non-distinction of otherness, only something specific is a cause and only something specific is an effect — well, this questioning of essential natures applies equally even to things that are distinct and do not stand in a cause-effect relation, with regard to the natural restriction (<s>svabhāvapratibandha</s>). Therefore, this too amounts to nothing definite. By what means of valid cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>), then, is this natural connection grasped? In the case of things whose connection is perceptible, [it is grasped] by perception. For indeed, just as with the discrimination of the nature of fine jewels, we consider it proper that the sense faculty itself, aided by the disposition (<s>saṃskāra</s>) generated from repeated observation, grasps the natural connection of smoke etc. with fire etc. Similarly, in cases where the connection is known through other means of valid cognition, those very other means of valid cognition, each assisted by repeated observation in its own domain, are to be adduced as the authorities for grasping the natural connection. And reasons (<s>hetu</s>) that are naturally restricted to their own provable property (<s>sādhya</s>) — if they could exist without the provable, they would deviate from their very nature — hence, assisted by logical reasoning (<s>tarka</s>) that removes the doubt that they might occur in the absence of the provable, wherever they are observed, they necessarily present their own provable.

children.text: atrocyate | iha khalu bhede tadutpattir eva vyāptiḥ | na cāsāvanyo vā svata evāvinābhāvalakṣaṇaḥ svābhāvikaḥ sambandho bhūyodarśanamātrataḥ sidhyati | tathā hi, kiṃ yatra bhūyodarśanapravṛttis tatra niyatatvavyavasthā, yatra vā niyatatvam asti tatraiva bhūyodarśanapravṛttiḥ | prathamapakṣe ghaṭād api kulaṭā, pārthivatvād api lohalekhyatvaṃ sidhyet, bhūyodarśanasambhave 'pi niyatatvasambhavāt |
children.translated_text: Here we reply: In this system, <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion/invariable concomitance) is precisely the origination of [the mark] from that [which is to be inferred], given their distinctness. And neither this [origination-based pervasion] nor any other natural connection characterized by invariable co-presence (<s>avinābhāva</s>) is established merely from repeated observation (<s>bhūyodarśana</s>). For consider: Is it the case that wherever repeated observation occurs, there the ascertainment of necessity obtains? Or is it that only where necessity exists does repeated observation occur? On the first alternative, even from a pot one could infer an unchaste woman, and from earthiness one could infer inscribability on metal — because even where repeated observation is possible, necessity might also be possible.

children.text: vyabhicāradarśanān naivam iti cet | kasya punarvyabhicāradarśanam yasya kasyacit śāstrakārasya, pratipattur vā | prathamapakṣe pratipattuḥ kim āyātaṃ yato nānumānam ayaṃ kuryāt | anyathānyasya tadviṣayapratyakṣīkāreṇaiva so 'pi kṛtārtha iti kim avaśyam anumānam anveṣate | na cāptavacanād avyabhicāradarśanād anumānam | āptasya niścetum aśakyatvād ity anyatra prasādhanāt | śāstrakāraṃ ca pṛṣṭvā dṛṣṭasambandho 'pi dhūmād agnim anumāsyata ity alaukikam | pratipattus tu nāvaśyaṃ sann api vyabhicāro gocarībhavati | na hi yatra vyabhicāras tatraiva tāvati kāle deśe vāvaśyaṃ pratītim avatarati | apratīyamānaś ca nāsty eveti na niyamaḥ | saty api vyabhicāre darśanasāmagryabhāvāt tasyādarśanāt | aticirakālavyavadhāne 'pi darśanāt brāhmaṇyādivyabhicāravat ||
children.translated_text: If [you say] this is not so because of observation of deviation (<s>vyabhicāra</s>) — whose observation of deviation? That of some treatise-author, or that of the person making the inference? On the first alternative, what bearing does it have on the person making the inference, such that he should not make the inference? Otherwise, since the other person could simply perceive that domain directly, he too would be satisfied — so why must he necessarily seek inference? And inference does not arise from the statement of a trustworthy person that no deviation has been observed, because the trustworthiness of a person cannot be ascertained — as has been established elsewhere. Moreover, that even one who has observed the connection [by himself] would infer fire from smoke only after consulting the treatise-author is extraordinary indeed. But for the person making the inference, deviation, even if it exists, does not necessarily become perceptible. For it is not the case that wherever deviation exists, at that very extent of time and place, it necessarily enters into awareness. And the fact that it is not perceived does not mean it simply does not exist — there is no such rule. For even though deviation exists, due to the absence of the aggregate of conditions for its perception, it may go unperceived. Just as with deviation in cases like Brahminhood etc. — even after very long intervals of time, [deviation] may be observed.

children.text: ghaṭapārthivādau pratipattaiva pravṛttaḥ | tadaiva krameṇa vā vyabhicāraṃ paśyed iti cet | yadi tāvad asau kathañcit pravartate, pravṛtto 'pi vā sāmagryabhāvāvyabhicāraṃ na paśyet | vajraṃ vā lohena vyāpārayet | vyaktaṃ tasya tāvat tad apy amānam āpannam iti mahat pāṇḍityam | tasmād yadi vyabhicāradarśanād anumānaṃ tadādṛṣṭavyabhicārasya pratipattur ghaṭapārthivatvād apy asti | tathā adarśanamātreṇa vyabhicārābhāvo na sidhyati, yogyānupalabdher eva sarvatrābhāvasādhane 'dhikārāt | tato bahulaṃ sahacāramātreṇa na vyabhicārī na vyāvyabhicārī niścita iti śaṅkāvakāśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Regarding pot-earthiness etc., the person making the inference himself has engaged [in observation]. At that very point, or subsequently, he might observe deviation — if so: if he somehow engages [in inference], even after engaging, he might not observe the deviation due to the absence of the conditions. Or he might try to work with iron using a diamond! Clearly, for him too, that [inference] has become a non-means-of-valid-knowledge — what great scholarship [indeed]! Therefore, if inference exists because of the observation of deviation, then for the inferring person who has not observed deviation, [inference] exists even from pot-earthiness etc. Moreover, the absence of deviation is not established merely from its non-observation, because only capable non-apprehension (<s>yogyānupalabdhi</s>) has authority in establishing absence everywhere. Therefore, merely from frequent co-occurrence, [the mark] is neither determined as non-deviating nor as definitely non-deviating — and this is the scope for doubt.

children.text: yady evam adṛṣṭavyabhicārād api dhūmād anumānaṃ mā bhūt | na | īdṛśasya śaṅkāvakāśasya sarvatra tadutpattirahite sambhavād iti | atha kadācit pratipattā pravṛtto vyabhicāraṃ paśyati | na tarhi yatra bhūyodarśanam, tatra niyatatvasthitiḥ | tatra kuto dhūme pratibandhasiddhiḥ | bhūyodarśanasyānyatra niyatatvopasthāpakatvakṣatau malinapauruṣatvena sarvatrānāśvāsāt ||
children.translated_text: If so, then even inference from smoke should not occur, since deviation has not been observed [by the inferrer himself]. Not so — because such a scope for doubt is possible everywhere in [cases] devoid of origination from that [source]. Now suppose that sometimes the inferring person, having engaged [in observation], does observe deviation. Then it is not the case that wherever there is repeated observation, there the ascertainment of necessity holds. In that case, how can the establishment of restriction (<s>pratibandha</s>) be achieved for smoke? Because when the capacity of repeated observation to present necessity has been undermined elsewhere, [it follows that] due to its tainted efficacy (<s>malinapauruṣa</s>), there is no confidence anywhere.

children.text: yady evaṃ dvicandrādau cakṣurādipratyakṣaṃ malinapauruṣam upalabdham iti ghaṭādikam api nopasthāpayed iti cet | na | indriyaviṣayakāryaṃ hi pratyakṣam | na dvicandrādijñānam īdṛśam arthakāryatvābhāvāt | tato bhinnalakṣaṇasya pratyakṣābhāsattve 'pi ghaṭajñānaṃ pratyakṣam eva | na caiva dhūmādau pārthivatvādau ca vyāptigrāhakasya bhūyodarśanasya lakṣaṇabhedo yenaikatrāśvāsaḥ syāt ||
children.translated_text: If [one objects]: In that case, in the case of double moons etc., sense-perception by the eye etc. has been found to be of tainted efficacy — so it should not present even pots and the like. Not so. For perception is an effect of the sense faculty and its object. But cognition of double moons etc. is not of this kind, because it is not an effect of the real object. Therefore, even though the perceptual semblance (<s>pratyakṣābhāsa</s>) has a different defining characteristic, the cognition of a pot is indeed perception. But in the case of smoke etc. and earthiness etc., there is no difference in the defining characteristic of repeated observation that grasps the <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion), such that there could be confidence in one [case] and not the other.

children.text: ete evārthakāryatvākāryatve lakṣaṇabheda iti cet | na | ghaṭādijñānasya hy arthakāryatvavivāde pramāṇāntarato 'rthakriyālābhato vā niścayaḥ, na pratijñāmātreṇa | na cātra dhūmasyāgnisahacāraḥ sadātano 'yam atha suhṛddvayasyeva sātyayo gṛhīta iti saṃśaye sadātanasahacāraprasādhakapramāṇāntarasaṅgatir asti, tatkāryaṃ vā kiñcid upalabhyate | tarhi bādhyamānatvābādhyamānatvalakṣaṇo lakṣaṇabhedo bhaviṣyatīty api na vaktavyam, avyabhicāragrahākasya bhūyodarśanasya bādhitatvāsiddheḥ | abādhamātraṃ hi prasajyapratiṣedho 'pramāṇam | pramāṇāntarasaṅgatir arthakriyālābho vā prayudāsaś cāsiddha iti na tāvat prathamaḥ pakṣaḥ | nāpi dvitīyaḥ | niyatatvābhāve 'pi pārthivatvādau bhūyodarśanasambhavād iti na bhūyodarśanagamyā vyāptiḥ ||
children.translated_text: If [it is said]: These very characteristics — being an effect of a real object and not being so — constitute the difference in defining marks. Not so. For the determination of the cognition of pots etc. as being an effect of a real object is made either through another means of valid cognition or through the attainment of practical efficacy (<s>arthakriyā</s>) — not by mere assertion. And here, in the doubt whether 'is this perpetual co-occurrence of smoke with fire, or is it accidental like that of two friends?' — there is no corroboration by another means of valid cognition establishing perpetual co-occurrence, nor is any effect of it observed. Then it should also not be said that the difference in defining marks consists in [the pervasion] being or not being contradicted (<s>bādhyamānatva/abādhyamānatva</s>), because it is not established that repeated observation — which is supposed to grasp the non-deviation — is contradicted. For mere non-contradiction is a <s>prasajyapratiṣedha</s> (verbally negating proposition) — it is a non-means-of-valid-knowledge. And corroboration by another means of valid cognition or attainment of practical efficacy as a <s>paryudāsa</s> (nominally negating proposition) is unestablished. So the first alternative does not hold. Nor does the second — because repeated observation is possible even in earthiness etc. where necessity is absent. Thus, <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) is not knowable through repeated observation.

children.text: trilocana
children.translated_text: <s>Trilocana</s>:

children.text: codye 'pi brūmaḥ | yadi pratyakṣaṃ svalakṣaṇaviṣayam ity ayogavyavacchedenocyate tadā siddhasādhanam | anyayogavyavacchedas tv asiddhaḥ, pratyakṣānumānādisarvajñānānāṃ grāhyāvaseyabhedena viṣayadvaividhyānatikramāt | yad dhi yatra jñāne pratibhāsate tad grāhyam | yatra tu tat pravarte tad adhyavaseyam | tatra pratyakṣasya svalakṣaṇaṃ grāhyam | adhyavaseyaṃ tu sāmānyam, atadrūpaparāvṛttasvalakṣaṇamātrātmakam | anumānasya tu viparyayaḥ | tataś ca
children.translated_text: In response to this challenge too, we say: If perception is said to have <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (the particular) as its object in the sense of exclusion of the unfit (<s>ayogavyavaccheda</s>), then this is proving what is already established. But exclusion of the fit (<s>anyayogavyavaccheda</s>) is unestablished, because all cognitions — perception, inference, etc. — do not transcend the twofold nature of their objects, divided into the apprehended (<s>grāhya</s>) and the determined (<s>avaseya</s>). For that which appears in a given cognition is its apprehended object. That toward which [the cognition] is directed in action is the determined object. In the case of perception, the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular) is the apprehended object. But the determined object is the universal (<s>sāmānya</s>), which consists merely of the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> as excluded from what is not of that nature (<s>atadrūpaparāvṛtta</s>). For inference, the reverse [holds].

children.text: sāṃvyavahārikapramāṇāpekṣayā rūparasagandhasparśasamudāyātmakasya ghaṭasya rūpabhedamātragrahaṇe 'pi pratyakṣataḥ samudāyasiddhivyavasthā | tathaikasyātadrūpaparāvṛttasya grahaṇe 'pi sādhyasādhanasāmānyayor atadrūpaparāvṛttavastumātrātmanor ayogavyavacchedena viṣayabhūtayor vyāptigraho yukta eva | ata eva vikalpānām avastv eva viṣayaḥ, vastu tu teṣāṃ parokṣam evety api durjñānam, sarvavikalpānām adhyavaseyāpekṣayā vastuviṣayatvāt | śāstre 'pi tathaiva pratipādanāt | na ca manasā tajjātīyānāṃ vyāptigrahaḥ śakyaḥ, manaso bahir asvātantryāt | anyathā andhabadhir ādyabhāvaprasaṅgāt | na ca vahnivyabhicāre dhūma upādhirahitaṃ sambandham atikrāmed iti vaktum ucitam, svakapolakalpitasvābhāvikasambandhasya yācitakamaṇḍanatvād iti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, just as — with respect to conventional valid cognition (<s>sāṃvyavahārikapramāṇa</s>) — even when only a particular aspect of form is perceptually grasped from a pot that is an aggregate of form, taste, smell, and touch, the determination of the aggregate is established through perception; similarly, even when grasping just one [particular] as excluded from what is not of that nature, by the exclusion of the unfit, it is proper that the <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) of the universals of the provable and the proving — whose objects consist merely in things excluded from what is not of their nature — is grasped. For this very reason, it is also wrong to say that concepts (<s>vikalpa</s>) have only the unreal as their object and that real entities are always beyond their reach — because all concepts have real entities as their object with respect to the determined (<s>adhyavaseya</s>). This is presented in the treatises as well. Nor can the mind grasp the <s>vyāpti</s> of those belonging to the same class, because the mind lacks independence apart from the external [senses]. Otherwise, the absurd consequence of the non-existence of blind and deaf persons etc. would follow. Nor is it proper to say that smoke, in a deviation from fire, would not transgress a connection free of limiting conditions (<s>upādhi</s>) — because the natural connection that you have fabricated from your own imagination has the status of borrowed ornament.

children.text: yad api vācaspatijalpitam, yo yatropādhinā niyatas tatra tasya svābhāvikaḥ sambandhaḥ | yathā dahane dhūmasya | tadupādher dṛśyasyānupalabhyamānatvāt kvacid vyabhicārasyādarśanād ity atredaṃ vicāryate | yasyādarśanataḥ svābhāvikaḥ sambandho vavasthāpanīyaḥ, sa khalu dhūmasvarūpād arthāntaram upādhir vaktavyo yathā dahanād indhanam | arthāntaraṃ ca kiñcid dṛśyam adṛśyaṃ ca kiñcit, na tu sarvam eva dṛśyatāniyatam | tataś ca dhūmasyāpi hutāśane syād upādhiḥ, na copalabhyate ity upādhimātrānupalabdhir anaikāntikī | tat katham adarśanamātrān nāsty evopādhiḥ, yataḥ svābhāvikasambandhasiddhiḥ syāt | dṛśyopadhyabhāvasādhane tu siddhasādhanam | paramadṛśyopādhiśaṅkāsambhave svābhāvikatvapratirodhas tadavstha eva | kvacid vyabhicārādarśanād ity asambaddham eva, upādhivat vyabhicārasyāpy adarśanamātrād abhāvāsiddheḥ | vyabhicārasya sarvadeśakālayoḥ sambhave 'pi sarvadā sarvatra sarveṇa sāmagryabhāvād api niścetum aśakyatvāt | brāhmaṇyādivyabhicāravad evāhatyādarśane 'pi deśakālāntare taddarśanasya niṣeddham aśakyatvāt |
children.translated_text: Moreover, regarding what <s>Vācaspati</s> has stated: 'Where something is restricted by a limiting condition (<s>upādhi</s>) to something [else], there is a natural connection between them — as of smoke with combustion. Since the limiting condition, being visible, is not observed, and since deviation is not seen anywhere' — here the following is to be examined: The <s>upādhi</s> (limiting condition), whose non-observation is supposed to establish the natural connection, must be stated as something different from the nature of smoke itself — just as fuel is different from combustion. And that something different is partly visible and partly invisible — not everything is necessarily restricted to being visible. Therefore, even smoke might have a limiting condition with respect to fire, and it is not observed — hence the mere non-observation of a limiting condition is inconclusive (<s>anaikāntikī</s>). How then, merely from non-observation, can one conclude that there is simply no limiting condition, from which the establishment of a natural connection would follow? In establishing the absence of a visible limiting condition, there is the fallacy of proving what is already established (<s>siddhasādhana</s>). And when there is the possibility of doubt about an extremely subtle visible limiting condition, the obstruction to establishing naturalness remains exactly the same. 'Because deviation is not seen anywhere' — this is simply incoherent, because the absence of deviation too is not established merely from its non-observation, just like a limiting condition. Because even though deviation might exist at all places and times, it cannot be ascertained with certainty by everyone everywhere at all times, due to the absence of the aggregate of conditions. Just as with deviation in cases like Brahminhood etc. — even though not observed for a very long time, the observation of it at another place and time cannot be precluded.

children.text: nanu yadi dhūmasyāpekṣaṇīyam arthāntaram upādhiḥ syāt kathaṃ dhūma ity eva pāvakasattāniyama iti cet | nanv idam eva cintyate kiṃ dhūme saty avaśyam agniḥ sambhavī na veti | kadācid arthāntaram upādhim apekṣya dhūmo 'pi syān nāgnir iti kim atra niṣṭabdhaṃ kāraṇam | tasmāt pāvakaparādhīnodayo dhūmaḥ pariniṣṭhitaḥ kathaṃ tadabhāve bhāvaṃ svīkuryād ity eva sādhu |
children.translated_text: Now, if smoke requires something different [from itself] as a limiting condition, how can there be a rule that where there is smoke, there is necessarily fire? But this is precisely what is being examined — whether when smoke is present, fire necessarily exists or not. Sometimes, requiring something else as a limiting condition, smoke too might exist without fire — what firm ground is there in this? Therefore, this is well-established: smoke, whose arising is dependent on fire, being firmly established [as such] — how could it accept existence in [fire's] absence? This alone is sound.

children.text: atha vyaktau jātau vā vahnivyabhicāro na dṛṣṭaḥ, kathaṃ tatra śaṅkyata iti cet | tat kiṃ sthāṇuvyaktau jātau vā puruṣatvaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ yena sthāṇau śaṅkyate | anyatrordhvatāliṅgite dṛṣṭam iti cet | ihāpy anyatra bhūyaḥ sahacāriṇi pārthivatvādau dṛṣṭa eva vyabhicāraḥ | yatraiva tu yat saṃśayate tatraiva tasya darśanam apekṣyata ity alaukikam | yadi dhūmavyaktau vyabhicāro dṛṣṭas tadā dhūmasāmānyaṃ vyāptau bahirbhūtam eva, kathaṃ saṃśayaḥ | atha jātau dṛṣṭas tadāpi vyabhicāraniścaya eva, kathaṃ saṃśayaḥ | ato dhūmajātāv adṛśyamāno 'pi vyabhicāra upādhir vā darśanāyogyatayā niṣeddhum aśakya iti saṃśayo durvāraprasaraḥ | sa cedānīm upādher vyabhicārasya vā saṃśayaḥ svābhāvikatvasaṃśayasvabhāvaḥ svābhāvikatvaniścayaṃ tāvad avaśyaṃ pratibadhnāti | tasmāt svābhāvikatvaniścayapratibandha evārthataḥ, niścayam antareṇa gamakasya svayam akiñcitkaratvāt | tad evam upādhyanupalabdhir vyabhicārasyānupalabdhir vā 'naikāntikī na tayor abhāvaṃ sādhayati, yataḥ sambandhasya svābhāvikatvasiddhiḥ syāt | asiddhā ceyam upādhyanupalabdhiḥ | yathā dahano nendhanena vinā dhūmena sambadhyate tathā dhūmo 'pi na vināgninā sambadhyata iti samānam upādhitvam indhanasyobhayatra |
children.translated_text: [Objection:] Deviation from fire is not observed with respect to the individual or the universal [of smoke] — so how can it be doubted? [Reply:] But has humanity been observed in a stump or its universal, that doubt should arise in the stump? [Objection:] It has been observed elsewhere, in what is marked by the sign of being upright. [Reply:] Here too, deviation has been observed elsewhere, with respect to frequently co-occurring properties such as earthiness and the like. [Objection:] One requires observation of the deviation precisely where one doubts — [Reply:] that is extraordinary! If deviation has been observed with respect to the individual of smoke, then the universal of smoke is entirely outside the scope of pervasion — how can there be doubt? If observed with respect to the universal, then there is certainty of deviation — how can there be doubt? Therefore, even though deviation or an extraneous condition (<s>upādhi</s>) is not observed with respect to the universal of smoke, it cannot be denied because of its unsuitability for observation — so the doubt has irresistible momentum. And this doubt — whether of an extraneous condition or of deviation — being of the nature of a doubt about the natural-ness [of the connection], necessarily obstructs the certainty of natural-ness. Therefore, the obstruction of the certainty of natural-ness is in effect [the result], since without certainty the indicator (<s>gamaka</s>) is itself ineffective. Thus, the non-apprehension of an extraneous condition or of deviation is inconclusive — it does not establish their absence, from which the natural-ness of the connection would follow. And this non-apprehension of an extraneous condition is itself unestablished. For just as fire is not connected with smoke without fuel, so too smoke is not connected without fire — the extraneous-condition-hood of fuel is the same in both cases.

children.text: atha siddhasyāgner indhanasāhityena dhūmalābha ity upādhivyavasthā, asiddhasya tu dhūmasya tannimittātmalābhatayāvyabhicārāt svābhāvikaḥ sambandha iti vyavasthāpyata iti cet | evam api saiva tadutpattir āyātā | saiva svābhāvikaḥ sambandhaḥ | na punaḥ pratijñāsiddhaḥ sahacāramātrātmakaḥ | kiṃ ca svābhāvikatvād avyabhicāraḥ sarvatra, sarvatrāvyabhicārāc ca svābhāvikatvam atītaretarāśrayatvam anivāryam | yasya tu sakṛttadutpattipratītir eva sarvatrāvyabhicārapratītis tasya nāyaṃ prasaṅgaḥ |
children.translated_text: [Objection:] The determination of the extraneous condition is that smoke is obtained along with fuel for an [already] established fire, whereas for smoke — which is unestablished — since it obtains its very existence by virtue of that [fire], the connection is natural due to non-deviation. [Reply:] Even so, what has arrived is that very origination from it [fire]. That very thing is the 'natural connection' — but not a mere co-occurrence that is asserted without proof. Moreover, non-deviation everywhere follows from natural-ness, and natural-ness follows from non-deviation everywhere — the mutual dependence (<s>itaretarāśraya</s>) is inescapable. But for one for whom the very apprehension of origination from that [cause] on a single occasion is the apprehension of non-deviation everywhere, this consequence does not apply.

children.text: yady evaṃ mamāpi bhūyodarśanād avyabhicārasiddhir iti cet | na | bhūya ity apariniṣṭhitavārasaṃkhyatvāt kiyatā darśanena lakṣaṇānusārī nirvṛtim āsādayet | asmākaṃ tu pratyakṣānupalabdhau parigaṇitasaṃkhyāv eva | yad āhuḥ
children.translated_text: [Objection:] If so, then for me too, the establishment of non-deviation follows from repeated observation. [Reply:] No, because the number of times implied by 'repeated' is indeterminate — after how many observations would one who follows the defining characteristic be satisfied? For us, however, the number is precisely delimited in the case of perception and non-apprehension. As they say:

— but if this [maxim] is given scope, then the goblin of doubt, having gained entry through the transgression of ordinary convention, would exist nowhere [that it does not exist], and so one would never act anywhere — because anything whatsoever could somehow be a ground for suspecting some harm, and because the suspicion of harm is a factor in the cessation [of activity] for the discerning. [For] even in the consumption of nourishing food and drink, death has been observed. Therefore, one who upholds the conduct of life sanctioned by valid cognition should entertain doubt only in accordance with what has been observed — not about what has never been previously seen. For doubt requires the recollection of a specific [alternative] — it does not arise without memory. And memory cannot operate regarding what has never been experienced. As the author of the <s>Mīmāṃsāvārttika</s> [<s>Kumārila</s>] has stated: 'Doubt without evidence is not [legitimate].' Therefore, having diligently searched for a limiting condition (<s>upādhi</s>) and not finding one, we ascertain that it does not exist and conclude that the relation is natural (<s>svābhāvika</s>).

children.text: prāg adṛṣṭau kramāt paśyan veti hetuphalasthitim |
children.translated_text: 'Before the two [positive and negative concomitances] are seen, one sees them step by step and ascertains the cause-effect relation.',

children.text: dṛṣṭau vā kramaśo 'paśyann anyathā tv anavasthitiḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'or, even after seeing [them], one does not see [them] step by step — but otherwise, there is [merely] instability.'

children.text: iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: yat tv anupalabhyamānasyāpi kalpanānupapatter iti vilapitam, tadbālasyāpy asāmpratam | anupalabhyamāne 'rthe ca kalpanāvakāśāt | na hi dṛśyamāno ghaṭaḥ kalpita ucyate | na ca sandihyamāna upādhiḥ sambandhasya svābhāvikatvaṃ pratibadhnātīti yuktam, sādhakabādhakābhāva eva saṃśayasya nyāyaprāptatvāt | ata eva na sarvatra śaṅkāpiśācāvakāśaḥ | tat kathaṃ nāyaṃ pravarteta |

pramāṇaviṣaye 'pi śaṅkā kartuṃ śakyata iti cet | na | svīkṛtapramāṇasya hi niścayaphalatvāt pramāṇasyāvipratipannapramāṇaviṣaye niścayasvīkāranāntarīyaka eva tatsvīkāraḥ | na ca śaṅkety eva na pravṛttiḥ, arthasaṃśayenāpi pravṛtter anivāryatvāt snigdhānnapānopayogavat | tadupayoge kadācin maraṇadarśane 'pi koṭiśo jīvitadarśanāt | na ca prāmāṇikalokayātrākṣatiḥ, prāmāṇikair eva pramāṇābhāve saṃśayasya vihitatvāt | yathādarśanam āśaṅkanīyam ityādy api siddhasādhanam, anyatra dṛṣṭasyaivopādher vyabhicārasya vā śaṅkitatvāt | kiṃ ca bādhakādarśane 'pi sādhakābhāvād api śaṅkā syād eva |
children.translated_text: [Objection:] Doubt can be raised even regarding what is the object of a valid means of knowledge. [Reply:] No, because for one who has accepted a means of valid cognition — since the accepted means of valid cognition has certainty as its result — in a subject matter where the means of valid cognition is uncontested, the acceptance of certainty is inseparable from the acceptance of that [means]. Nor is it the case that one would simply not engage because of doubt, since engagement even from doubt about [possible] benefit cannot be prevented — like the consumption of rich food and drink. Even when death has occasionally been observed upon consuming them, life has been observed millions of times. Nor is the worldly conduct [sanctioned by] valid cognition damaged, since doubt in the absence of valid cognition is sanctioned precisely by those who are committed to valid cognition. [The claim that] 'one should doubt only in accordance with what has been observed' and so forth — that too proves what is already established, since the extraneous condition or deviation that is doubted has been observed precisely elsewhere. Moreover, even when a defeater is not observed, doubt may arise precisely from the absence of an establisher.

children.text: yad api syād etad iti valgitaṃ tad api niḥsāram | pramāṇasiddhe hi rūpe svābhāvāvalambanam | na tu svabhāvāvalambanenaiva vastusvarūpavyavasthā | tad yadi niyataviṣayānvayavyatirekagrāhakapratyakṣānupalambhapramāṇasiddhe hetuphalabhāve svabhāvavādas tat kim āyātaṃ svābhāvikasambandhe | yatra tadutpattisāmagrīṃ hṛdayena dūrīkṛtyānyataḥ sahacaritadvayād viśeṣeṇa pratītau pratyupāya eva davīyān | tatsāmagryapakṣaṇe ca tadutpattir eva sā | kim āhopuruṣikayā nāmāntarakaraṇena | kena punaḥ pramāṇena eṣa svābhāvikaḥ sambandho gṛhyata ityādis tadgrahaṇaprakāraḥ pūrvam eva nirākṛtaḥ | tathā svābhāvikatvāsiddhau svabhāvataś ca pratibaddhā hetava ityādy upasaṃhāro 'pi manorājyamātram | tasmād arthāntare gamye kāryahetus tadbhāvasiddhiś ca pratyakṣānupalambhād iti sthitam | tad evaṃ svābhāvikavādena hṛdayānulepanam aśucin eva parihāryaṃ dūrata iti |
children.translated_text: As for the boast 'It would follow that...' — that too is hollow. For the appeal to essential nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) is based on a form established through valid cognition. But the determination of the real nature of an entity is not accomplished merely by appealing to essential nature. Therefore, if in a cause-effect relation established by the valid cognitions of perception and non-apprehension — which grasp the positive and negative concomitance of restricted objects — there is an appeal to essential nature, then what does it amount to [different from] a natural connection? Where, having mentally set aside the aggregate of conditions for its origination, and the method for specific apprehension from a co-occurring pair [of properties] is exceedingly remote [from anything provable]. And when the aggregate of conditions is included, that very thing is origination from it [the cause]. What is the use of heroic posturing by giving it a different name? And the manner of grasping [the connection] — 'By what means of valid cognition is this natural connection grasped?' and so forth — has already been refuted. Similarly, the conclusion 'When natural-ness is unestablished, and logical reasons are bound by [their] essential nature...' and so forth is mere castle-building. Therefore, it is established that when something else is to be inferred, the cause-based reason and the establishment of its [causal] status [come] from perception and non-apprehension. Thus, the anointing of the heart with the doctrine of essential nature is impure and should be avoided from afar.

As for the prattle that 'even what is not apprehended cannot be imagined' — even a child would find that inappropriate. For there is room for imagination precisely regarding an object that is not apprehended. For a pot that is being directly perceived is not said to be 'imagined.' Nor is it correct that a merely doubted extraneous condition obstructs the natural-ness of the connection, since doubt is logically warranted precisely in the absence of both establishing and defeating [evidence]. For this very reason, the demoness of doubt does not have scope everywhere. How then would one not engage [in action]?

children.text: || vyāptinirṇyaḥ samāpto ratnakīrtipādānām ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Vyāptinirṇaya</s> (Determination of Pervasion) of <s>Ratnakīrti</s> is completed.

children.text: Sthirasiddhidūṣaṇam
children.translated_text: <s>Sthirasiddhidūṣaṇam</s> (Refutation of the Proof of Permanence)

children.text: namas tārāyai ||
children.translated_text: Salutation to <s>Tārā</s>!

children.text: yadyogād andhavad viśvaṃ saṃsāre bhramad iṣyate |
children.translated_text: That sinful [notion of] the proof of permanence, by whose connection the entire universe is regarded as wandering in <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of rebirth) like a blind person,

children.text: sā kṛpāvaśagaiḥ pāpā sthirasiddhir apāsyate ||
children.translated_text: is to be dispelled by those who are under the power of compassion.

children.text: iha pare sakalapadārthasthairyaprasādhanārthaṃ pratyakṣam anumānam arthāpattiṃ [ca] pramāṇāny ācakṣate |

tathā hi | sa evāyaṃ ghaṭasphaṭikādir iti pratyabhijñākhyaṃ pratyakṣam udīyamānaṃ sthairyam utthāpayati | na cedam apramāṇam abhidhātavyam | aprāmāṇyaṃ hi bhavad aprāmāṇyakāraṇopapattyā vā bhavet, prāmāṇyalakṣaṇavirahād vā |
children.translated_text: For thus: perception called recognition (<s>pratyabhijñā</s>) — 'This is that very same pot, crystal, etc.' — when arising, establishes permanence. And this should not be called invalid. For invalidity would be either through the applicability of a cause of invalidity, or through the absence of the defining characteristic of validity.

children.text: yady ādyaḥ pakṣaḥ | kiṃ aprāmāṇyakāraṇam, mithyātvam ajñānaṃ saṃśayo vā |
children.translated_text: If the first alternative: what is the cause of invalidity? — falsity (<s>mithyātva</s>), ignorance (<s>ajñāna</s>), or doubt (<s>saṃśaya</s>)?

children.text: na tāvad atra mithyātvam | mithyātvaṃ hi tadviṣaye bādhakapratyayād vā hetūktadoṣato vā sambhāvyeta |
children.translated_text: To begin with, there is no falsity here. For falsity could be suspected either through a sublating cognition (<s>bādhaka</s>) regarding its object, or through defects stated in the reason.

children.text: na tāvad bādhagandho 'pi sambhavati | deśakālanarāntareṣv apy asambhavāt | na cānavagatāpi bādhā kadācid api bhaviṣyatīti śaṅkā yuktimatī | nirbījaśaṅkānupapatteḥ |
children.translated_text: To begin with, not even a trace of sublation is possible, because it does not occur in other places, times, or persons either. Nor is the suspicion rational that sublation, even though not yet known, may occur at some future time — because groundless suspicion is unjustified.
Here, opponents cite perception, inference, and <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) as the means of valid knowledge for establishing the permanence of all entities.

children.text: avaśayaṃ śaṅkayā bhāvyaṃ niyāmakam apaśyatām |
(PV I 324cd)

children.translated_text: 'Doubt is necessary for those who do not see a determining factor' —

children.text: iti dattāvakāśā saṃśayapiśācī labdhaprasarā na kvacin nāstīti nāyaṃ kvacit pravarteta | antataḥ snigdhānnapānopayoge 'pi maraṇadarśanena sarvatra śaṅkānivṛtteḥ | tasmāt prāmāṇikalokayātrām anupālayatā yathā darśanam eva śaṅkanīyaṃ nādṛṣṭapūrvam api |
yad uktaṃ Kārikāyāṃ nāśaṅkā niṣpramāṇikā
children.translated_text: As stated in the <s>Kārikā</s>: 'There is no doubt without a basis in valid cognition.'

children.text: (ŚV II 60d)

|
	iti | Bṛhaṭṭīkāyām api
children.translated_text: In the <s>Bṛhaṭṭīkā</s> also:

but the demoness of doubt, having been given scope, having gained free play, does not stop anywhere — so one would never engage [in action]. Ultimately, because suspicion cannot be eliminated anywhere on account of the observation of death even in the consumption of rich food and drink. Therefore, one who upholds worldly conduct [sanctioned by] valid cognition should doubt only in accordance with what has been observed, not something never seen before.

children.text: utprekṣeta hi yo mohād ajñātam api bādhakam |
children.translated_text: 'He who, out of delusion, would imagine a defeater that has never been known,

children.text: sa sarvavyavahāreṣu saṃśayātmā kṣayaṃ vrajet ||
children.translated_text: that one, whose nature is [consumed by] doubt in all transactions, would be ruined.'

children.text: iti |
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text: kṣaṇabhaṅgasādhanaṃ bādhakam asyeti cet | na | anumānasya paramparayāpi pratyakṣapūrvatvāt pratyakṣam pradhānam | prādhānyāc cānumānasya bādhakam | na tv anumānam asya | pratyakṣāntaraṃ tu bādhakaṃ bhavati | yathā sarpādipratyayasya rajjvādipratyakṣam | tac cātra na sambhavati |
nanu pratyakṣe 'pi bādhake kasmān na bhavati parasparapratibhandhena dvayor apy apratyakṣatā |
children.translated_text: [Objection:] Even when perception is the defeater, why should there not be the invalidity of both through mutual obstruction?

children.text: na, arthakriyāsamarthavastuviṣayāviṣayatvena samānatvābhāvād ekasya pratyakṣābhāsatvād iti na sadviṣayatvabādhakapratyayān mithyātvam |
children.translated_text: [Reply:] No, because there is no equality [between them] — one has a real entity capable of causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyāsamartha</s>) as its object, and the other does not. Because one is a mere semblance of perception [while the other is genuine]. Therefore, there is no falsity through a sublating cognition regarding what has a real object.

children.text: nāpi hetūktadoṣataḥ | deśakālanarāntareṣv avisaṃvādāt |
children.translated_text: Nor [is there invalidity] through defects stated in the reason, because [recognition] is non-deceptive in other places, times, and persons.

children.text: nāpy ajñānam aprāmāṇyakāraṇam atrāsti | pratyabhijñānasaṃvedanasambhavāt |
children.translated_text: Nor is ignorance present here as a cause of invalidity, because the experience of recognition is possible.

children.text: na ca saṃśayaḥ | na hi tad evedaṃ syād vā na veti sphaṭikādiṣūdayati matiḥ | kiṃ tu tad evedaṃ sphaṭikādikam iti nirastā vibhramāśaṅkā | tan nāprāmāṇyakāraṇopapattyā pratyabhijñānasyāprāmāṇyam |
children.translated_text: Nor is there doubt. For the thought does not arise regarding crystals and the like: 'This might or might not be the very same one.' Rather, 'This is indeed the very same crystal and the like' — the suspicion of error is dispelled. Therefore, there is no invalidity of recognition through the applicability of a cause of invalidity.

children.text: nāpi lakṣaṇakṣayāt | yad eva hi utpannam asandigdham aduṣṭakāraṇajanyaṃ deśakālanarāntareṣv abādhitaṃ ca tad eva pramāṇam iti naḥ siddhāntaḥ | tad uktam |
children.translated_text: Nor through the loss of the defining characteristic [of validity]. For our established doctrine is that whatever has arisen, is free from doubt, is produced from an undefective cause, and is not sublated in other places, times, and persons — that alone is a valid means of cognition. As stated:

[Objection:] The proof of momentary destruction is the defeater of this [recognition]. [Reply:] No. Because inference is ultimately preceded by perception through a chain [of reasoning], perception is primary. And because of its primacy, [perception] is the defeater of inference, not inference of this [perception]. Rather, another perception can be a defeater — just as the perception of a rope [sublates] the cognition of a snake and the like. And that [sublating perception] does not occur here.

children.text: tasmād dṛḍhaṃ yad utpannaṃ na visaṃvādam ṛcchati |
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, that cognition which has arisen firmly and does not encounter contradiction

children.text: jñānāntareṇa vijñānaṃ tat pramāṇaṃ pratīyatām ||
children.translated_text: from another cognition — let that be acknowledged as a valid means of knowledge.'

children.text: tathā Bṛhaṭṭīkāpi
children.translated_text: Similarly, the <s>Bṛhaṭṭīkā</s> too [states]:

children.text: tatrāpūrvārthavijñānaṃ niścitaṃ bādhavarjitam |
children.translated_text: 'A cognition that apprehends a novel object, that is determinate, free from sublation,

children.text: aduṣṭakāraṇārabdhaṃ pramāṇaṃ lokasammatam ||
See also PVA 21,17f = PVAO 53,4f; TBV 13,24f, 318,25f, 394,16f; TR 126,21, ; Ravigupta, D304b1-2 (vol 9) = Q151a1:; cf. Mimaki 1976: 88f and 284f.

children.translated_text: and initiated by an undefective cause — is a valid means of knowledge according to common consensus.'

children.text: iti | etac ca lakṣaṇam uktanyāyena pratyabhijñāne 'pi sambhavatīti pramāṇam evedam |
nanv idam ekam eva na bhavati kāraṇabhedāt, viṣayabhedāt, svabhāvavirodhāc ca |
children.translated_text: [Objection:] This [recognition] is not a single [cognition] at all, because of the difference of causes, the difference of objects, and the contradiction of essential natures.

children.text: tathā hi | sa iti saṃskārakāryam | ayam iti cendriyakāryam | na ca kāraṇabhede 'pi kāryābhedo viśvavaicitryāhetukatvaprasaṅgāt |
children.translated_text: For thus: 'That' (<s>sa</s>) is the effect of a latent impression (<s>saṃskāra</s>). 'This' (<s>ayam</s>) is the effect of a sense-organ. And there is no identity of effects when the causes differ — otherwise, the diversity of the world would be causeless.

children.text: tathā saty api sphaṭikaḥ sphaṭika iti vyapadeśābhede pūrvadeśakālasambandhāparadeśakālasambandhābhyāṃ viruddhadharmābhyāṃ yogāt sphaṭikaḥ pūrvāparakālayor bhidyata iti viṣayabhedo vaktavyaḥ |
children.translated_text: This being so, even though there is no difference in designation — 'crystal' and 'crystal' — nevertheless, because of the conjunction of contradictory properties, namely the connection with the former place and time and the connection with the latter place and time, it must be stated that the crystal is different at the earlier and later times — thus there is a difference of objects.

children.text: tathā sa iti parokṣam | ayam iti sākṣātkāraḥ | na cānayoḥ svabhāvaviruddhayor dahanatuhinayor iva śakyā śakreṇāpy ekatā āpādayitum | trailokasyaikyaprasaṅgāt |
children.translated_text: Similarly, 'that' (<s>sa</s>) is indirect [cognition]; 'this' (<s>ayam</s>) is direct apprehension. And unity between these two, which are contradictory in essential nature like fire and frost, cannot be brought about even by <s>Indra</s> — because there would follow the consequence of the unity of all three worlds.

children.text: na cāsya prāmāṇyam, vikalpatvenāvastunirbhāsitvāt, smārtād aviśeṣāc ca | tasmāt pratyabhijñā ekatvaṃ sthāpayati bhāvānām iti manorathamātram |
children.translated_text: And this [recognition] is not a valid means of knowledge, because, being a conceptual construction (<s>vikalpa</s>), it manifests a non-real [object], and because it is no different from memory. Therefore, [the claim that] recognition establishes the unity of entities is mere wishful thinking.

children.text: atrocyate | ekam evedaṃ pratyabhijñānaṃ samākhyātam,
children.translated_text: To this we reply: This recognition has been declared to be a single [cognition],

children.text: yady apīndriyaṃ kevalam asamartham, yady api saṃskāramātram, saṃskārasadhrīcīnaṃ tu indriyaṃ bhāvayiṣyati pratyabhijñām | tadbhāvābhāvānuvidhānāt pratyabhijñābhāvābhāvayoḥ | na hi nājījanad bījamātram aṅkuram iti mṛdādisahitam api na janayati |
children.translated_text: even though the sense-organ alone is insufficient [and] even though the latent impression alone [is insufficient], the sense-organ accompanied by the latent impression will produce recognition — because the presence and absence of recognition conform to the presence and absence of that [combination]. For it is not the case that because a seed alone does not produce a sprout, it does not produce [one] even when accompanied by earth and the like.

children.text: atha bhavatu deśakālayos tatsaṃsargayor vā parasparanānātvam | na tadavacchinnasya padmarāgasya | tasya tābhyāṃ tatsaṃsargābhyāṃ cānyatvāt |
children.translated_text: Let there be mutual difference between place and time, or between the connections with them. But not of the ruby (<s>padmarāga</s>) that is delimited by them — because it is different from those two and from the connections with them.

children.text: tato 'nyatve tatsaṃsargayoḥ kutas tadīyatvam iti cet | svabhāvād eveti saṃsargaparīkṣāyāṃ nipuṇataram upapādayiṣyate |
children.translated_text: [Objection:] If it is different from the connections, whence do the connections belong to it? [Reply:] From essential nature itself — this will be demonstrated more carefully in the examination of connection (<s>saṃsargaparīkṣā</s>).

children.text: na ca svabhāvavirodhaḥ, anumānasyāpy anekatvaprasaṅgāt | tad api hi pratyakṣam apratyakṣaṃ ca | avikalpo vikalpaś ca | asamāropaḥ samāropaś ca |
children.translated_text: Nor is there a contradiction of essential natures, because [by that logic] even inference would have the consequence of being multiple. For it too is both perception and non-perception, both non-conceptual and conceptual, both non-superimposed and superimposed.

children.text: svānubhavāvasthāpitābhedasya svarūpatadgrāhyabhedāpekṣayā pratyakṣādīnām avirodha iti cet | na, ihāpi sāmyāt | na khalv etad api vijñānaṃ tattedantādhikaraṇam ekam ābhyām anuraktaṃ sphaṭikaṃ gocarayad abhinnaṃ nānubhūyate nāvasīyate vā | ekatve 'pi ca vastunas tadanurañjakatattedantābhedāpekṣayā pratyakṣatāparokṣate na virotsyete, sahasambhavāt | vijñānaikatvasya ca pramāṇasiddhatvāt |
children.translated_text: If it is said that there is no contradiction among perception and other <s>pramāṇas</s> (valid cognitions) with respect to the distinction between the intrinsic nature and what is apprehended by it, since non-difference has been established by one's own experience — no, because of parity in this case too. For indeed, this cognition too, having as its object the single crystal (<s>sphaṭika</s>) colored by both 'that' and 'this,' is neither not experienced nor not ascertained as non-different. And even when the entity is one, the perceptual and non-mediate character [of cognition], with respect to the non-difference of the coloring agent and the 'that' and 'this,' will not be contradictory, since they can co-exist. And because the unity of cognition is established by <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid cognition).

children.text: na ca sa iti pūrvadeśakālasaṃsargo 'yam iti ca sannihitadeśakālasaṃsarga ekasya virudhyate | yato yuktaṃ yat padmarāgasya svarūpe paricchidyamāne tadabhāvo vyavacchidyata iti tadavyavacchede tatsvarūpāparicchedāt, svapracyutivyavacchedyasvabhāvatvāt padmarāgabhāvasya tadanavacchede tatparicchedānupapatteḥ |
children.translated_text: Nor is there a contradiction in the case of a single [entity having] the association with a prior place and time as 'that' and the association with the present place and time as 'this.' Therefore it is proper that when the intrinsic nature of the ruby (<s>padmarāga</s>) is being determined, the absence of that [other nature] is excluded — because if that [absence] is not excluded, the intrinsic nature is not determined, since the nature of the existence of the ruby (<s>padmarāga</s>) is such that it is excludable by the exclusion of its own departure, and without that exclusion, the determination of it would be impossible.

children.text: kasmāt punas tadanye puṣparāgādayo vyavacchidyante | tadabhāvāvinābhāvād iti cet, sa eva kutaḥ | pratyakṣeṇa kadācid api puṣparāgapadmarāgayos tādātmyānupalambhād iti cet | yatra tarhi tatas tādātmyapratītiḥ, tatra tadavinābhāvaḥ | samasti ca so 'yaṃ padmarāga iti deśakalāvasthānugatam ekaṃ padmarāgam avabhāsayantī sākṣātkāravatī pratītiḥ |
children.translated_text: Then why are others such as topaz (<s>puṣparāga</s>) excluded? If it is said: because of the invariable co-presence with the absence of that — then whence comes that [invariable co-presence]? If it is said: because by perception there is never an apprehension of identity between topaz (<s>puṣparāga</s>) and ruby (<s>padmarāga</s>) — then wherever there is a cognition of identity with that, there is invariable co-presence with that. And there exists a cognition possessing direct acquaintance, manifesting a single ruby (<s>padmarāga</s>) persisting through [different] places, times, and conditions, [in the form] 'this is that same ruby (<s>padmarāga</s>).'

children.text: na vikalparūpatayāsyā aprāmāṇyam | abhilāpasaṃsargapratibhāsatvaprāmāṇyayor avirodhāt |
children.translated_text: Its invalidity is not [established] by its being of the nature of conceptual construction (<s>vikalpa</s>), since there is no contradiction between appearing with association with verbal expression and being a valid cognition (<s>prāmāṇya</s>).

children.text: na cedaṃ smārtam | adeśakālāvasthāvato 'sya deśakālāvasthānugatatvenādhikyād iti |
children.translated_text: Nor is this a memory-cognition (<s>smārta</s>), because it exceeds [mere memory] insofar as it [apprehends its object] as persisting through place, time, and condition, whereas [the object of memory] lacks [present] place, time, and condition.

children.text: atha keśakuśakadalīstambādau saty api bhede pratyabhijñānam utpannam iti cet | utpadyatāṃ ko doṣaḥ | kim anena pratipāditaṃ bhavati | kiṃ pratyabhijñāyāḥ sādhāraṇānaikāntikatvam, atha śabdasāmyād ubhayor apy aprāmāṇyam, uta saṃśayāpādanamātram |
children.translated_text: Now, if it is said that <s>pratyabhijñā</s> (recognition) arises even in the case of hair, grass, and plantain stems where there is actually difference — then let it arise, what is the fault? What is established by this? Is it the over-pervasion (<s>sādhāraṇa anaikāntika</s>) of <s>pratyabhijñā</s> (recognition)? Or the invalidity of both due to mere verbal similarity? Or is it merely the production of doubt?

children.text: prathamaḥ pakṣo 'nabhyupagamād eva nirastaḥ | na hīyam anumānatvenopanyastā | anumānatve 'py abādhitatvād iti viśeṣaṇe na doṣa iti pratipādayiṣyāmaḥ |
children.translated_text: The first alternative is refuted simply by non-acceptance [of the premise]. For this [<s>pratyabhijñā</s>] has not been presented as an inference (<s>anumāna</s>). And even if it were an inference, we shall demonstrate that there is no fault in the qualification 'being uncontradicted' (<s>abādhitatva</s>).

children.text: nāpi dvitīyaḥ pakṣaḥ | dṛṣṭāntamātrataḥ sādhyasiddher ayogāt | keśoṇḍukādiviṣayasya cakṣurvijñānasyāpy aprāmāṇye ghaṭādipratyakṣasyāprāmāṇyaprasaṅgāt |
children.translated_text: Nor is the second alternative [correct], because it is impossible to establish the <s>sādhya</s> (what is to be proved) from a mere example alone. For if the visual cognition directed at hair-coils and the like were also invalid, there would be the undesirable consequence that perception of pots and the like would also be invalid.

children.text: saṃśayamātraṃ tu vyavahārocchedakatvān nāśraṇīyam eveti pratipāditam iti na tṛtīyo 'pi pakṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: And as for mere doubt, it has been demonstrated that it is not to be relied upon, since it would cut off all practical activity — thus the third alternative is also [refuted].

children.text: kiṃ ca keśādau yadi pratyabhijñā vyabhicāriṇī, kāryakāraṇapratītiḥ kiṃ na vyabhicāriṇī | yā vyavicāriṇī sā kāryakāraṇapratītir eva na bhavatīti cet | yady evaṃ yā visaṃvādinī sā pratyabhijñaiva na bhavati tadābhāsatvād iti samānam | pratyabhijñānasya ca sati prāmāṇye 'numānādiṣv anantarbhāve pratyakṣaiva | saṃskārasahāyendriyānvayavyatirekānuvidhāyitvāc ca | satsaṃprayoge satīndriyāṇāṃ bhāvāc ca | tad iyaṃ pratyabhijñā 'nekadeśakālāvasthāsambaddham ekaṃ sphaṭikādikaṃ gocarayantī sthairyaṃ vyavasthāpayati |
children.translated_text: Moreover, if <s>pratyabhijñā</s> (recognition) deviates in the case of hair and the like, why does the cognition of cause and effect not also deviate? If it is said that whatever deviates is simply not a cognition of cause and effect — then equally, whatever is discordant is simply not <s>pratyabhijñā</s> (recognition), since it is merely an appearance of it. And if <s>pratyabhijñā</s> (recognition) is a valid cognition and is not included within inference and the like, then it is perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) itself. And because it conforms to the positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvaya-vyatireka</s>) of the sense faculties aided by <s>saṃskāra</s> (latent impression), and because the sense faculties are present when there is contact with a real object. Therefore, this <s>pratyabhijñā</s> (recognition), having as its object a single crystal (<s>sphaṭika</s>) and the like connected with multiple places, times, and conditions, establishes permanence (<s>sthairya</s>).

children.text:
tathānumānato 'pi sthiratāsiddhiḥ | prayogaḥ |
	vivādādhyāsitaḥ sa evāyaṃ sphaṭika ityādi pratyabhijñāpratyayo yathārthaḥ | abādhitapratyayatvāt | yāvān abādhitapratyayaḥ sa sarvo yathārtha upalabdhaḥ | yathā svasaṃvedanapratyayaḥ | abādhitaś cāyam | tasmāt tatheti | abādhitañ ca parodbhāvitakṣaṇikatvasādhanabādhakoddhārān niśceyam |
children.translated_text:
Likewise, the establishment of permanence (<s>sthiratā</s>) [follows] also from inference (<s>anumāna</s>). The formal argument (<s>prayoga</s>):
The cognition of recognition (<s>pratyabhijñā</s>) in dispute, [of the form] 'this is that same crystal (<s>sphaṭika</s>)' and so on, is veridical (<s>yathārtha</s>), because it is an uncontradicted cognition (<s>abādhita-pratyaya</s>). Whatever is an uncontradicted cognition has been found to be veridical — as, for example, the cognition of self-awareness (<s>svasaṃvedana</s>). And this [recognition] is uncontradicted. Therefore it is so. And its being uncontradicted is to be ascertained from the removal of the proofs and sublating cognitions (<s>bādhaka</s>) for momentariness (<s>kṣaṇikatva</s>) raised by the opponent.

children.text: athāparaḥ prayogaḥ | vivādādhyāsitā bhāvāḥ pūrvāparakālayor ekasvabhāvāḥ abādhitapratyabhijñayā pratyabhijñāyamānatvāt | yad yad abādhitapratyabhijñayā pratyabhijñāyate tat sarvam abhinnam, yathā yas tvayā dṛṣṭo nīlo 'rthaḥ sa eva mayā dṛṣta iti nīlo 'rthaḥ pratyabhijñāyate | tathā caite bhāvāḥ | tasmāt tatheti | pūrvaṃ pratyayasya dharmitā | adhunā bhāvānām iti viśeṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: Now another formal argument (<s>prayoga</s>): The entities in dispute are of one nature at the earlier and later times, because they are recognized through uncontradicted <s>pratyabhijñā</s> (recognition). Whatever is recognized through uncontradicted <s>pratyabhijñā</s>, all that is non-different — just as the blue object recognized [in the form] 'the blue object seen by you is the very same one seen by me.' And these entities are likewise. Therefore they are so. The previous [argument established] the property-bearerness (<s>dharmitā</s>) of the cognition; now the distinction is that it is [the property-bearerness] of the entities.

children.text: kiṃ ca sahetukatvād vināśasya sthairyaṃ siddham | prayogaḥ | vivādāspadībhūtā bhāvā yathāsvaṃ vināśahetusannidheḥ prāṅ na vināśinaḥ | sahetukavināśatvāt | yad yaddhetukaṃ tat tadasannidhau na bhavati | yathā vahnyādyabhāve dhūmādiḥ | sahetukavināśāś cāṃī bhāvāḥ | tasmāt tatheti |
children.translated_text: Furthermore, since destruction has a cause, permanence (<s>sthairya</s>) is established. The formal argument (<s>prayoga</s>): The entities in dispute do not perish before the proximity of their respective causes of destruction, because their destruction has a cause (<s>sahetuka-vināśa</s>). Whatever has a cause does not occur in the absence of that [cause] — just as smoke and the like [do not occur] in the absence of fire and the like. And these entities have caused destruction. Therefore they are so.

children.text: sahetukavināśatvaṃ ca ghaṭasyāgnidhūmayor iva pratyakṣānupalambhato mudgaravināśayor api kāryakāraṇabhāvasiddhau siddham | na ca vināśahetor asāmarthyavaiyarthyābhidhānam ucitam | aṅkurādihetor api tathātvaprasaṅgāt | śakyaṃ hi vaktum arthasya bhaviṣṇutāyāṃ asamartho janmahetuḥ | bhaviṣṇutāyāṃ vyartha iti |
children.translated_text: And the fact that destruction has a cause is established — just as in the case of a pot, fire and smoke, through perception — and also through the apprehension (<s>upalambha</s>) of the causal relation (<s>kāryakāraṇabhāva</s>) between a hammer-blow and destruction. Nor is it proper to assert the incapacity or purposelessness of the cause of destruction, because the same absurd consequence would apply to causes like sprouts as well. For one could equally say: the cause of origination is incapable of [producing] the entity's future existence, or that it is purposeless for [that] future existence.

children.text: api ca akṣaṇikāḥ santaḥ | kāraṇavattvāt | yat kāraṇavat tad akṣaṇikam | yathā bhāvavināśaḥ | kāraṇavantaś ceme santaḥ | tasmād akṣaṇikā iti |
children.translated_text: Moreover, existing things are non-momentary (<s>akṣaṇika</s>), because they possess causes (<s>kāraṇavattva</s>). Whatever possesses a cause is non-momentary — as, for example, the destruction of an entity. And these existing things possess causes. Therefore they are non-momentary.

children.text: kāraṇavattvasya sādhyaviparyaye vṛttiśaṅkā vināśasya sahetukatvam eva nivartayatīti prasiddhavyāptikāt kāraṇavattvād akṣaṇikatvasiddhir iti |
children.translated_text: The suspicion that the property of possessing causes occurs in the counter-thesis [i.e., in momentary things] is itself what removes the thesis that destruction has a cause — therefore, from the property of possessing causes, whose pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>) is well-established, the establishment of non-momentariness (<s>akṣaṇikatva</s>) [follows].

children.text:
tathā Śaṅkaraḥ Sthirasiddhau prāha |
	notpattyanantaravināśī bhāvaḥ prameyatvāt | vastuvyāvṛttivad iti |
children.translated_text:
Likewise, <s>Śaṅkara</s> states in the <s>Sthirasiddhi</s>:
An entity does not perish immediately after origination, because it is an object of valid cognition (<s>prameyatva</s>) — like the exclusion of [what is] other than a real entity.

children.text: avidyamānavipakṣatvād anvayy eva hetuḥ | prameyatvasya kṣaṇikatvena virodhābhāvāt sandigdhavyatirekitvam iti cet |
children.translated_text: If it is said that the reason (<s>hetu</s>) is merely of the positive-concomitance-only type (<s>anvayin</s>), since there is no existent counter-example (<s>vipakṣa</s>), and that because there is no contradiction between <s>prameyatva</s> (being an object of cognition) and <s>kṣaṇikatva</s> (momentariness), the negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>) is doubtful —

children.text: na khalu kṣaṇikatve kasyacit prameyatvaṃ sidhyati | kṣaṇasthitidharmaṇaḥ pramāṇakāle 'pātāt | atītasya ca prameyatve 'tiprasaṅgād iti |
children.translated_text: Indeed, under [the thesis of] momentariness, <s>prameyatva</s> (being an object of cognition) is not established for anything, because what has the property of lasting [only] a moment does not fall within the scope of a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid cognition) at the time of cognition. And if what is past were an object of cognition, there would be an over-extension [of the concept].

children.text: evam eva prayogam upastuvan
children.translated_text: Endorsing precisely this formal argument,

children.text: trilocano
children.translated_text: <s>Trilocana</s>

children.text:
'py āha |
	akṣaṇikāḥ sarvabhāvāḥ | prameyatvāt | yat pramīyate tad akṣaṇikam | yathā bhāvavināśaḥ | prameyāś ca sarvabhāvāḥ | tasmād akṣaṇikā iti |
children.translated_text:
also says:
All entities are non-momentary (<s>akṣaṇika</s>), because they are objects of valid cognition (<s>prameya</s>). Whatever is cognized is non-momentary — as, for example, the destruction of an entity. And all entities are objects of cognition. Therefore they are non-momentary.

children.text: asiddho dṛṣṭāntadharmīti cet | na svakāraṇakalāpād utpattimato bhāvasyāntareṇa nivṛttiprasavaṃ sarvadāvasthānaprasaṅgāt | tadaiva bhāvo 'sti na pūrvaṃ na paścād ity api śabdaḥ kṣaṇikaparyāyatveneṣyamāṇaḥ kṣaṇād ūrdhvaṃ sattāvicchedopajananam antareṇa nārthavān devair api śakyaḥ parikalpayitum | vināśakālāpekṣayā hi kṣaṇo 'lpīyān kālaḥ | tena so 'syāstīti kṣaṇiko vaktavyaḥ | itarathā janmavināśayor ekasmin kāle bhavatoḥ tulyahetukatvenaikatvaprasaṅgaḥ | ekatve tu dvayor ekataraḥ prahātavyaḥ | tatra janmaprahāṇe bhāvā niḥsvabhāvāḥ prasajyeran | nivṛttipratiyāge ca janmino bhāvā nityā iti durnivāraḥ prasaṅgaḥ | tat siddho dṛṣṭāntaḥ |
children.translated_text: If it is said that the subject of the example (<s>dṛṣṭānta-dharmin</s>) is unestablished — no, because an entity that has originated from its own causal aggregate would, without the production of cessation, absurdly persist forever. Even the expression 'the entity exists only at that [moment], not before, not after' — which is intended as a synonym for 'momentary' — cannot be rendered meaningful, even by the gods, without the generation of a break in existence beyond a single moment. For a <s>kṣaṇa</s> (moment) is a duration shorter than the time of destruction. Therefore, one must say that it [destruction] has that [moment as its measure], hence it is momentary (<s>kṣaṇika</s>). Otherwise, since origination and destruction would occur at the same time, there would be the absurd consequence of their identity, due to having the same cause. And if they were identical, one of the two would have to be abandoned. If origination were abandoned, entities would be devoid of intrinsic nature (<s>niḥsvabhāva</s>). And if cessation were relinquished, entities that originate would be permanent (<s>nitya</s>) — an inescapable absurd consequence. Therefore, the example is established.

children.text: nanu prameyatvakṣaṇikatvayor virodhāsiddheḥ sandigdhavipakṣavyāvṛttikaṃ prameyatvam iti cet |
children.translated_text: Now, if it is said that since the contradiction between <s>prameyatva</s> (being an object of cognition) and <s>kṣaṇikatva</s> (momentariness) is not established, <s>prameyatva</s> has doubtful exclusion from the counter-thesis (<s>vipakṣa</s>) —

children.text: naitad asti | yasmād arthaṃ kiñcit prāpayat pratyakṣaṃ tena pratyāsannatvāt prāpayati | pratyāsattiś ca tadutpattir evāvakalpate | na tādātmyam | sākāranirākāravādayor aprakṛtatvāt | anyatra nirākṛtatvāc ca | sā ca niyatavastupratibhāsākṣiptā kāryakāraṇabhāvalakṣaṇā pratyāsattis tulyakālaṃ pramāṇaprameyayor anupapannā, sevyetaraviṣāṇayor iva | tataḥ pramāṇam arthasattāṃ bodhayat tadadhīnotpādatayā bodhayati | kāraṇabhāvamātrānubandhitvāc ca tasya pūrvakālasattyā bhavitavyam | ataḥ pūrvakālasattvena vyāptaṃ prameyatvam | pūrvakālasattvaṃ ca kṣaṇikatve 'nupapannam iti vyāpakānupalabdhyā vipakṣāt kṣaṇikatvād vyāvartamānaṃ prameyatvam akṣaṇikatvena vyāpyata iti asandigdho vyatirekaḥ |
children.translated_text: This is not so. Because perception, which brings about some object, brings it about due to its proximity to that [object]. And that proximity amounts to nothing other than the origination of that [cognition from the object]. It is not identity (<s>tādātmya</s>), since the doctrines of cognition-with-form (<s>sākāra</s>) and cognition-without-form (<s>nirākāra</s>) are not at issue here, and have been refuted elsewhere. And that proximity — characterized by a causal relation (<s>kāryakāraṇabhāva</s>), implied by the appearance of a determinate object — is impossible between <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of cognition) and <s>prameya</s> (object of cognition) at the same time, just as between a hare's horn and its counterpart. Therefore, a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of cognition), in revealing the existence of an object, reveals it through being dependent on that [object] for its own origination. And since it is invariably connected only with the causal status [of the object], that [object] must have existence at a prior time. Hence <s>prameyatva</s> (being an object of cognition) is pervaded by prior-temporal existence. And prior-temporal existence is impossible under momentariness (<s>kṣaṇikatva</s>). Therefore, through <s>vyāpakānupalabdhi</s> (non-apprehension of the pervader), <s>prameyatva</s> — being excluded from the counter-thesis of <s>kṣaṇikatva</s> (momentariness) — is pervaded by non-momentariness (<s>akṣaṇikatva</s>). Thus the negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>) is not doubtful.

children.text: tad evam anumānapramāṇasiddho 'kṣaṇika iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus, [the entity] is established as non-momentary (<s>akṣaṇika</s>) through the <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means of cognition) of inference (<s>anumāna</s>).

children.text: evam arthāpattir apy asya sādhikā | tathā hi kāryakāraṇabhāvagrahaṇaṃ kramayaugapadyagrahaṇaṃ smaraṇam abhilāṣaḥ svayaṃnihitapratyanumārgaṇaṃ dṛṣṭārthakutūhalaviramaṇaṃ karmaphalasambandhaḥ saṃśayapūrvakanirṇayaḥ bandhamokṣaḥ mokṣaprayatnaḥ śubhādike karmaṇi pravṛttiḥ pratyabhijñā kāryakāraṇabhāvaḥ | upādānopādeyabhāvaprabhṛtayaḥ sthirasattām antareṇānupapadyamānāḥ sthairyaṃ sādhayanti | pratikṣaṇaṃ bhede saty anubhavitur vinaṣṭatve 'nyasya kāryakāraṇabhāvagrahaṇādyanupapatter iti kathaṃ kṣaṇabhaṅgaśaṅkā 'pi ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) also serves as a proof for this. For the apprehension of cause-and-effect relations (<s>kāryakāraṇabhāva</s>), the apprehension of sequence and simultaneity, memory (<s>smaraṇa</s>), desire (<s>abhilāṣa</s>), the search for something one has placed oneself, the cessation of curiosity about a seen object, the connection between action and result (<s>karmaphala-sambandha</s>), determination preceded by doubt, bondage and liberation (<s>bandha-mokṣa</s>), effort toward liberation (<s>mokṣa-prayatna</s>), engagement in virtuous and other actions, <s>pratyabhijñā</s> (recognition), cause-and-effect relation (<s>kāryakāraṇabhāva</s>), the relation of material cause and product (<s>upādāna-upādeya-bhāva</s>), and the like — being impossible without enduring existence (<s>sthira-sattā</s>) — establish permanence (<s>sthairya</s>). Since, if there were difference at every moment, and the experiencer were destroyed, the apprehension of cause-and-effect relations and the rest by another [experiencer] would be impossible — how then could there even be a suspicion of momentary destruction (<s>kṣaṇabhaṅga</s>)?

children.text: atrābhidhīyate | apramāṇam evāyaṃ pratyabhijñākhyo vikalpo mithyātvaṃ ca sadviṣayatvabādhakapratyayāt |
