children.translated_text: To this we reply: This conceptual construction (<s>vikalpa</s>) called <s>pratyabhijñā</s> (recognition) is simply not a valid means of cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>), and its falsity [is established] through a sublating cognition (<s>bādhaka-pratyaya</s>) that contradicts its having a real object.

children.text: nanv asya bādhakaṃ pratyakṣam asambhavi | anumānaṃ cāsamartham āveditam iti cet | nanv asya pratyabhijñānasya svārthāvinābhāvadārḍhye pratyakṣasahasreṇāpi kim | saṃvādaśaithilye tu bādhakapratyakṣavad anumānam api prāptāvakāśam | pramāṇasyaiva siddhibādhyor adhikārāt | tathā hi māyākāraḥ śirasi nimajjitaṃ golakam āsyena niḥsārayatīti pratyabhijñā śirasi cchidraprasaṅgasaṅgatenānumānena bādhyamānā pratītaiva | bādhyamānā na pratyabhijñeti prastute 'py astu |
children.translated_text: If it is said that a sublating perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) of this [recognition] is impossible, and that inference (<s>anumāna</s>) has been shown to be incapable [of sublating it] — well then, if the invariable connection of this <s>pratyabhijñā</s> (recognition) with its object is firm, what could even a thousand perceptions do? But if the concordance is weak, then inference too finds its opportunity, just like a sublating perception, since it is <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid cognition) alone that has authority for both establishment and refutation. For example, the recognition that 'a magician causes a ball swallowed into the head to emerge from the mouth' — this <s>pratyabhijñā</s> is clearly sublated by the inference connected with the absurd consequence of a hole in the head. It is well-established that what is sublated is not [genuine] <s>pratyabhijñā</s> (recognition) — let this apply to the present case as well.

children.text: yathā 'vanatākāśapratibhāsaḥ sarvasaṃpratipattāv api bādhya eva tadvad ekatāgrahaḥ sarvasaṃpratipattāv api bādhyo 'stu | tasmād asyāḥ pratyakṣatākīrtanaṃ yācitakamaṇḍanamātram atrāṇam | katham ataḥ sthairyasthitir astu |
children.translated_text: Just as the appearance of a dome-like sky, even though universally accepted, is nevertheless sublatable — so too, the apprehension of unity, even though universally accepted, should be sublatable. Therefore, proclaiming the perceptual character of this [recognition] is mere borrowed ornament (<s>yācitaka-maṇḍana</s>) — no protection. How then can the establishment of permanence (<s>sthairya</s>) stand?

children.text: tataś cānumānatvam apy asyā dhvastam | uktakrameṇābādhitatvaviśeṣaṇaviruddhabādhyamānatāyāḥ prasādhanād iti  viśeṣaṇāsiddho hetuḥ |
children.translated_text: Consequently, the inferential character of this [recognition] is also destroyed. Since, by the method stated [above], the property of being-sublated — which contradicts the qualification 'being uncontradicted' (<s>abādhitatva</s>) — has been demonstrated, the reason (<s>hetu</s>) has an unestablished qualifier (<s>viśeṣaṇāsiddha</s>).

children.text: yadāpi kṣaṇabhaṅgasādhakaṃ bādhakaṃ nocyate asyās tadāpīyam apramāṇam eva | lūnapunarjātakeśādau vyabhicāropalambhāt |
children.translated_text: Even when the sublating cognition for momentary destruction (<s>kṣaṇabhaṅga</s>) is not invoked as the <s>bādhaka</s> (sublator) of this [recognition], it is still not a valid means of cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>), because deviation (<s>vyabhicāra</s>) is observed in the case of hair that has been cut and regrown, and the like.

children.text: nanūktaṃ yā vyabhicāriṇī sā na pratyabhijñetyādi |
children.translated_text: If it is objected: 'But it was stated that whatever deviates is not <s>pratyabhijñā</s> (recognition)' and so on —

children.text: yuktam etat | yadi kāryakāraṇabhāvapratītival lakṣaṇabhedaḥ pratipādayituṃ śakyeta | yathā hy anvayavyatirekagrahaṇapravaṇapratyakṣānupalambhād upapanno niścayaḥ kāryakāraṇabhāvapratītir anyas tadābhāsapratītir ity anayor lakṣaṇabhedaḥ, tathā yadi pratyabhijñe 'pi lakṣaṇabhedo darśitaḥ syāt, darśayituṃ vā śakyo vyabhicārāvyabhicāropayogī, tadā bhavatu pratyabhijñātadābhāsayor vivekaḥ | na tv evam asti | sarvatrātyantasadṛśe vastuni pṛthagjanapratyabhijñāyā ekarasatvāt |
children.translated_text: This is appropriate — if a distinction in defining characteristics could be demonstrated, as in the case of the apprehension of the causal relation. For just as the certainty established through perception and non-apprehension, which tend toward grasping positive and negative concomitance, that the apprehension of the causal relation is different from the apprehension of its semblance — if such a distinction in defining characteristics were shown in the case of recognition (<s>pratyabhijñā</s>) too, or could be shown as useful for establishing deviation and non-deviation, then let there be a discrimination between genuine recognition and its semblance. But this is not so, because in all cases, when the object is extremely similar, the ordinary person's recognition is of a uniform character.

children.text: saṃvāditvāsaṃvāditve lakṣaṇabheda iti cet | na | aliṅgasya hi vikalpasya saṃvādo nāma pramāṇāntarasaṅgatir athakriyāprāptir vā |
children.translated_text: If it is said that the distinction in defining characteristics consists in concordance (<s>saṃvāditva</s>) and discordance (<s>asaṃvāditva</s>) — no. For the concordance of a conceptual cognition (<s>vikalpa</s>), which has no inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>), is either agreement with another means of valid cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>), or the attainment of purposeful action (<s>arthakriyā</s>).

children.text: tatra na tāvad ādyaḥ pakṣaḥ | paścād api sa evāyam iti svatantraikādhyavasāyamātrād aparasya pramāṇagandhasyāpy abhāvāt |
children.translated_text: Of these, the first alternative does not hold, because even afterwards, from the mere independent determination "this is that very same thing," there is not even a trace of any other means of valid cognition.

children.text: nāpi dvitīyaḥ pakṣaḥ saṅgacchate | na hi pūrvāparakālayor ekavastupratibaddhā siddhā kācid arthakriyā | bhinnenāpi tatsamānaśaktinā tādṛgarthakriyāyāḥ karaṇāvirodhāt | tathā hi yathaiko ghaṭo vāri dhārayatīti tatkālabhāvino 'py anyasya deśāntaravartino na vāridhāraṇavāraṇam, tathā dvitīyādikṣaṇo 'py anyo yadi vāri dhārayati, kīdṛśo doṣaḥ syāt | visadṛśakriyāyāṃ tu cintaiva nāsti | tat kathaṃ pratyabhijñānasya saṃvādasambhavaḥ |
children.translated_text: Nor does the second alternative hold. For there is no established purposeful action (<s>arthakriyā</s>) bound to a single entity across earlier and later times. Because there is no contradiction in the performance of such purposeful action even by a different entity possessing the same capacity. For just as one pot holds water, yet this does not prevent another pot existing at another place at that same time from also holding water, similarly, if another entity at the second moment and so on also holds water, what fault would there be? And in the case of a dissimilar action, there is no question at all. Therefore, how is concordance of recognition possible?

children.text: nanu yady ekam pratyabhijñānaṃ visaṃvādi dṛṣṭam iti sarvam eva pratyabhijñānaṃ visaṃvādi śaṃkyate, tadaikam indriyajñānaṃ keśoṇḍukadvicandrādau visaṃvādyupalabdham iti ghaṭādiṣv api sarvam eva pratyakṣaṃ visaṃvādi sambhāvyatām | indriyajanyatvasyaikalakṣaṇasya sarvatra sambhavād iti cet |
children.translated_text: [Objection:] If, because one instance of recognition is seen to be discordant, all recognition whatsoever is suspected of being discordant, then since one instance of sensory cognition is found to be discordant in the case of hair-nets, floaters, double moons and the like, let all perception whatsoever be suspected of being discordant even with respect to pots and so on — since the single defining characteristic of being produced by the senses obtains everywhere.

children.text: na, tatrāpi lakṣaṇabhedasya sadbhāvāt | tathā hi bahirarthasthitāv indriyārthakāryatayā sākṣād arthākārānukāritvaṃ pratyakṣatvam | tac cābhyāsaviśeṣāsāditapaṭimnā pratyakṣeṇa niścīyate | kvacit tv arthakriyāprāptijñānād iti pratyakṣatvaṃ anavadyam eva | dvicandrādau tv arthavinākṛtena timirādiviplutacakṣurmātreṇa tajjñānaṃ janitam iti pratyakṣābhāsam eva | dvicandrādyarthābhāvas tu deśakālanarāntarair dvicandrāder arthasya bādhitatvād avyāhata iti pratyakṣābhāsapariihāre 'pi pratyakṣeṣu ka āśvāsavirodhaḥ |
children.translated_text: No, because even there a distinction in defining characteristics exists. For when an external object is present, perception (<s>pratyakṣatva</s>) consists in directly mirroring the form of the object, as being an effect of the sense organ and object. And this is ascertained by perception that has acquired proficiency through repeated practice. In some cases, it is ascertained from the knowledge of the attainment of purposeful action — thus perception is entirely faultless. But in the case of double moons and the like, that cognition is produced merely by a sense organ affected by an eye-disease (<s>timira</s>) and the like, devoid of the object — thus it is merely a semblance of perception (<s>pratyakṣābhāsa</s>). And the absence of the object such as a double moon is uncontradicted, since the object of double moons and the like is sublated by other places, times, and persons. Therefore, even when semblances of perception are set aside, what contradiction is there to confidence in genuine perceptions?

children.text: pratyabhijñāne 'pi sarvam idam astīti na yuktam | yathā hi pūrvaṃ pāvakādau pākādikriyā pratibaddhā siddhā paścād anubhūyamānā dahanajñānasya saṃvādam āvedayati | anyathā bāhyārthocchedān nirīhaṃ jagaj jāyate | na tathā prathamacaramakālayor ekībhāvapratibaddhā kācid arthakriyā upalabdhigocarā pūrvāparakālayor ekatvam antareṇa vā pravṛttyādikṣatir yenaikatāvagraho 'pi saṃvādī syāt |
children.translated_text: But it is not appropriate to say that all this applies to recognition as well. For just as the cooking and other actions previously established as bound to fire and the like, when experienced afterwards, confirm the concordance of the cognition of fire — otherwise, with the destruction of external objects, the world would become inert — there is no such purposeful action bound to the identity of a single entity across the first and last moments that falls within the range of apprehension, nor is there any occurrence of activity and the like without the oneness of earlier and later times, by which the apprehension of identity too would be concordant.

children.text: tad iyam anumānabādhitatvād vyabhicāraśaṅkākalaṅkitatvāc ca na pratyakṣam anumānaṃ veti | katham ataḥ sthairyasiddhir anumānapratihatir vā |
children.translated_text: Therefore, since this is contradicted by inference and tainted by the suspicion of deviation, it is neither perception nor inference. How then can the establishment of permanence (<s>sthairya</s>) or the refutation of inference follow from this?

children.text: yat punar Vācaspatir uvāca | saṃskārendriyayor militayor eva pratyabhijñānaṃ prati kāraṇatvam iti, tad ayuktam | bhinnasāmagrīprasūtatvād anayor jñānayoḥ | tathā hi nimīlite cakṣuṣi sa ity atrendriyavinākṛtasyaiva saṃskārasya sāmarthyam upalabdham | prathamadarśane tv ayam ity atra saṃskārarahitasyaivendriyasya sāmarthyaṃ dṛṣṭam | tasmāt sāmagrīdvayapratibaddhaṃ jñānadvayam idam avadhāritam | katham ubhābhyāṃ militvaikam eva pratyabhijñānam utpāditam ity udghuṣyate | bījakṣityādyos tu pṛthak sāmarthyaṃ na dṛṣṭam ity ekaiva sāmagrīty aṅkuro 'py eka evāstu |
children.translated_text: Now, as for what <s>Vācaspati</s> said — that the causal efficacy with respect to recognition belongs to the disposition (<s>saṃskāra</s>) and the sense organ only when combined — that is wrong. Because these two cognitions arise from different causal complexes (<s>sāmagrī</s>). For when the eyes are closed, only the disposition without the sense organ is seen to have efficacy with respect to the 'that' component; and in the first perception, the sense organ alone without any disposition is seen to have efficacy with respect to the 'this' component. Therefore, it is established that these two cognitions are bound to two different causal complexes. How can it be proclaimed that from both combined a single recognition is produced? In the case of a seed and earth, however, since no separate efficacy is observed, there is a single causal complex — and accordingly, the sprout too is a single entity.

children.text: tathā pūrvadeśakālāparadeśakālābhyāṃ tatsambaddhābhyām anyatvāt padmarāgasyābheda ity apy asaṅgatam | viruddhayor dharmayoḥ padmarāgād anyatve 'pi viruddhadharmayogāt padmarāgasya bhedaḥ katham apahnūyate | trailokaikatvaprasaṅgasya durvāratvāt | na hi dharmadharmiṇor anyatve 'pi brāhmaṇatvacaṇḍālatve ekādhāre bhavitum arhata iti padmarāgasya bhedo duratikramaḥ |
children.translated_text: Likewise, the claim that the ruby (<s>padmarāga</s>) is non-different because it is other than the two — namely the prior place-and-time and the later place-and-time and their associates — is also incoherent. Even though the contradictory properties are other than the ruby, how can the difference of the ruby be denied when contradictory properties are conjoined in it? For the absurd consequence that the entire three worlds would be one is unavoidable. Just as <s>brāhmaṇa</s>-hood and <s>caṇḍāla</s>-hood cannot reside in a single substratum even though properties and property-bearer are different, so the difference of the ruby is inescapable.

children.text: tathā ca na svabhāvavirodho 'numānasyāpy anekatvaprasaṅgāt | tad api pratyakṣam apratyakṣaṃ cāvikalpo vikalpaś cāsamāropaḥ samāropaś cety apy ayuktam | anumānasya hi paramārthataḥ svasaṃvedanapratyakṣātmano 'vikalpasyāsamāropasvabhāvasyāpratyakṣatvavikalpatvasamāropatvādeḥ parāpekṣayā prajñaptatvād viruddhadharmādhyāsābhāvāt kathaṃ bhedasiddhiḥ | sa evāyam iti tu pratyabhijñānasya sa ity aspaṣṭākārayogitvam, ayam iti spaṣṭākārayogitvam iti viruddhadharmadvayaṃ bhedakam |
children.translated_text: And similarly, the objection that there is no essential contradiction and that inference too would be subject to the absurd consequence of multiplicity — and that inference too would be both perception and non-perception, both non-conceptual and conceptual, both non-superimposition and superimposition — is also wrong. For since inference, which is ultimately of the nature of self-awareness (<s>svasaṃvedana</s>) — a perception, non-conceptual, and of the nature of non-superimposition — is designated as non-perceptual, conceptual, superimposition and so on only conventionally in relation to other things, there is no superimposition of contradictory properties, so how is difference established? But in the case of recognition 'this is that same one,' the fact that recognition possesses an indistinct form with respect to the 'that' component and a distinct form with respect to the 'this' component — these two contradictory properties are what establish difference.

children.text: nacaivaṃ vaktavyam | tattedantāpekṣayā pratyabhijñānasyāpy ekasyaiva pārokṣyāpārokṣyam aviruddham iti | na hīdam ekākāratayā vyavasthitam, yenānumānavad asyāpi pārokṣyāpārokṣyavyavasthāmātraṃ syāt | yāvad atītārthākārānukāro vartamānārthānukāraś ca svadharmo na bhavati tāvat tadarthagocarataiva nāsti | kutaḥ pārokṣyāpārokṣyavyavahāro bhaviṣyati | tasmāt spaṣṭāspaṣṭākāradvayaviruddhadharmādhyāsāt pratyabhijñānaṃ pratyayadvayam etad iti sthitam ||
children.translated_text: Nor should it be said that just as with respect to 'that' and 'this,' the indirect and direct character of recognition, being a single cognition, is non-contradictory. For this is not established as having a single form, such that, like inference, it would merely have the status of being indirect and direct. So long as the mirroring of the form of the past object and the mirroring of the present object are not its own properties, there is no reference to those objects at all. Whence would the usage of indirect and direct arise? Therefore, because of the superimposition of the contradictory properties of the two — distinct and indistinct forms — it is established that recognition is in fact two cognitions.

children.text: tathā sahetukavināśatvād ayam apy asiddho hetuḥ | yat punar atroktam | sahetukavināśatvaṃ ghaṭasyāgnidhūmayor iva pratyakṣānupalambhato mudgraghaṭavināśayor api kāryakāraṇabhāvasiddhau siddham iti | tad asaṅgatam | agnidhūmayor api dṛśyatvāt, pratyakṣānupalambhato dhūmasya vahnikāryatā sidhyatu | vināśaśabdavācyas tv artho na kaścid idantayā dṛṣṭaḥ | karparam eva ghaṭamudgarābhyām utpadyamānam upalabdham |
children.translated_text: Likewise, the argument that 'because destruction has a cause' is also unestablished. Now, what was stated here — that caused destruction (<s>sahetukavināśatva</s>) is established through the establishment of the causal relation between the hammer and the destruction of the pot from perception and non-apprehension, just as between fire and smoke — that is incoherent. For even in the case of fire and smoke, since both are visible, let the fact that smoke is an effect of fire be established from perception and non-apprehension. But the referent denoted by the word 'destruction' (<s>vināśa</s>) is not perceived as 'this' by anyone. What is perceived is only the potsherds (<s>karpara</s>) being produced from the pot and hammer.

children.text: yad āhur guravaḥ |
children.translated_text: As the masters have said:
And this defining characteristic is possible even in recognition, by the reasoning stated — so this is indeed a valid means of knowledge.

children.text:
dṛṣṭas tāvad ayaṃ ghaṭo 'tra ca patan dṛṣṭas tathā mudgaro dṛṣṭā karparasaṃhatiḥ paramato nāśo na dṛṣṭaḥ paraḥ | 
	tenābhāva iti śrutiḥ kva nihitā kiṃ vātra tatkāraṇaṃ svādhīnā palighasya kevalam iyaṃ dṛṣṭā kapālāvaliḥ ||
children.translated_text: "First this pot was seen, and a hammer falling upon it was seen, and the collection of potsherds was seen; but beyond that, no destruction was seen. Therefore, where is the statement 'it is an absence' grounded? And what is its cause here? Only this row of potsherds, dependent on the iron bar, was seen."

children.text: tad ayam abhāvo dṛśyānupalabdhibādhitaḥ kathaṃ pratyakṣato mudgarādikāryam avadhāryaḥ |
yat punar asminn adṛśyamāne 'pi dṛśyata iti bāgjālaṃ sā bhaṇḍavidyā | tadvacanād gṛhṇann api paśur eva | tatha hi
children.translated_text: Now, the verbal trickery of saying 'it is seen' even when this is not being seen — that is a conjurer's art (<s>bhaṇḍavidyā</s>). One who accepts it on the basis of such a statement is nothing but an animal. For thus:
Therefore, how can this absence (<s>abhāva</s>), which is contradicted by the non-apprehension of the visible, be ascertained from perception as an effect of the hammer and the like?

children.text:
kasyacit pratibhāsena sādhyate 'pratibhāsi yat |
	pratibhāso 'sya nāsyeti nopapattes tu gocaraḥ || iti |
athaivaṃ vaktavyam | kim anyena dhvaṃsena, karparam eva ghaṭadhvaṃso 'stu | tathā ca sati mudgarādyabhāve karparābhāvāt ghaṭasthairyam avyāhatam iti
children.translated_text: Now, if one were to say: what need is there for a separate <s>dhvaṃsa</s> (destruction as an entity)? Let the potsherd itself be the destruction of the pot. And in that case, in the absence of a hammer and the like, since there would be no potsherds, the permanence (<s>sthairya</s>) of the pot is uncontradicted —

children.text: durāśā khalv eṣā | tathā hi yathā nāśaśabdena karparam ucyate tathā yady abhāvaśabdenāpi karparam evocyate tadaikatra pradeśe ghaṭam ekam apanīya ghaṭāntaranyāse tatrāpanītaghaṭasyābhāvavyavahāro na syāt | tatpradhvaṃsakapālayos tatrānutpādāt | tasmād yathāpanītaghaṭasya pracyutimātrāpekṣayā nyastaghaṭe 'bhāvavyavahāras tathā mudgarādikāraṇābhāvāt pradhvaṃsakarparayor anupāde 'pi pracyutimātrāpekṣayaiva pratikṣaṇam anyānyatvavyavahāro ghaṭasya sidhyatīti kutaḥ sthairyasiddhiḥ | tasmāt pradhvaṃsakarparābhāve 'pi pracyutimātrātmakabhāvāpekṣayāpy asmanmatam avyāhatam |
children.translated_text: this is indeed a vain hope. For if, just as the word 'destruction' refers to the potsherds, the word 'absence' also refers only to the potsherds, then when one removes one pot from a certain place and puts another pot there, there would be no usage of 'absence' with respect to the removed pot, since neither the <s>pradhvaṃsa</s> (posterior absence) nor the potsherds of that pot have arisen there. Therefore, just as the usage of 'absence' with respect to the removed pot depends merely on its departure even when another pot is placed there, similarly, even without the production of <s>pradhvaṃsa</s>-potsherds, depending merely on departure, the usage of being-other-at-each-moment with respect to the pot is established at every moment — so whence is permanence established? Therefore, even in the absence of <s>pradhvaṃsa</s>-potsherds, our position is uncontradicted, depending merely on the nature of departure.

children.text: yad āhur guravaḥ |
children.translated_text: As the masters have said:
"When something that does not appear is established by the appearance of something else, and one says 'this appears, that does not' — this is not within the scope of valid reasoning."

children.text:
āstāṃ karparapaṃktir eva kalaśadhvaṃso na ceyaṃ purā 
	tena sthairyam api prasidhyatu tato bhinnena nāśena kim |
children.translated_text: "Let the row of potsherds itself be the destruction of the pot, and let this not have existed before — thus let permanence too be established from that. Then what need is there for a separate destruction?"

children.text: atrottaram,
children.translated_text: Here is the reply:

children.text:
nāsaḥ saiva yathocyate yadi tathābhāvo 'pi kumbhāntaranyāse
	'bhāvavacaḥ kathaṃ matam ataḥ sidhyaty abhāve 'pi naḥ || iti |

nanu yadi svahetujanito nāśo nāsti, kathaṃ kvacid eva deśe kāle ghaṭo naṣṭa iti pratītiniyamaḥ | na ca mudgarād anyo nāśasya hetur vaktavyaḥ | prāg api nāśasambhave naṣṭaghaṭabuddhisambhavaprasaṅgāt | yad āhuḥ |
children.translated_text: [Objection:] If there is no destruction produced by its own cause, how is there the invariable cognition that the pot is destroyed only at a certain place and time? Nor can any cause of destruction other than the hammer be stated, for otherwise the cognition of a destroyed pot would arise even before [the hammer strikes]. As they have said:

"If destruction is said to be just that [the potsherds], then absence too — when another pot is placed, how is the usage of 'absence' justified? Therefore, our position is established even with respect to absence."

children.text:
nāśo nāsti yadi svahetuniyataḥ kiṃ desakāle kvacit kumbho naṣta iti pratītiniyamas tenāsti kāryaś ca saḥ |
	nāpy anayat kila kāraṇaṃ rayavato daṇḍāt purāpy anyathā nāśotthānakṛtā vinaṣṭaghaṭadhīḥ kenoddhurā vāryate ||
children.translated_text: "If destruction is not determined by its own cause, why is there the invariable cognition 'the pot is destroyed' only at a certain place and time? Therefore that [destruction] exists and is an effect. Nor is any other cause possible — for otherwise, even before the forceful blow of the stick, the cognition of a destroyed pot, produced by the arising of destruction, could not be prevented."

children.text: iti cet |

tarhīdānīm arthāpattyā pradhvaṃsaṃ prasādhya mudgarādhīnatvam asya sādhayitum ārabdham | tathā ca sati dhūmāgnivat pratyakṣataḥ pradhvaṃsasya mudgarādikāryatvaṃ siddham ity utphullagallam ullapitaṃ vyāluptam |
children.translated_text: Then what has been attempted is to first establish <s>pradhvaṃsa</s> (posterior absence) through presumption (<s>arthāpatti</s>) and then prove its dependence on the hammer. And in that case, the boastful declaration that the fact that <s>pradhvaṃsa</s> is an effect of the hammer and the like is established from perception, just like smoke and fire, is demolished.

children.text: na cārthāpattito 'pi tatsiddhiḥ sampadyate, ghaṭo naṣṭa iti pratīter anyathāpy upapadyamānatvāt | vināśaṃ vināpi hi ghaṭadarśanavato mudgarakṛtakapālānubhava eva naṣṭaghaṭāvasāyasādhanaḥ, kim apareṇa nāśena kartavyam | ghaṭo naṣṭa iti buddher ghaṭaniścayapūrvakamudgarakṛtakapālānubhavamātrānvayavyatirekānuvidhānadarśanāt |
children.translated_text: Nor is its establishment accomplished even through presumption (<s>arthāpatti</s>), since the cognition 'the pot is destroyed' can be accounted for otherwise as well. For even without positing destruction, for one who has seen the pot, the very experience of potsherds produced by the hammer is what establishes the determination of the destroyed pot — what need is there for any further destruction? Because the cognition 'the pot is destroyed' is seen to follow invariably the mere experience of potsherds produced by the hammer, preceded by the ascertainment of the pot.

children.text: na ceyaṃ sāmagrī pūrvam apy asti | mudgarābhāve karparapaṃkter evābhāvāt kathaṃ prāg api naṣṭaghaṭabuddhiprasaṅgaḥ saṅgato nāma |
children.translated_text: Nor does this causal complex exist previously — since in the absence of the hammer, the row of potsherds itself is absent. How then is the absurd consequence of the cognition of a destroyed pot arising even before [the hammer strikes] coherent?

children.text: yad āhur guravaḥ |
children.translated_text: As the masters have said:
If so [one might say] —

children.text:
dṛṣte 'mbhobhṛti mudgarādijanitāṃ dṛṣtvā kapālāvalīṃ saṅketānugamād vinaṣṭaghaṭadhīs tāvat samutpādyate |
	sāmagryām iha nāśanāma na kim apy aṅgaṃ na cāsyām api syād eṣā na kadāpi nāpi ca purāpy eṣā samagrā sthitiḥ ||
	arthāpattir ato gatā kṣayam iyaṃ na dhvaṃsasiddhau prabhuḥ | iti |
yadi nāśānubhavo nāsti kapālānubhavāt kapālakalpanaiva syāt | na naṣṭaghaṭabuddhir iti cet |
children.translated_text: [Objection:] If there is no experience of destruction, then from the experience of potsherds there would only be the conceptual construction of potsherds, not the cognition of a destroyed pot.

children.text: tad etad atisāhasam | ghaṭaniścayapūrvakakapālavalayadarśanād eva naṣṭaghaṭabuddheḥ sākṣād evānubhūyamānatvāt | tadapalāpe dhūmādīnām api dahanādipūrvakatvaniścayo na syād ity atiprasaṅgaḥ |
children.translated_text: That is exceedingly reckless. Because the cognition of a destroyed pot is directly experienced from the very seeing of the ring of potsherds preceded by the ascertainment of the pot. If one were to deny that, then even the ascertainment that smoke and the like are preceded by fire and so on would not hold — and this would be an overextension (<s>atiprasaṅga</s>).

children.text: nanu ghaṭo naṣṭa iti buddhir viśeṣyabuddhiḥ | sā ca vināśaṃ viśeṣaṇam ākṣipatīti cet |
children.translated_text: Objection: The cognition 'the pot is destroyed' is a qualified cognition (<s>viśeṣyabuddhi</s>). And that [cognition] implies destruction as a qualifier (<s>viśeṣaṇa</s>).

children.text: tad asat, yataḥ |
children.translated_text: That is wrong, because:

"When a pot has been seen and then a row of potsherds produced by a hammer and the like is seen, the cognition of a destroyed pot arises through following convention. In this causal complex, there is no element whatsoever called 'destruction,' nor would this cognition ever arise without this complex, nor was this complex ever complete before. Therefore this presumption (<s>arthāpatti</s>) has come to naught — it has no power to establish <s>dhvaṃsa</s> (destruction)."

children.text: svabuddhyā rajyate yena viśeṣyaṃ tad viśeṣaṇam |
children.translated_text: A qualifier is that by which a qualificand is colored [i.e., characterized] through its own cognition.

children.text: ucyate | na cāvidyamānam adṛśyaṃ vā svabuddhyā kiñcid rañjyati |

prayogo 'tra | yasya na svarūpanirbhāsas tan na kasyacit svānuraktapratītinimittam | yathā karikeśaraḥ | nāsti ca svarūpanirbhāso dhvaṃsasyeti vyāpakānupalabdhiḥ | nāsyā asiddhiḥ | abhāvasya svarūpeṇaivedantayā nirbhāsābhāvāt | na ca viruddhatā, sapakṣe bhāvāt | nāpy anaikāntikatvam | pratibhāsābhāve 'pi svānuraktapratītihetutve śaśaviṣāṇāder api tathātvaṃ syād ity atiprasaṅgaḥ |
children.translated_text: The formal argument here is: That which has no appearance of its own form is not the ground of anyone's cognition as colored by itself — like the mane of an elephant. And destruction (<s>dhvaṃsa</s>) has no appearance of its own form — this is a non-apprehension of the pervader (<s>vyāpakānupalabdhi</s>). This [reason] is not unestablished, because absence (<s>abhāva</s>), being of this very nature as its own form, has no appearance. Nor is there contradiction, because it is present in the similar example. Nor is there inconclusiveness — because if [something] could be the cause of a cognition colored by itself even without appearing, then a hare's horn and the like too would be such — that would be an over-extension.

children.text: nanu
children.translated_text: Objection:
It is said: Nothing that is non-existent or invisible colors [anything] through its own cognition.

children.text:
na dhvaṃsena vinā vinaśyati jagad bhāvena sārdhaṃ sa cet sac cāsac ca kim astu vastu niyataṃ bhāvānujo 'sau tataḥ|
	bhāvāt tena tu bhinnakāraṇatayā tatkāraṇāsambhave 'bhāvāt tena kṛtānyatāpi galitā bhaṅgaḥ koto 'nukṣaṇaṃ ||
atrocyate | kāraṇāntarād utpadyamāno dhvaṃso 'bhinno bhinno vā |
children.translated_text: To this we reply: Is the destruction that is produced from another cause identical with or different from [the positive entity]?

children.text: nādyaḥ pakṣaḥ | bhinnakāraṇatvāt, tair anabhyupagatatvāc ca | atha dvitīyaḥ pakṣaḥ | tadā kaḥ punar bhāvasya pradveṣo yena pradhvaṃsākhye vastuni svahetor utpanne nivartate nāma |
children.translated_text: The first alternative is not [tenable], because of the difference in cause, and because it is not accepted by them. Now, the second alternative: then what grudge does the positive entity have against [anything], such that when a thing called 'subsequent destruction' (<s>pradhvaṃsa</s>) is produced from its own cause, [the positive entity] ceases to exist?

children.text: yat punar etad ucyate | nābhāvasyotpāde bhāvasya parā nivṛttiḥ | kiṃ tv abhāvotpattir eva tannivṛttir iti | katham anyasyotpāde 'nyasya nivṛttiḥ | atra svabhāvabhedair uttaraṃ vācyam ye parasparaparihārasthitayaḥ svahetubhyo jāyante, na hi svato 'nyasyāṅkurasya vahnir na kāraṇam ity anyatvāviśeṣād bhasmano 'pi na kāraṇam | svabhāvabhedena tu kāryakāraṇabhāvasamarthanaṃ parasparaparihārasthitiniyame 'pi tulyam | yathā cotpādasya purastād akhilasāmarthyarahitasyāṅkuraprāgabhāvasyāpakāraṃ kiñcid akurvanto 'pi bījādayo 'ṅkuram ārabhamāṇāḥ prāgabhāvaṃ nivartayanti | tadutpādasyaiva tatprāgabhāvanivṛttirūpatvāt | evaṃ tadabhāvahetavo 'pi bhāvarūpe 'kiñcitkarā api tadabhāvam ādadhānās tan nivartayanti | abhāvotpādasyaiva bhāvanivṛttirūpatvāt | tena pūrvavan nārthakriyākaraṇaprasaṅga iti |
children.translated_text: As for the further statement: 'It is not that upon the production of absence, the positive entity has a separate cessation. Rather, the production of absence itself is its cessation' — how can the production of one thing be the cessation of another? Here the answer must be given in terms of essential natures that are mutually exclusive and arise from their own causes. For it is not the case that fire, being different from sprout, is not the cause [of sprout-destruction] — and if mere otherness [were the ground for non-causation], it would not be the cause of ash either. But justifying the cause-effect relation through difference in essential nature is equally applicable to the restriction of mutual exclusion. Just as the seed and the like, while doing no harm to the prior absence of the sprout — which is utterly devoid of all capacity before the sprout's arising — nevertheless, by initiating the sprout, remove the prior absence, because the production of the sprout itself is of the nature of the removal of its prior absence. Similarly, the causes of the absence of that [entity], even while doing nothing to the positive form, by establishing the absence of that [entity], remove it — because the production of absence is itself of the nature of the cessation of the positive entity. Therefore, as before, there is no consequence of [absence] performing causal efficacy.

children.text: tad ucitaṃ syād yadi kāryakāraṇayor evāsyāpy ātmā pramāṇapratītaḥ syāt | kevalaṃ dṛśyānupalambhagraste 'py etasminn upalabhyata iti pralāpo vyaktam iyaṃ bhaṇḍavidyety uktam |
children.translated_text: That would be appropriate if the essential nature of this [destruction] too, being [of the nature] of cause and effect, were apprehended by a means of valid cognition. But to prattle that it is apprehended even when it is consumed by the non-apprehension of the visible — this is clearly charlatanry, as has been said.

children.text: arthāpattir api kṣīṇety api prāgabhāvasya ca dṛṣṭāntatvenopanyāso bhaṇḍālekhyanyāyaḥ |
children.translated_text: The <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) [argument] is also exhausted, and the citation of prior absence (<s>prāgabhāva</s>) as an example is [fallacious like] the logic of a charlatan's painting.

children.text: kiñ ca kaḥ punar atra virodhaḥ |
children.translated_text: Moreover, what exactly is the contradiction here?

The world does not perish without destruction. If it [i.e., destruction] coexists with the positive entity, then let the thing be both existent and non-existent — but that is impossible. So it follows after the positive entity. But since it has a cause different from the positive entity, and since that cause [of destruction] is impossible [if separate], the otherness produced [by destruction] from non-existence is also lost — how then [does] destruction [occur] at every moment?

children.text:
sahasthānābhāvo yadi tava virodho 'rthavipadoḥ 	sahasthānāsaṅgaḥ kṣaṇam api yathā śītaśikhinoḥ |
	sa ca dhvaṃso dhvaṃsāntaram upanayan saṃprati bhaved virodhī so 'py anyaṃ kṣayam iti na nāśaḥ katham api ||
anyathā siddhasattāmātreṇa virodhitve sarvaṃ sarveṇa viruddhaṃ prasajyeta | svabhāvālambhanam apy adarśanād eva nirastam iti |
children.translated_text: Otherwise, if contradiction consisted in mere established existence, everything would be contradictory with everything — and the [alleged] grasping of essential nature is also refuted simply from non-observation.

If your [notion of] contradiction between a thing and its cessation is the impossibility of co-location — just as cold and fire cannot coexist even for a moment — then that destruction, bringing about another destruction, would now be the contradictory [of the entity]. But that [second destruction] too [brings about] another cessation — so how is there destruction at all?

children.text: athānyonyābhāvaprakṛtikatayārthe sati tadā kṣayasyaivābhāvaḥ saha bhavatu vā hetubalataḥ |
children.translated_text: But if, through being of the nature of mutual absence, when the [positive] thing exists, then the absence of cessation [exists], or let [the thing] coexist [with cessation] through the force of a cause.

children.text: anena dhvaṃse ca prakṛtahatir asya tv anudaye balīyān evārthaḥ svayam apacaye 'nyena kim iha ||
children.translated_text: By this, [the opponent's] thesis is struck in the matter of destruction; but if it [i.e., destruction] does not arise, the stronger [position] is the thing itself [ceasing] on its own — what need here of another [entity for] decay?

children.text: sac cāsac ca kim astu vastv iti tu prasaṅgas
trilocana
children.translated_text: [raised by] <s>Trilocana</s>

children.text: prastāve nirākaraṇīyaḥ | ata evātra prastāve bhuvanaikagurūn bhagavataḥ Kīrtipādān avamanyamānaḥ êaṅkaraḥ paśor api paśur iti kṛpāpātram evaiṣa jālmaḥ |
children.translated_text: should be refuted in this context. For this very reason, in this context, [the one called] <s>Śaṅkara</s>, who disparages the blessed <s>Kīrti</s> [i.e., <s>Ratnakīrti</s>/<s>Dharmakīrti</s>], the sole teacher of the world, is an animal even among animals — this wretch is merely an object of compassion.
As for 'let the thing be both existent and non-existent' — that consequence

children.text: yad apy āha
Trilocanaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Trilocana</s>

children.text: | bhāvavyatiriktāṃ nivṛttim anicchadbhir aśakyā svarūpanivṛttir avasthāpayitum | yā hi tasya prāktanī kācid avasthā bhavadbhir arthakriyānirvartanayogyā dṛṣṭā saiva yady uttarakālam apy anuvartate tarhi svarūpeṇaiva nivṛtto bhāvaḥ katham avasthāpyate | tadānīm ayaṃ naṣṭo nāma yadi svahetupratilabdhasvarūpavyatirekinī tasya kācid avasthotpādyata, utpattau saiva tasyātmāntaraṃ jātam ity atādavasthyam evāsya vināśaṃ brūmaḥ | tādavasthyatādātmye ca svarūpeṇa nivṛtto bhāva ity asya śabdasya satyam arthaṃ na vidmaḥ |
children.translated_text: says: 'For those who do not accept a cessation distinct from the positive entity, it is impossible to maintain cessation of [the entity's] own form. For if that former state of it, which you have observed as capable of performing causal efficacy, continues even at a later time, then how can a positive entity that has ceased in its own form be maintained? At that time, [the entity] is said to be destroyed — if some state different from its form obtained from its own cause is produced, and upon its production, that [state] is just another self that has arisen — we call precisely this change of state its destruction. But as for the true meaning of the expression "the positive entity has ceased in its own form," when there is neither change of state nor change of self, we do not understand it.'
And as for what

children.text: svarūpanivṛttiḥ khalv iyaṃ bhavantī bhāva eva syāt, bhāvād anyā vā | tattve svakāraṇebhyo niṣpannasyārthasyānyathānupapattāv utpatter ārabhya sattvān nityatvaṃ prasajyeta | anyatve ca tad eva nivṛtter anyatvanirvṛtir iti priyam anuṣṭhitaṃ priyeṇa | tasmād utsṛjya vibhramaṃ nāśotpattir eva naṣṭatvam abhyupagantavyam iti |
tad etad ajñānaphalam | tathā hi
children.translated_text: This is the fruit of ignorance. For thus:

'This cessation of own form, when it occurs, would be either the positive entity itself or something other than the positive entity. If [it is] the former, then since the thing produced from its own causes cannot be otherwise explained, permanence would follow from the fact of its existence from the time of its production. If [it is] the latter, then the otherness of cessation is just [another] cessation — [so] the beloved has accomplished what is dear [i.e., you have merely restated our position]. Therefore, abandoning confusion, one should accept the arising of destruction as being-destroyed' —

children.text: svakāraṇād eva yathānyadeśavicchinnarūpaḥ samudeti bhāvaḥ |
children.translated_text: Just as a positive entity arises from its own cause with a form that is excluded from other locations,

children.text: vicchinnabhinnakṣaṇavṛttir evaṃ svakāraṇād eva na jāyate kim ||
children.translated_text: so too, with its occurrence excluded from different moments — why would it not arise from its own cause in just the same way?

children.text: abhāvato 'rthāntararūpabādhe tatrāpy abhāvāntaram īkṣaṇīyam |
children.translated_text: If the form of another thing is precluded by absence, then in that [case] too, another absence must be envisioned.

children.text: pradīpadṛṣṭāntamataṃ na kāntaṃ svarūpasandarśanaviprayogāt ||
JNA 140,4ff.

children.translated_text: The example of the lamp is not pleasing, because of [its] dissociation from the manifestation of [its] own form.

children.text: yathā hi deśāntaraparāvṛttam anīlādiparāvṛttaṃ ca svahetor utpannaṃ vastu tathā dvitīyakṣaṇātaraparāvṛttaṃ api | yathā cānyadeśānavasthāyitvaṃ taddeśāvasthāyitvenāviruddham, viruddhaṃ ca deśāntarāvasthāyitvenaiva | tathā dvitīyakṣaṇānavasthāyitvaṃ prathamakṣaṇāvasthāyitvenāviruddham | viruddhaṃ punar dvitīyakṣaṇāvasthāyitvenaiva | kevalaṃ deśāntaradvitīyakṣaṇayos tatpracyutimātraṃ vyavahriyate | tad anyonyābhāvapradhvaṃsābhāvayoḥ padārthayoḥ sadbhāve 'py avāryam | abhāvāntarāsvīkāre 'pi bhāvābhāvayor apy amiśratvāsvīkāre tādātmyaprasaṅgāt | tasmād abhāvābhāvayos tādātmyam iti |
yathārthakriyākāritvasya taddeśavartitvanīlatvādibhinnavirodhas tathā dvitīyakṣaṇānavasthāyitvenāpīti vivakṣitam | paramārthatas tu dharmidharmayos tādātmyaṃ vyāvṛttikṛto bhedavyavahāra iti
children.translated_text: Just as causal efficacy has a different contradiction from existence in that location, blue-ness, and the like — so too [it should be understood] with respect to non-existence in a second moment — this is the intended [meaning]. But ultimately, property-bearer and property are identical, and the conventional usage of difference is based on exclusion — as has been

children.text: apohasiddhau
children.translated_text: established in the <s>Apohasiddhi</s>.

children.text: prasādhitam | etac coktakrameṇāviruddham āpāditam | evāvati tu tattve vākchalamātrapravṛttā dveṣaviṣajvalitātmānaḥ kṣudrāḥ pralapantīti kim atra brūmaḥ |
children.translated_text: And this has been demonstrated as non-contradictory in the manner stated. But when the truth is thus, base persons — their minds ablaze with the poison of hatred — engage in mere verbal trickery and prattle. What can we say about this?

children.text: tataś ca vyatiriktanivṛttyutpattim antareṇa svarūpanivṛtter upapatteḥ kathaṃ kṣaṇād ūrdhvaṃ prāktanasattāvasthitiḥ | tasmād utsṛṣṭavibhramaṃ naṣṭavyavahāramātram astu | na tv asyānyat kiñcij jāyeta |
children.translated_text: Therefore, since cessation of own form is tenable without the production of a separate cessation, how can the former state of existence persist beyond the moment? Therefore, let there be merely the convention of 'destroyed,' with confusion abandoned. But let nothing else be produced for it.

children.text: bhāvasya tādavarthyaprasaṅgāt | abhāvaḥ kathaṃ niṣidhyata iti cet |
children.translated_text: [Objection:] Since there would follow the consequence of the entity's remaining in the same state — how is absence (<s>abhāva</s>) denied?

children.text: na, tadanutpattimātraviṣayasya vācāniścayena ca paścād abhāvavyavahāramātrapravartanasyeṣṭatvād vastūtpatter eva niṣiddhatvāt |
children.translated_text: [Reply:] No, because it is accepted that the mere non-production of that [entity] is the referent [of the word 'absence'], and that afterwards, through words and determination, there is merely the operation of the convention of absence — and because what is denied is only the production of a [separate] thing.

children.text: nanu keyaṃ vācoyuktiḥ, abhāvavyavahāramātram iṣyate paścān nābhāva iti | evaṃ sati visaṃvāditāprasaṅgo abhāvavyavahārasya | abhāvaś ca mithyeti bhāva eva pratiṣeddhavyaḥ syāt | sa cābhāvaḥ paścād bhavatīti sphuṭataram asya kādācitkatvam ātmahetukatvam, vastutvaṃ ceti |
children.translated_text: Objection: What kind of verbal reasoning is this — 'merely the convention of absence is accepted afterwards, but not absence itself'? In that case, there would follow the consequence of the convention of absence being deceptive. And since absence is false, only the positive entity would have to be denied. And that absence occurs afterwards — clearly this shows its occasionality, its being caused, and its thinghood.

children.text: asad etat | abhāvākhyavastvantarāsvīkāre 'pi pracyutimātrāpekṣayāpi vyavahārasya caritārthatvapratipādanāt | yat tu tadviviktabhūtalāder viṣayatvam āśaṅkyoktam, na bhūtalāder vastvantaratvāt | na ca vastvantare pratipādite pratīte vā ghaṭādi vastubhūtam iti pratipāditaṃ vā bhavati |
children.translated_text: That is wrong. Because even without accepting a separate thing called absence, it is demonstrated that the convention is fulfilled merely with reference to departure. As for the objection raised by imagining that the bare ground and the like are its object — the bare ground and the like are [themselves] different things. And when a different thing is conveyed or cognized, it does not follow that the pot and the like, being real things, have been conveyed.

children.text: evaṃ vastvantaram eva nāśa iti | asmin mate yad dūṣaṇam uktaṃ tat svayam eva parihṛtaṃ syād iti, tad apy asambaddhaṃ, kevalaṃ hi bhūtalam asya viṣaya iti kathaṃ na ghaṭāder abhūtatvabodhaḥ | yaiva hi ghaṭādyapekṣayā kaivalyāvasthā pradeśasya sa eva ghaṭavirahaḥ | vacanādināpy evaṃ kevalapradeśapratipādane katham iva na prakṛtaghaṭādyabhāvapratipādanam | kaivalyaṃ cāsahāyapraseśād avyatibhinnam eva |
children.translated_text: [Objection:] Thus, destruction is just a different thing. On this view, the objection raised would answer itself. [Reply:] That too is incoherent. For how does the bare ground being the referent [of the cognition] not give rise to the knowledge of the non-existence of the pot and the like? For the very state of aloneness of the location with respect to the pot and the like is itself the absence of the pot. Even when the bare location alone is conveyed through words and the like, how is it not the conveyance of the absence of the pot and the like in question? And aloneness is simply indistinct from the unaccompanied location.

children.text: na ceha ghaṭo nāstīti pratyayasya ghaṭavaty api pradeśe prasaṅgaḥ | svahetos tathotpannasya saghaṭapradeśasya kevalapradeśād anyatvāt |
children.translated_text: Nor does the cognition 'the pot is not here' arise with respect to a location that does have a pot. Because the location-with-pot, having arisen in a certain way from its own cause, is different from the bare location.

children.text: na ca pratyabhijñānataḥ saghaṭāghaṭapradeśayor ekatvaṃ pūrvam asya nirākaraṇāt |
children.translated_text: Nor should the unity of the location-with-pot and the location-without-pot be [established] through recognition (<s>pratyabhijñā</s>), since that has already been refuted.

children.text: na ca vināśahetor asāmarthyavaiyarthyābhidhāne 'ṅkurādihetor api tathābhidhātum ucitam | asiddhe hi kārye hetor āśrayaṇam avāryam | siddhe ceyaṃ cintā, yadi hetor nityo 'nityo vā 'rtho jātaḥ kiṃ nāśakāraṇeneti hetupuraskāreṇaiva pravṛtteḥ | na caivam asiddhe 'ṅkurādau kārye śakyam abhidhātum | svarūpasyaivābhāvāt | taddharmakatvā[tad]dharmakatvādiparyanuyogasya nirviṣayatvāt |
children.translated_text: And the objection regarding the powerlessness and pointlessness of the cause of destruction should equally apply to the cause of a sprout and the like. For when the effect is not yet established, the reliance on a cause is not to be denied. And this inquiry [arises only] when [the effect] is established: whether what has arisen from the cause is permanent or impermanent, what [need] is there of a cause of destruction? — because the process operates with the cause at the forefront. But when the effect — sprout and the like — is not established, one cannot make the same objection — because its own form does not yet exist, and the inquiry into whether it possesses this or that property is without a referent.

children.text: nanu tvayāpi bhāvābhāvayor lakṣaṇabhedo 'bhihitaḥ | tat katham ekatvaṃ sarvārthānām | lakṣaṇabhedād eva bhedavyavasthā | tato 'pi cen na bhedavyavasthitiḥ, na kasyacit kutaścid bhedavyavasthitir ity advaitaprasaṅga iti cet |
children.translated_text: Objection: But you too have stated a difference in defining characteristics between positive entity and absence. Then how can there be unity of all things? The establishment of difference is from the very difference in defining characteristics. And if even from that there is no establishment of difference, then there would be no establishment of difference of anything from anything — resulting in the consequence of non-dualism (<s>advaita</s>).

children.text: na | yo hi naśvarasvabhāvaḥ sa eva nāśo naśyatīti bahulādhikārāt kartari ghañaḥ prasādhanāt taṃ nāśaṃ bhāvasvabhāvam icchāmaḥ | naśanaṃ nāśa iti prasajyātmā dvidhā kartavyaḥ | tattvatas tāvad vastutvavirahāt tattvānyatvavirahita evāsau bhāvo na bhavatīti tadbhāvaniṣedhamātram āyātaṃ tu bhavati | kharaśṛṅgādivat | saṃvṛtau tu yathā kālabhedena vikalpyamānaḥ kādācitka iva pratibhāti tathā sarvopākhyāviraharūpatayā bhāvād bhinna iva pratibhātīti nāvastutvopalakṣaṇabhedākhyānavirodhaḥ | evaṃ ca sati saṃvṛttyā lakṣaṇabhede bhāvābhāvayor bhedasyeṣṭatvāt | tattvena ca lakṣaṇaikatāvirahe bhāvasya tenaikyaniṣedhāt katham advaitaprasaṅgopālambhaḥ |
children.translated_text: [Reply:] No. For that which has a perishable nature — that very [thing] is destruction, [the word 'destruction' being derived from the root] 'naś' (to perish) — by applying the <s>ghañ</s> suffix to the agent [of the action], following the rule of multiple applicability, we maintain that destruction is the nature of the positive entity. [The word] 'destruction' (<s>nāśa</s>) [derived as] 'the act of perishing' must be treated in two ways, as expressing a negative predicate. Ultimately, since it is devoid of thinghood, that positive entity — devoid of both reality and otherness from reality — simply does not exist as that [separate thing]. What results is merely the negation of its existence — like a donkey's horn. But conventionally, just as [the entity], when conceptualized through temporal distinction, appears as if occasional, so too, through having the form of the absence of all designations, it appears as if different from the positive entity — hence there is no contradiction with the statement of difference in defining characteristics as a mark of non-thinghood. And this being so, since difference between positive entity and absence is accepted conventionally through difference in defining characteristics, and since ultimately, in the absence of unity of defining characteristics, the unity of the positive entity with that [absence] is denied — how can there be the reproach of the consequence of non-dualism?

children.text: syād etat | na ca vivekāpratītau tadviviktagrahaṇaṃ bhavati | tadvivekaś ca na bhūtalādisvarūpam eva viśeṣaṇatvād iti |
children.translated_text: It might be [objected]: When the distinction [from the pot] is not cognized, there can be no apprehension of what is distinguished from it. And that distinction is not the mere own form of the bare ground and the like, because it is a qualifier.

children.text: tad etan nyāyabahiṣkṛtam | viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvo hi saṅkalpārūḍhe rūpe bāhyārthasparśe vikalpaśabdaliṅgāntarāṇāṃ vaiyarthyaprasaṅgād iti śāstre vistareṇa pratipādanāt | sa ca saṅkalpo 'bhinnam api bhāvaṃ bhinnam ivākalayati | yathā śilāputrakasya śarīram, śarīre karaṇādayaḥ | lambakarṇo Devadatta ityādi | tasmāt kalpanādhīno viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvaḥ | abhinne 'pi bhāve bhedavivakṣāpekṣo bhedavyavahāraḥ kathaṃ bhedaniyatam ātmānam ātanotu |
children.translated_text: This is excluded from proper reasoning. For the qualifier-qualificand relation pertains to a form that has been taken up by conceptual construction; since it does not touch external reality, the treatise has extensively demonstrated that conceptual cognition, words, inferential marks, and other [means] would be rendered purposeless. And that conceptual construction represents even a non-different entity as though it were different — for example, the body of a stone statue, the sense-organs and the like in a body, '<s>Devadatta</s> with long ears,' and so on. Therefore, the qualifier-qualificand relation is dependent on conceptual construction. Since the convention of difference, which depends on the intention to express difference even in a non-different entity, how can it extend to an entity that is essentially confined to difference?

children.text: skhaladgatir ayaṃ rāhoḥ śira ity ādinirdeśa itic cet |
children.translated_text: [Objection:] But this is a stumbling designation, like 'the head of <s>Rāhu</s>' and the like.

children.text: yadi satyam etat, tadā śiro 'tiriktasya rāhor iva kṣmātalāder atiriktasya vivektasya dṛśyānupalambhabādhitatvād ayam api nirdeśaḥ skhaladgatir eva, tathāpi neti koṣapānaṃ pramāṇam | tasmāt saghaṭāt pradeśāntarāt pradeśa evāyam anyo ghaṭaviviktaḥ svahetor utpanno na tu ghaṭavivekena viśeṣitaḥ | svahetor utpannasya viviktasyābhāve vivekasyābhāvāt |
children.translated_text: If this is true, then just as <s>Rāhu</s> as distinct from the head [does not exist], so too, since separation as distinct from the ground and the like is refuted by the non-apprehension of the visible (<s>dṛśyānupalambha</s>), this designation too is simply a stumbling one — yet [the objector says] 'not so,' but that is [mere] drinking from a treasury [i.e., unfounded assertion]. Therefore, this locus is simply different from the other locus that has a pot — it is separated from the pot, having arisen from its own cause — but it is not qualified by separation from the pot. Because in the absence of the separated [entity] that has arisen from its own cause, there is no separation.

children.text: kiṃ ca
children.translated_text: Moreover,

For just as a thing produced from its own cause is excluded from other locations and excluded from non-blue and the like, so too it is excluded from a second moment. And just as non-existence in another location is not contradictory with existence in that [particular] location, but is contradictory only with existence in another location — so too non-existence in a second moment is not contradictory with existence in the first moment, but is contradictory only with existence in the second moment. It is merely in the case of other locations and second moments that the departure from them alone is conventionally expressed. That [departure] is not precluded even when the two entities — mutual absence (<s>anyonyābhāva</s>) and subsequent absence (<s>pradhvaṃsābhāva</s>) — exist. Even without accepting another [type of] absence, if the unmixed nature of positive entity and absence is not accepted, there would follow the consequence of identity [of everything]. Therefore, positive entity and absence are identical.

children.text:
vyāptaṃ bhidā yadi viśeṣyaviśeṣaṇatvaṃ bhedātyayān nanu tadā tadabhāva eva |
	deśo viśiṣṭa iti nāsti yathā tathedam apy asti dṛśyamatabhedadṛg asti neti ||
tasmān nābhāvo nāma kaścid yatra kāraṇavyāpāraḥ | tad evaṃ sahetukavināśatvād iti hetuḥ svarūpāsiddha iti sthitam ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, there is no such thing as 'absence' in which causal activity operates. Thus it is established that the reason 'because destruction has a cause' (<s>sahetukavināśatvāt</s>) is essentially unestablished (<s>svarūpāsiddha</s>).

children.text: satām akṣaṇikatvaṃ kāraṇavattvād ity apy asambaddham eva | kṣaṇikatvakāraṇavattvayor virodhābhāvād akṣaṇikatvena kāraṇavattvasya vyāpter asiddheḥ | sandigdhavyatirekatvāt | na cāsya viparyaye vṛttiśaṅkā nāśasya sahetukatvam eva nivartayati | uktakrameṇa nāśasyaivābhāvād iti ||
children.translated_text: The [argument] 'existing things are non-momentary because they possess causes' is also entirely incoherent. Because there is no contradiction between momentariness and possessing causes, the pervasion of possessing causes by non-momentariness is unestablished — it has doubtful negative concomitance. Nor does the suspicion of [the reason's] occurrence in the contrary case eliminate merely the fact that destruction has a cause — because, in the manner stated, destruction itself does not exist.

children.text: tathā prameyatvād api sthirasiddhir manorathamātram | sākāravedanodayapakṣasthitau hi dvitīyakṣaṇānuvṛttāv apy arthasya vyavahitatvāt, prakāśānupapatter viṣayasvarūpavedanam eva jñānasya viṣayavedanam | evaṃ ca vartamānānurodhaḥ, atīte 'pi tatpratyāsatter apracyuteḥ | na cātiprasaṅgaḥ | anantarātītād anyena kṣaṇena sārūpyāsamarpaṇāt | tataś ca kāraṇatvād yadi nāma prameyatvasya pūrvakālasattvena vyāptis tathāpi prameyatvavat pūrvakālasattvam api kṣaṇike 'viruddham iti prameyatvākṣaṇikatvayor vyāptisādhano vyāpakānupalambho 'siddhaḥ | jñānākārārpakatvaṃ hi hetutvam, prameyatvaṃ prāmāṇikapratītam | tac cānantarātīta eva kṣaṇe samupapadyate |
children.translated_text: Likewise, the establishment of permanence from knowability (<s>prameyatva</s>) is also mere wishful thinking. For, in the position where the arising of cognition-with-form (<s>sākāravedanodaya</s>) is maintained, even though the object persists to the second moment, since it is separated [from the cognition], and because illumination would be inexplicable [otherwise], the cognition's apprehension of the object is simply the awareness of the object's own form. And thus there is conformity with the present; even with respect to what is past, since the proximate relation (<s>pratyāsatti</s>) to that has not lapsed. And there is no over-extension, because a moment other than the immediately preceding one does not bestow similarity of form. Therefore, even if there is pervasion of knowability by existence in a prior time due to causality, still, just as knowability [is compatible with the momentary], so too existence in a prior time is not incompatible with the momentary — hence the non-apprehension of the pervader that would establish the pervasion of knowability and non-momentariness is unestablished. For the causality [here] is the bestowal of a cognitive image, and knowability is what is cognized through a valid cognition. And that is possible even in the immediately preceding moment alone.

children.text: jñānasattāsamaye 'rthānuvṛtter abhāvān nirviṣayateti cet |
children.translated_text: [Objection:] Since the object does not persist at the time of the cognition's existence, [the cognition] would be without an object.

children.text: nanv ananuvṛttāv api tadarpitākārasvarūpasaṃvedanam eva tadvedanam | tad eva ca saviṣayatvam | iyaṃ ca pratyāsattir anantarātīte 'pi kṣaṇe 'kṣīneti na dvitīyakṣaṇānuvṛtter anurodha ity uktam | ataḥ sandigdhavyatirekitvād anaikāntikam eva prameyatvam |
children.translated_text: But even without persistence, the awareness of the intrinsic form of the image bestowed by that [object] is itself the awareness of that [object]. And that itself constitutes having an object. And this proximate relation is not diminished even in the immediately preceding moment — hence there is no need for the object's persistence to the second moment, as stated. Therefore, knowability is inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>) due to having doubtful negative concomitance.

children.text: atha sākāravādavidveṣād anākārajñānagrāhyatvaṃ prameyatvam abhipretaṃ tadā 'siddhatā 'sya hetoḥ |
children.translated_text: But if, out of hostility to the theory of cognition-with-form (<s>sākāravāda</s>), what is intended by 'knowability' is 'being graspable by formless cognition' — then this reason is unestablished.

children.text: indriyārthasannikarṣāder jñānam utpadyatāṃ nāma |
children.translated_text: Let cognition arise from the contact of sense-organ and object, and the like.

children.text: tac cānubhavaikarasatvena sarvatrārthe sadṛśākāratvāt kasya grāhakam astu,
children.translated_text: But since that [cognition], being of a uniform experiential nature, has a similar form with respect to every object, of what would it be the apprehender —

children.text: yenābhisambaddham iti cet |
children.translated_text: [Objection:] Of that with which it is connected.

children.text: ātamamanaḥsaṃyogādīnām api grahaṇaṃ syāt |
children.translated_text: [Reply:] Then there would also be apprehension of the self-mind conjunction and the like.

children.text: janakasya grahaṇam iti cet |
children.translated_text: [Objection:] It is the apprehension of the cause [that is intended].

children.text: tathāpy ātmādīnāṃ grahaṇaprasaṅgaḥ | viṣayatvena janakasya grahaṇam ity apy asādhu | viṣayatvasyādyāpy aniścayāt |
children.translated_text: [Reply:] Even so, there would be the absurd consequence of apprehending the self and the like [as objects]. And to say 'it is the apprehension of the cause qua object' is also improper, since objecthood has not yet been determined.

children.text: idaṃ dṛṣṭam śrutaṃ vedam ity adhyavasāyo yatrārthe sa viṣaya iti cet |
children.translated_text: [Objection:] The object is that with respect to which there is the determination 'this was seen,' 'this was heard.'

children.text: nanv asty eva pratiniyato vyavahāraḥ | kaḥ punar atra pratyāsattiniyama iti pṛcchāmaḥ | sa ced upavarṇayituṃ na śakyate, vyavahāro 'pi tvanmate niyato na syād iti brūmaḥ |
children.translated_text: [Reply:] There is indeed a fixed convention. But we ask: what is the determining factor of the proximate relation here? If it cannot be described, then we say: in your view, the convention too would not be fixed.

children.text: asti tāvad iti cet |
children.translated_text: [Objection:] It does exist, at any rate.

children.text: ata evārthasārūpyam asādhāraṇaṃ pratyāsattinimittam astu | nirnimitte niyamāyogāt |
children.translated_text: [Reply:] For precisely this reason, let the resemblance to the object (<s>arthasārūpya</s>) be the unique ground of the proximate relation. Because there can be no invariable restriction without a ground.

children.text: nanu sārūpyam apy arthādarśane katham avadhāryate | tac ca kim ekadeśena, sarvātmanā vā | ādye pakṣe sarvaṃ sarvasya vedanaṃ syāt | dvitīye tu jñānam ajñānatāṃ vrajet | kiṃ ca sārūpyād arthavedane 'nantaraṃ jñānaṃ tulyaviṣayaṃ viśayaḥ syād iti cet |
children.translated_text: [Objection:] But how can resemblance be ascertained without seeing the object? And is that [resemblance] partial or total? In the first alternative, everything would be the cognition of everything. In the second, cognition would become non-cognition. Moreover, if due to resemblance there is awareness of the object, the immediately subsequent cognition having the same object would [itself] become an object.

children.text: mā bhūd arthasya darśanam | ākāraviśeṣabalād adhyavasitārthasyārthakriyāprāpter evārtho 'pīdṛśa iti sārūpyavyavahāro 'viruddhaḥ | ata eva sthūlagataṃ paramāṇugataṃ vā sārūpyaṃ na cintyate | jñānākārasya sthūlatve 'py ekasāmagrīpratibaddhapuñjaviśeṣād apy abhīṣṭakriyākaraṇāt puruṣārthasiddheḥ |
children.translated_text: [Reply:] Let there be no seeing of the object [as such]. Due to the force of a specific cognitive image, the attainment of causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyā</s>) with respect to the determined object [suffices] — hence the convention of resemblance as 'the object too is like this' is uncontradicted. For this very reason, resemblance in gross [objects] or in atoms is not considered — because even though the cognitive image is gross, since the desired action is accomplished through a specific cluster bound to a single causal aggregate, the human purpose is fulfilled.

children.text: sārūpyaṃ caikadeśenaiva | na cātra sarvavedanaprasaṅgaḥ | sarveṣāṃ jñānaṃ praty ajanakatvāt | janakānāṃ ca svavyapadeśanimittāsādhāraṇaikadeśārpakatvena grāhyatvāt |
children.translated_text: And the resemblance is only partial. Nor is there the absurd consequence of cognizing everything, because not all [objects] are causes of cognition. And among the causes, since each bestows a unique partial [form] that is the ground of its own designation, it is graspable.

children.text: nāpi tulyaviṣayānantarajñānagrahaṇaprasaṅgaḥ, tasya svasaṃvedanād eva pramāṇāt siddhatvāt | pramāṇāntarasya tatra vaiyarthyāt | jaḍatve saty ākārārpakasya vastuno grāhyatvād ity asyārthasyābhīṣṭatvāc ca | bāhyārthasthitau ceyaṃ cinteti sarvam anavadyam |
children.translated_text: Nor is there the absurd consequence of apprehending the immediately subsequent cognition having the same object, because that is established through the <s>pramāṇa</s> of self-awareness (<s>svasaṃvedana</s>) alone — another <s>pramāṇa</s> being superfluous for that. And because the intended meaning is: when [cognition] is insentient, the real entity that bestows the image is what is graspable. And this analysis applies when external objects are maintained — hence everything is faultless.

children.text: tad evam ayaṃ prameyatvād iti hetuḥ sākāravādapakṣe sandigdhavyatirekaḥ | nirākārapakṣe cāsiddha iti sthitam ||
children.translated_text: Thus, this reason 'because of knowability' has doubtful negative concomitance in the <s>sākāravāda</s> (cognition-with-form) position, and is unestablished in the <s>nirākāra</s> (formless cognition) position. This is established.

children.text: na cārthāpattir api sthirātmasādhanī | kāryakāraṇabhāvagrahaṇādīnām anyathopapatteḥ |
children.translated_text: Nor does <s>arthāpatti</s> (postulation) prove a permanent self either, because the apprehension of causal relation and the like can be explained otherwise.

children.text: tathā hi upādānopādheyabhāvasthitacittasantatim apy āśrityeyaṃ vyavasthā sustheti katham ātmānaṃ pratyujjīvayatu | tatra kāryakāraṇabhāvapratītis tāvad anākulā | tathāpi prāgbhāvivastuniścayajñānasyopādeyabhūtena tadarpitasaṃskāragarbheṇa paścādbhāvivastujñānenāsmin satīdaṃ bhavatīti niścayo janyate | tathā prāgbhāvivastvapekṣayā kevalabhūtalaniścayakajñānopādeyabhūtena tadarpitasaṃskāragarbheṇa paścādbhāvivastvapekṣayā kevalabhūtalaniścāyakajñānenāsmin asatīdaṃ na bhavatīti vyatirekaniścayo janyate | yathoktam |
children.translated_text: For thus: this arrangement is well-established even on the basis of a mental continuum (<s>cittasantati</s>) that rests in the relation of material cause and product (<s>upādānopādheya</s>) — so how can it revive the self? In this regard, first, the cognition of the causal relation is unproblematic. Even so: a cognition of a subsequently existing object, which is the product of and contains the latent impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>) deposited by the prior cognition that ascertains a previously existing object, generates the certainty 'when this exists, that exists.' Likewise, a cognition that ascertains the bare ground alone with respect to a subsequently existing object, which is the product of and contains the latent impressions deposited by a cognition that ascertains the bare ground alone with respect to a previously existing object, generates the negative concomitance certainty 'when this does not exist, that does not exist.' As stated:

If the qualifier-qualificand relation is pervaded by difference, then upon the disappearance of difference, there would simply be the absence of that [relation]. Just as 'the locus is qualified' does not [hold in the absence of difference], so too this [claim] — 'one who perceives the difference apprehended [says] it exists or does not exist' — [is refuted].

children.text: ekāvasāyasamantarajātam anyavijñānam anvayavimarśam upādadhāti |
children.translated_text: A cognition of another [object], born immediately after a single determination, provides the reflection of positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>).

children.text: evaṃ tadekavirahānubhavodbhavānyavyāvṛttidhīḥ prathayati vyatirekabuddhim ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, a cognition of exclusion from another [object], born from the experience of the absence of that single [object], manifests the cognition of negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>).

children.text: ata eva devadattenāgnau pratīte yajñadattena ca dhūme pratīte na kāryakāraṇabhāvagrahaṇaṃ tajjñānayor upādānopādeyabhāvābhāvāt | yatra tv ekasantāne jñānakṣaṇayor upādānopādeyabhāvas tatra kāryādigrahaḥ sugrahaḥ | anyathā saty api nityātmani pratisandhātari kāryakāraṇabhāvādīnām apratītir eva syāt |
tathā hi ātmanaḥ sakāśāt pratisandheyabuddhīnām abhedo bhedo vā bhedābhedo vā |
children.translated_text: For thus: the relation of the self to the cognitions that are to be synthesized is either non-difference, or difference, or difference-and-non-difference.

children.text: prathamapakṣe ātmaiva syāt pratisandhātā | buddhaya eva vā syuḥ pratisandheyā iti kaḥ pratisandhārthaḥ |
children.translated_text: In the first alternative, the self itself would be the synthesizer, or the cognitions themselves would be what is synthesized — so what purpose would synthesis serve?

children.text: bhedapakṣe 'pi buddhibhyo bhidyamānasya jaḍasyātmanaḥ kaḥ pratisandhānārtha iti na vidmaḥ |
children.translated_text: In the alternative of difference too, we do not know what purpose synthesis would serve for a self that is insentient and different from cognitions.

children.text: buddhiyogād draṣṭṛtvavat pratisandhātṛtvam iti cet |
children.translated_text: [Objection:] Through conjunction with cognition, it has the capacity to synthesize, just as it has the capacity to see.

children.text: buddhir eva tarhi draṣṭrī pratisandhātrī ceti niyamasvīkāre tadyogād asya tathātvam iti kim anena yācitakamaṇḍanena |
children.translated_text: [Reply:] Then, if we accept the rule that cognition itself is the seer and the synthesizer, what need is there for this borrowed ornament [i.e., the self], saying 'through conjunction with that, it becomes such'?

children.text: buddhīnāṃ kartṛtvābhāvād iti cet |
children.translated_text: [Objection:] Because cognitions lack agency.

children.text: taddvāreṇāpi tarhi tasyātmano draṣṭṛtvādivyavahārānupapattiḥ | yadi hi buddhir hetoḥ phalasya vā draṣṭṛī syāt tadānantaryapratiniyamasya cānusandhātrī kalpitā | tadyogād draṣṭṛtvaṃ pratisandhātṛtvaṃ cocyata iti syād api prativiṣayam alabdhaviśeṣāyāṃ ca buddhau sambandho 'pi na viśeṣaṃ vyavahārayitum īśaḥ | adhunā nibandhanādhigantā | adhunā phalasya | idānīṃ pratisandhāteti | tathāpi ca buddhiyutaviśeṣasvīkāre tu kim apareṇātmanā kartavyam | tāvataiva paryāptatvād vyavahārasya |
children.translated_text: [Reply:] Then, even through that [cognition as intermediary], the convention of the self being a seer and the like would be untenable. For if cognition were the seer — whether of the cause or of the effect — then it would be posited as the synthesizer through the restriction of immediate succession. And it would be said that through conjunction with that, [the self] has the nature of seer and synthesizer — but this would be possible only if, when cognition has not obtained any distinction with respect to each object, the relation too is incapable of producing a distinction in the convention: 'now it ascertains the ground,' 'now [it ascertains] the effect,' 'now it synthesizes.' And if so, upon accepting a distinction in [cognition] conjoined with cognition, what need is there for a separate self? — since the convention is complete with just that much.

children.text: sthirātmānam antareṇa saiva buddhir na syād iti cet |
children.translated_text: [Objection:] Without a permanent self, that very cognition would not exist.

children.text: kenaivaṃ pratārito 'si | aho mohamāhātmyaṃ yad īdṛśān api paravaśīkaroti | tathā hi nedam idam antareṇa yad ucyate tat khalv anyatra pratyakṣānupalambhābhyāṃ sāmarthyāvadhāraṇe sati yujyate vahner iva dhūme | cakṣurādivad vā dṛṣṭakāraṇāntarasāmagyā kāryādarśane paścād darśane ca kiñcid anyad apekṣaṇīyam astīti sāmānyākāreṇa |
children.translated_text: [Reply:] Who has deceived you thus? Ah, the greatness of delusion, that it subjugates even such [minds]! For thus: the statement 'this does not [exist] without that' is properly applicable only when the capacity [of the cause] has been ascertained elsewhere through perception and non-apprehension — as in the case of fire with respect to smoke. Or, as with the eye and the like, when a seen effect is not observed despite the presence of the rest of the known causal aggregate, and is then observed [when a further factor is added], it is [known] in a general way that something else must be required.

children.text: ādyaḥ pakṣas tāvan nāstīti vyaktam | dvitīyo 'pi na sambhavī | na hi kāraṇabuddhisamanantaraṃ kāryabuddhau satyāṃ niścayapravṛttasyedam asyānantaraṃ dṛṣṭam mayeti pratisandhānam adṛṣṭapūrvaṃ kadācit | yato 'nyasya sāmarthyaparikalpanaṃ syād ity udasya vyāmoham uktakrameṇaiva kārykāraṇagrahaṇavyavasthā svīkartavyā |
children.translated_text: The first alternative clearly does not exist. The second too is impossible. For when a causal cognition is immediately followed by an effect-cognition, one who proceeds with certainty has never previously observed the synthesis 'this was seen by me immediately after that.' Therefore, there would be no ground for postulating the capacity of something else. Hence, rejecting this delusion, the arrangement of the apprehension of causal relations should be accepted precisely in the manner stated [above].

children.text: bhedābhedapakṣas tu dhakkāra eva | tasyaiva tadapekṣayā bhedābhedaviruddhadharmādhyāsād ekatvānupapatteḥ | tataś ca yad bhinnaṃ bhinnam evābhinnṃ cābhinnam iti naikasya bhedābhedau | tathapy abheda viśvam ekam iti yugapadutpādasthitipralayaprasaṅgaḥ |
children.translated_text: The alternative of difference-and-non-difference is simply nonsensical — because, due to the superimposition of the contradictory properties of difference and non-difference upon that very [self] with respect to that [cognition], unity is untenable. And therefore, what is different is simply different, and what is non-different is simply non-different — so both difference and non-difference do not belong to one [entity]. And if [one insists on] non-difference, the universe would be one, and the absurd consequence would follow of simultaneous origination, persistence, and destruction.

children.text: evaṃ kramivastugrāhakaiḥ kramijñānair upādānopādeyabhūtaiḥ sākṣāt pāramparyeṇa krameṇāmī jāyanta iti niścayo janyate | ekakālikānekavastugrāhakair eva tajjñānair ekopādānatvāt sakṛd imāni jātānīti vikalpaḥ kriyata iti kramākramagrahaṇam apy anavadyam |
children.translated_text: Thus, through successive cognitions that apprehend successive objects and that stand in the relation of material cause and product, the certainty 'these arise in succession, directly and indirectly' is generated. And through those very cognitions that apprehend multiple objects existing at one time, since they have a single material cause, the conceptual construction 'these arose simultaneously' is produced. Thus the apprehension of both succession and simultaneity is faultless.

children.text: katham anekajñānād ekavikalpa iti cet |
children.translated_text: [Objection:] How can a single conceptual cognition arise from multiple cognitions?

children.text: ko doṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: [Reply:] What is the fault?

For this very reason, when fire is cognized by <s>Devadatta</s> and smoke by <s>Yajñadatta</s>, there is no apprehension of the causal relation, because the relation of material cause and product does not exist between those two cognitions. But where, in a single mental continuum, the relation of material cause and product exists between two cognitive moments, there the apprehension of cause and the like is easily grasped. Otherwise, even if a permanent self existed as the synthesizer, there would be no cognition at all of causal relations and the like.

children.text: bhavantu bhinnā matayas tathāpi tā dadhaty upādānatayaikakalpanam |
children.translated_text: Let the cognitions be different; nonetheless, as material causes, they sustain a single conceptual construction.

children.text: na bhinnasaṃkhyā phalahetubādhanī na cānyasantānabhavā ivākṣamāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The plurality of number does not obstruct the cause-effect [relation], nor are they incapable like [cognitions] belonging to another continuum.

children.text: yad apy uktaṃ
Śaṅkareṇa
children.translated_text: by <s>Śaṅkara</s>:

children.text:
: atha pūrvottarakṣaṇayoḥ saṃvittī |
	tābhyāṃ vāsanā, tayā hetuphalabhāvādhyavasāyī vikalpa iti cet |
children.translated_text: [Objection:] 'But there are the two awarenesses of the prior and subsequent moments; from those two, a latent impression (<s>vāsanā</s>); from that, a conceptual cognition that determines the cause-effect relation' —

children.text:
tat kim idānīṃ yat kiñcid
	āśaṅkitena | vaktavyam ity evaṃ vidhir anuṣṭhīyate bhavatā | vikalpo
	hy agṛhītānusandhānam atadrūpasamāropo vā syāt |
children.translated_text: what is the point now of raising just any objection? You observe the injunction 'something must be said' [as a formality]. For a conceptual cognition would be either a synthesis of what has not been apprehended, or a superimposition of a form that does not belong to it.

children.text:
na tāvat pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ |
	adṛṣṭānvayavyatirekasya puruṣasya hetuphalabhāvāgrahe
	'nusandhānapratyayahetor vāsanāviśeṣasyaivānupapatteḥ | agṛhītasya
	cānusandhāne 'tiprasaṅgād iti |
children.translated_text: The first alternative is certainly not [viable]. Because for a person (<s>puruṣa</s>) whose positive and negative concomitance is unobserved, when the cause-effect relation is not grasped, the latent impression (<s>vāsanāviśeṣa</s>) — which is the cause of the recollective cognition — is itself inexplicable. And because if what is ungrasped could be recollected, there would be the absurd consequence [of recollecting anything whatsoever].

children.text:
tad
	etan na samyag ālocitam | yato hetuphalabhūtayoḥ pūrvottarakṣaṇayor
	ekaikena jñānenānanubhave 'py upādānopādheyabhūtābhyāṃ kramijñānābhyāṃ
	hetuphalatve gṛhīte eva | kevalaṃ hetukāle phalābhāvāt
	tadviṣayasāmarthyagrahaṇe 'pi phalādarśanāt tadavasāya evāpravṛttaḥ
	kāryadarśanena pravartyate | tathā phalāvalokane 'pi tatkāryatā
	gṛhītaiva vikalpenānusandhīyata iti gṛhītānusandhānarūpa evāyaṃ vikalpa
	iti yat kiñcid etat |
children.translated_text: This has not been properly considered. Because even though a single cognition does not experience both the earlier and later moments that are cause and effect, the cause-effect relation is indeed grasped through the two successive cognitions that are related as material cause (<s>upādāna</s>) and effect (<s>upādeya</s>). It is merely that because the effect is absent at the time of the cause, even when the capacity regarding its object is grasped, since the effect is not seen, the determination regarding it has not [yet] occurred — [but] it is set in motion by the observation of the effect. Similarly, even upon observing the effect, its being an effect is indeed grasped — it is recollected through a conceptual construction (<s>vikalpa</s>). Thus this conceptual construction is of the nature of recollecting what has been grasped — so this [objection] amounts to nothing.

children.text:
yad āha
	Mahābhāṣyālaṅkāraḥ |
children.translated_text: As the author of the <s>Mahābhāṣyālaṅkāra</s> has said:
And as for what was stated

children.text: yadi nāmaikam adhyakṣam na pūrvāparavittimat |
children.translated_text: Even if a single perception does not cognize the earlier and the later,

children.text: adhyakṣadvayasadbhāve prākparāvedanaṃ katham || iti |
children.translated_text: when two perceptions exist, how is the cognition of the earlier and the later [possible]?

children.text: tathā smaraṇam abhilāṣaḥ, svayaṃnihitapratyanumārgaṇaṃ, dṛṣṭārthakutūhalaviramaṇaṃ, karmaphalasambandhaḥ, saṃśayapūrvakanirṇayaś ca pūrvapūrvārthānubhavair upādānakāraṇaiḥ samarpitasaṃskāragarbhair uttarottarārthānubhavair evopādeyabhūtair janyamāno yujyata iti kim adhikenātmānā parikalpitena |
upādānopādeyabhāvaniyamād eva ca na santānāntare smaraṇādiprasaṅgaḥ saṅgataḥ | kim idam upādānam iti cet |
children.translated_text: And precisely because of the invariable rule of the material-cause-and-effect relation, the absurd consequence of memory and the like arising in another mental continuum (<s>santāna</s>) does not hold. [Objection:] What is this 'material cause'?

children.text: ucyate | yatsantānanivṛttyā yad utpadyate tat tasyopādānakāraṇam | yathā mṛtsantānanivṛttyotpadyamānasya kumbhasya mṛd upādānam iti śāstre prapañcitam | na cātra paralokakṣatiḥ |
children.translated_text: [Reply:] It is said: That by the cessation of whose continuum something arises — that is the material cause (<s>upādānakāraṇa</s>) of it. Just as clay is the material cause of a pot that arises by the cessation of the clay-continuum — this has been elaborated in the treatise. And there is no damage to the next world here.
