children.text: pravṛttyākṣepabuddhyātmabhāve vācyavyavasthitiḥ ||
children.translated_text: through a cognition that triggers engagement, in the presence of the nature of [that] cognition, the convention of the denotable is established.

children.text: iti |
children.translated_text: Thus.
As for the statement that the external is not an object of conceptual cognition, and that its apprehension is conjoined with words, and therefore conceptual cognition too is hard to maintain —

children.text:
tasmād vastu vā ghaṭapaṭādi
      sandigdhavastu vā sādhakabādhakātikrāntam, avastu
      vātmadikkālākṣaṇikādikam adhyavasitam iti, apratibhāse 'pi
      pravṛttiviṣayīkṛtam ity arthaḥ | ayam eva
      cāropaikīkaraṇādhyava

sāyābhedagrahādīnām arthaḥ sarvatra śāstre
      boddhavyaḥ | tasmād adhyavasāyasyākāraviśeṣayogād agṛhīte 'pi
      pravartanayogyatā nāma yo dharmas tayā bāhyādhyavasāyayor
      grāhyagrāhakabhāvaś cet savṛttyā duṣpariharaḥ, tadā viṣayiviṣayabhāvo
      'pi labdha ity adhyavasāyamātreṇa viṣayaviṣayitvam uktam iti yuktam |
      yad āha
children.translated_text: of superimposition, unification, determination, apprehension of non-difference, and the like should be understood everywhere in the treatise. Therefore, if the property called 'fitness to prompt engagement even toward what is not grasped,' which belongs to determination by virtue of a specific form, [establishes that] the relation of grasped and grasper between the external [object] and determination is conventionally difficult to avoid, then the object-possessor relation too is obtained — and it is fitting to say that objecthood and possessor-of-object-hood are [established] through determination alone. As

children.text: Alaṅkārakāraḥ
children.translated_text: the author of the <s>Alaṅkāra</s> [<s>Prajñākaragupta</s>] states:

Therefore, what is determined is either a real entity such as a pot or cloth, or a thing of doubtful [reality] that is beyond the reach of establishing and refuting [evidence], or a non-entity such as the self, space, time, the non-momentary, and the like — and even though it does not appear, it is made the object of engagement — this is the meaning. And this very meaning

children.text: kathaṃ tadviṣa
yatvaṃ tatra pravartanād iti |
children.translated_text: Because [engagement] proceeds toward that.
How is that its object?

etena yad uktam, katham
      avasīyamānas
tayā so 'rtho
children.translated_text: that object

children.text:
na prakāśyata ityādi, tan nirastam, tadaprakāśe 'pi
      tadadhyavasāyasya vyavasthāpitatvāt | asati cārthe sā na syād ity apy
      ayuktam, ātmāder adhyavaseyasya pratibhāsapratikṣepe buddhyā saha
      tādātmyābhāvāt | na ca sarvākāraniścayaprasaṅgadoṣaḥ saṅgataḥ |
      sarvākāraniścayo
children.translated_text: not be illuminated?' and so on, is refuted — because even without the illumination of that [object], the determination of it has been established. And the [claim] that 'in the absence of the object, that [determination] would not exist' is also unjustified, because when the determinable — such as the self and the like — is denied appearance, there is no identity with the cognition. Nor is the fault of the absurd consequence of determining all forms coherent. For 'determining all forms'

children.text:
hi sarveṣv ākāreṣu pravṛttikārakatvātmā niruktaḥ, na
      caikākārollekhino vikalpasyākārāntare pravartanaśaktir anubhavaviṣaya
      iti kutaḥ śabdapramāṇāntarānapekṣeti yuktam |
children.translated_text: is defined as having the nature of causing engagement toward all forms, and the capacity of a conceptual cognition that delineates a single form to prompt engagement toward another form is not within the scope of experience — hence it is fitting [to say] that it does not require words or other <s>pramāṇas</s>.

tatra nirvikalpakaṃ
      spaṣṭapratibhāsatvād grāhakaṃ vyavasthāpyate |
children.translated_text: In this regard, non-conceptual [perception] is established as the apprehender, because of the clarity of its appearance.

vikalpas tv
      aspaṣṭai
children.translated_text: Conceptual cognition, however,

kavyāvṛttyullekhād āropakādivyavahārabhājanam | yathā ca bāhye
      sati kvacid bhramavyavasthā
children.translated_text: because it delineates only an indistinct single exclusion, is the bearer of the convention of superimposition and the like. And just as, when external [objects] exist, the convention of error is [established] in some cases,

children.text:
tathāntarnaye 'pi sarvatra | kevalaṃ
      bahirmukhapravṛtyapekṣayā kriyamāṇo nātmani kaścid bhrama ity uktaṃ
      bhavati | na ca gosvalakṣaṇaprakāśāvakāśaḥ, svākārasyaiva sphuraṇāt,
      svalakṣaṇe ca saṃketāyogāt | vikalpikaiva na syād iti tu
      svarūpāpekṣayā siddhasādhanam | bāhyāpekṣayā tv adhyavasāyavad
      vikalpikaiva sā buddhis tathā | tasmād aśeṣagovyaktisā
children.translated_text: so too in the internalist position (<s>antarnaya</s>), [it is established] everywhere. The only [difference is that] with respect to the self, when considered in relation to outward-directed engagement, no error is said to apply — this is what is stated. And there is no scope for the manifestation of the particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) of a cow [in conceptual cognition], because only one's own form flashes forth, and because convention cannot apply to the particular. And [the objection that] 'it would not be a conceptual cognition at all' is, with respect to its own nature, a proof of what is already established (<s>siddhasādhana</s>). But with respect to the external, like determination, that cognition is indeed a conceptual cognition. Therefore, through establishing all cow-instances

children.text:
dhāraṇena
      gotvena gobuddhir alīkena sābhilāpena viplavāt prakhyātīti tathā
      prakhyānam asyā gavāvasāya ity eṣṭavyam ity api neṣṭavyam eva, caraṇam
      ardanādinā pratyavasthāne 'pi yuktiśāstravahirbhūtatvād etadabhāve 'pi
      kathitadoṣapradhvaṃsāt | na hi vikalpabuddhāv alīkākārasphuraṇam eva
      bāhyasyādhyavasāya iti kācid arthasaṅgatiḥ, arthasyeti
      sambandhānupapatteḥ
children.translated_text: by the unreal cowhood, that cow-cognition — accompanied by verbal expression and arising from error — becomes renowned [as conceptual cognition]. And that its renown is 'this is the determination of a cow' should be accepted. But even [the claim that] this need not be accepted [is fine], because even when countered by means of reasoning and scripture, since this is outside the purview of reasoning and scripture, and since the stated defects are destroyed even without this [acceptance]. For there is no coherent connection in [the claim that] the flashing of an unreal form in conceptual cognition is itself the determination of the external — because the genitive 'of the object' lacks a [viable] relation,

children.text: bodhe ca
children.translated_text: and when there is awareness,

children.text: bhramābhāvāt
children.translated_text: because of the absence of error,

children.text:
pratyakṣataiva, katham
      adhyavasāyaḥ | apratibhāsamānasyāpi svalakṣaṇasya bhrāntyāvasāyād iti
      tu na budhyāmahe | avasāyena hi tadvittisparśe pratibhāsaḥ ko 'paraḥ |
      tadvittāv apy aspaṣṭatvād adhyavasāya ity apy ayuktam, tadrūpavittāv
      aspaṣṭatvasyaivābhāvāt |
children.translated_text: it is direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) itself — how then is it determination? And as for [the claim that] 'even though the particular does not appear, it is determined through error' — we do not understand this. For when there is contact with the awareness of that through determination, what other appearance is there? And [the claim that] 'even when there is awareness of its form, it is determination because of indistinctness' is also unjustified, because when there is awareness of its [actual] form, indistinctness itself is absent.
By this, the statement 'how can, through being determined,

children.text: jāto nāmāśrayo 'nyonyaś cetasāṃ tasya vastunaḥ |
children.translated_text: [Verse:] The mutual basis of cognitions for that object has arisen;

children.text: ekasyaiva kuto rūpaṃ bhinnākārāvabhāsi yat ||
children.translated_text: how can there be, for a single [entity], a form that appears with different aspects?

children.text: ity ācāryaḥ smaryatām | na ca tadā

sau bhrāntir bhavitum arhati,
      vastusvarūpasyaiva nirbhāsāt ||
children.translated_text: there should be no error, because what shines forth is the very nature of the real entity.

children.text:
alīkavṛtter iti cet | saivāstu |
      bāhyasyāsphurato 'dhyavasāyaḥ katham | saiva sa iti cet | alīkam idam
      iti viduṣo bāhyādhyavasāyavyasthābhāvāt, bāhyāsphuraṇāt
      tadapratibaddhatvāc ca | pratibandhe 'pi tasyeti syāt, na punas
      tadadhyavasāyaḥ, tadasphuraṇasphuraṇayor api tadayogād ity
children.translated_text: [Objection:] Because the operation is upon something unreal. [Reply:] Let it be so. But how can there be determination of the external when [the external] does not flash forth? [Objection:] That itself is that [determination]. [Reply:] For one who knows 'this is unreal,' the convention of determining the external does not hold — because the external does not flash forth, and because [the determination] is not bound to it. Even if there were a connection to it, it would be of that [unreal form], not a determination of that [external object] — because neither the non-flashing nor the flashing of that [unreal form] is suited to that [external object].

children.text: alam atinirba
children.translated_text: Enough with this excessive

children.text: ndhena
children.translated_text: elaboration.

children.text:
| tad evam
      apratibhāsino 'pi vipakṣād adhyavasāyamātrasiddhād eva vyāvṛtto
      doṣatrayanirmuktaḥ prakāśamānatātmako hetur
children.translated_text: Thus, this reason — whose nature is being manifest (<s>prakāśamānatā</s>) — which is excluded from the dissimilar domain through mere determination (even though [the object] does not appear), which is free from the three defects, and which is established —

children.text: yāvatprakāśāvadhijñā
children.translated_text: establishes the unity of the variegated array of forms whose nature is cognition, extending as far as the limit of manifestation,

children.text:
nātmakacitrākāracakrasyaikatvaṃ sādhayaty eva || yad
      āhur guravaḥ
children.translated_text: which has the nature of cognition. As the teachers say:
Let the <s>Ācārya</s> [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] be recalled here. And at that time,

children.text: bhāsate yat tad ekaṃ tad yathā citre sitākṛtiḥ |
children.translated_text: Whatever appears, that is one — just as in a painting, the form of white;

children.text: bhāsate cākhilaṃ citraṃ pītaśītasukhādikam ||
children.translated_text: and the entire painting appears — yellow, cool, pleasant, and the like.

children.text: nātrāsiddhiḥ prakāśasya citre dharmiṇi
darśanāt |

children.translated_text: Here there is no unestablishedness [of the reason], because manifestation (<s>prakāśa</s>) is observed in the subject (<s>dharmin</s>), namely the painting.

children.text: na ca sādhyaviyuktatvaṃ dṛṣṭāntasyāpi dṛśyate ||
children.translated_text: Nor is the example seen to be devoid of the provable.

children.text: ekaikāṇunimagnatvāt saṃvittir na parasparam |
children.translated_text: Because each atom is submerged [in the whole], there is no mutual awareness [of atoms by each other].

children.text: na caikāṇuprakāśo 'sti sthūlam eva sphuraty ataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Nor is there a manifestation of a single atom — only the gross [aggregate] shines forth. Therefore:

children.text: bāhyāṇūnāṃ pratībhāso buddhir ekā sthavīyasī |
children.translated_text: The cognition of external atoms is a single, gross [cognition]. But for cognitive atoms, what single

children.text: jñānāṇūnāṃ ka ekas tu pratibhāso bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: manifestation could there be?

children.text: tasmāt sthūlatayā vyāpto nirbhāsas tannivṛttitaḥ |
children.translated_text: Therefore, manifestation is pervaded by grossness. From the cessation of that [grossness],

children.text: nivartamāno 'nekasmād ekatve viniyamyate ||
children.translated_text: [manifestation,] ceasing from multiplicity, is restricted to unity.

children.text: yathā sajā
tīyamatād bhāgād bhedanirākriyā |
children.translated_text: aspect [is achieved] by the consequence of non-appearance, so too from the heterogeneous aspect.
Just as [the refutation of] difference from the homogeneous

children.text: anābhāsaprasaṅgena vijātīyamatāt tathā ||
children.translated_text: Similarly [it is achieved] by the consequence of non-appearance from the heterogeneous aspect.

children.text: tan nāstu sādhyo dṛṣṭānto na ca śaṅkāviparyaye |
children.translated_text: Therefore, the provable is not absent, the example [is not deficient], and there is no reversal of the doubt.

children.text: ato nirdoṣato hetoś citrādvaitavyavasthitiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Hence, from the faultlessness of the reason, the establishment of variegated non-duality (<s>citrādvaita</s>) [is achieved].

children.text: saṅgrahaślokaś ca
children.translated_text: And the summary verse:

children.text:
ekatvena yathāptimān abhimato bhāsas tathā vyāpyate 
	sthaulyenāpy aṇuśo na hi kvacid idaṃ svapne 'pi nirbhāsanam |
children.translated_text: 'Just as manifestation, accepted as having unity, is also pervaded by grossness — for this [cognition] never manifests atom by atom, not even in a dream.

children.text: tena pratyaṇubhedanety uparataṃ tadvyāpa

kasyātyayād
	ekatvena parītam ākṛticayaś cāyaṃ vinirbhāsate
children.translated_text: this collection of forms shines forth as encompassed by unity.'
Therefore, the [proposed] splitting atom by atom has been abandoned. And since that pervader [viz., grossness] has been eliminated,

children.text: || iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text:
nanu cātra dṛṣṭāntadārṣṭāntikayor
      ubhayatrāpy ekatvaṃ pratyakṣato 'numānāc ca
      viruddhadharmādhyāsalakṣaṇāt pratihatam, tat katham anumānād
      ekatvasiddhir iti cet | ucyate | yad etat pratyakṣaṃ bhedasādhakam
      upanīyate, tat kiṃ nīlādīnām anātmabhūtam ātambhūtaṃ vā |
      prathamapakṣe, āstāṃ tāvad eṣām ato bhedasiddhiḥ,

sattāmātram api na
      sidhyet | sa hi nīlādiko 'rtho jaḍo vijñānāntarātmālīkasvabhāvo vā
      svīkartavyaḥ | triṣv api pakṣeṣu prakāśyaprakāśakabhāvābhāvaḥ | tathā
      hi jñānasya prakāśakatvaṃ nāma kiṃ vidyamānatvaṃ vyāpārāveśo vā |
      prathamapakṣe sarvasarvadarśitvaprasaṅgaḥ,
      sarvapuruṣajñānavidyamānatāyāḥ sarvaṃ pratyaviśiṣṭatvāt | tathā
      nīlādibhir api jñānasya grahaṇaprasaṅgaḥ, teṣām api
      vidyamā
children.translated_text: even mere existence would not be established. For that object, blue and the like, must be accepted as either inert (<s>jaḍa</s>), or as being the nature of another cognition, or as having a false nature. In all three alternatives, the relation of illuminable and illuminator is absent. For thus: does the illuminating capacity of cognition mean mere existence, or engagement in an operation? In the first alternative, there would follow the consequence that everyone perceives everything, because the existence of all persons' cognitions is undifferentiated with respect to everything. Likewise, there would follow the consequence that blue and the like also apprehend cognition, because even they have the possibility of apprehending [that has] the defining characteristic of mere

children.text: natvalakṣaṇagrāhakatvasambhavāt ||
children.translated_text: existence.

[Objection:] But here, in both the example and the exemplified, unity is opposed in both cases by perception and by inference characterized by the superimposition of contradictory properties. So how can unity be established through inference? [Reply:] It is said: This perception that is adduced as establishing difference — does it belong to [something] that is not the nature of blue and the like, or to [something] that is their nature? In the first alternative: let alone the establishment of difference from this [perception] —

children.text: atha jñānatve sati vidyamānatvam iti saviśeṣaṇaṃ lakṣaṇam ucyate | tat kiṃ nīlādīnām ajñānatve kośapānam āyuṣmatā kartavyam, yena sattāmātreṇa samasamayaṃ sphurator vijñānanīlādyoḥ pratijñāmātrād ekasya jaḍatvālīkatvabādhyatvāprakāśatvādi vyavasthāpyate |
children.translated_text: Now if the qualified definition is stated — 'existence when possessing the nature of cognition' — then should one toast to the health of [the doctrine that] blue and the like lack the nature of cognition, since, for two [things] that shine forth at the same time — cognition and blue and the like — having identical [status as] mere existents, by mere assertion alone one is determined as inert, unreal, sublatable, non-manifest, and so forth?

children.text: atha dvitīyas tadā sa kiṃ vyāpāraḥ pratya
kṣasyātmā jñānāntaram, arthasyātmārthāntaraṃ vā syāt | prathamavikalpe svātmani kāritravirodhaḥ |
kāritra actually in ms, not kāritva
dvitīyapakṣe jñānāntaraṃ yady anyaviṣayam arthasya na kiñcit | tadviṣayatvaṃ cādyāpi na siddham, tatpratyāsatter eva cintyamānatvāt ||
children.translated_text: In the second alternative, if a different cognition has a different object, it does nothing for [the original] object. And its [the cognition's] having that [original object] as its object is not yet established, since precisely the proximity to it is what is being examined.

Now if the second [alternative is taken] — then what would that operation be? Is [that operation] the very nature of perception, a different cognition, the nature of the object, or another object? In the first alternative, there is a contradiction of activity in one's own self.

children.text: tṛtīye punaḥ saṅkalpe nīlādikaṃ kṛtam eva syāt, na prakāśitam, tailavartyādibhir iva pradīpaḥ | prakāśas tu svaya
m eva | tathā ca jñānāntaratvāt santānāntaravad apratibhāsaprasaṅgaḥ |
children.translated_text: And therefore, being a different cognition, there would follow the consequence of non-appearance, like [something belonging to] another mind-stream.
In the third supposition, moreover, blue and the like would be produced, not illuminated — like a lamp [produced] by oil, wick, and the like. But manifestation belongs to [the cognition] itself.

children.text: caturthe tu vikalpe arthāntare kṛte nīlādikaṃ tadavastham eva | na cānātmaprakāśanasāmarthyaṃ jñānasya svīkartum ucitam, vyāpāravat prakāśanasyāpy evaṃ nirākartavyatvāt | na cāgnidhūmayoḥ kāryakāraṇabhāva iva jñānajñeyayor api svābhāviko grāhyagrāhakabhāvo
vaktavyaḥ, pramāṇasiddhakāryakāraṇabhāvavad grāhyagrāhakasvarūpayor adyāpi nirvaktum aśakyatvād iti kva nīlādivārtāpi yadbhedasiddhipratyāśā pratyakṣataḥ sampadyate ||
children.translated_text: natural (<s>svābhāvika</s>), like the cause-effect relation between fire and smoke — because the own-nature of apprehended and apprehender cannot be articulated to this day, unlike the cause-effect relation established through valid means of knowledge. So where is there even talk of blue and the like, that the hope of establishing their difference would be fulfilled from perception?

In the fourth alternative, however, when a different object is produced, blue and the like remain in their original state. Nor is it appropriate to accept that cognition has the capacity to illumine what is not its own self — because illumination, like operation, is also to be rejected in this very manner. Nor should the relation of apprehended and apprehender between cognition and the knowable be said to be

children.text: athātmabhūtaṃ tat pratyakṣam iti dvītyaḥ pakṣaḥ, tadātmasvasaṃvedanam eva bhedasādhakam abhyupagataṃ bhavet | tac ca yadi pratyākāraṃ bhinnaṃ tadā sarveṣāṃ svasvarūpanimagnatvā
c citraprakāśapraṇāśaprasaṅga ity uktam |
children.translated_text: respective natures — there would follow the consequence of the destruction of the variegated manifestation, as has been stated.

Now if the second alternative [is taken] — that perception belongs to the very nature [of blue and the like] — then it would be admitted that self-awareness (<s>svasaṃvedana</s>), which is of that nature, is what establishes difference. And if that [self-awareness] is different for each form, then — since all [forms] are submerged in their own

children.text:
athaitad doṣabhayāt sarveṣām ākārāṇām ekatvam eva
      svabhāvabhūtaṃ svasaṃvedanam iṣyate, tadaitad eva citrādvaitaṃ
      vijñānam ucyate, yad anekābhimatānāṃ sahopalabdhānāṃ
      nīlasukhādyākārāṇāṃ svabhāvabhūtākhaṇḍasvasaṃvedanapratyakṣaṃ nāma |
      yad āhur guruvaḥ
children.translated_text: Now if, out of fear of this fault, the self-awareness that belongs to the very nature [of cognition] is accepted as the unity of all forms — then that is precisely what is called the variegated non-dual cognition (<s>citrādvaita vijñāna</s>): namely, the undivided self-awareness that is the perception of the very nature of the forms of blue, pleasure, and the like — which are held to be many [but are] simultaneously apprehended. As the teachers say:

children.text: bhramābhramākalpanakalpanāni śātāsitādīny akhilākṣajāni |
children.translated_text: 'Cognitions arising from all the senses — [including] those construed as erroneous and non-erroneous, as pleasant, as blue, and so forth —

children.text: jñā
nāny abhinnāni sahopalabdheḥ pūrvāparatvaṃ tu na vedyam eva ||
children.translated_text: cognitions are non-different because of simultaneous apprehension; but temporal sequence is simply not cognizable.'
these

children.text: iti |
children.translated_text: Thus.

children.text:
tad evaṃ dṛṣṭāntadārṣṭāntikayor ubhayatrāpi
      svasaṃvedanapratyakṣasiddham ekatvam avidyāvaśād vipratipattau satyām
      anumānataḥ sādhyate | ata eva svasaṃvedanapratyakṣād anumānāc ca
      ekatvasiddhau na pratyakṣāntaram | nāpi viruddhadharmādhyāsalakṣaṇam
      anumānaṃ bhedasādhanāya prāptāvasaram, bhedagrāhakasya bhinnasya
      pratyakṣasyo
ktakrameṇāprāmāṇyāt, pakṣasya pratyakṣādibādhitatvāt |
children.translated_text: stated above, and because the thesis is sublated by perception and the like.

Therefore, in both the example and the exemplified, the unity established by the perception of self-awareness — when there is dispute due to the force of ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) — is proved through inference. For this very reason, when unity is established through the perception of self-awareness and through inference, there is no other perception, nor does the inference characterized by the superimposition of contradictory properties have occasion to establish difference — because the distinct perception that apprehends difference is shown to be invalid by the method

children.text:
nanu brūyān nāma kiñcit, tathāpi pratibhāsabhedād bheda eva,
      na hi dṛṣṭe 'nupapannaṃ nāmeti cet | hanta pratibhāsaśabdena kim
      abhipretam, kim ākāracakraṃ sphuraṇaṃ vā | tatra yadi prathamaḥ
      pakṣaḥ, tadā bāhye 'rthe pratyetavye buddhyākāraḥ pramāṇam |
      tathācākārabhedo vyavahartavya eva | anyathā bāhya
children.translated_text: [Objection:] Let [the Yogācāra] say whatever he wishes; even so, there is difference because of the difference in appearances — for what is well-known cannot be said to be impossible. [Reply:] Well then, what is meant by the word 'appearance'? Is it the aggregate of forms (<s>ākāracakra</s>), or [their] shining forth (<s>sphuraṇa</s>)? If the first alternative: then when an external object is to be cognized, the mental form is the means of valid knowledge. And so the difference of forms must indeed be admitted. Otherwise, the difference of externals

children.text:
bhedo na sidhyet |
      yadā punar ākāracakram eva prameyam svasaṃvedanaṃ ca pramāṇaṃ tadā
      tenaiva nīlādīnāṃ svabhāvabhūtenākhaṇḍātmanā ekīkṛtānāṃ katham
      apramādī bhedam ācakṣīta |
children.translated_text: would not be established. But when the aggregate of forms itself is the object of cognition and self-awareness is the means of valid knowledge — then how could one who is not careless assert difference of those [forms], namely blue and the like, which have been unified by that [self-awareness] as undivided, being of the same nature?

children.text:
dvitīyapakṣe tu sphuraṇaṃ
      svabhāvabhūtākhaṇḍasvasaṃvedanam evoktam iti | tathāpi kathaṃ
      bhedas tasmād yathordhvam indriyapratyakṣataḥ kṣaṇabhede pratīte
      'py avidyāva
children.translated_text: In the second alternative, [since] shining forth has been stated to be precisely the undivided self-awareness that belongs to [cognition's] very nature — then too, how is there difference? Therefore, just as — looking upward [in time] — even when momentary difference is cognized through sense-perception, there is the determination of unity due to the force of ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>),

children.text:
śād
      ekatvādhyavasāyaḥ tathā tiryak svasaṃvedanapratyakṣeṇākārābhede
      'dhigate 'py avidyāvaśād eva bhedāvasāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: so too — looking sideways [across simultaneous forms] — even when the non-difference of forms has been ascertained through the perception of self-awareness, there is the determination of difference due to the very force of ignorance.

children.text:
yady evaṃ viruddhadharmādhyāsato vijñānākāracakravad vyāpto
      'pi na bhidyeteti cet | na, bāhye dharmiṇy anekatvasya sādhyasya
      pratyakṣādyabādhitatvāt | buddhyākārakadambake tūktakrameṇa
      svasaṃvedanādisiddhaikatve 'nekatva
children.translated_text: [Objection:] If so, from the superimposition of contradictory properties, even the aggregate of cognitive forms — though pervaded [by unity] — would not be differentiated. [Reply:] No, because in the case of an external property-locus, the provable — multiplicity — is not sublated by perception and the like. But in the case of the aggregate of mental forms, since unity is established by self-awareness and the like in the manner stated, and multiplicity has been rejected —

children.text:
sya pratyākhyānād bādhakāvatāra eva
      nāsti | tasmād vijñānatve satīti hetuviśeṣaṇaṃ kartavyam yena
      bāhyasyaiva bhedaḥ sidhyati ||
children.translated_text: there is simply no room for a defeater to enter. Therefore, the qualification must be made: 'when possessing the nature of cognition' — [as a qualifier of] the reason, so that only the difference of the external is proved.

children.text:
nanu yadi vijñānātmakaṃ
      vicitrākāracakram ekaṃ tadā nīlākāra eva pītādyākāravṛndaṃ praviśet |
      tathā prakāśākāracakrayor abhedo vyaktisāmānyavat prakāśa eva,
      ākāracakram eva vā syād iti cet | asa
children.translated_text: [Objection:] If the variegated aggregate of forms possessing the nature of cognition is one, then the blue form itself would absorb the cluster of yellow and other forms. Likewise, the non-difference of the manifestation and the aggregate of forms — like universal and particular — would be either manifestation alone or the aggregate of forms alone. [Reply:] This is

children.text:
d etat | tathā hi dvayor apy
      anayoḥ
children.translated_text: wrong. For of these two

children.text: prasaṅgaviparyayayoḥ  bhedaḥ
children.translated_text: consequences and their reversals, there is difference,

children.text:
, sa ca bāhyārthavāda eva yujyate,
      tatra bhedagrāhakasyendriyapratyakṣasyeṣṭatvāt | vijñānavāde tv
      anātmaprakāśābhāvāt svasaṃvedanam evaikaṃ pramāṇam | tato 'pi
      viparyayasya
children.translated_text: and that is appropriate only in the externalist (realist) doctrine, because there the sense-perception that apprehends difference is accepted [as valid]. But in the idealist (<s>vijñānavāda</s>) doctrine, since there is no illumination of what is not one's own self, self-awareness alone is the single means of valid knowledge. And since from that too,

children.text: bhedasya siddheḥ
children.translated_text: the reverse — namely, difference — is established,

children.text:
prasaṅgo 'py
      asaṅgataḥ ity advaitam eva |
children.translated_text: the consequence too is incoherent. So it is non-duality alone.

children.text:
kiṃ ca evaṃ sthūlanīlādyākāro 'pi paramāṇumātre praviśed ity
      apratibhā
children.translated_text: Moreover, in this way, even the form of a gross blue [object] and the like would be absorbed into a single atom — and thus

children.text:
saṃ jagad āpadyeta | asti ca pratibhāsaḥ | tasmād
      yathāvasthitānām evākārāṇām akhaṇḍasvasaṃvedanātmataivaikatvam, na
      bhedo na saṃkocaḥ svīkartavyo 'pratibhāsaprasaṅgāt | tathā
      kṛtakatvasyānityatvavastutvādibhir abhede kṛtakatvam evānityatvam eva
      vā syād ity api prasaṅgo vaktavya āpadyeta, sāmānyavyaktyor
children.translated_text: the world would have the consequence of non-appearance. But there is appearance. Therefore, the unity of forms as they actually are is [precisely] their being the undivided self-awareness that is their very nature — neither difference nor contraction should be accepted, because of the consequence of non-appearance. Likewise, one should state that the consequence would apply that — if there were non-difference between being-produced (<s>kṛtakatva</s>) and impermanence, being a real entity, and the like — then being-produced would be nothing but impermanence, or [impermanence] alone [would be nothing but] being-produced. [But that consequence fails] because those two are actually non-different,

children.text:
iva tayor
      vastuto 'bhedo
children.translated_text: like universal and particular — their non-difference

children.text: 'khaṇḍātmatvāt ||
children.translated_text: being due to [their] undivided nature.

children.text: vyāvṛttibheda eva param iti cet |
children.translated_text: [Objection:] There is only a difference of exclusion (<s>vyāvṛtti</s>). [Reply:]

children.text:
yady evaṃ prakāśanīlādyor
      apy ayam eva kramo jāgartīty ekāvaśeṣaprasaṅgo bālapralāpaḥ | tad evaṃ
children.translated_text: If so, this very same principle applies to manifestation, blue, and the like as well — and the consequence that only one remains [viz., that everything collapses into one] is childish prattle. Therefore:

children.text: bāhyaṃ na naśyati bhidāṇutayāpi sattvād arthakriyāvirahasaṃkaratātmabhede |
children.translated_text: 'The external does not perish [under this analysis], because, even as atoms, existence [is maintained], and because the distinction of own-nature [is maintained] through the absence of causal efficacy, confusion [of properties], and [real] difference of self.

children.text: buddhis tu naśyati bhidaiva vidaiva sattvāc citrāpy ato na bhidam eti kim atra kurmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But cognition perishes [under the opponent's analysis], because difference is [its very] knowledge, because existence [is maintained only] through knowledge. And the variegated [cognition], therefore, does not undergo division — what can we do about it?'

children.text: nanu deśavitānāptir nātmāntaraviyoginaḥ |
children.translated_text: [Objection:] 'The attainment of spatial extension does not belong to what is not separated from another self.

children.text: na deśavitānahānau ca
MS
deśavitānahānau na bhāsa ity a
children.translated_text: And without the loss of spatial extension, appearance [of multiplicity] too' — it can be

children.text: pi śakyate ||
children.translated_text: said [is impossible].

children.text: iti cet |
children.translated_text: [Reply:]

children.text: na svātmāntaram anyātmā sa bāhyasyaiva yujyate |
children.translated_text: 'One's own self is not another, [and] another's self — that applies to the external alone.

children.text: buddheḥ svavittiniṣṭhāyā yaḥ paras tasya kā gatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: For cognition, which rests on its own self-awareness — what recourse has what is other to it?'

children.text: hanta tathāpi
children.translated_text: Well then, even so:

children.text: nīlādivat tad ekaṃ ca katham etat sametu cet |
children.translated_text: '[Objection:] It is one, like blue and the like — but how can this be coherent? [Reply:]

children.text: nīlam aṃśāntaraṃ caikaṃ kathaṃ tadbhāti saṅgatam ||
children.translated_text: Blue is one part, and one — how does it appear? That is coherent [in the same way].

children.text: neṣṭaṃ tad api cet tarhi kvāṇvantarbhidi bhāsanam |
children.translated_text: [Objection:] If that too is not accepted, then where would there be appearance in the division within an atom?

children.text: na
parīkṣākṣamaṃ cāṇuḥ
children.translated_text: does not withstand examination —

children.text: kutas tasya tadā bhidā ||
children.translated_text: whence then its division?
An atom

children.text: mā bhūd avastubhāvāc cet so
'py ekatvahatau bhavet |
children.translated_text: too would result in the destruction of unity.
[Objection:] Let [the atom] not be [real] because of being a non-entity. [Reply:] That

children.text: nirbhāsād ekatāsiddhau svavitter vastutā sthitā ||
children.translated_text: When unity is established from appearance, reality is established from self-awareness.

children.text: na pratītyasamutpādo 'nutpādo vāsya bādhakaḥ |
children.translated_text: Neither dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>) nor non-origination is its defeater —

children.text: ekānekaviyoge 'pi sphūrtimātreṇa sattvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: because even in the absence of oneness and multiplicity, existence [is maintained] through shining forth alone.

children.text: kiṃ ca pūrvāparajñānam advaite yan na vidyate |
children.translated_text: Moreover, prior and subsequent cognition — which in non-duality does not exist —

children.text: pratītyotpannatā tasmād asiddher apy asādhanam ||
children.translated_text: [the claim of] being dependently originated is therefore a non-prover, since even [its] unestablished-ness [makes it so].

children.text: anutpādo 'py anekānto 'kāryakāraṇarūpakam |
children.translated_text: Non-origination too is inconclusive — because of not having the form of cause and effect.

children.text: hāne 'pi hetuphalayoḥ sphura
drūpaṃ kva gacchatu ||
children.translated_text: form — where would it go?
Even if the cause-effect [relation] is abandoned, the shining

children.text: ekānekatayā vastuvyāptiḥ siddhā yadi kvacit |
children.translated_text: If the pervasion of real entities by oneness and multiplicity is established somewhere [as a premise],

children.text: sarvaśūnyatvasamaye hetur iṣṭavighātakṛt ||
children.translated_text: [then] in a system of universal emptiness, the reason would destroy what is desired [by the opponent himself].

children.text: atha lokaprasiddhau ca na sarvalokakalpitam |
children.translated_text: Now if [it is said that the premise rests on] common consensus — even so, not everything is imagined by all people.

children.text: vastuvyavasthā śaraṇaṃ kiṃ tu mānena saṅgatam ||
children.translated_text: The determination of real entities is the refuge — but [only] what is coherent with a valid means of knowledge [counts].

children.text: na cādhyakṣānumānābhyām anaṅgaṃ kvacid īkṣitam |
children.translated_text: And neither by perception nor by inference is any non-component (<s>anaṅga</s>) ever observed

children.text: yasya rāśir anekaṃ syān nāpi vastu ca kiñcana ||
children.translated_text: whose heap would be many [but which itself] would not be any real entity whatsoever.

children.text: yasya caikataratvābhyāṃ sattvavyāptiḥ sa hanyatām |
children.translated_text: Let him whose pervasion of existence by either [oneness or multiplicity] be defeated.

children.text: abhrā
ntavittimātreṇa sattāvādī tu jitvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: awareness alone is invincible.'
But the proponent of existence through non-erroneous

children.text: ||samāptaś citrādvaitaprakāśavādo 'yam ||
children.translated_text: Thus is completed the <s>Citrādvaitaprakāśavāda</s> (Treatise on the Manifestation of Variegated Non-Duality).

children.text: grāhyaṃ na tasya grahaṇaṃ na tena jñānāntaragrāhyatayāpi śūnyaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'It is not its apprehended object, nor is apprehension through it [possible]; it is empty of being the object of another cognition.

children.text: tathāpi ca jñānamayaḥ  prakāśaḥ pratyakṣapakṣas tu tavāvirāsīt ||
children.translated_text: And yet the manifestation, which is of the nature of cognition — your thesis of perception has thus appeared.'

children.text: Santānāntaradūṣaṇam
children.translated_text: <s>Santānāntaradūṣaṇam</s> (Refutation of Other Mind-Streams)

children.text: atheha prakāśasahopalambhādisādhanabalena jaḍapadārtharāśāvapāste nīlapītādyaśeṣapadārthajāte ca svacittapratibhāsātmani svapnamāyādivad advayarūpe siddhe santānāntarasadasattānirūpaṇārtham idam ārabhyate |

evaṃ hi kecid āhuḥ | asty eva santānāntaram anumānapratītam | tathā hīcchācittasamanantaravyāhāravyavahārābhāsasya darśanāt tadabhāve cādarśanād upalambhānupalambhasādhanam anvayavyatirekaśarīram icchācittena saha vyāhārādyābhāsasya kāryakāraṇabhāvam ātmasantāne 'vadhāryecchācittasyāpratisaṃvedanasamaye 'pi vicchinnavyāhārādyābhāsadarśanāt tatkāraṇabhūtam icchācittam anumīyamānaṃ santānāntaram eva vyavatiṣṭhata iti |
children.translated_text: For thus some say: Other mental continua (<s>santānāntara</s>) indeed exist, known through inference (<s>anumāna</s>). For, since one observes the appearance of verbal behavior (<s>vyāhāra-vyavahāra-ābhāsa</s>) immediately following desire-consciousness (<s>icchā-citta</s>), and since one does not observe it in its absence, one ascertains in one's own continuum (<s>ātma-santāna</s>) the cause-effect relation (<s>kārya-kāraṇa-bhāva</s>) of the appearance of verbal behavior etc. with desire-consciousness, having the form of positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvaya-vyatireka</s>), which constitutes the proof through apprehension and non-apprehension (<s>upalambha-anupalambha</s>). Then, even at a time when desire-consciousness is not directly experienced, since one observes the appearance of disconnected verbal behavior etc., the desire-consciousness inferred as its cause establishes itself as belonging to another continuum (<s>santānāntara</s>) alone.

children.text: atredam ālocyate | tadicchācittaṃ vyāhārādyābhāsasya kāraṇatayā vyavasthāpyamānam anumātur darśanayogyam atha dṛśyādṛśyaviśeṣaṇānapekṣam icchāmātram | yadi tāvad ādyo vikalpas tadānumātur darśanayogyatvād icchācittasyānumānakāle 'nupalabdhir abhāvam eva gamayatīty anupambhākhyapratyakṣabādhitatvāt kvānumānāvakāśas tasya | yadi punar icchācittam anumānakāle 'py anubhūyeta, tadā kim asyānumānena | athaivam agnidhūmayos tadutpattisiddhyanantaraṃ naganikuñje dhūmam upalabhamāno nāgnim apy anuminuyāt, tatrāpy agner anupalabdhibādhitatvāt, upalambhe cānumānavaiphalyāt | naivam, anumānasamaye deśaviprakarṣavato vahner darśanāyogyatvena dṛśyānupalabdhivirahāt, adṛśyānupalambhasya cābhāvasādhanatvavirodhāt | icchācittasya tu nāsti deśaviprakarṣaḥ | icchācittaṃ hi svasambaddham evānumātur darśanayogyam, tasya ca deśādiviprakarṣa ity alaukikam etat |
children.translated_text: Here the following is considered: Is that desire-consciousness (<s>icchā-citta</s>), when established as the cause of the appearance of verbal behavior etc., something fit to be perceived (<s>darśana-yogya</s>) by the inferring person, or is it mere desire (<s>icchā-mātra</s>) without regard to the qualification of being visible or invisible (<s>dṛśya-adṛśya</s>)? If the first alternative is taken, then since the desire-consciousness is fit to be perceived by the inferring person, its non-apprehension (<s>anupalabdhi</s>) at the time of inference establishes its absence alone; and since it is contradicted by the direct perception called non-apprehension (<s>anupalambha</s>), where is there any scope for inference? If, on the other hand, the desire-consciousness were experienced even at the time of inference, then what need would there be for its inference? Now, if one were to object: just as with fire and smoke — after establishing the origination of the latter from the former, one who perceives smoke in a mountain grove would not also infer fire, since there too fire would be contradicted by non-apprehension, and since inference would be pointless when there is direct apprehension — this is not so. For at the time of inference, fire being remote in location is unfit for perception, and hence there is no non-apprehension of the visible (<s>dṛśya-anupalabdhi</s>); and non-apprehension of the invisible (<s>adṛśya-anupalambha</s>) does not contradict the establishment of absence. But desire-consciousness has no remoteness in location (<s>deśa-viprakarṣa</s>). For the desire-consciousness that is to be inferred is fit to be perceived by the inferring person as connected with oneself, and to attribute spatial remoteness etc. to it is extraordinary indeed.

children.text: atha dvitīyo vikalpaḥ | tathā hīcchācittamātraṃ svaparasantānasādhāraṇadṛśyādṛśyaviśeṣaṇānapekṣaṃ vyāhārādyābhāsaṃ prati kāraṇatayāvadhāryate | tadavadhāraṇaṃ kena pramāṇena | vyāhārādyābhāsasya hīcchāmātrābhāve 'bhāvaṃ pratītya tadutpattisiddhigaveṣaṇā | na cecchāmātrasya svaparasantānasādhāraṇasya svasaṃvedanenānyena vābhāvaḥ śakyāvagamaḥ | yathā hi vahnimātrasya deśakālavyavahitasyāpi dhūmotpādadeśakālayor yadi syād upalabhyetaiva mayeti sambhāvitasyānumātṛpuruṣendriyapratyakṣeṇa dhūmotpādāt prāgabhāvo 'vadhāryamāṇas tadutpattisiddhim adhyāsayatīti vyavahitadeśakālasyāpi vahner dhūmamātraṃ prati kāraṇatvāvadhāraṇam, svabhāvaviprakṛṣṭasya tu jaṭharabhavādisādhāraṇasya sarvathānumātṛpuruṣāśakyābhāvapratītikasya vyāptibahirbhāva eva | tathātrāpīcchācittaṃ parasantānasādhāraṇam api yāvad yadīha syād upalabhyetaiva mayeti yadi sambhāvayituṃ śakyeta tadā tadvyatirekasiddhidvāreṇa kāraṇatayāvadhāryate | kevalaṃ svabhāvaviprakṛṣṭe cittamātre 'stamiteyaṃ katheti ||
children.translated_text: Now the second alternative. Suppose that mere desire-consciousness (<s>icchā-citta-mātra</s>), without regard to the qualification of being visible or invisible — which is common to both one's own and another's continuum (<s>sva-para-santāna-sādhāraṇa</s>) — is ascertained as the cause of the appearance of verbal behavior etc. By what means of valid cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>) is that ascertainment made? For the investigation into the establishment of the origination of the appearance of verbal behavior etc. proceeds by first cognizing its absence in the absence of mere desire. But the absence of mere desire, which is common to one's own and another's continuum, cannot be ascertained either by <s>svasaṃvedana</s> (self-awareness) or by any other means. For just as the absence of mere fire prior to the production of smoke is ascertained at the place and time of smoke's production — since fire, even when remote in space and time, if it were present at the place and time of smoke's production, would certainly be apprehended by the sense-perception of the inferring person, and the absence ascertained prior to smoke's production confirms the establishment of its origination — thus the ascertainment of mere fire's causal status with respect to mere smoke is possible even when spatially and temporally remote. But that which is remote in nature (<s>svabhāva-viprakṛṣṭa</s>), common to things like that which exists in the womb, and whose absence can in no way be cognized by the inferring person, falls entirely outside the scope of pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>). Likewise here too, even though desire-consciousness common to another's continuum, if it could be supposed that 'were it present here, I would certainly apprehend it,' then its causal status could be ascertained through establishing its negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>). But when the mere consciousness in question is remote in nature (<s>svabhāva-viprakṛṣṭa</s>), this line of reasoning has come to an end.

children.text: na ca pracittaṃ kālaviprakṛṣṭaṃ varamānatvād asya, atītānāgatayor eva kālaviprakṛṣṭatvena vyavahārāt |
children.translated_text: Nor is the other's consciousness (<s>para-citta</s>) remote in time (<s>kāla-viprakṛṣṭa</s>), since it is present; for the designation 'temporally remote' applies only to the past and the future.

children.text: nāpi deśaviprakṛṣṭam, yasminn eva hi śuklaśaṅkhādideśe svacittaṃ śuklākārapratibhāsi svasaṃvedanena vedyate taddeśavarty eva pītākārapratibhāsi parasantānabhāvi cittaṃ na vedyate | tat katham eṣa deśaviprakarṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Nor is it remote in location (<s>deśa-viprakṛṣṭa</s>), for in the very location of a white conch-shell etc., where one's own consciousness (<s>sva-citta</s>) — appearing with the form of white — is cognized through <s>svasaṃvedana</s> (self-awareness), the consciousness belonging to another's continuum (<s>parasantāna-bhāvi citta</s>), appearing with the form of yellow, present in that very same location, is not cognized. How then can this be called remoteness in location?

children.text: athecchācittamātraṃ svasaṃvedanamātrāpekṣayā na svabhāvaviprakṛṣṭam | na hy agnir apy eko yenaivendriyavijñānena dṛśyate tenaivānyo 'pi dṛśyam | tatra yathā cakṣurvijñānamātrāpekṣayā agnimātraṃ dṛśyam iti vyavasthāpyate tathātrāpi svasaṃvedanamātrāpekṣayā icchācittamātraṃ svaparasantānasādhāraṇam api dṛśyam eveti |
children.translated_text: Now suppose: mere desire-consciousness is not remote in nature (<s>svabhāva-viprakṛṣṭa</s>) with respect to mere <s>svasaṃvedana</s> (self-awareness). For even a single fire is not such that the very same sense-cognition (<s>indriya-vijñāna</s>) by which one fire is perceived also perceives another. Just as in that case mere fire is established as visible with respect to mere visual cognition (<s>cakṣur-vijñāna</s>), so here too mere desire-consciousness, even though common to one's own and another's continuum (<s>sva-para-santāna-sādhāraṇa</s>), is simply visible with respect to mere <s>svasaṃvedana</s>.

children.text: atrocyate | kim atra mātraśabdenānumātṛpuruṣasambandhāsambandhābhyām aviśeṣitaṃ yasya kasyacit puruṣasyendriyajñānaṃ vastuviṣayīkurvāṇam asya dṛśyatāsambhave 'pi nānimittam abhimatam | yady evaṃ piśācādir api dṛśyaḥ syāt | so 'pi hi kasyacit puṃso yogyādeḥ svajātīyasya vā piśācāntarasya bhavaty evendriyajñānagocara iti na kaścit svabhāvaviprakṛṣṭaḥ syāt | tasmād anumātṛpuruṣasambandhitvam anapāsya vijñānasya svalakṣaṇādibhedanirāsapara eva mātraśabdo yuktaḥ | etad evāśaṅkya Dharmottareṇābhihitam -
children.translated_text: To this we reply: What is meant here by the word 'mere' (<s>mātra</s>)? Is it intended to mean a cognition of any person whatsoever, undifferentiated by connection or non-connection with the inferring person, making an object its content — so that even if the possibility of its being visible to this person is absent, it would not be without a basis? If so, then even <s>piśācas</s> (demons) and the like would be visible. For they too are objects of the sense-cognition of some person — a <s>yogin</s> or another <s>piśāca</s> of their own kind — and thus nothing would be remote in nature (<s>svabhāva-viprakṛṣṭa</s>). Therefore, without removing the connection with the inferring person, the word 'mere' is appropriate only as negating distinctions such as <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular characteristics) and the like of cognition. Anticipating precisely this objection, <s>Dharmottara</s> has stated —

Now, here — when by the force of proofs such as the co-apprehension of manifestation and the like, the mass of inert objects has been set aside, and the entire collection of objects such as blue, yellow, and the like has been established as having the nature of the appearance of one's own mind, as non-dual in form like a dream or illusion — this [treatise] is commenced for the purpose of determining the existence or non-existence of other mind-streams.

children.text: ekapratipattrapekṣaṃ cedaṃ pratyakṣalakṣaṇam |
children.translated_text: "This definition of perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) is relative to a single cognizing subject" —

children.text: ityādi | tenaivaṃ dṛśyatāsambhāvanā yadīha deśe kāle vā syād ghaṭādir niyamenopalabhyeta, madīyasya cakṣurvijñānamātrasya viṣayībhaved iti | paricitte tu na śakyam evam | yadīha paricittaṃ syāt niyamena madīyasya svasaṃvedanamātrasya viṣayi syād iti ||

yadi cecchācittamātraṃ tadutpattigrhaṇasamaye dṛśyatayā sambhāvayitavyam, tadānumānakāle 'pi dṛśyatayā sambhāvya tadanupalambhenābhāvasādhane katham anumānaṃ pravartayitum idam ārabdham, pratyakṣeṇaiva pakṣabādhāt | na ca kālabhedena svabhāvaviprakarṣetarāv iti yatkiñcid etat | tasmād icchācittamātrasya svaparasantānasādhāraṇasya dṛśyatayā sambhāvayitum aśakyatvāt vyahārādyutpādāt prāg anupalambhe 'py abhāvasiddhau na tadabhāvaprayukto vyāhārādyabhāvaḥ pratīyata iti kathaṃ kāraṇatvasiddhir yataḥ kāryahetudvāreṇānumīyeta | icchācittaviśeṣas tu svasantānabhāvī na bhavaty evānumātur dṛśyaḥ | kiṃ tu tasya dṛśyānupalambhāj jijñāsitaviśeṣe dharmiṇi bādhitasya katham anumānam ity uktam eva ||
children.translated_text: And if mere desire-consciousness must be supposed as visible at the time of establishing its origination, then at the time of inference too, by supposing it to be visible and establishing its absence through its non-apprehension (<s>anupalambha</s>), how could this inference have been undertaken to operate — since the thesis (<s>pakṣa</s>) would be contradicted by direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) itself? Nor is it of any consequence to say that remoteness in nature (<s>svabhāva-viprakarṣa</s>) and its opposite vary with difference in time. Therefore, since mere desire-consciousness, being common to one's own and another's continuum, cannot be supposed as visible, even though there is non-apprehension prior to the production of verbal behavior etc., the absence of desire-consciousness is not established from that non-apprehension, and so the absence of verbal behavior etc. as caused by its absence cannot be cognized — how then can the causal relation be established, by means of which one could infer through the effect-as-reason (<s>kārya-hetu</s>)? As for the particular desire-consciousness belonging to one's own continuum (<s>svasantāna</s>), it is simply never visible (<s>dṛśya</s>) to the inferring person. Rather, from the non-apprehension of the visible (<s>dṛśya-anupalambha</s>) regarding it, when the thesis (<s>pakṣa</s>) is contradicted with respect to the property-possessor (<s>dharmin</s>) under investigation — how can inference proceed? This has already been stated.

children.text: tad evam icchācittaviśeṣe svasantānabhāvini sādhye pakṣasya pratyakṣabādhaḥ, icchācittamātre 'pi svaparasantānasādhāraṇe sādhye yady anupalambhamātreṇa dṛśyaviśeṣaṇānapekṣeṇa pratibandhasiddhisamaye tasyābhāvaḥ pratīyate, tadā pakṣīkṛte dharmiṇi tatheti sa eva doṣaḥ | atha na pratīyate tadā sandigdhavyatireko hetvābhāso vyāhārādir iti sthitam |
children.translated_text: Thus, when the particular desire-consciousness belonging to one's own continuum is the property to be proven (<s>sādhya</s>), the thesis is contradicted by direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>). And even when mere desire-consciousness common to one's own and another's continuum is the property to be proven — if at the time of establishing the invariable connection (<s>pratibandha</s>), its absence is cognized through mere non-apprehension without regard to the qualification of 'visible' — then the same defect applies to the property-possessor (<s>dharmin</s>) that has been made the thesis. If, on the other hand, its absence is not cognized, then verbal behavior etc. constitutes a fallacious reason (<s>hetvābhāsa</s>) with unascertained negative concomitance (<s>sandigdha-vyatireka</s>). This is established.

children.text: evaṃ tarhi santānāntarasādhakasyābhāvād bādhakasyāpi kasyacid adarśanād bhavatu tatra sandeha eveti kecit | tair idaṃ bādhakam abhidhīyamānam avadhīyatām | yadi hi santānāntaraṃ sambhavet tadā tato bhedena svasantānasyāvaśyaṃ bhavitavyam | anyathā svasantānād api prakāśamānāt tasya parasantānābhimatasya bhedo na syāt | na cābhedas tayor iti svasantānād bhedābhedābhyām abādhyasya parasantānasya sāmānyaśaśaviṣāṇādivad abhāva evāyāta iti kathaṃ sandehaḥ | tasmāt parasantānāpekṣayā svasantānasya bhedo 'py avaśyambhāvyah | sa ca bhedaḥ santānasya svabhāvaḥ svasantāne pratibhāsamāne niyamena pratibhāseta | katham aparathā pratibhānāpratibhānalakṣaṇaviruddhadharmādhyāse 'pi svasantānasya parasantānād bhedaḥ svabhāvatām āsādayet ||
children.translated_text: Some then say: Since there is no proof establishing another continuum (<s>santānāntara</s>), and since no refutation is observed either, let there simply be doubt regarding it. Let those who hold this view attend to the following refutation. For if another continuum were possible, then one's own continuum (<s>svasantāna</s>) would necessarily have to possess difference (<s>bheda</s>) from it. Otherwise, since one's own continuum is also manifest, the other continuum as conceived would not differ from it. And since there is no non-difference (<s>abheda</s>) between them either, the absence of the other continuum — which is uncontradicted by either difference or non-difference from one's own continuum — is established, just like a universal or a hare's horn (<s>śaśa-viṣāṇa</s>). How then can there be doubt? Therefore, the difference of one's own continuum relative to another continuum must also necessarily exist. And that difference, being the essential nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) of the continuum, would necessarily appear when one's own continuum appears. How otherwise — even if one were to superimpose contradictory properties (<s>viruddha-dharma</s>) characterized by appearing and not-appearing — could the difference of one's own continuum from another continuum attain the status of essential nature?

children.text: na cāsau bhedaḥ pratibhāsate | bhedapratibhāse hi upagamyamāne tadavadhibhūtasyāpi parasantānasya pratibhāso durapahnavaḥ syāt |
children.translated_text: And that difference does not appear. For if the appearance of difference were admitted, then the appearance of the other continuum (<s>parasantāna</s>) too, which serves as the limit (<s>avadhi</s>) of that difference, would be difficult to deny.

and so forth. Thus the supposition of visibility means: 'If a pot etc. were present at this place or time, it would necessarily be apprehended; it would become the object of my mere visual cognition (<s>cakṣur-vijñāna</s>).' But with regard to another's consciousness (<s>para-citta</s>), one cannot reason thus: 'If another's consciousness were present here, it would necessarily become the object of my mere <s>svasaṃvedana</s> (self-awareness).'

children.text:
asmād bhinnam itīdaṃ cet svarūpaṃ svasya cetasaḥ |
      sāvadher asya bhāsaḥ syān na vā grāhyaṃ tadātmanā ||
children.translated_text:
'If this is the nature of one's own mind (<s>cetas</s>), as different from that,
then either the appearance of this would include its limit (<s>avadhi</s>), or it would not be grasped in that manner.'

children.text: bhede 'nyaleśam api naiti kuto bhinnaḥ | evam ādikam aśeṣam iha pravacanapradīpaśrīsākārasaṅgrahādivacanam anusmryatām |

yathā hi svasantānamātre parisphurati śaśaviṣāṇād asphurato na bhedaḥ pratibhāti tathā parasantānād api sphuraṇavirahiṇo na bhāty eva bhedaḥ | na hi parasantānāpekṣayā kaścid viśeṣaleśaḥ svasantānasya parisphurati yo nāsti śaśaviṣāṇāpekṣayā | na ca śaśaviṣāṇaparasantānāv apekṣya samāne svasantānapratibhāse śaśaviṣāṇāpekṣayā na bhedo nāpy abhedaḥ pratibhāti | parasantānāpekṣayā tu bheda eva bhātīty evam avasthāpayituṃ śakyam |
children.translated_text: For just as when one's own continuum (<s>svasantāna</s>) alone shines forth, no difference appears from a hare's horn (<s>śaśa-viṣāṇa</s>) which does not shine forth, likewise no difference appears from another continuum (<s>parasantāna</s>) either, which is devoid of shining forth. For no trace of any distinguishing feature (<s>viśeṣa</s>) of one's own continuum appears relative to another continuum that is not also absent relative to a hare's horn. And it cannot be maintained that when the appearance of one's own continuum is the same relative to both hare's horn and other continuum, relative to the hare's horn neither difference nor non-difference appears, but relative to the other continuum difference alone appears.

children.text: bhedābhedayor abhāvaparihāreṇa hi yathā bhedo vyavasthitaḥ tadvad bhedapratibhāso 'pi bhedābhedābhāvapratibhāsavilakṣaṇa evocito bhavitum, na ca tathānubhūyate | tathāpi bhedaḥ pratibhātīti vacanaracanam etat | bhāṣyakāranyāyo 'py atra bhedapratibhāsadūṣaṇe vistarato 'vagantavyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For just as difference is established by the exclusion of the absence of both difference and non-difference, so too the appearance of difference ought to be established as distinct from the appearance of the absence of both difference and non-difference. But it is not so experienced. To say 'nonetheless, difference appears' is mere verbal construction. The reasoning of the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> (commentator) regarding the refutation of the appearance of difference should also be understood here in detail.

children.text: yadi cāvadhipratibhāsavirahe 'pi bhedapratibhānam idaṃ paracittānukampayā kṣamitavyaṃ tarhi bahirarthasyāpi katham abhāvaḥ sidhyati | śakyaṃ hi tatrāpi sandeham avatārayitum, na bahirarthaḥ kasyacid ābhāsate, parasantānas tu parasya pratibhāsata eva, tataś cātraiva sandeho na bahirartha iti cet | etad api sakalaṃ sandigdham eva | na hy avaśyaṃ parasantānaḥ parasyābhāsate, kadācid asau nāsaty eva na cāsāv avabhāsata ity api vaktuṃ śakteḥ |
children.translated_text: And if this appearance of difference without the appearance of its limit (<s>avadhi</s>) is to be tolerated out of compassion for the doctrine of other minds (<s>para-citta</s>), then how is the non-existence of external objects (<s>bahirārtha</s>) also established? For doubt can be introduced there as well. If one objects that external objects do not appear to anyone, while another's continuum does appear to the other person himself, and therefore doubt applies only here and not to external objects — even this entire position is doubtful. For it is not certain that another's continuum appears to the other person; perhaps that other person does not exist at all, and one cannot even say that 'it does not appear to him.'

children.text: kiṃ ca mā nāma bhāsiṣṭa bahirarthaḥ kasyacid api tathāpi kathaṃ tadabhāvasiddhir bhedapratibhāsābhyupagamavādina itīyanmātram iha vivakṣitam | na cātra kaścid doṣaḥ | tasmād bahirarthena sādhāraṇaṃ santānāntaram iti kathaṃ vijñāptivādinām api saṃmataṃ bhaviṣyati | kiṃ ca kāryakāraṇabhāvo 'pi vijñānadvayasya bhedapratibhāsavādinā bādhitum aśakyaḥ | pūrvabhāvinī hi saṃvittiḥ parasaṃvittyapekṣayā bhedaṃ pūrvatvaṃ cātmano gṛhṇāty evāvadhipratibhāsavigame 'pi ||
children.translated_text: Moreover, let external objects (<s>bahirārtha</s>) not appear to anyone at all — still, how is their non-existence established for one who upholds the appearance of difference (<s>bheda-pratibhāsa</s>)? This alone is what is intended here. And there is no fault in this. Therefore, how will it be accepted even by proponents of <s>vijñaptivāda</s> (consciousness-only doctrine) that other continua (<s>santānāntara</s>) are on par with external objects? Furthermore, even the cause-effect relation (<s>kārya-kāraṇa-bhāva</s>) between two cognitions cannot be refuted by one who upholds the appearance of difference. For a prior cognition (<s>saṃvitti</s>), relative to a subsequent cognition, grasps its own difference and priority — even without the appearance of the limit (<s>avadhi</s>).

children.text: parabhāviny api saṃvittiḥ pūrvasaṃvittyapekṣayā bhedaṃ paratvaṃ cātmano 'dhigacchaty eva santānāntaravad iti niyatapūrvāparabhāvalakṣaṇe kāryakāraṇabhāve 'vabhāsamāne 'vasīyamāne ca nīlādicitrākāravat katham
children.translated_text: A subsequent cognition (<s>saṃvitti</s>) too, relative to the prior cognition, ascertains its own difference and posteriority — just as with another continuum (<s>santānāntara</s>). Thus, when the cause-effect relation characterized by the fixed sequence of prior and posterior appears and is ascertained — like the variegated forms of blue etc. — how

'In difference, not even a trace of the other is reached — from what then is it different?' Let all such statements from the <s>Pravacanapradīpa</s>, the illustrious <s>Sākārasaṅgraha</s>, and other works be recalled here.

children.text: saṃvṛttyāstu yathā tathā
(PV III 4d)

children.translated_text: "let it be so conventionally (<s>saṃvṛttyā</s>)" —

children.text: iti bhagavato Vārtikakārasya vacanena phalitam atra mate | api ca citrākāracakre dharmiṇy advaitasādhanārtham upanyastasya prakāśamānatvādihetor bhedagrāhakapratyakṣāpahṛtaviṣayatvam udbhāvayataḥ prativādino bhedagrahaṇam anumanyamānena santānāntarasandehaṃ ca vinā katham uttaritavyaṃ bhavatā |

nanv evam api santānāntarābhāvaḥ kena pramāṇena siddhaḥ | na tāvat pratyakṣeṇa, tasya vidhiviṣayasya pratiṣedhasādhanānadhikārāt | nāpy anumānena, tasya dṛśyābhāvasādhananiyatasyātīndriyaparacittābhāvasādhane 'navatārād iti cet | atra brūmaḥ | santānāntarasambhave niyatabhāvaḥ tato bhedaḥ svacittasya | abhede svasantānāt parasantāna eva syāt | yathā ca yad upalabhyamānaṃ yena rūpeṇa na bhāsate na tat tena rūpeṇa sadvyavahārayogyaṃ yathā nīlaṃ pītarūpeṇa | nopalabhyate ca svacittam upalabhyamānaṃ parasantānād bhinnena rūpeṇeti bhedasya svacittatādātmyaniṣedhe dṛśyaviśeṣaṇaprayogānapekṣā svabhāvānupalabdhir iyam ||
children.translated_text: [Objection:] Even so, by what means of valid knowledge is the non-existence of other mental continua (<s>santānāntara</s>) established? Not by perception, since that — being confined to positive entities as its objects — has no authority to establish a negation. Nor by inference, since that — being restricted to proving the absence of what is visible (<s>dṛśyābhāsa</s>) — has no entry into proving the absence of other minds, which are beyond the senses. [Reply:] To this we say: If other mental continua were possible, the difference of one's own mind from them would be invariably [present]. In the absence of difference, one's own continuum would simply be the other's continuum. And just as what is being perceived does not appear in a certain form and is not fit for conventional designation as existing in that form — as blue [is not fit for designation] as yellow — so too one's own mind, though being perceived, is not perceived in a form that is different from another continuum. This is an essential-nature non-apprehension (<s>svabhāvānupalabdhi</s>) that does not require the qualification of visibility in negating the identity of one's own mind [with something different from other continua].

children.text: nāpy asiddhiḥ, bhedapratibhāse tadavadher api pratibhāsaprāpteḥ | avadhyapratibhāse tu bhedapratibhāsābhāvaḥ śaśaviṣāṇabhedapratibhāsābhāvavat siddha eva | evam anena pramāṇena santānāntarasya svacittāpekṣayā bhede pratikṣipte abhede ca svayam evāsambhavini bhedābhedābhyām avācyatvaṃ siddham | sāmānyādivad vastutāpahatir iti, kathaṃ bādhakābhāvāt santānāntare sandeho 'bhidhīyate | etac ca śāstrīyaprameyasmāraṇamātraphalaṃ kiñcil likhitam iti | param iha svayam anusandheyam |
children.translated_text: Nor is this [reason] unestablished, because when difference appears, the limit [i.e., the other continuum] from which [the difference would obtain] would also be expected to appear. But when the limit does not appear, the absence of the appearance of difference is established — just as the absence of the appearance of difference from a hare's horn [is established]. Thus, by this means of valid knowledge, when difference of the other continuum relative to one's own mind is rejected, and when identity [of it with one's own mind] is itself impossible, [the other continuum's] being inexpressible as either different or identical is established. Like universals (<s>sāmānya</s>) and the like, its status as a real entity is destroyed. So how can it be said that there is doubt regarding other continua due to the absence of a defeater? And this [discussion] has been written as having the mere fruit of recalling a doctrinal matter from the treatises. The rest should be investigated here by oneself.

children.text: api ca santānātare tāvad arvāgdṛśāṃ sandeho bhavadbhir anumanyate | bhagavatas tu kim avasthāpyatām | saṃdehāvasthāpane kathaṃ sarvajñatā | vidyamānam eva kadācit santānāntaraṃ bhagavatā nāvadhāryate tathāpy asau sarvajña iti katham etat | anumānaṃ ca santānāntaraviṣayaṃ prāg eva cintitam | na cānumānena pratītāv api sarvajñatā bhavitam arhati | pratyakṣeṇa paracittapratītau grāhyagrāhakabhāvo 'pi paracittasya bhagavaccittena sahāyāta iti bahirarthavāda eva mukhāntareṇopagataḥ syāt, katham ayaṃ vañcayati vādaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Moreover, regarding other continua — let it be conceded by you that ordinary people (<s>arvāgdṛś</s>) have doubt. But what is to be maintained regarding the <s>Bhagavān</s> (the Blessed One)? If doubt is maintained, how can there be omniscience (<s>sarvajñatā</s>)? [If you say] an existing other continuum is sometimes not ascertained by the <s>Bhagavān</s>, and yet he is omniscient — how is this [coherent]? And the inference regarding other continua has already been considered previously. And even if [other continua are] cognized through inference, omniscience cannot [thereby] be [established]. And if other minds are cognized through perception, then the subject-object relation (<s>grāhyagrāhakabhāva</s>) would have also arrived between the other mind and the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s mind — so the external-realist doctrine (<s>bahirarthavāda</s>) would have been adopted through the back door. How does this doctrine deceive?

children.text: asmadīyam etena tu paracittaṃ nāsty eveti tadavadhāraṇakṛto [na] bhagavataḥ sarvajñatākṣatidoṣaḥ | yāvac ca bhedagrahaṇābhimānarūpā saṃvṛsttitāvat santānāntare sandehāt tadavabodhanārthaṃ vacanādir api pravartata iti svavacanavirodho 'pi na sambhavaty eva | na khalu santānāntaraviṣayaḥ sarvathā sandeho nāsty evety abhimatam asmākam, api tu paramārthagatir iyam upadarśitā | idam hi santānāntarābhāvasādhanam advayasādhanena sādhāraṇam iti naikaniyataḥ svavacanādivirodhas tatparihāro vā | citrākārasambhavamātreṇāpi ca vedāntadhvāntāpasāro Bhāṣyakāreṇa darśitaḥ | tathā ca
children.translated_text: Our [position], however, is this: another mind simply does not exist — so there is no defect of damage to the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s omniscience arising from the ascertainment of it [as non-existent]. And as long as the conventional truth (<s>saṃvṛti</s>) endures — which consists in the semblance of the apprehension of difference — there is doubt about other continua, and for the purpose of instructing them, speech and the like also operate. Thus, self-contradiction too is simply impossible. For it is not at all our position that doubt regarding other continua absolutely does not exist — rather, this ultimate truth (<s>paramārtha</s>) has been indicated. For this proof of the non-existence of other continua is shared with the proof of non-duality (<s>advayasādhana</s>) — so the self-contradiction and the like, and its resolution, are not restricted to this alone. Moreover, the author of the <s>Bhāṣya</s> [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] has shown that the dispelling of the darkness of <s>Vedānta</s> [is accomplished] merely by the possibility of variegated forms (<s>citrākāra</s>). As [he says]:

this is the implication in this system, by the words of the blessed <s>Vārtikakāra</s>. Moreover, when the opponent, in order to refute the appearance of difference in the property-possessor (<s>dharmin</s>) — namely, the array of variegated forms (<s>citrākāra-cakra</s>) — where a reason such as 'being manifest' (<s>prakāśamānatva</s>) has been adduced for establishing non-duality (<s>advaita</s>), brings up that this reason has its domain removed by a perception that grasps difference — how can you, who concede the grasping of difference, respond without also introducing doubt about other continua (<s>santānāntara</s>)?

children.text: ātmā sa tasyānubhavaḥ sa ca nānyasya kasyacit
(PVA III 326ab)

children.translated_text: 'The self (<s>ātman</s>) is its experience, and that does not belong to anyone else.'

children.text: ityādivārtikavyākhyānabhāṣyam |
ātmavādas tarhi prasakta iti cet | na citrākārasaṃvedanāt
children.translated_text: [Objection:] Then the doctrine of a self (<s>ātmavāda</s>) would follow. [Reply:] No, because of the awareness of variegated forms (<s>citrākārasaṃvedana</s>).

children.text: ityādi dveṣacikaluṣāśeṣā eva tuṣākāro 'pi vedāntasiddhānta ity alakṣita tadgranthānutthāpayantī santānāntarāpekṣayā paṭhitavatīty avasthā (?) sarvā saṃvṛtisatyāntaḥpātinī hy evāpaitīti sakalam anākulam iti ||
children.translated_text: And so forth — all the <s>Vedānta</s> doctrines, including even the one [that appears as subtle as] a husk, are entirely tainted by aversion [to the truth]. [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>], not having noticed this, did not raise the texts [of the <s>Vedānta</s>] with respect to other continua — such is the situation (?). [In any case,] all [these objections] fall within the scope of conventional truth (<s>saṃvṛtisatya</s>) and thus depart [without consequence] — so everything is unperturbed.
— and so forth is the commentary-<s>bhāṣya</s> on the <s>Vārttika</s>.

children.text: || santānāntaradūṣaṇaṃ samāptam ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Santānāntaradūṣaṇa</s> (Refutation of Other Mental Continua) is completed.
